In the diocese of Bergamo: the monastery of Saint James of Ponticla, with these dependencies: Presiate, Mediolacum, Portiziana, Mauringo, Glariola, Verziliano, Maglo, Sala, and Vultulina; Saint Paul, with these dependencies: Saint Mary of Sarnecho, Saint Peter of Umbriano, the Holy Trinity of Cremina, Saint Peter of Madegniacum, Saint Michael of Sencino, Saint Martin of Rudiliano, Saint Julia of Cazacum, Saint Thomas of Quintianum, the Holy Savior of the Camonica Valley, Saint Andrew of Brigniano, Saint Mary of Canturi, and Saint Giles of Vergesima.

The monastery of Saint Peter of Rodingo; Saint Peter of Provallo, with these cells: Triguli and Alfianello.

Saint Gabriel of Cremona, with its cells situated in the castle of Fontanella, Trigulo, Grumello, Scandolario, and Brixiana beside Virola.

In Piacenza: the monastery of Saint Gregory, with these cells: the church of Saint Leo of Miradolo and Saint Lawrence of Cuminiacum.

In the diocese of Lodi: the monastery of Saint Mark, with these cells: Saints Firmus and Rusticus of Fratta, the Holy Cross of Vicodardus, and Saint Mary of Calventianum.

The monastery of Saint John of Vertumade, with its churches: the churches of the holy martyrs Cassian and Hippolytus of Ulzade, Saint Mary of Laveno, and Saint Helia of Monte Veglimo, together with all their appurtenances and dependencies.

We confirm that all these things, and whatever in the future, with God’s help, you may justly acquire, shall be perpetually governed, ordered, and possessed by you and your successors, so that no one may ever be permitted to withdraw any part of them from the unity of the monastery of Cluny.

Moreover, just as was established by Pope Gregory of blessed memory in the Roman synod, and recently by us at Piacenza, by the authority of this present privilege we decree that no archbishop, no bishop, and no legate of the Apostolic See shall have the power, without a specific command of the Roman pontiff, to pronounce a sentence of excommunication or interdict against you or your monastery, nor to bring your cases to trial against your will.

We grant to you, and likewise to your successors, for the greater love of your religious observance, the use of the dalmatic, the compagum [sandals], the gloves, and the mitre on the eight principal feast days, just as this use has been granted to you.

If any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly aware of this privilege, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after being warned a second and a third time, if he does not make suitable correction, let him lose the dignity of his power and honor, and know himself to stand accused before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed. Let him be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ, and at the final judgment let him be subjected to strict punishment.

But let the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all who observe what is just toward that place. Amen.

Given at Piacenza by the hand of John, cardinal deacon of the holy Roman Church, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of April, in the third indiction, in the year of the Incarnation of the Lord 1095, in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Urban II, pope.

### CXXXVIII. Pope Urban II’s privilege for the church of Saint Peter of Guastalla. (Year 1095.)

*[Affò, History of the City and Duchy of Guastalla. Guastalla, 1785, quarto, vol. I, p. 325.]*

[Col. 0412D]

Urban, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Andrew, archpresbyter of the Church of Blessed Peter situated in the Guastalla district, and to his brothers, both those present and those who shall canonically be appointed in perpetuity.

It is fitting that we, who, although unworthy, appear by the Lord’s disposition to stand as guardians and proclaimers of justice in the watchtower of the Church of the apostles Peter and Paul, the chief apostles, should assent to just vows and lend our ears to just petitions. Therefore, dearest son in Christ, Andrew, granting our assent to your devout prayers, we receive under the special protection of the Apostolic See the church of the blessed apostle Peter, over which, by the Lord’s appointment, you preside, established at Guastalla on his estate and offered to God and blessed Peter by the most beloved daughter of blessed Peter, Queen Ermengard, and by Lord Garimanus, founder of that church, and raised and consecrated by our predecessor, Pope Gregory V of blessed memory, from the status of a chapel to that of a parish church. We grant and confirm it to you and to your canonically appointed successors in perpetual right, together with three chapels, namely those of Saint Bartholomew, Saint George, and Saint Martin, and with all their possessions or tithes belonging to them.

We establish that no one may presume to build a church within the boundaries of your parish without your permission, and that any such church must be subject to you. Whatever your church now justly and legally possesses, or whatever in the future you may justly and canonically acquire through the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, or the offering of the faithful, we decree by the authority of this present privilege shall remain secure for you and your successors.

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb that Church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass them with rash vexations. Rather, let everything be preserved intact, so that it may in every way benefit the uses of those for whose support and administration it was granted.

When you, the present head of that place, or any of your successors, die, no one shall be appointed there through any trickery or violence, except one whom the brothers, by common agreement, or the sounder part of the brothers’ council, shall regularly elect according to the fear of God. Neither you yourselves nor any minister of that place shall have the power to grant the church’s goods in fief to soldiers or to any secular persons.

We also add this to the present decree: let that church and its canons be secure from every intrusion of secular service and removed from every burden of worldly oppression, diligent and peaceful in the observance of holy religion, and subject on no grounds to anyone other than the Roman Apostolic See, whose jurisdiction they are under.

You shall freely receive chrism, holy oil, the consecrations of churches, the ordinations of clerics, and the other ecclesiastical mysteries from whatever Catholic bishop you wish.

For the rest, if any archbishop, bishop, abbot or abbess, duke, margrave, count, viscount, judge, gastald, or any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly aware of this privilege should attempt to act against it, then, after being warned a second and third time, if he does not make suitable correction, let him lose the dignity of his power and honor, and know himself to stand accused before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed. Let him be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ, and at the final judgment let him be subjected to the strict judgment.

But let the peace of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ be with all who observe what is just toward that place, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find the rewards of eternal peace before the strict judge. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Urban, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at Piacenza by the hand of John, cardinal of the holy Roman Church, on the day before the Kalends of April, in the third indiction, in the year of the Incarnation of the Lord 1096, in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Urban II, pope.

### CXXXIX. Letter of Pope Urban II to Richard, cardinal of the holy Roman Church. (Year 1095.)

*[Duchesne (François), History of All the French Cardinals; Paris, 1660, folio, vol. II, p. 40.]*

[Col. 0414B]

Urban, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved brother in Christ and fellow presbyter Richard, cardinal of the holy Roman Church and abbot of Marseille, and to his successors who shall be regularly appointed in perpetuity.

It is fitting that we, who, although unworthy, appear by the Lord’s disposition to stand as guardians and proclaimers of justice in the lofty watchtower of the apostles Peter and Paul, should assent to just vows and lend our ears to just petitions. Since, therefore, the zeal of your predecessors and of yourself has watched diligently and carefully over the restoration of the condition of certain monasteries, we have rightly decided to grant your petition, so that in ordering those monasteries—that is, in appointing and correcting abbots—we should entrust our authority to you and to your legitimate successors, just as it was entrusted by our predecessor, Gregory of apostolic memory, to your predecessor, the venerable man Bernard, and confirmed by the religious bishops and princes in whose dioceses the monasteries are located:

Namely, the monastery of Saint Mary of Riupoly in the diocese of Ausona; in the diocese of Girona, the monastery of Saint Stephen of Baleols and Saint Peter of Bisaldunum; in the diocese of Elne, the monastery of Saint Michael of Coxano; in Bigorre, the monastery of Saint Savinus and Saint Severus; in the diocese of Albi, the monastery of Saint Benedict of Castres, where blessed Vincent, deacon and martyr, rests; in the diocese of Toulouse, the monastery of Saint Mary of Soricinum; in Rodez, the monastery of Saint Amantius and that of Vabres; in Carcassonne, the monastery of Saint Mary of Crassa; in Nîmes, the monastery of Saint Peter of Psalmodi; in Arles, Saint Peter of Montmajour.

In all these places, when an abbot dies, it shall be the concern of you and your successors, with the common counsel of the religious brothers, regularly to elect a successor from their own congregation. If no one suitable for this governance can be found among them, let them take an abbot from your congregation—that is, the congregation of Marseille—from which they appear to have received the beginnings of their institution and religious life. If, God forbid, an appointed abbot should deviate from the rectitude of his order, it shall be your concern, with the counsel of the diocesan bishop, to correct the abbot’s offenses with regular severity. In this matter the bishops themselves shall not be permitted to resist you by any perverse action.

Moreover, whatever your zeal has acquired through the concession of bishops, the generosity of princes, or the offering of the faithful, we confirm by the authority of this present decree that you and your successors shall possess it perpetually for the use of your brothers, without prejudice to the canonical reverence owed to the bishops. Namely:

Near the city of Avignon, the cell of Saint Saturninus; in the diocese of Uzès, the cell of Saint Mammes of Lurs; in the archdiocese of Aix, the parish church of Cretis, the parish of Affuel, the parishes of Boch and Caudalonga with the same castle, the parish of Roseth, the parish church of Sparo, and Arhga; the castle of Papia near Marimanna, with the port of Bagnères, and the parish of Cofors; in the diocese of Fréjus, the parish church of Grimal, the parishes of Aix and Flayosco, the church of Saint Peter with the parish church of Salernes, the church of Saint Mary with the adjoining church of Cabaza, and the parish of Luch; in the diocese of Carpentras, the church of Saint Felix; in the archdiocese of Embrun, the parish of Turries; in the diocese of Gap, the church of Saint Erigius in the castle of Medoilo at Zénia; the cell of Saint Victor, built under the proprietary right of the monastery of Marseille.

In Sardinia, in the diocese of Gallura, the church of Saint Stephen of Posada, together with the other churches that both the bishop and the judge have bestowed upon the monastery of Mallileni.

In the judicature of Cagliari, the church of Saint Lucifer with its dependent churches; the church of Saint Catherine at Semellia; and likewise the monastery of Saint Saturninus and Saint Antioch, which the bishop of Cagliari handed over to you, we confirm in perpetuity for your monastery, namely in such a way that, by virtue of the decree which our venerable brother and fellow bishop Hugh obtained from us, the bishops of Catalitani shall claim no right over them beyond the right of episcopal obedience.

We wish bishops to be forbidden to excommunicate or interdict your places or churches without consulting you or the heads of those places. Moreover, in churches under interdict we grant you permission, when you come to those places, to celebrate the divine offices separately.

But if hereafter any archbishop or bishop, emperor or king, prince or duke, margrave, count, viscount, judge, or any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly aware of this decree should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after being warned a second and third time, if he does not make suitable correction, let him lose the dignity of his power and honor, and know himself to stand accused before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed. Let him be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ, and at the final judgment let him be subjected to strict punishment.

But let the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all who observe what is just toward your monastery, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find the rewards of eternal peace before the strict judge. Amen.

[Col. 0416A] Enacted at Piacenza by the hand of John, cardinal deacon of the holy Roman Church, on the day before the Nones of April, in the third indiction, in the year of the Incarnation of the Lord 1096, in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Urban II, pope.

### CXL. Decree of Urban II establishing that, after the death of Bishop William, the Church of Orange shall be joined to the Church of Tricastin. (Year 1095.)

*[Mansi, Councils, vol. XX, p. 809.]*

Urban, etc. We wish it not to remain unknown to the knowledge of the present or to the memory of those to come that a long-standing dispute has existed between the people of Tricastin and those of Orange: the people of Tricastin contending over the union, and those of Orange over the division of the parish churches. And in the dispute with our most reverend predecessor Pope Gregory [lacuna], the people of Orange [lacuna], sending letters, he promised that he would send them a legate to investigate this matter; but afterward [lacuna] we were unable to investigate it. During this suspension [lacuna] G [lacuna] was elected and consecrated bishop of the church.

Pontius, therefore, bishop of Tricastin, asserting that the Church of Orange had been possessed for many years by his predecessors, arranged for this complaint to be presented at several Transalpine councils, since he could not bring it to our ears because of the many persecutions suffered by the Roman Church. Finally, when it came to our knowledge, we too ordered that it be deferred for consideration at the next council to be held.

Meanwhile, we took care to inform our venerable brother William, bishop of Orange, that, when he came to the synod, he should prepare himself to defend this matter. When he came, however, he was unable to produce canonical grounds for this division. The bishop of Tricastin, on the other hand, defended his case on the basis of the long-standing possession—more than a century—of the venerable Roman pontiffs, and on the privileges of Gregory and Alexander.

Therefore, because a certain dispute arose among our brothers concerning Gregory’s decree, by which the Church of Orange had been acquired, it seemed good to establish another interval for deciding the case. During it, the bishop of Orange might obtain whatever defense he could, and the clerics of the Church of Tricastin might assure us by oath concerning the same privilege.

When [lacuna] had assembled, and our fellow bishop of Orange, contrary to his promise, had not come, nor had he sent any excuses beforehand, it then seemed good to us to postpone the conclusion of the matter to another time. But when the clerics, pleading the difficulty of the journey and the great expense of their affairs, and crying out most insistently that they could endure no longer delay, our brothers, both the bishops and the cardinals of our Apostolic Church, judged that we ought to accept the satisfaction offered by the clerics of Tricastin.

Accordingly, three clerics of the Church of Tricastin swore upon the holy Gospels that they had seen and read the privilege of the bull of the Roman pontiff Gregory, granted to Boniface, bishop of Tricastin, by which the aforesaid churches had been united. Following the terms of that privilege, Pope Alexander II of holy memory had judged that the aforesaid churches should always remain under one bishop.

After this, the bishop of Orange came with the clerics of his church and produced the letters of Pope Gregory VII mentioned above. He also displayed other written records, by which the truth of the matter became clearer and the account of the people of Tricastin gained strength.

And so, strengthened by such documents, and in accordance with the judgment of our brothers, we decree by this present enactment that, when our venerable brother, the bishop who presently presides over the Church of Orange, dies, both churches shall immediately return to their former unity—unless, after the next Pentecost which, with the Lord preparing the way, we await, it should within the space of one year [lacuna] be established that they were divided by a definite command and decree of the Roman pontiff.

Otherwise, let the whole matter be settled [lacuna], so that when our fellow brother, the bishop named above, dies, that same Church shall pass to the other. The one which has hitherto been regarded as first shall thereafter retain the primacy.

Yet this shall be done in such a way that the bishop who presides over both shall not permit anything to be diminished, in any way or on any pretext, from the provisions, revenues, ornaments, or ministries of the clerics that are held in the patrimonies of either church, however they may be held.

If anyone, however, [the remainder of the formula is omitted in the supplied text].

Enacted at Cremona on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of May [lacuna], in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1095.

### CXLI. Apostolic privilege of Pope Urban II for the monastery of Saint Abundius of Como. (Year 1095.)

*[Tatti, Sacred Annals of the City of Como. Como, 1663, vol. II, p. 864.]*

[Col. 0417C]

Urban, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his son Joseph, abbot of the monastery of Saint Abundius, situated beside the city of Como, and to his successors who shall be regularly appointed in perpetuity.

A desire that is shown to pertain to a religious purpose and the salvation of souls must, with God as its author, be fulfilled without any delay. Since, therefore, your devotion has humbly sought the protection of the Apostolic See, we, assenting to your just petitions, fortify by the authority of this present decree the monastery of the confessor Saint Abundius, over which you preside by the Lord’s generosity.

For we establish that whatever this monastery now possesses through the concession of Catholic pontiffs, the generosity of princes, or the offering of the faithful, and whatever in the future, with God’s help, it may justly and canonically acquire, shall remain secure and inviolate for you and your successors.

Therefore we decree that no one whatsoever may rashly disturb that place, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass them with rash vexations. Rather, let everything be preserved intact, so that it may in every way benefit the uses of those for whose support and administration it was granted, without prejudice to the canonical reverence owed to the Roman Church.

But if hereafter any archbishop or bishop, emperor or king, prince or duke, margrave, count, viscount, judge, or any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly aware of this decree should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after being warned a second and third time, if he does not make suitable correction, let him lose the dignity of his power and honor, and know himself to stand accused before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed. Let him be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ, and at the final judgment let him be subjected to strict punishment.

But let the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all who observe what is just toward that place, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find the rewards of eternal peace before the strict judge. Amen, amen, amen.

Given at Milan by the hand of John, cardinal deacon of the holy Roman Church, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of June, in the third indiction, in the year of the Incarnation of the Lord 1096, in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Urban II, pope.

### CXLII. Apostolic letter of Urban II confirming the rule established by Peter, bishop of Carcassonne, for regular clerics in the church of Saint Nazarius and elsewhere. (Year 1095.)

*[Gallia Christiana, vol. VI, Instruments, p. 431.]*

[Col. 0418C]

Urban, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved brother Peter, bishop of Carcassonne, greetings and apostolic blessing.

Recognizing the justice of your petition, we confirm by the authority of these present letters the institution of regular clerics which, with the Lord’s cooperation, your prudent care has established at the mother church of Saint Nazarius and at the churches of Saint Mary and Blessed Stephen, and we receive it under the protection of the Apostolic See.

Therefore we command, and by the power of the Holy Spirit forbid, that none of your successors, and no one possessing secular or ecclesiastical authority, may overturn those canonical communities or remove the regular way of life established there by you.

Whatever has been granted to those canons through your generosity, or shall hereafter be granted, and whatever other faithful people shall hereafter grant from their own right, let it always remain secure and inviolate, entirely benefiting the uses of the clerics serving there under the observance of regular life.

But if anyone, God forbid, should attempt to oppose this decree of ours, once its authority is known, let him be struck by the punishment of the spiritual sword. Let peace from God and perpetual mercy be preserved for those who observe it.

Given at Milan on the twelfth day before the Kalends of June, in the year 1088.

*[Note: [Col. 0417D] The date is false. Jaffé.]*

### CXLIII. Urban II receives under his protection the Church of Saint Peter of Standalmont, which Countess Matilda handed over to Blessed Peter, and confirms its possessions, on condition that the clerics pay one gold denarius each year, or a bezant every fourth year, to the Lateran palace. (Year 1095.)

*[Dom Calmet, History of Lorraine, Documents, p. 505.]*

[Col. 0419A]

Urban, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons in Christ Leubricus and Guacelinus, and to the other servants of God, both clerics and laymen living with them, at the place called Standalmont in the diocese of Metz, and to their successors who shall remain in the same religious observance in perpetuity.

A desire that is shown to pertain to a religious purpose and the salvation of souls must, with God as its author, be fulfilled without any delay. Therefore, moved by your prayers, venerable sons in Christ, and by the intercessions of the most beloved daughter of blessed Peter, Countess Matilda, we receive under the special jurisdiction and protection of the Apostolic See the place of your habitation, called Standalmont, and the church dedicated to the name of the chief of the apostles.

This place, enclosed by defined boundaries, the aforesaid Countess Matilda, daughter of blessed Peter, handed over to your religious community for the conduct of a common and canonical life, subject to an annual census of one gold denarius to be paid to the Lateran palace.

Therefore, by the authority of the Apostolic See, we establish through this present privilege that all the gifts and possessions which the same countess has granted to your church, or may grant in the future under divine inspiration; whatever any of the faithful may hereafter offer from their own right in any diocese for the salvation of their souls; and whatever you may justly and canonically acquire through the concession of pontiffs or the generosity of princes, shall remain secure and inviolate for you and your successors.

Therefore we decree that no one whatsoever may rashly disturb that place, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass them with rash vexations. Rather, let everything be preserved intact, so that it may in every way benefit the uses of those for whose support and administration it was granted.

When the head of your congregation dies, no one shall be appointed there through any trickery or violence, except one whom the brothers, by common agreement, or the sounder part of the brothers’ council, shall judge should be elected according to the fear of God and canonical institution.

We also establish that, after making his profession, no brother may leave that cloister without the permission of the head or of the congregation. No abbot or bishop, no monk or canon, shall receive one who departs without a common letter of security.

You shall receive the consecrations of churches and the ordinations of clerics from the bishop in whose diocese you are, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the grace and communion of the Apostolic See, and is willing to perform these services freely and without corruption. Otherwise, you shall be free to receive them from any Catholic bishop you choose.

We add that the bishop shall not dare to burden the place itself or impose any custom that would harm the peace of the regular brothers.

Moreover, in the churches which you possess under the jurisdiction of your place in various dioceses, we grant you the free power to appoint rectors from among the brothers of your congregation, without prejudice to the right of the Catholic bishop in whose diocese the churches are situated.

As a sign of the liberty received from the Roman Church, you shall pay the aforesaid census each year, or a bezant in the fourth year, to the Lateran palace.

But if hereafter any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly aware of this decree should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after being warned a second and third time, if he does not make suitable correction, let him lose the dignity of his power and honor, and know himself to stand accused before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed. Let him be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ, and at the final judgment let him be subjected to strict punishment.

But let the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all who observe what is just toward that place, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find the rewards of eternal peace before the strict judge. Amen.

Given at Milan by the hand of John, cardinal deacon of the holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Kalends of June, in the third indiction, in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Urban II, pope.

### CXLIV. Letter of Pope Urban II to the people of Salmoriacum, both clerics and laymen. (Year 1095.)

*[D. Bouquet, Collection, vol. XIV, p. 760.]*

[Col. 0420C]

Urban, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, both clerics and laymen, living in the district of Salmoriacum, greetings and apostolic blessing.

Since our brother, the archbishop of Vienne, has refused to obey the judgment of ourselves and of the council held at Piacenza by the Lord’s generosity—namely, that he restore the archdeaconry of Salmoriacum to the bishop of Grenoble, just as he had been invested with it—we command you by the authority of these present letters that, setting aside your submission to the same archbishop of Vienne, which he appears to be violently demanding from you, you henceforth obey the bishop of Grenoble as your own bishop, until, with both parties present, the same matter is determined by canonical judgment before us or our legate.

But if even now the archbishop of Vienne should presume to harass you concerning this investiture until canonical judgment is rendered, we meanwhile withdraw you from obedience to him.

Given at Milan on the seventh day before the Kalends of June.

### CXLV. Privilege of Urban II for the Church of Besançon. (Year 1095.)

*[Dunod, History of the Sequani, vol. II, p. 585.]*

[Col. 0421A]

Urban, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son Hugh, third archbishop of the holy Church of Besançon, and to his successors who shall be canonically appointed in perpetuity.

The Church acknowledges that the power of binding and loosing in heaven and on earth was principally entrusted, by God as its author, to blessed Peter and his successors, in these words: “Whatever you bind on earth shall be bound also in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth shall be loosed also in heaven.” By that same God, its firmness and the confirmation of another’s faith are granted to him when it is said: “I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail; and you, when you have turned back, strengthen your brothers.”

Therefore it is fitting that we, who, although unworthy, appear to sit in Peter’s place by the Lord’s disposition, should correct what is wrong, confirm what is certain, and govern the whole Church according to the judgment of the inner Judge, so that our judgment may proceed from his countenance and our eyes may see equity.

Therefore, dearest son in Christ, Hugh, assenting to your just petitions, we establish that the holy Church of Besançon, over which you appear by God’s authority to preside by the authority of the Apostolic See, and all the cities and parishes which, in the time of your predecessors, the concession of the Apostolic See subjected to that metropolitan church, shall remain perpetually subject to it.

We also grant that the abbeys within the city, which the Church of Besançon is known to have possessed by ancient right, shall always belong to that same possession.

With regard to those situated outside the city—namely, Balma, Castrum Canonis, Laon, Alta-Petra, Cusat, Valleclus, Palma, Luxeuil, Lure, Faverney, Saint Ursicinus—let your fraternity possess the same right which it is established that your predecessors held by permission of the Apostolic See.

Furthermore, whatever possessions and goods the industry of your predecessors or of yourself has continually and lawfully acquired for the holy Church of Besançon, or may in the future, with the Lord’s generosity, acquire, we decree shall always remain secure and inviolate.

Moreover, we grant you the pallium—that is, the fullness of pontifical dignity—through the kindness and grace of the Apostolic See. Your fraternity shall remember to use it within your church when celebrating the solemnities of Mass, only on those days on which its use was granted to your predecessors by the authority of apostolic privileges.

We also grant your devotion permission to carry the cross before you, according to the ancient custom of your church.

As for the dignity of the pallium, we wish you to vindicate it in every respect, together with the honor, humility, and justice belonging to this garment. Therefore, with your whole mind, let your fraternity hasten to show itself humble in prosperity and, should adversity ever arise, strong; allied with justice, which is the friend of the good and opposed to the wicked; never looking upon anyone’s face against the truth, and never suppressing anyone who speaks in defense of the truth; applying the resources of mercy in proportion to your means, yet desiring to exceed that proportion; sympathizing with the weak, rejoicing with those who prosper, exulting in the joys of others as in your own; fierce in correcting vices, soothing the minds of your hearers by fostering virtues; maintaining judgment in anger without anger, yet in tranquility not abandoning the discipline of just severity.

This, dearest brother, is the dignity of the pallium you have received. If you preserve it carefully, what you have shown yourself to have received outwardly, you will possess inwardly.

May heavenly favor preserve your fraternity unharmed for many years.

Given at Ostia, by the hand of John, cardinal deacon of the holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Kalends of July, in the third indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1096, and in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban II.

## CXLVI. Letter of Urban II to Lambert, Bishop of Arras (1095)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XX, 694.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved brother Lambert, bishop of Arras: greetings and apostolic blessing.

Let your Dilection know that, in the coming November, namely on the octave of Saint Martin, with the Lord’s approval, we have scheduled a synodal council at Clermont. We invite your Prudence to it, so that, setting aside every excuse, you may not fail to attend at the appointed time and place. Know furthermore that the bishop of Cambrai, by letters and messengers sent to us, has strongly interceded on behalf of the Church of Arras, saying that he and his Church are fortified by Roman privileges. Therefore your Prudence ought to come, prepared to answer this matter, together with your clergy.

[Col. 0422C]

Given at Le Puy on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of August.

[Note: [Col. 0421D] Read: the eighteenth day before the Kalends of September.]

## CXLVII. Privilege of Pope Urban II for the monastery of nuns of Saint Peter of Blasilia (1095)

[COCQUELINES, *Collection of Summaries of the Bulls and Privileges of the Supreme Pontiffs*, II, 108.]

[Col. 0422D]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughter in Christ, Florentia, abbess of the monastery of Saint Peter of Blasilia [also: of Bleffe], and to those who shall regularly succeed her in the government of that place, forever.

We recognize that, by God’s providence, we have been promoted to the service of the Apostolic See for this purpose: that we ought effectively to assist its children who implore help and, as the Lord grants, defend and protect those obedient to it. Therefore we ought to extend the hand of protection over venerable places and provide with particular care for the peace of God’s servants and handmaids.

[Col. 0423A]

Accordingly, assenting to your prayers, beloved daughter in Christ Florentia, we receive under the jurisdiction and protection of the Apostolic See the monastery of Saint Peter of Blasilia, situated in the county of Auvergne, over which you preside by God’s authority. It was built by Countess Ermengard and handed over to the Roman Church, and it is established that our predecessors received it in the same manner. Therefore, by this present page of privilege, we decree by apostolic authority that whatever the same monastery justly possesses today, or shall justly and canonically possess or be able to acquire in the future—cells, churches, villages, and all other movable or immovable property—shall always remain secure and inviolate for you and your sisters, both present and future, who shall live there according to the rule.

[Col. 0423B]

We therefore decree that absolutely no person shall be permitted rashly to disturb that monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass them by reckless vexations. Rather, everything shall be preserved intact for those for whose support and governance it was granted, and shall be wholly beneficial to their needs, saving the canonical right of the Apostolic See.

As a token of the liberty received from the Roman Church, you shall pay five solidi of your coinage each year to the Lateran Palace. If, in the future, any archbishop, bishop, emperor, king, prince, duke, count, viscount, judge, or any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly aware of this page of privilege, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after being warned once and twice or three times, if he does not make suitable correction through appropriate satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor.

[Col. 0423C]

The remainder is missing.

## CXLVIII. The canons of the Church of Cahors are confirmed in the profession of the regular life which they had recently made (1095)

[COCQUELINES, volume II, p. 84.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons in Christ, Gosbert the prior and his brothers who have professed the canonical life in the Church of Cahors, and to their successors who shall remain in the same religious observance, forever.

A devout request ought to be completed by the fulfillment that follows, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth laudably and the benefit sought may unquestionably acquire strength. Therefore, since you, beloved sons in Christ, inspired by divine grace, have resolved to restrain your conduct under the discipline of the regular life and to serve Almighty God together according to the institution of the holy Fathers, we grant assent to your vows and petitions with paternal kindness.

Accordingly, by the authority of this present privilege, we confirm the order of the canonical life which you have professed. We also prohibit anyone, after making his profession, from leaving the cloister without the permission of the prior or the community. We fortify both you and all that belongs to you with the protection of the Apostolic See.

[Col. 0424A]

Therefore we decree that you and your successors who remain in the same religious observance shall possess forever all that our venerable brother Gerald, bishop of Cahors, is known to have bestowed for your support and governance: namely, the church of Saint Julian of Bovena; the church of Saint Peter of Mortrado; the revenues of the village called Pardinas; half the offerings from the altar of Saint Stephen; half the monetary census of Cahors which appears to belong to the bishop; one-third of the *paratae* which parishioners customarily purchase for the bishop; and everything else which that bishop has already bestowed upon you or, with the Lord’s generosity, shall bestow in the future.

Also, whatever was formerly granted for the use of the canons of Cahors but was subsequently worn away through their negligence and scattered into the hands of soldiers and other secular persons.

We therefore decree that absolutely no person shall be permitted rashly to disturb that canonical community, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass them by reckless vexations. Rather, everything shall be preserved intact for those for whose support and governance it was granted, and shall be wholly beneficial to their needs.

We also establish by this page of the present decree the provision made by the aforementioned bishop: that the provostship, the archdeaconry, and the other ecclesiastical offices of the Church of Cahors shall be arranged according to the counsel of you and your successors.

If in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly aware of this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after being warned once and twice or three times, if he does not make suitable correction through appropriate satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him acknowledge that he is guilty before the divine judgment because of the iniquity committed; let him be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him be subjected to strict punishment at the final judgment.

But let there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ for all who observe what is just toward that place, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

[Col. 0424D]

[lacuna] of John, cardinal deacon of the holy Roman Church, on the tenth day before the Kalends of September, in the third indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1096 [Note: [Col. 0423D] Read: 1095], [lacuna] Urban II, pope, in his eighth year.

## CXLIX. Privilege for the monastery of Casa-Dei (1095)

[MABILLON, *Benedictine Annals*, V, 337.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Pontius, abbot of the monastery called Casa-Dei, and to the entire community: greetings and apostolic blessing.

Since the grace of Almighty God has arranged that we should visit your monastery and dedicate the basilica of that monastery in honor and under the name of the holy martyrs Vitalis and Agricola, we have judged it fitting—both on account of the merits of blessed Robert, who once founded the monastery through his own work and now protects it by his merits, and on account of the reverence due to your religious observance—to bestow spiritual gifts of the Apostolic See upon you and your successors who shall remain in the observance of the regular discipline. We therefore receive you as special sons of the Roman Church, and so forth.

Given at the borough of Saint-Gilles by the hand of John, cardinal deacon of the holy Roman Church, on the eighth day before the Ides of September, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1095, in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban II.

## CL. Urban exhorts all the faithful throughout Gothia and Provence to contribute to the construction of the Church of Saint Nicholas on an estate granted by Countess Stephanie to the monastery of Saint Victor of Marseille through Urban himself at Tarascon (1095)

[MARTÈNE, *Amplified Collection*, I, 556.]

[Col. 0425B]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to all the faithful throughout Gothia and Provence: greetings and apostolic blessing.

We wish your Dilection to know that Countess Stephanie, together with the nobles of her land, for the salvation of their souls, has granted through our hand to the Marseilles monastery of the blessed martyr Victor a certain small estate at Tarascon, for the construction of a church of the blessed confessor Nicholas.

Therefore [lacuna], beloved sons, we admonish you by these present letters to devote your aid and assistance to the construction of the same [structure] and to the support of the brothers serving God there. Whoever takes care to enlarge that place by alms from his own property, whoever assists by his help and counsel the monks serving God there, and whoever preserves free and inviolate the cemetery established beside the aforementioned church, shall obtain from the Lord forgiveness of his sins and shall be granted the grace of that same God and the blessing of the apostles Peter and Paul.

## CLI. Bull of Pope Urban II for the monastery of Saint-Gilles (1095)

[*Gal. Christ.*, VI, p. 183.]

[Col. 0425D]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons in Christ, Odo, abbot of the monastery of Saint-Gilles, and the entire community: greetings and apostolic blessing.

Thanks are owed to the mercy of heavenly grace both through us and through your religious community, because it has arranged that we should reach your monastery and celebrate with you the solemnity of the blessed Giles. Therefore, burning with greater devotion toward the blessed Giles, we take care to protect and confirm both you and all that belongs to you with the greater protection of the Apostolic See.

Accordingly, by this page of the present decree, we too strengthen every liberty or immunity granted to you and your monastery through the privileges of our predecessors, as well as everything which we are known to have granted you concerning it up to the present.

Providing still more attentively for your peace, we have also endeavored by our authority to restrain the bishop of Nîmes, who was hostile to you. For when he was troubling you over the church of Saint Andrew of Bernice and certain other properties which you had possessed in the time of his predecessors, we ordered him entirely to cease from such molestations and to leave everything to you in peace, just as it was established that you had possessed it in the time of our predecessors.

Furthermore, by apostolic authority we confirm for you and your successors the abbey of Saint Eusebius and all the possessions which you appear justly to possess today, to be possessed forever.

[Col. 0426B]

We also establish that henceforth no archbishop shall be permitted to extend over your monastery or abbot the hand of excommunication or interdict. Rather, by the grace of Almighty God, you shall always remain peaceful and free in the hand of blessed Peter and his vicars.

We grant penitents who seek the basilica of your monastery for the forgiveness of their crimes—the basilica in which the body of blessed Giles is known to rest—the right to enter it and there fulfill their vows to the Lord. We also grant that persons free from marriage may be admitted to the monastic life without episcopal opposition.

For the merits of that same blessed Giles and out of reverence for your religious observance, we wish you to remain entirely peaceful and to be guarded like the pupil of our eye.

To ensure that all these provisions remain firm and inviolate forever, we sanction them by the judgment and authority of Almighty God, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

[Col. 0426C]

Given at Avignon by the hand of John, cardinal deacon of the holy Roman Church, on the day before the Ides of September, in the third indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1096 [1095], in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban II.

## CLII. Pope Urban II confirms the regular discipline of the canons of the Church of Avignon, receiving them and all property belonging to that canonical community under the protection of the Apostolic See (1095)

[COCQUELINES, volume II, p. 81.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Sylvester the provost and his brothers who have professed the canonical life in the Church of Avignon, and to their successors, forever.

A devout request ought to be completed by the fulfillment that follows, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth laudably and the benefit sought may unquestionably acquire strength. Therefore, since you, beloved sons in Christ, inspired by divine grace, have resolved to restrain your conduct under the discipline of the regular life and to serve Almighty God together according to the institution of the holy Fathers, we rejoice in your vows with paternal affection.

Accordingly, with the kindness that is due, we grant assent to your petition and, by the authority of this present privilege, confirm the order of the canonical life which you have professed. We prohibit anyone, after making his profession, from possessing anything privately or from leaving the cloister without the permission of the provost of the community. We fortify both you and all that belongs to you with the protection of the Apostolic See.

[Col. 0427A]

Therefore we decree that you and your successors who remain in the same religious observance shall possess forever all that you appear at present to possess for the support of the common life: namely, the church of Saint Agricola of Lupera; the church of Saint Paul of Palude; Saint Domi…; the church of Saint Columba of Cortedune; the church of Saint George of Garriga; a quarter part of the district of Mairranica and of the islands belonging to it.

Furthermore, we confirm for the use of your community all the prebends, offices, or administrations of the Church of Avignon which you, who by the Lord’s authority are leading the canonical life, possess today, as well as those which certain clerics hold who have not yet renounced their private property, whenever it may happen that these become available; and whatever you may henceforth justly and canonically acquire through the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of princes, or the offerings of the faithful.

We also decree that, when the bishop of your Church dies, the election of his successor shall principally remain with you and with your successors who shall have lived canonically. We judge that the same provision shall perpetually be observed in the election of the provosts and administrators of the entire Church, or of your cloister.

[Col. 0427C]

If in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly aware of this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, if he does not make suitable correction through appropriate satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him acknowledge that he is guilty before the divine judgment because of the iniquity committed; let him be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him be subjected to strict punishment at the final judgment.

But let there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ for all who observe what is just toward that community, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace.

Given at Avignon by the hand of John, cardinal deacon of the Roman Church, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of October, in the third indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1095, in the eighth year of the pontificate of Pope Urban.

## CLIII. Privilege granted by Urban II to the Church of Saint-Ruf, with the canonical reverence due in all matters to the bishop of Avignon preserved (1095)

[*Gal. Christ. vet.*, IV, p. 802.]

[Col. 0427D]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons in Christ, Arbert, abbot, and his brothers who have professed the canonical life in the Church of Saint-Ruf, and to their successors who remain in the same religious observance, forever.

A desire which is shown to pertain to a religious purpose and the salvation of souls ought, with God’s help, to be fulfilled without delay. Therefore, since you, beloved sons in Christ, inspired by the grace of Almighty God, have resolved to renew the manner of life of the infant Church, which has long been neglected, so that with one heart and one soul, under the yoke of the rule, you may serve Almighty God according to the institutions of the holy Fathers, we rejoice in your religious observance with paternal affection.

And so that the religious life once begun may, with God’s help, always remain inviolate, we cherish both you and all that belongs to you in the bosom of the Apostolic See and fortify you by the authority of this present privilege.

We establish that, after making their profession, none of you may possess anything privately, nor may anyone freely leave the cloister without the permission of you, Abbot Arbert, and of those who succeed you in the same government, or without the common permission of the community. If anyone should depart and, after being warned, disdain to return, you and your successors shall have the power to prohibit him everywhere from exercising his offices; and no bishop or abbot shall receive one who has been placed under that prohibition.

Furthermore, by this page of the present decree, we confirm for you by apostolic authority the church of Saint Mary within the city of Lyons; the church of Saint Peter beside the Dia; the church of Saint James of Melgueil; the church of Buxa; the church of Turre; the church of Caneyrag; the church of Venees; the church of Armazanazas with its chapel; the church of Boterita; and everything which Benedictus Rostagnus and Gibillinus, bishops of Avignon, bestowed upon your Church.

In addition, we decree that whatever your monastery justly possesses today, or may justly and canonically acquire in the future through the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of princes, or the offerings of the faithful, shall always remain secure and inviolate for you and your successors who remain in the same religious observance.

[Col. 0428C]

We therefore decree that absolutely no person shall be permitted rashly to disturb that monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass them by reckless vexations. Rather, everything shall be preserved intact for those for whose support and governance it was granted, and shall be wholly beneficial to their needs, while the canonical reverence due in all matters to the bishop of Avignon remains safeguarded.

Given at Tricastin, by the hand of John, cardinal deacon of the holy Roman Church, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of October, in the third indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1096, in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban II.

## CLIV. Privilege of Pope Urban II for the Church of Mâcon (1095)

[*Gal. Christ.*, IV, supplementary volume, p. 284.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved brother Landricus, bishop of Mâcon, and to his successors canonically promoted, forever.

It is fitting that we give assent to just vows and lend our ears to just petitions, since, although unworthy, we appear by the Lord’s arrangement to be guardians and heralds placed upon the lofty watchtower of the chief apostles Peter and Paul.

Therefore, assenting to your just petitions, most reverend brother in Christ Landricus, we fortify by the authority of the Apostolic See the holy Church of Mâcon, over which you preside by God’s authority.

We establish that the churches of Prisciacum, Fabricis, Verchessotum, and Mardubrium; the church of Saint Amor; and everything else which your Fraternity has recovered from the hands of enemies, as well as everything else known justly to belong to that same Church, shall always be preserved free and inviolate for you and your successors.

We also prohibit that, once you have been summoned to the Lord, or any of your successors, anyone should dare, against the will of the clergy of your Church, to take away, plunder, or alienate the property of the bishops or of the Church. We decree that the cloister of the clergy itself and the houses of the cloister shall always remain so free that no one may inflict violence upon them.

In addition, we decree that whatever your Church may henceforth justly and canonically acquire through the generosity of princes or the offerings of the faithful shall remain secure and inviolate for you and your successors.

If any archbishop, bishop, emperor, king, duke, count, viscount, judge, or any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly aware of this page of privilege, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after being warned once and twice or three times, if he does not make suitable correction through appropriate satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him acknowledge that he is guilty before the divine judgment because of the iniquity committed; let him be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him be subjected to strict punishment at the final judgment.

But let there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ for all who observe what is just toward that Church, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at Cluny by the hand of John, cardinal deacon of the holy Roman Church, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of November, in the third indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1096, in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Urban II.

## CLV. Letter of Urban II to Warner of Châtillon: he orders him, under penalty of excommunication, to release Lambert, bishop of Arras, who had been captured while traveling to the synod (1095)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XX, 695.]

[Col. 0429D]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son Warner, son of Pontius: greetings and apostolic blessing, if he obeys.

We have heard that you captured our venerable brother, the bishop of Arras, while he was coming to the council, and we are greatly surprised at the reason for your capture of him. For the king of the Franks not only does not prevent others from coming to us; he has even granted all the bishops and abbots under his authority permission to come to the council.

Therefore, by this present letter, we admonish you, out of reverence for blessed Peter and love for us, to permit the captured bishop to depart freely, together with all his people. Otherwise, for as long as you hold him, we subject both you and your land to excommunication.

## CLVI. Letter of Urban II to the archbishop of Sens: he orders him to admonish Warner to release the bishop of Arras (1095)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XX, 695.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his most beloved brother Richerius, archbishop of Sens: greetings and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0430B]

We have heard that Warner, son of Pontius, captured and continues to hold our venerable brother, the bishop of Arras, while he was coming to the council. Therefore, by this present letter, we order you to admonish that same Warner to restore the captured prelate, together with all his people, to liberty. If he refuses, then, for as long as he holds him, subject both Warner himself and his territory to excommunication.

## CLVII. Privilege for the monastery of Silviniacum (1095)

[*Bibliotheca Cluniacensis*, p. 309.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons in the Lord, the monks of the monastery of Silviniacum: greetings and apostolic blessing.

Since, by the manifold favor of heavenly blessing, it has been brought about that we ourselves should be privileged to visit your monastery and to transfer the body of blessed Majolus within the church to another place, we have judged it fitting—both because of our special affection for the monastery of Cluny, to which you cling uniquely as members to the head, and because of our reverence for your religious observance—to fortify you and your place more particularly with the protection of the Apostolic See.

Therefore, in the presence of our fellow bishop, our venerable brother Durantius, bishop of Auvergne, we establish that your monastery shall never at any time suffer the loss of an interdict on account of a general excommunication or interdict of the parish. Nor shall any living person have the power, within the monastery or the bounds of the neighboring village, to make an assault, capture anyone, or engage in plunder.

Accordingly, we caused the distinguished knight Archimbaud, under the pledge of his own hand, to promise in our presence, over the tomb of his own father, that throughout his entire life he would preserve inviolate everything which his father or grandfather had bestowed upon your place, both in property and in immunities and customary rights, and so forth.

Given at Monticello by the hand of John, cardinal deacon of the holy Roman Church, on the Ides of November, in the third indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1097, in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban.

## CLVIII. Settlement made between Godfrey, bishop of Maguelonne, and Peter, abbot of Aniane, at the Council of Clermont (1095)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XX, 910.]

[Col. 0431A]

When Lord Pope Urban II was presiding at a council at Clermont, the city of Auvergne, with the primates of various provinces, many archbishops, and abbots seated in the same council, Godfrey, bishop of Maguelonne, came before the venerable pope and lodged a complaint against Abbot Peter and the monks of the monastery of Aniane.

He alleged that they sought or received the ordinations of the monks and abbot, and the consecrations of churches, from somewhere other than the Church of Maguelonne; and that, contrary to what was lawful, by illicit presumption and under the pretext of possessing the privilege of granting penance, excommunicating, absolving, reconciling, or indiscriminately receiving for burial parishioners from anywhere whatsoever, they claimed an unheard-of license.

When this was reported in the council, it greatly displeased everyone. It pleased Lord Pope Urban and the entire holy college that such a privilege should be annulled and erased, and that Peter, abbot of Aniane, should come in the middle of the council before the bishop of Maguelonne and promise in his hand the obedience due to the Church of Maguelonne concerning ordinations, consecrations, and judgments, while nevertheless preserving the privileges of the monastery of Aniane insofar as they had been established according to the canons for the salvation and stability of that monastery.

[Col. 0431C]

Pope Alexander II had previously made this same settlement between the two Churches, writing as follows:

“Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the abbot and the entire community of the monastery of Aniane: greetings and apostolic blessing.

A complaint from the bishop of Maguelonne concerning your intolerable presumption and disobedience has reached us. Although you know that the Roman Church recognizes and tolerates him as a bishop, you attribute to him no honor of episcopal reverence. Indeed, by contempt for him and by usurping what is unlawful for you, you commit a grave and wicked offense against the body of the whole Church.

For when, unsupported by any authority, you receive those whom he has excommunicated, and when, disregarding the laying on of his hands, you seek your ordinations elsewhere at your pleasure, you thereby corrupt the institutions of canonical tradition and produce a serious scandal in the Church by your reprehensible example.

Therefore, by apostolic authority, we admonish you to abandon these and similar practices completely and henceforth to render to the aforementioned bishop, your bishop, the obedience and reverence that are due in all respects. Know that, if this complaint is brought to us again, the obstinacy of your presumption will call down upon itself strict vengeance.”

[Col. 0431D]

To ensure that no occasion for dissension or discord should remain between the Churches of Maguelonne and Aniane, Lord Pope Urban ordered this settlement to be written down and confirmed the written document with the seal of the Apostolic See.

Given in Auvergne on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of December, by the hand of John, cardinal deacon of the holy Roman Church, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1095, in the third indiction, in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban II.

## CLIX. Bull confirming the privileges of the monastery of Celsiniacum (1095)

[BALUZE, *Miscellany*, II, 175.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the monks of the monastery of Celsiniacum: greetings and apostolic blessing.

We recognize that, by the Lord’s arrangement, we have been promoted to the service of the Apostolic See for this purpose: that we ought effectively to assist its children who implore help and, as the Lord grants, defend and protect those obedient to it. Therefore we too ought to extend the hand of protection over venerable places and provide with particular care for the peace of God’s servants.

Accordingly, both on account of your special religious observance and out of affection for our venerable brother Hugh, abbot of Cluny, under whose care your place belongs by right of the monastery of Cluny, we assent to your prayers, beloved sons in Christ, and fortify your monastery by the authority of this present decree.

We establish that whatever your monastery justly possesses today, or may justly and canonically acquire in the future through the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of princes, or the offerings of the faithful, shall always remain secure and inviolate for you and your successors. Among these we have judged that the following should be specified by their proper names:

In the borough adjoining the monastery itself: Saint Mary and Saint Martin;

in the district of Usson: the church of Saint Remigius of Carniac, Saint James of Varennes, Saint Quintinus, Saint Stephen, Saint Julian of Palearia, Saint Mary of Masliac, Saint Germanus of Brennacum, the new church in the district of Lurdan, the monastery of Calcidium, Saint Mary of Beverias, the church of Monterevello, of Viverolo, of Bafia, of Grandrivo, of Zalmantanias, of Ambert, of Marcac, and of Teuleria;

the church of Saint Mary of Monte, Saint Ferreolus, and Saint Eligius;

in the district of Privas: the church of Saint Florina, Saint Gervasius, the church of Abulnac, Burnunculum, Leuton, Lendan, Clais, Vescon, and Girmac;

in the district of Talende: the church of Saint Hilary, Saint Martial, the church of Chidrac, Monte Acuto, Plauzac, Ozac, and Soletis, and the chapel of Monte;

in the district of Todorn: the church of Saint Lupus, Saint Julian, and Saint Mary at Cauriacum; the church of Matesc with the churches belonging to that place;

in the district of Talu: the church of the holy martyrs Cyricus and Julitta, Saint Pardulfus, Saint Donatus, and Saint Victor; and the church of Cingulis, with all their possessions and appurtenances.

Furthermore, we decree that absolutely no person shall be permitted rashly to disturb that church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass them by reckless vexations. Rather, everything shall be preserved intact for those for whose support and governance it was granted, and shall be wholly beneficial to their needs, while the reverence due in all matters to the abbots of Cluny remains safeguarded.

No one shall have the power to invade or plunder the borough adjoining the monastery, or to impose any harmful customary exactions upon it.

We also decree that the burial ground of that place shall be entirely free, so that no one may obstruct the devotion and final wish of those who decide to be buried there, unless they happen to be excommunicated.

And because, by the Lord’s generosity, the church of your monastery has been consecrated by our hands, we add this to the present chapter: out of reverence for blessed Peter and for our consecration, no one shall henceforth dare to pronounce a sentence of excommunication or interdict against the same monastery. Thus, secure from every harassment of individual servitude and removed from every burden of worldly oppression, may you diligently and peacefully observe the holy religion and strive with every virtue of mind and soul to please Almighty God.

[Col. 0433C]

If any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly aware of this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after being warned once and twice or three times, if he does not make suitable correction through appropriate satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him acknowledge that he is guilty before the divine judgment because of the iniquity committed; let him be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him be subjected to strict punishment at the final judgment.

But let there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ for all who observe what is just toward that place, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

Given at the town of Saint-Flour by the hand of John, cardinal deacon of the holy Roman Church, in the third indiction, on the seventh day before the Ides of December, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1095, in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Urban II.

## CLX. Letter of Urban II to the canons of Angoulême, confirming the grant of the provostship of Juliacum made to them by Ademar (1095)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XX, 919.]

[Col. 0433D]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the canons of the Church of Angoulême: greetings and apostolic blessing.

The authority of our office urges us to be concerned for the condition of the Churches and to establish what has been rightly decreed. Accordingly, by the authority of these present letters, we confirm that constitution which our venerable brother Ademarus, bishop, established concerning that provostship which is in the village of Juliacum, in the district of Saintes. For we decree that this provostship shall never be alienated by sale, nor ever be withdrawn from the governance and sustenance of the brothers [Col. 0434A] living in common in the church of Angoulême on the pretext of kinship or succession, so that none of the bishops of Angoulême may claim the revenues of that village or provostship for other uses. Rather, both that property and all the other things which you rightly possess today, as well as whatever you may recover from what has been lost or may lawfully acquire elsewhere, shall always remain entire and inviolate for you and your successors who continue in the common life. But if anyone should obstinately attempt to oppose this constitution and decree of our authority, then, after having been admonished with suitable intervals, unless he corrects his conduct by making appropriate satisfaction, let him be punished by the sword of the Holy Spirit and by the vengeance of apostolic discipline.

Given at Clermont in Auvergne, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of December, [Col. 0434B] by the hand of John, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman Church, in the third indiction, in the year of the Lord 1096 [1095], in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban II.

### CLXI. Pope Urban II confirms the possessions and rights of the monastery of Aubechies. (Year 1095.)

[Gallican Christian History III, Documents, p. 17.]

[Col. 0434C]

Urban, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son Roger, abbot of the monastery situated in the diocese of Cambrai, on the island called Abbatias: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The authority of our office urges us to establish what has been rightly decreed. Therefore, most beloved son Roger, inclining the ears of apostolic benevolence to your petitions, by the authority of the present decree we fortify the monastery of the Most Holy Trinity, over which, by God’s authority, you preside. We also decree by apostolic authority that whatever goods our venerable brother Gerard, bishop of Cambrai—by whose donation that place itself is evidently known to have been founded—gave to the aforesaid monastery, and whatever else any of the faithful have granted from their own right, shall always remain entire and inviolate. We have therefore decreed that no one at all shall be permitted rashly to disturb that place, or to take away, diminish, or harass with reckless vexations its possessions; [Col. 0434D] rather, everything shall be preserved intact and shall in every way benefit the uses of those for whose support and governance it was granted. Whoever, out of reverence for divine fear, strives to enrich, protect, or exalt that place with his goods, according to his means, shall obtain the mercy of almighty God and the grace of his apostles. But whoever attempts obstinately to act contrary to the tenor of this decree of ours shall be punished by the sword of the Holy Spirit.

Given at Clermont in Auvergne by the hand of John, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Kalends of December, in the third indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1095; in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Urban II, pope.

### CLXII. Confirmation of Saint Dionysius of Nogent, made by Lord Pope Urban II. (Year 1095.)

[Cluniac Library, p. 544.]

[Col. 0435A]

Urban, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the entire congregation of the monastery of Saint Dionysius, situated between the river Iguna and the fortress of Nogent: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Just as access ought to be denied to those making unreasonable requests, so we ought to meet the desires of those making just requests with benevolent assent. Therefore we judged it right to grant the devotion of our beloved sons Count Geoffrey of Mauritania and his wife Beatrice.

This count had finally completed, through his own efforts, the monastery of the martyr Saint Dionysius in the diocese of Chartres, between the river Iguna and the fortress of Nogent. It had been founded by his grandfather Geoffrey and partly built by his father Rotrocus. After completing it and endowing it with his possessions, with the assent of the venerable men Richer, archbishop of Sens, and Geoffrey, bishop of Chartres, and with the praise and signatures both of his above-named wife Beatrice and of his son Rotrocus, he offered it to the holy apostles Peter and Paul and to the monastery of Cluny, in the presence of our most reverend brother Hugh, abbot. They requested that this offering be confirmed by our authority.

Therefore we decree that the aforesaid monastery of blessed Dionysius, together with everything belonging to it, shall perpetually remain under the jurisdiction and disposition of the Cluniac brothers. [Col. 0435C] We command and forbid under threat of anathema that anyone should ever withdraw that place from the unity of the monastery of Cluny.

We also establish by apostolic authority that whatever gifts and possessions the aforesaid counts or any other faithful people have granted from their own right to that monastery shall always remain entire and inviolate under the protection of the apostolic see:

The village adjoining the church mentioned above, with ten agripenns of meadow; all the land surrounding the church as far as the river Rodua; and two mills upon that river. Burchard’s land with its orchard. The land of Belseria, of the village of Ascon. The church of Saint Hilary with all its tithes and appendages. The church of Saint Leobinus of Flaciacum; Saint Leobinus of Bracle; Saint Hilary of Bebanisuilla; [Col. 0435D] Saint Albinus of Coldreciolum; Saint Mary of Margon; Saint Peter of Bruyeria; Saint Martin of Berduys. The churches of Saint John of Mauritania, Saint Macutus, and Saint Germanus. The church of Saint Albinus of Campo Rotundo, with all the land of Nigella and all its appendages on the river Era.

At the place called Vivariis, all cultivated and uncultivated land, both that already surveyed and that still to be surveyed, with meadows, woods, and the property of the servants residing there and in the county of Mauritania. In the diocese of Le Mans, the church of Saint Peter of Cetone, and the customary woodland both for the use of the church and for the use of the monks and their people, except the woodland of Perticulus. In all the woods, free pasture for the monastery’s swine.

At the place called Oratorius, the land of one plough. At Morisim, the land of one plough. In Fracta Vallis, ten agripenns of vineyard and the mill of Ruitaria. The land of Bremuncurtum and the land of Bonnac with their toll-bridges. A fishery in the river Lognia, from the ford of Bellivilaris to the water called Edera; half of Bebanisvilla; and the wood called Ostenganis.

The tenth part of the toll of the fortress of Mauritania. Likewise, the tenth part of the toll of the fortress of Nogent. Also, the tenth part of the forest of Pasnadius, which is called Resno. Likewise, the church of Saint Stephen and Saint John in the fortress of Nogent.

Saint Hilary, Saint John, Saint Stephen, and Saint Mary in the fortress of Noiomi. Saint Martin of Magon; Saint Albinus of Campo Rotundo; Saint Albinus of Codricellum; Saint Mary Magdalene of Ferraria; Saint Hilary of Belenvilla. Saint John of Petrafixa; Saint Peter [Col. 0436B] of Aponviller; Saint Anastasius of Ronviller; Saint Saviour of Campo Rotundo; Saint Peter of Boscniletum; Saint Martin of Unverre; Saint Leobinus of Flacci; and the church of Oratorius with all its appendages and tithes.

These possessions are in the diocese of Chartres. In the diocese of Le Mans: the church of Saint Peter of Cetone; the church of Saint Ulfacius; Saint Peter of Mauvis; Saint Praejectus of Vileris; Saint Hilary, which is beside Saint Ceronna; Saint Mary of Bure; Saint Martin of Loiseel; Saint Germanus of Loisilz; Saint Mary, Saint John, and Saint Macutus of Mauritania; Saint Audoenus of Tesval; Saint Gervasius of Feris; Saint Audoenus of Verreriis; Saint Martin of Belotus; Saint Martin of Berziis; Saint Martin of Jamagiis; and Saint Peter of Bruyeria.

Moreover, whatever your monastery rightly possesses today or may hereafter lawfully and canonically acquire shall remain secure and inviolate for you and your successors. We therefore decree that no one at all shall be permitted rashly to disturb that monastery, or to take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass them with reckless vexations. Rather, everything shall be preserved intact and shall in every way benefit the uses of those for whose support and governance it was granted, without prejudice to the canonical reverence due to the bishop of Chartres.

If in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly confronting this decree, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after being admonished a second or third time, unless he corrects his conduct by making appropriate satisfaction, let him lose the dignity of his power and honor, acknowledge himself condemned by divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ, and be subject to strict punishment at the final judgment.

But let there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ for all who preserve what is just for that monastery, so that both here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

### CLXIII. Pope Urban II’s letter to Count Guigo. (Year 1095.)

[D. Bouquet, Collection, vol. XIV, p. 761.]

Urban, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to Guigo, count, and to the clergy and people of Grenoble: greeting and apostolic blessing.

You should know that the complaint of our venerable brother Hugh, your bishop, concerning the district of Salmorica, which had long been under dispute, was settled by the authority of the council that we celebrated at Clermont, a city in Auvergne. Since our brother Guido, archbishop of Vienne, had often been admonished both by our letters and by the living voice of our mouth, yet had scorned to obey in this matter and had refused to carry out the investiture that we made to the same bishop of yours at Piacenza, we restored to our aforesaid brother and to the church of Grenoble that possession which both the same brother Hugh and some of his predecessors are known to have possessed. And for as long as the archbishop of Vienne refuses to obey this decision, we withdraw both that same Bishop Hugh and the church of Grenoble from the archbishop’s obedience. We also forbid all who dwell in that district, clergy and laity alike, to obey the archbishop of Vienne until either he carries out the judgment that has been rendered or this complaint, having been examined before us by canonical judgment between the two parties, receives a definitive conclusion.

Given on the third day before the Kalends of December at Clermont in Auvergne.
