Let the whole world experience and see that what has been cast down is raised up, what has grown old is renewed, and that through him from whom all things took their beginning everything returns to wholeness. Through him.

**Prayer.** Grant, we ask, almighty God, that the splendor of your brightness may shine forth, and that the light of your light may confirm, through the illumination of the Holy Spirit, the hearts of those who have been reborn by your grace. Through him.

**Secret.** Sanctify, O Lord, we ask, the gifts offered [Col. 0850B], and cleanse our hearts through the illumination of the Holy Spirit. Through him.

**Communicantes.** And celebrating the most sacred day of Pentecost, on which the Holy Spirit appeared to the apostles in various tongues. But also keeping the memory—

**Hanc igitur.** This offering of our service, and also of your entire household, which we offer to you for those also whom you have deigned to regenerate from water and the Holy Spirit, granting them remission of all sins, we ask, O Lord, that you receive it favorably, and our days—

**Communion.** May the infusion of the Holy Spirit cleanse our hearts, O Lord, and make them fruitful through the sprinkling of his dew. In unity.

## ON THE HOLY DAY OF PENTECOST

[Col. 0850C] O God, who on this day taught the hearts of the faithful through the illumination of the Holy Spirit, grant us in that same Spirit to think rightly and always to rejoice in his consolation. Through him.

**Secret.** Sanctify, we ask, O Lord, the gifts offered, and cleanse our hearts through the illumination of the Holy Spirit. Through him.

**Preface.** (+) Eternal God, through Christ our Lord, who, ascending above all the heavens and sitting at your right hand, poured forth on this day the promised Holy Spirit upon the children of adoption. Therefore the whole world throughout the earth rejoices with overflowing joys, and the heavenly powers and angelic authorities sing the hymn of glory without end, saying—

[Col. 0850D] **Communicantes:** As above.

**Hanc igitur:** As above.

**Communion.** “Of the Holy Spirit, O Lord, of your …” The remainder is in the vigil.

## AT THE DEDICATION OF A CHURCH

O God, who each year renew for us the day of the consecration of this holy [Col. 0851A] temple of yours and preserve us unharmed through the sacred mysteries, hear the prayers of your people and grant that whoever enters this temple to seek benefits may rejoice that he has obtained them all. Through him.

**Secret.** Give ear, we ask, O Lord, to our prayers, so that all of us who are enclosed within the precincts of this temple, whose anniversary of dedication we celebrate, may please you through complete and perfect devotion of body and soul; so that, while we render these present vows, we may, with your help, deserve to come to eternal rewards. Through him.

**Postcommunion.** O God, who have deigned to call your Church a bride, so that she who possessed grace through devotion to God might also possess piety in name [Col. 0851B], grant that all this people, serving your name, may deserve to be worthy of sharing this title; and that your Church, gathered to you in the temple whose anniversary is celebrated, may fear you, love you, and follow you, so that, while she continually walks in your footsteps, she may, with you as guide, deserve to reach the heavenly promises. Through him.

[**Note:** [Col. 0851C] This Mass, with its preface, belongs to the Ambrosian rite, though it has been somewhat altered. Father Blanchinus gives the Ambrosian preface in these words: “Eternal God, and on this day of today’s festival, on which blessed John the Baptist arose, to rejoice—he who, before he was born, sensed the voice of the Lord’s Mother, and, while still enclosed in the womb, carried the coming of human salvation in prophetic exultation; who by his conception removed the barrenness of his mother and by his birth released his father’s tongue; and who alone among all the prophets showed the Redeemer of the world whom he had announced,” and so forth. What follows in the Ambrosian rite is omitted in ours; but what continues in our Sacramentary is taken from the Gregorian rite, namely: “and so that the nature of the waters might receive the effect of sacred purification, by sanctifying the streams of the Jordan he washed with baptism the Author of baptism himself.” And therefore, etc.]

## ON THE NATIVITY OF SAINT JOHN THE BAPTIST

O God, who have made this present day honorable for us through the nativity of blessed John, grant your peoples the grace of spiritual joys, and direct the minds of all the faithful into the way of eternal salvation. Through him.

**Secret.** O Lord, we heap your altars with gifts, celebrating with due honor the nativity of him who both sang that the Savior of the world was to come and showed that our Lord Jesus Christ was present [Col. 0851C].

**Preface.** (+) Eternal God, on this day of today’s festival, on which blessed John the Baptist arose: he who, before he was born, sensed the voice of the Lord’s Mother, and, while still enclosed in the womb, carried the coming of human salvation in prophetic exultation; who by his conception removed the barrenness of his mother and by his birth released his father’s tongue; and who alone among all the prophets showed the Redeemer of the world whom he had foretold; and so that the nature of the waters might receive the effect of sacred purification, by sanctifying the streams of the Jordan he washed with baptism [Col. 0852A] the Author of baptism himself. And therefore with—

**Postcommunion.** May your Church, O God, take joy in the birth of blessed John the Baptist, through whom she recognized Jesus Christ your Son, the author of her rebirth.

## ON THE NATIVITY OF THE APOSTLES PETER AND PAUL

O God, who consecrated this day to the martyrdom of your apostles Peter and Paul, grant that your Church may follow their teaching in all things, through whom she received the beginning of religion. Through him.

**Secret.** May the apostolic prayer pursue, O Lord, the sacrifices which we offer to be consecrated to your name; through it grant that we may be cleansed and defended. Through him.

**Preface.** (+) It is right and salutary humbly to beseech you, O Lord, that you, eternal Shepherd, may not abandon your flock [Col. 0852B], but guard it through the continual protection of your blessed apostles, so that it may be governed by those same rulers whom you have appointed as shepherds to preside over it as vicars of your work. And therefore with—

**Communion.** Guard from every adversity, O Lord, through the intercession of the apostles, those whom you have satisfied with heavenly nourishment. Through him.

## ON THE NATIVITY OF SAINT LAWRENCE

Grant us, we ask, almighty God, to extinguish the flames of our vices, who granted blessed Lawrence to overcome the fires of his torments. Through him.

**Secret.** Receive, we ask, O Lord, the gifts graciously offered, and grant that, through the assisting merits of blessed Lawrence, they may reach the aid of our salvation [Col. 0852C]. Through him.

**Postcommunion.** Satisfied with the sacred gift, we humbly beseech you, O Lord, that what we celebrate in the duty of our service may be experienced by us as an increase of your salvation. Through him.

[**Note:** [Col. 0851D] There are various opinions concerning the time at which, before the eleventh century, the feast of the blessed Virgin assumed into heaven was celebrated; Martene reports them. Mabillon, in *Gallican Liturgy* (Book II), writes that it was celebrated on 18 January, and proves this by the authority of the most ancient martyrologies. Among them he cites Florentinius’s *Hieronymian Martyrology*, where it says: “On the fifteenth day before the Kalends of February, the burial of holy and glorious blessed Mary, Mother of Our Lord Jesus Christ”; and there he speaks most explicitly of this feast, transferred to 15 August by the command of the emperor Maurice, which he proves by the authority of Nicephorus [Col. 0852D]. The statement of Nicephorus should be understood in this way (*Book XVII*, chapter 28): the feast, already instituted by the Church, was propagated throughout the East by the sanction issued by Maurice. Consequently, Martene does not agree with those who assign the institution of this feast to the eighth century. Pagi should also be consulted in his *Breviary* (no. 26), under Sergius.

In this Mass the first and last prayers deserve notice, since they mention the death of the blessed Virgin and her assumption into heaven, in order to restrain the rashness of the heretical Collyridians, who asserted that the blessed Virgin, possessing a divine nature, escaped the corruption of death. The holy Roman Church has consistently recognized in her only a human nature, and that she possessed a mortal body and truly died. Therefore many martyrologies announce her dormition on 18 January. See Baronius’s notes on the martyrology for 15 August.]

## ON THE DAY OF THE ASSUMPTION OF HOLY MARY

Venerable to us, O Lord, is this day’s festival, on which the holy Mother of God underwent temporal death, yet could not be overcome by the bonds of death—she who gave birth from herself to your Son, our Lord, incarnate. Who lives and reigns with you.

[Col. 0853A] **Secret.** Be appeased, O Lord, by the gifts offered, and, through the intercession of blessed Mary ever-virgin together with all your saints, defend us from every danger. Through him.

**Secret.** May the prayer of the Mother of God come to the aid of your people, O Lord, so that, although we know that she departed according to the condition of the flesh, we may believe that in heavenly glory she prays before you for us. Through him.

**Preface.** (+) Eternal God, and to praise, bless, and proclaim you with rejoicing hearts in honor of the holy virgins, among whom the undefiled Virgin Mary, Mother of God, shone gloriously; whose assumption we celebrate. She conceived your Only-Begotten Son through the overshadowing of the Holy Spirit, and, while the glory of her virginity remained, poured forth eternal light upon this world: Jesus Christ our Lord [Col. 0853B]. Whom the angels praise.

**Postcommunion.** Having become participants in the heavenly table, we implore your clemency, O Lord our God, that we who celebrate the feasts of the Mother of God may be freed from impending evils through her intercessions. Through the same.

[**Note:** [Col. 0853C] We have in this Mass a valid argument against those who claim that this feast was instituted in the thirteenth century by Innocent IV. Cardinal Baronius discusses its antiquity brilliantly in his notes on the martyrology for 8 September. At what definite time it was instituted, however, is not clear. From ecclesiastical histories we know that the Gallican Church did not know this feast in the time of Charlemagne and Louis the Pious, as is evident from the Council of Mainz [Col. 0853D] held in 813. Its institution or propagation must therefore be assigned to after the ninth century. From our Missal, in which the Mass is written out, and in the final Appendix the preface also, we may suspect that this feast was propagated around the eleventh century.]

## ON THE NATIVITY OF HOLY MARY

Hear mercifully, O God, the supplication of your servants, so that we who gather on the nativity of the Mother and Virgin of God may, having been reconciled through her intercessions, be rescued by you from present dangers. Through him.

**Secret.** May the humanity of your Only-Begotten Son come to our aid, O Lord, so that he who, born from a Virgin, did not diminish but consecrated the integrity of his Mother may, in the solemn celebrations of her nativity, strip us of our offenses and make our offering acceptable to himself [Col. 0853C]. Through him.

**Postcommunion.** Having received the sacraments, may we, through the intercession of blessed and glorious Mary ever-virgin, Mother of God, advance toward the increase of eternal redemption. Through him.

[**Note:** [Col. 0853D] The feast of Saint Michael the archangel is assigned to the third day before the Kalends of October, on which day the dedication of his church on Mount Gargano is universally celebrated. In my fourteenth-century parchment breviary it reads: “On the third day before the Kalends of October, the dedication of the basilica of Saint Michael, a double feast.” Cardinal Baronius observes in his notes on the martyrology that the eighth day before the Ides of May concerns the apparition of Saint Michael, whereas this day concerns the dedication of the church, which seems to have taken place on the day when the solemn commemoration of all the angels was customarily celebrated in the ancient Church. Indeed, in our Sacramentary two prayers of this Mass are addressed to all the angels, the final prayer to all [Col. 0854C] archangels, while the preface concerns Saint Michael alone, the prince of the angels. Therefore the ancient rite mentioned by Baronius is preserved here, and on this feast the solemn commemoration of the individual angels is observed.]

## ON THE FEAST OF SAINT MICHAEL THE ARCHANGEL

[Col. 0854A]

O God, who arrange in wondrous order the ministries of angels and human beings, mercifully grant that, just as those who minister to you always stand before you in heaven, so through them our life on earth may be fortified. Through him.

**Secret.** We humbly offer you sacrifices of praise, O Lord, beseeching you that, through the same angels’ intercession on our behalf, you may both receive them favorably and grant that they may reach our salvation. Through him.

**Preface.** (+) Eternal God, while we proclaim the merits of Saint Michael the archangel—for although every angelic sublimity that stands in the presence of your majesty is worthy of our reverence, that one is nevertheless to be honored more earnestly which, in the dignity of its rank [Col. 0854B], deserved the primacy of the heavenly army—through Christ.

**Communion.** Filled with heavenly blessing, O Lord, we humbly implore you that what we celebrate through fragile service may, through the assistance of the holy archangels, prove beneficial to us. Through him.

[**Note:** [Col. 0854C] The feast of All Saints is later than the time of Saint Gregory. It began at Rome by order of Boniface IV and subsequently became common to the other Churches as well through the command of Gregory IV. Thus Baronius states in his note on the Martyrology, from the Chronicle of Sigebert under the year 835, where it says that Louis the Pious, at the urging of Gregory IV and with the other bishops agreeing, decreed that in Gaul and Germany the feast of All Saints should be observed on the Kalends of November. For their memory was not celebrated before Louis the Pious, as is clear from the Council of Mainz under Charlemagne, in which there is no mention of this feast. Here we have its own preface in the final Appendix.]

## ON THE FEAST OF ALL SAINTS

Almighty and eternal God, who have granted us to venerate the merits of all your saints in one celebration, we ask that through their multiplied intercessions you may bestow upon us the abundance of your desired favor. Through him.

**Secret.** We offer you, O Lord, the gifts of our devotion, that they may be pleasing to you in honor of all the just and, through your mercy, become salutary for us. Through him.

[Col. 0854C] **Communion.** Grant, we ask, O Lord, that the faithful peoples may always rejoice in the veneration of all the saints and be fortified by their perpetual supplication. Through him.

[**Note:** [Col. 0854D] On this same day we have another Mass for Saint Caesarius the martyr. His passion is also commemorated in the Roman Martyrology on the Kalends of November, just as in my previously mentioned Breviary it reads on the Kalends of November: “The feast of All Saints and of Saint Caesarius the martyr.” Baronius relates much about Saint Caesarius in his notes on the Martyrology, revealing the Benedictine order’s special devotion to him. Saint [Col. 0855C] Caesarius had Alberic, a deacon of the monastery of Cassino, as the writer of his acts, according to Peter the Deacon in *On Illustrious Men* (chapter 11). Gelasius II, supreme pontiff, formerly a monk of Cassino, adorned his acts with verses. At Rome an ancient church of Saint Caesarius was extremely famous, one of twenty-two abbeys which the same Baronius saw recorded in an ancient ritual book preserved in the Vatican Library, in the manuscript called the *Book of Censuses*. Today the cardinals of the holy Roman Church are adorned with the title of this church. The body of Saint Caesarius now rests at Santa Croce in Jerusalem, in the Sessorian district, with Benedictine-Cistercian monks. Relying on these arguments, I conjecture that the Benedictine monks were drawn to a special veneration for Saint Caesarius [Col. 0855D]; therefore, in our Sacramentary his memory is so conspicuously observed that perhaps two Masses were solemnly sung on this same day.]

## ON THE SAME DAY: SAINT CAESARIUS

O God, who gladden us through the annual solemnity of blessed Caesarius your martyr [Col. 0855A], mercifully grant that we may imitate the actions of him whose birthday we celebrate. Through him.

**Secret.** Graciously receive, O Lord, the sacrifices dedicated to you for blessed Caesarius your martyr, and grant us to reach perpetual assistance through his merits. Through him.

**Communion.** Almighty God, grant that we who have received heavenly nourishment may, through the intercession of blessed Caesarius your martyr, be fortified by it against every adversity. Through him.

[**Note:** [Col. 0855D] Another saint whom the Benedictine order pursued with special devotion was Saint Martin, bishop of Tours, whose Mass is found in the sacramentary books, including both the Gelasian and Gregorian. Saint Benedict himself erected an oratory on Monte Cassino in his honor. The feast of Saint Martin began to be celebrated immediately after his death; therefore, among confessors, he alone has a proper office in the oldest breviaries, because he was the first to receive public veneration from the Church, as Bona observes (*Book II*, chapter 12, no. 19). In the final Appendix he is distinguished by a proper preface.]

## ON THE FEAST OF SAINT MARTIN, BISHOP

O God, who see that we subsist through none of our own virtue, mercifully grant that through the intercession of blessed Martin your confessor we may be fortified against every adversity. Through him.

[Col. 0855B] **Secret.** Grant, merciful God, that this saving offering may continually free us from our own guilt and protect us from every adversity. Through him.

**Communion.** Grant, we ask, O Lord our God, that the sacraments whose votive celebration is taking place may, through the saving intercession of those whose feast it is, become beneficial to us. Through him.

## ON THE FEAST OF SAINT ANDREW

We humbly beseech your majesty, O Lord, that just as blessed Andrew the apostle was a preacher and ruler of your Church, so he may be before you our perpetual intercessor. Through him.

**Secret.** May the holy prayer of blessed Andrew make our sacrifice pleasing to you, O Lord, so that it may become acceptable through the merits of him in whose honor it is solemnly offered [Col. 0855C]. Through him.

**Communion.** We have received, O Lord, the divine mysteries, rejoicing in the feast of blessed Andrew. Perfect them, we ask, so that, just as they benefit your saints unto glory, they may benefit us unto forgiveness [Col. 0856A]. Through him.

[**Note:** [Col. 0855D] The solemn commemoration of Saint Nicholas began after the translation of his sacred body to Bari, which took place in the year 807, as Sigebert writes. Before that time there is scarcely any mention of Nicholas in manuscript sacramentary books or in the Gregorian order, nor is he read of in my parchment Breviary. His feast, however, was instituted in the eleventh century, as Gavantus writes in the *Acts of Saint Alexius*, on the authority of Zonaras (*Commentary on the Rubrics of the Breviary*, section 7, chapter 2).]

## ON THE FEAST OF SAINT NICHOLAS, BISHOP AND CONFESSOR

Almighty and eternal God, who on this day caused your most blessed confessor and pontiff Nicholas to enter the heavenly realms, grant, we ask, that your suppliants may worthily celebrate his solemn feast, so that through his venerable festival we may attain salvation and peace. Through him.

**Secret.** Sanctify the gifts dedicated to you, O Lord, and, through the intercession of blessed Nicholas your confessor and pontiff, mercifully regard us through them. Through him.

**Communion.** Protect, we ask, your people, O Lord, who trust in the patronage of blessed Nicholas the bishop [Col. 0856B], and make those whom you refresh with the divine sacraments continually adhere to your commandments. Through him.

[**Note:** [Col. 0856C] Before the first Sunday of Advent we have here a Mass of the Holy Trinity, which is very noteworthy. The decree of Alexander II should appropriately be read; it provides as follows: “The feast of the Most Holy Trinity, according to the custom of various Churches, has been celebrated by some on the octave of Pentecost and by others on the first Sunday of the Lord’s Advent. The Roman Church, however, does not have the practice of celebrating such a feast specially at any particular time, since each day ‘Glory be to the Father,’ and other expressions pertaining to praise of the Trinity, are likewise said. Micrologus writes (chapter 6) that in some Churches this feast was celebrated on their own authority. He rebukes this and also asserts that the Mass had been composed by Alcuin and the preface approved by Pelagius. Rupert speaks of this feast as though it had long since been instituted and universally received. Its memory is found neither in the Masses of the Mozarabs nor in the book of Gothic Prayers. The Church of Auxerre in 1217 celebrated on this very day—namely, the final Sunday after Pentecost—a feast of the Holy Trinity, as is read in the statutes of that Church, chapter 59, in Labbe (*New Library*, volume II, p. 498). Cardinal Bona asserts that the Cistercian monks formerly sang a Mass of the Trinity after None on every Sunday (*Book I*, chapter 8, no. 10).]

## MASS OF THE HOLY TRINITY

Almighty and eternal God, who have granted your servants, in confessing the true faith, to recognize the glory of the eternal Trinity and to adore the Unity in the power of its majesty, we ask that we may always be fortified against every adversity by the firmness of that same faith. Through him.

**Secret.** Sanctify, we ask, O Lord God, through the invocation of your name, the sacrificial offering of this oblation, and through it perfect us ourselves as an eternal gift to you. Through him.

**Preface.** Eternal God, who with your Only-Begotten Son and the Holy Spirit are one God and one Lord—not in the singularity of one person, but in the substance of one Trinity. For what we believe concerning your glory through your revelation, this we think concerning your Son and concerning the Holy Spirit, without difference of distinction, so that in the confession of true and everlasting divinity, the distinct property of the persons, unity in essence, and equality in majesty may be adored. Whom the angels praise, the archangels venerate, the thrones, dominions, principalities, and powers adore; whom the cherubim and seraphim do not cease to acclaim, saying—

**Postcommunion.** Lord God, almighty Father, always bless us, your servants subject to your majesty, through your only Son in the power of the Holy Spirit, and protect us, so that, secure from every enemy, we may continually rejoice in your praise. Through the same, etc., in unity.

## FIRST SUNDAY OF ADVENT

[Col. 0857B] Stir up your power, we ask, O Lord, and come, so that, protected by you, we may deserve to be rescued from the dangers of our sins that threaten us, and, freed by you, to be saved. You who live.

**Secret.** May these sacred gifts, cleansed by powerful virtue, make us come purer to their source. Through him.

**Communion.** May we receive your mercy, O Lord, in the midst of your temple, so that we may anticipate the coming solemnities of our restoration with fitting honors. Through him.

[**Note:** [Col. 0857D] The votive Masses that follow are all found in the sacramentary books published by Menard and Pamelius in the Gregorian rite, and by the distinguished Bishop Angelo Rota. This is the first votive Mass in this Sacramentary. No one should think, however, that it is duplicated because another occurs on the Kalends of November. That one concerns the solemnity of All Saints under a single celebration, whereas this votive Mass is in honor of all the saints, to implore their patronage. Below there is likewise another Mass among the votive Masses entitled “In honor of all the saints for the living and the dead,” with a single prayer; the other two may perhaps be taken from the present Mass, which is the first among the votive Masses.]

## MASS IN HONOR OF ALL THE SAINTS

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that the intercession of the holy Mother of God, the Virgin Mary, of all the holy apostles, martyrs, confessors [Col. 0857C], and virgins, and of all your elect everywhere, may gladden us, so that, while we recall their merits, we may experience their patronage. Through him.

**Secret.** Be appeased, we ask, O Lord, by the gifts offered, and, through the intercession of blessed Mary ever-virgin together with all your saints, defend us from every danger. Through him.

**Communion.** We have received the heavenly sacraments, O Lord, while commemorating blessed Mary ever-virgin and all your saints. Grant, we ask, that what we perform in time we may attain in eternal joys. Through him.

## MASS FOR A COMMUNITY

Almighty and eternal God, who alone perform great wonders [Col. 0857D], extend over your servants and over all the communities entrusted to them the spirit of saving grace, and continually pour upon them the dew of your blessing, so that they may please you in truth. Through him.

**Secret.** Mercifully regard, O Lord, the sacrifices of your servants, and grant that what they celebrate with devout mind in honor of your name may prove for them a remedy. Through him.

[Col. 0858A] **Communion.** Accompany perpetually with your protection, O Lord, what you refresh with a heavenly gift, and grant that those whom you never cease to cherish may become worthy of eternal redemption. Through him.

## MASS FOR PEACE

O God, from whom come holy desires, right counsels, and just works, grant your servants that peace which the world cannot give, so that our hearts, devoted to your commandments, and freed from fear of enemies, may have tranquil times under your protection. Through him.

**Secret.** O God, who do not allow peoples believing in you to be shaken by any terrors, deign to receive the prayers and sacrifices of the people dedicated to you, so that the peace granted through your mercy may make the territories of Christians secure from every enemy. Through him.

[Col. 0858B] **Communion.** O God, author and lover of peace, to know whom is to live and to serve whom is to reign, protect your suppliants from every attack, so that we who trust in your defense may fear the weapons of no hostility. Through him.

## MASS FOR TRAVELERS

Be present, O Lord, to our supplications, and arrange the way of your servants in the prosperity of your salvation, so that amid all the changes of this journey they may always be protected by your help. Through him.

**Secret.** Be favorable, O Lord, to our supplications, and graciously receive these offerings which we offer to you for your servants N. May your grace go before them and direct their way, and may you deign to accompany them with your grace following after, so that we may rejoice in their undertaking and safety [Col. 0858C] according to the protection of your mercy. Through him.

**Postcommunion.** May the sacraments we have received guard us who hope in you, O Lord, and protect your servants everywhere against every attack. Through him.

## MASS FOR RELATIVES AND FRIENDS

Almighty and eternal God, have mercy on your servants N. and direct them according to your clemency into the way of eternal salvation, so that, by your gift, they may desire what pleases you and accomplish it with all their strength. Through him.

**Secret.** May these offerings which we, your suppliants, present to your majesty advance, we ask, O Lord, toward the salvation of your servants N., so that through your providence their life may everywhere be directed amid adversity and prosperity. Through him.

**Communion.** As we receive the sacraments of perpetual salvation, we implore your clemency, that through them you may protect your servants from every adversity. Through him.

## VOTIVE MASS

O God, who justify the ungodly and do not desire the death of a sinner, we humbly beseech your majesty [Col. 0859A] that, in your kindness, you may protect your servant(s) N., who trust(s) in your mercy, with heavenly aid, and preserve him (them) through continual protection, so that he (they) may always serve you and not be separated from you by any temptations. Through him.

**Preface.** “O God, whose proper attribute it is,” etc. Receive, most merciful Father, the sacrifice of reconciliation and praise which I, your unworthy servant and priest, presume to offer to you for the honor and glory of your name and for the safety of your servant(s) N., so that he [they] may obtain forgiveness of all his [their] sins. Through him.

**Postcommunion.** May the holy sacraments which we have received purify us, we ask, O Lord, and grant that your servant(s) N. may be free from every fault [Col. 0859B], so that he (they) who is (are) bound by the guilt of his (their) conscience may rejoice in the fullness of heavenly healing. Through him.

## MASS FOR A SICK PERSON

Almighty and eternal God, eternal salvation of those who believe, hear us on behalf of your servant(s) N., for whom we implore the help of your mercy, so that, health being restored, he (they) may render thanksgiving to you in your Church. Through him.

**Secret.** O God, under whose governance the moments of our life pass, receive the prayers and sacrifices of your servant, for whom, in his illness, we implore your mercy, so that we may rejoice in the health of him whose danger we fear. Through him.

[Col. 0859C] **Communion.** O God, singular protection of human weakness, show the power of your help over your sick servant(s) N., so that, aided by the help of your mercy, he (they) may deserve to be presented before your holy Church. Through him.

## MASS FOR ONESELF

I humbly beseech you, God, almighty Father, creator of all things: while I confess that I, your servant, have gravely sinned before the omnipotence of your majesty, extend to me the hand of your mercy, so that, while I offer this oblation of your goodness, you may most mercifully deign to absolve what I have wickedly committed. Through him.

**Secret.** God of mercy, God of goodness, God of forgiveness, forgive me, I ask, and have mercy on me; and graciously deign to receive this sacrifice which I humbly offer to your goodness. As a merciful, favorable, and compassionate God, forgive the sins which I have contracted through slipping vices, so that, when pardon has been granted, I may deserve to receive from you an opportunity for repentance and abundant tears. Through him.

Postcommunion. God of charity and peace, who for the salvation of the human race accepted the gibbet of the cross and poured out your blood for our redemption, receive my prayers with favor and kindness, and grant me your mercy, so that when you command my soul to depart from the body, the evil one may have no power over me, but your angel of peace may place me among your saints and elect, where unfailing light and everlasting life remain. You who live and reign.

## MASS FOR ALL

By your loving-kindness, we beseech you, Lord, loose all the bonds of our sins; and, through the intercession of the blessed and glorious ever-virgin Mary, Mother of God, together with all your saints, preserve the lord pope, our bishops and abbot, our kings and princes, and all the Christian people, as well as us, your servants, and this place with all who dwell in it, in complete holiness. Purify from vices and enlighten with virtues all who are joined to us by kinship, friendship, or the recommendation of prayer; grant us peace and salvation; remove visible and invisible enemies; drive away carnal desires; grant us wholesome air; bestow charity upon our enemies; and mercifully forgive the sins of those who have given us their alms. Grant likewise to all the faithful, living and dead, life and eternal rest in the land of the living. Through the same Christ.

Secret. God, who by the singular sacrifice of your body loosed the sins of the whole world, appeased by this offering, wipe away the stains of our crimes, forgive the sins of all Christian believers, living and dead, and grant them eternal rewards. You who live.

Communion. May the heavenly sacraments we have received, we beseech you, Lord, cleanse all our crimes and drive far from us every wickedness and infirmity, as well as the fury of the enemy and sudden death, through the merits and intercession of the holy Mother of God and Virgin Mary and of all the saints; and may they benefit all the faithful, living and dead, for whose salvation they have been offered to you. Through Christ.

## ON SAINT URBAN

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that as we celebrate the solemnity of your blessed martyr and pontiff Urban, we may be openly aided by his intercessions. Through Christ.

Secret. May this offering, Lord, we beseech you, cleanse our sins and sanctify the bodies and minds of those subject to you for the celebration of the sacrifice. Through Christ.

Communion. Refreshed by participation in the sacred gift, we beseech you, Lord our God, that we may experience the effect of the worship whose celebration we perform. Through Christ.

## ON THE NATIVITY OF ONE APOSTLE

We beseech you, almighty God, that blessed N., your apostle, may implore your help for us, so that, absolved from our offenses, we may also be rescued from every danger. Through Christ.

Secret. We offer you, Lord, this sacred gift, by which, recalling the solemnity of blessed N., your apostle, we also implore purification for our minds. Through Christ.

> **Note.** [Col. 0859D] After the votive Masses have been completed, the Mass of Saint Urban, pope and martyr, follows in our Sacramentary. This is not surprising, since the monastic order pursued the holy pontiff with a particular devotion. See what Martène says on this matter (*De antiq. eccl. ritib.*, book IV, chapter 32, no. 12, and chapter 27) [Col. 0860D]. In our district of Pyrano there stands a noble church, sacred to Saint Urban, on the banks of the Aesinantis River; from the eleventh century an eminent monastery of the Order of Saint Benedict was attached to it, now at last fallen through age. [Col. 0861D] I write at greater length concerning it and the church in the *Antiquities of the Valley of Saint Clement* and in the *Dissertation on the Bishops of Camerino*, under Bishop Hugh [Col. 0862D]. The writers of the *Annals of Camaldoli* also treat of it (vol. I and this vol. II).

Communion. Having received the sacraments, we humbly entreat you, Lord, that, through the intercession of your apostle N., what we perform in honor of his venerable solemnity may profit us for healing. Through Christ.

## ON THE NATIVITY OF SEVERAL APOSTLES

God, who gladden us by the annual solemnity of your apostles N., grant, we beseech you, that we who rejoice in their merits may be instructed by their examples. Through Christ.

Secret. Mercifully receive, Lord, the gifts that we present for the solemnity of your apostles N., and turn away all the evils that we deserve. Through Christ.

Communion. We beseech you, Lord, filled with the mysteries, that we may be aided by the prayers of those whose solemnity we celebrate. Through Christ.

## ON THE NATIVITY OF ONE MARTYR

May the nativity of your martyr N., Lord, which we celebrate as a votive observance, always welcome us; may it pour into us the joy of his glorification and make us acceptable to you. Through Christ.

Secret. Look with serene kindness, Lord, upon these gifts that are present, we beseech you, so that they may be filled with the blessing of the Holy Spirit and pour into our hearts that strong love by which the holy martyr N. conquered every torment of the body. Through Christ.

Communion. As we receive, Lord, the gifts of the heavenly mystery, we beseech you, may we be aided by the merits of your blessed martyr N., whose solemnity we celebrate with due veneration. Through Christ.

## ON THE NATIVITY OF SEVERAL MARTYRS

Almighty and everlasting God, who through the glorious battles of their struggle brought your blessed martyrs N. to immortal triumphs, grant our hearts a joy worthy of their commemoration, so that we who rejoice in their merits may advance through their examples. Through Christ.

Secret. We offer you, Lord, the gifts of our devotion. May they be pleasing to you in honor of your righteous ones and, by your mercy, become salutary for us. Through Christ.

Communion. Grant us, we beseech you, Lord, through the intercession of your saints N., that what we touch with our mouth we may receive with a pure mind. Through Christ.

## ON THE NATIVITY OF PONTIFFS

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that the venerable solemnity of blessed N., your confessor and pontiff, may increase both our devotion and our salvation. Through Christ.

Secret. We beseech you, Lord, that holy N., the pontiff and confessor, may ask that the offerings placed upon the sacred altars bring us salvation. Through Christ.

Communion. Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that, giving thanks for the gifts we have received, we may, through the intercession of blessed N., your confessor and pontiff, receive greater benefits. Through Christ.

## ON THE NATIVITY OF CONFESSORS WHO WERE NOT PONTIFFS

Be present, Lord, to our supplications, which we offer in commemoration of your holy confessor N.; for although we have no confidence in our own righteousness, may we be aided by the prayers of him who pleased you. Through Christ.

Secret. We offer you, Lord, sacrifices for the commemoration of your holy confessor N., whom no temptation separated from union with your body. Through Christ.

Communion. May your blessed confessor N., we beseech you, approach as an intercessor, so that your sacrifices may bring us salvation, Lord. Through Christ.

## ON THE NATIVITY OF VIRGINS

God, who gladden us by the annual solemnity of blessed N., your virgin and martyr, graciously grant that we may be aided by her merits, whose examples of chastity shine upon us. Through Christ.

Secret. We offer prayers and gifts, Lord, rejoicing in honor of your holy virgin and martyr N.; grant, we beseech you, that we may perform these things fittingly and obtain everlasting healing. Through Christ.

Communion. May these holy mysteries that we have received aid us, we beseech you, Lord, together with the venerable intercession of blessed N., your virgin and martyr. Through Christ.

# THE ORDER FOR MAKING A MONK BEGINS

Let the novice throw himself down before the altar.

Our Father. Have mercy on me. Chapter: Show us, Lord. Be with him, Lord. Send to him, Lord. Lord, hear us.

Prayer. God, Father of forgiveness, who, tempering your truth with discernment, granted that the son should not bear the iniquity of the father, and who, by a wondrous dispensation, frequently work through evil people also by the grace of your favor, we beseech your clemency: let not that which this servant of yours, N., has received through us—who are unworthy of so great and such a thing—by the religious habit hinder him; rather, may you inwardly accomplish through the gift of the Holy Spirit the ministry that is outwardly carried out through us. Through Christ.

Another prayer. God, who through your co-eternal Son created all things, and who deigned to renew the world grown old in sins through the mystery of his holy Incarnation, we humbly beseech you to look mercifully upon this servant of yours, N., who professes renunciation of the world. May he thereby be renewed in the spirit of his mind, put off the old man with his deeds, and deserve to put on the new man, who was created according to God. Through Christ.

Blessing of the cowl. Lord Jesus Christ, who deigned to put on the covering of our mortality, we beseech the immense abundance of your generosity: deign to bless this kind of garment, which the holy Fathers decreed should be worn by those renouncing the world as a sign of innocence or humility, so that this servant of yours who uses it may deserve to put you on. Through Christ.

Another prayer. God, giver of eternal goods and generous pourer-out of every blessing, we beseech you with earnest prayers: deign to bless and sanctify this garment, which your servant N. wishes to put on as a sign of chastity, so that he may be known among other people as devoted to you. Through Christ.

Then let him remove his secular garment, saying:

May the Lord strip you of the old man with his deeds.

As he puts on the monastic garment, let him say:

May the Lord clothe you with the new man, who was created according to God in the righteousness and holiness of truth.

Blessing of the garment. God, who promised your faithful a saving garment and clothing of eternal joy, we humbly implore your clemency: graciously bless these garments, signifying humility of heart and contempt for the world, with which your servant N. is visibly being formed in his purpose; and may the habit of blessed chastity, which he has received through your inspiration, be kept under your protection. Through Christ.

## FOR PUTTING ON THE MONASTIC GARMENT

Receive this holy and monastic garment, which you are to carry without stain before the tribunal of our Lord Jesus Christ, through the virtue and mercy of the same Christ, who with the eternal Father and the Holy Spirit lives and reigns throughout endless ages of ages. Amen.

Sovereign Lord, God our Savior, preserve this servant of yours, N., under this yoke until the end; make him worthy to be among those who have pleased you; clothe him with the robe of sanctification; gird his loins with sobriety; show him to be a creator in all abstinence; perfect him in the gifts of spiritual grace, to the glory of your praiseworthy power, for you are our God, who desire all people to be saved. You who live.

Prayer. We invoke you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, over this servant N., who has vowed to serve you with a pure mind and clean heart. Deign to join him among those 144,000 innocent ones (*infantes*), who remained virgins and did not defile themselves with women, in whose mouth no deceit was found. So also make this servant of yours, N., remain among them through your immaculate Son, our Lord, with whom you live and reign, God, throughout all ages of ages. Amen.

# FOR MAKING A CLERIC

Prayer. Let us pray, dearest brothers, to our Lord Jesus Christ for this servant of yours, N., who hastens to cut off the hair of his head for the love of Christ: that he may give him the Holy Spirit, who will perpetually preserve the religious habit in him; guard his heart from the hindrance of the world and from secular desire; and, just as his appearance will be changed, so may the right hand of your power grant him the practice of perfect good works, open his eyes from every spiritual blindness, and grant him the light of eternal grace. Through Christ.

While cutting his hair, say the antiphon:

You are the one, Lord, who will restore my inheritance to me.

The Lord is the portion of my inheritance [sic].

Glory to the Father.

Another antiphon:

This is the generation of those who seek the Lord, who seek the face of the God of Jacob. He shall receive a blessing from the Lord.

After he has been tonsured:

Prayer. Almighty and everlasting God, be merciful to our sins, and, as this servant of yours, N., lays aside secular servitude, may your grace always flourish in him. Just as we have caused him to wear upon his head an ornament resembling your crown, so may he, by your power, deserve to pursue his inheritance in his heart. Through Christ.

Another prayer. Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that your servant N., whose hair we have today removed from his head for divine love, may remain perpetually in your love, and that you may preserve him without stain forever. Through Christ.

> **Note.** In the order for initiating a monk, we find a rite for cutting the beard. In ancient times secular men wore and cultivated very long beards; consequently, a long and extended beard was a sign of vanity. To reject every vanity of the world, monks cut the beards of their novices. See what the writers of the *Annals of Camaldoli* say about this custom (vol. I, p. 380). Nevertheless, monks appeared beardless without any softness being visible in their faces—which would certainly have been excessive had they used a razor. For this reason they cut their beards with shears. We add that Saint Albertinus, prior of Fonte Avellana, is depicted without a beard in a very ancient icon painted in the church of his monastery. Likewise, an ancient image of Saint Peter Damian, dating from the declining thirteenth century and painted in colors on the panel of the high altar of Saint Exuperantius at Cingoli, where the Avellanese monks lived for a long time, shows him with a shaggy but short beard, like those often shortened with shears.
>
> That this custom of shaving the beard existed in the eleventh century in some churches, but was not equally accepted by all, is proved by an authentic monument preserved by Papebroch in the *Acts of the Saints*. In his *Exegesis of the Milanese Bishops* he presents an image of Heribert, bishop of Milan around the year 1046, showing the bishop bearded and wearing the pallium. The same very learned man also proves that the Roman pontiffs were not so strict in maintaining this discipline of shaving the beard that they did not consider themselves free to depart from it at will. On the ivory cover of the other part of this book, Saint Theodore is sculpted, and indeed bearded; Saint Theodore was Greek, and the Greeks did not cut their beards, contrary to the custom of the Latins. Thomassinus (*book II, chapter 41, no. 1*) observes that in this same eleventh century the Council of Bourges, held in 1031, decreed in canon 7 that clerics should have the ecclesiastical tonsure—that is, a shaved beard—and a crown on the head. Likewise, the Council of Coyac, in 1050, decreed in canon 3 that they should always have open crowns and shave their beards. Gregory VII, who flourished in this same eleventh century, when assigning to the prefect of the island of Sardinia the reason why he had ordered the bishop of Cagliari to shave his beard, wrote: “So that he may accommodate himself to the most ancient customs of the Western Church.”
>
> He also urged the prefect to compel the entire clergy to shave their beards, to deprive the disobedient of their goods, and to assign them to the property of the Church. Saint Charles Borromeo (*Acts of the Milanese Church*, p. 1061) commands clerics to observe the institution of shaving the beard, confirmed by the Fathers at the Fourth Council of Carthage. What wonder, then, if in this eleventh century, when the vanity of long beards had grown, monks, contradicting the pomp of the world, laid aside their beards?

# FOR CUTTING THE BEARD

God, by whose Spirit every mature creature rejoices, hear our prayers over this servant of yours, N., rejoicing in the beauty of youthful age and at the first beginning of being shorn [reading uncertain]. Hear us, so that, protected by all the aid of your protection, he may receive the heavenly blessing and rejoice in the supports of both this present life and the eternal life. Through Christ.

> **Note.** This rite for imposing penance is extremely common among ancient monks. It should be understood that their custom was this: whoever, converted to God from the world, entered a monastery had first to disclose the stains of his conscience to the prior or abbot of the monastery and confess all his sins individually, receiving penance according to the prescriptions of the sacred canons. Among the Carthusians, according to their ancient laws, monks made a manifestation of conscience not only when they received the monastic habit but also whenever a new prior was elected. This confession, however, does not seem to have been sacramental. On this matter consult what the learned Bishop Sarti, most devoted to me, has observed in Observation VIII on chapter 4, p. 43, of the *Life of Saint John of Lodi*. This rite of imposing penance was not private but public.

# THE RITE FOR IMPOSING PENANCE BEGINS

Take his right hand and say:

We have received your mercy, O God, as far as your right hand.

Glory to the Father.

Chapter: Save your servant. My God. Send him help, Lord. And from Zion. Lord, hear my prayer. And let my cry. Arise, Lord, help me. And deliver us. The Lord be with you. And with your spirit.

Prayer. Hear, we beseech you, Lord, the prayers of your supplicants, and spare the sins of your servants who confess to you, so that in your kindness you may grant us both pardon and peace. Through Christ.

Another prayer. May your mercy, Lord, go before this servant of yours, we beseech you, and may all his iniquities be erased by swift forgiveness. Through Christ.

Another prayer. We beseech your clemency, Lord, and the great mercy of your majesty: deign to release your servant N., who confesses his sins and crimes, from his guilt and forgive the offenses of the past. You who brought the lost sheep back to the fold upon your shoulders, who were appeased by the prayers and confession of the tax collector, be likewise appeased by this servant of yours, Lord. Graciously receive his prayers; forgive him, Lord, all crimes and sins, and grant him pardon in place of punishments and life in place of death, so that he who has fallen into such great hope of heavenly glory, trusting in your mercy, may, under your protection, reach eternal joys. Through Christ.

# THEN THE LITANY BEGINS WITH THE SEVEN PSALMS

Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy. God the Father in heaven, have mercy on us. God the Son, Redeemer of the world, have mercy on us. God the Holy Spirit, have mercy on us. Holy Trinity, one God, have mercy on us.

Holy Mary, pray for us. Holy Michael, pray. Holy Gabriel, pray. Holy Raphael, pray. Holy John the Baptist, pray. Holy Peter, pray. Holy Paul, pray. Holy Andrew, pray. Holy John the Evangelist, pray. Holy Thomas, pray. Holy James, pray. Holy Philip, pray. Holy Bartholomew, pray. Holy Matthew the Evangelist, pray. Holy Matthias, pray. Holy Barnabas, pray. Holy Mark the Evangelist, pray. Holy Luke the Evangelist, pray. Holy Stephen, pray. Holy Clement, pray. Holy Apollinaris, pray. Holy Vitalis, pray. Holy Lawrence, pray. Holy Vincent, pray. Holy Felix, pray. Holy Fortunatus, pray. Holy Cornelius, pray. Holy Cyprian, pray. Holy Sebastian, pray. Holy Cosmas, pray. Holy Damian, pray. Holy Blaise, pray. Holy Sylvester, pray. Holy Martin, pray. Holy Ambrose, pray. Holy Augustine, pray. Holy Jerome, pray. Holy Severus, pray. Holy Nicholas, pray. Holy Leo, pray. Holy Benedict, pray. Holy Maurus, pray. Holy Placid, pray. Holy Philibert, pray. Holy Columban, pray. Holy Majolus, pray. Holy Gall, pray. Holy Guido, pray. Holy Felicitas, pray. Holy Perpetua, pray. Holy Agatha, pray. Holy Agnes, pray. Holy Cecilia, pray. Holy Lucy, pray. Holy Justina, pray. Holy Anastasia, pray. Holy Savina, pray. Holy Columba, pray. Holy Barbara, pray. All saints, pray.

Be favorable; spare us. From every evil, deliver us. From the snares of the devil, deliver us. From the danger of death, deliver us. From the persecution of the enemy, deliver us. From many sins, deliver us. From every temptation, deliver us. From every evil thought, deliver us. From every iniquity, deliver us. From every impurity, deliver us. From sudden death, deliver us. From the fire of Gehenna, deliver us.

Merciful God, we beseech you. Redeemer of the world, we beseech you. We sinners, we beseech you. That you grant us peace, we beseech you. That you grant us forgiveness of our sins, we beseech you. That you grant us the grace of penance, we beseech you. That you grant us contrition of heart, we beseech you. That you grant us a fountain of tears, we beseech you. That you grant us steadfastness of mind, we beseech you. That you grant us remission of sins, we beseech you. That you deign to lead us to eternal life, we beseech you. That you deign to hear us, we beseech you.

Son of God, we beseech you, hear us twice. Lamb of God, who take away the sins of the world, spare us. Lamb of God, who take away the sins of the world, hear us. Lamb of God, who take away the sins of the world, have mercy on us. Christ, hear us twice. Lord, have mercy three times. Our Father.

Chapter: I said, Lord, heal me. May your mercy be upon us, Lord. As. Lord, turn your face away. And all our iniquity. Convert us, God our Savior. And turn away your anger. Lord, hear my prayer. And let my cry. Arise, Lord, help me. And deliver us. The Lord be with you. And with your spirit.

Prayer. Hear our prayers, Lord, and spare the sins of this servant of yours who turns to you, so that the guilt of his conscience, which accuses him, may be absolved by your merciful forgiveness. Through Christ.

Another prayer. God, who purify the hearts of all who confess to you and absolve from every bond of iniquity those who accuse their own conscience, grant forgiveness to your servant and provide medicine to the wounded, so that, with the dominion of sin removed, he may serve you with a free mind. Through Christ.

Another prayer. Grant, Lord, we beseech you, to this servant of yours, N., the fruit of worthy penance, so that, having sinned and departed from the integrity of your holy Church, he may be restored to its mystery by obtaining forgiveness and be made innocent. Through Christ.

# THE TRUE FAITH OF THE PENITENTS BEGINS

Do you believe in God the almighty Father, and in the Son, and in the Holy Spirit? **Response:** I believe.

Do you believe that these three persons, as we have said—the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit—are three and one God? **Response:** I believe.

Do you believe that in this flesh in which you now are, in that same flesh you will rise again and receive either the good or the evil that you have done? **Response:** I believe.

Do you wish to forgive those who have sinned against you, as the Lord says: “If you do not forgive people their sins, neither will your Father forgive you your sins”? **Response:** I forgive.

If you have sinned by criminal sins—that is, pride, sacrilege, homicide, adultery, theft, robbery, or other sins too numerous to list—then Saint Paul, Augustine, and the other holy Fathers have determined that abundant almsgiving and a lengthy fast must be performed for these sins: clerics, five years; deacons, seven; priests, ten; monks, seven; bishops, twelve. If it has been habitual, penance is to be added.

Then let us sing: Let us pray.

Almighty and everlasting God, who according to your great mercy blot out the sins of penitents and, in your swift kindness, come to the aid of those who hope in you, grant, we beseech you, to your servant N. remission of all sins, and, being appeased, receive his vows. Renew in him, most merciful Father, whatever has been corrupted by earthly frailty and whatever has been violated by diabolical intrusion. Have mercy, Lord, on his sighs; have mercy on his tears, so that through your mercy he may be transferred from sorrow to joy. Through Christ.

Secret. Almighty God, merciful God, gracious God, who confine your forgiveness by no law of time, receive the prayers and offerings that we bring to you for the forgiveness of your servant N.; mercifully grant him pardon for his sins and deign to fulfill the upright desires of his heart. Through Christ.

Postcommunion. God, who grant prosperity to those who seek the help of your mercy and drive away adversity, cleanse every obstacle that opposes your servant N.; and, with every temptation removed, may he deserve to praise you with unwearied thanksgiving. Through Christ.

> **Note.** It is an apostolic tradition to offer sacrifice for the dead (Bona, book II, chapter 15, no. 4), and it was the error of Aëtius to deny that sacrifice should be offered for them, as Epiphanius writes (*Heresies*, 75). The custom then arose of celebrating a sacrifice for the dead not only on the day of their death and burial, but also on the thirtieth, seventh, and third days and on the anniversary of their death. Here we have only Masses for the day of burial, the thirtieth day, and the anniversary, with proper prefaces both for the day of burial and for the anniversary. Muratori (*Antiquities of the Middle Ages*, vol. IV, dissertation 55) proves by many examples the antiquity of the rite of annual commemorations of the days of death for the dead. Missing here is the Mass for the commemoration of the faithful departed on the second day of November, which was instituted by Saint Odilo, abbot of Cluny, only in the year 1040. This rite was later spread throughout the universal Church by the authority of the pontiffs, as Baronius notes (*Notes on the Martyrology*, 2 November).

# MASS ON THE DAY OF BURIAL

God, whose nature is always to have mercy and spare, we humbly beseech you for the soul of your servant N., whom today you commanded to depart from this world: do not hand it over to the power of the enemy, nor forget it forever, but command that it be received by the holy angels and led to the homeland of paradise, so that he who hoped and believed in you may not suffer the punishments of hell but possess eternal joys. Through Christ.

Secret. Be merciful, we beseech you, Lord, to the soul of your servant N., for whom we offer you this sacrifice, humbly imploring your majesty that through these acts of devout appeasement he may deserve to reach everlasting rest. Through Christ.

Preface. Eternal God, who, by your gratuitous kindness, granting forgiveness to sinners, prepared life for the dead, so that those whom mercy had freed from guilt might not remain longer in punishment: therefore, Lord, we pour out humble prayers to you and commend to you the soul and spirit of your servant N., so that, received among the ranks of the saints, he may not know the places of the underworld. May nothing harm him, Lord, whatever he committed under the attraction of the frailty of the flesh, or whatever he sinned in deed, word, or thought, burdened by the habit of human desire; but, secure, may he follow the footsteps of the Savior with infinite sweetness and in the presence of truth. Having also been reminded of the redemption of his body, may he confidently await it, and whatever he previously possessed in faith may he receive as a gift. Through Christ.

Postcommunion. Grant, we beseech you, Lord, that the soul of your servant N., who today departed from this world, purified by these sacrifices and freed from every sin, may receive both forgiveness and everlasting life. Through Christ.

Then let the following be said: Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy. Lord, and so forth. The Lord be with you.

Prayer. To you, Lord, we commend the soul of your servant N., so that, dead to the world, he may live for you; and if he committed any sins through the frailty of worldly conduct, wipe them away by the forgiveness of your most merciful kindness. Through Christ.

Another prayer. We beseech you, Lord, grant this mercy to your servant N., that he may not receive in punishment the due return of his deeds, since he held your will in his desires; and just as true faith joined him to the ranks of the faithful, so may your mercy there associate him with the angelic choirs. Through Christ.

Another prayer. Do not enter into judgment with your servant, Lord, for no human being will be justified in your sight unless remission of all sins is granted through you. Therefore, we beseech you, do not let your judicial sentence weigh upon him whom the true supplication of Christian faith commends to you; but, with your grace coming to his aid, may he deserve to escape the judgment of vengeance—he who, while he lived, was marked with the sign of the Holy Trinity. Through Christ.

Another prayer. God, giver of life and restorer of human bodies, who willed to be entreated by sinners, hear the prayers that we pour out to you with particular devotion and tears for the soul of your servant N. Deign to free it from the torments of hell, place it among the ranks of your saints, clothe it also in a heavenly garment and the robe of immortality, and cherish it in the delight of paradise. Through Christ.

Another prayer. God, eternal lover of human souls, make the soul of your servant N., who held the true faith while he remained in the body, free from every torment of hell, so that, separated from the prisons of the underworld, it may be worthy to be joined to the company of the saints. Through Christ.

Another prayer. Do not remember, Lord, the sins of the youth and the ignorances of your servant N.; but according to your great mercy, remember him in the life of your brightness. May the heavens be opened to him; may the angels rejoice; receive your servant, Lord, into your kingdom.

# ABSOLUTION OVER THE TOMB

Trusting in that power or authority which our Lord Jesus Christ granted to the blessed apostle Peter, saying, “Whatever you bind on earth will be bound also in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed also in heaven,” and which he said to the other disciples: “Whose sins you forgive are forgiven them”: to the extent permitted to us, we absolve you from every bond of sins, so that whatever you have committed at the persuasion of the devil, by will or by action, to the extent that with God’s help we are able, to that extent we forgive you. Thus, with the chain of all sins broken from your neck, may you come free and absolved before the tribunal of our Lord Jesus Christ in eternal life, receiving from him the inheritance of the heavenly kingdom and joy without end throughout the ages of ages. Amen.

Then, for all who sleep in Christ in the same cemetery:

Psalm with antiphon: Blot out, Lord, their iniquities.

Psalm: Have mercy on me, God, according to your mercy.

Our Father. And lead us not. From the gate of hell. Deliver their souls, Lord. The Lord be with you.

Prayer. God, by whose mercy the souls of the faithful rest, graciously grant forgiveness of sins to your male and female servants, or to all who rest here in Christ, so that, absolved from every guilt, they may rejoice without end. Through Christ.

May they rest in peace. Amen.

# MASS ON THE THIRTIETH DAY

We beseech you, Lord, grant to your servant N., whose thirtieth day after his death we commemorate— or the seventh or third day, as applicable— a share in the company of your saints and elect, and pour upon him the dew of your enduring mercy. Through Christ.

Secret. Be present, Lord, to our supplications, and graciously and kindly receive this offering that we present to you for the thirtieth day of his burial—or the seventh or third day, as applicable—for the soul of your servant N. Through Christ.

Postcommunion. Almighty and everlasting God, deign to place the soul of your servant N., whose thirtieth day after his burial we celebrate—or the seventh or third day, as applicable—in the bosoms of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, so that, when the day of recognition of you has come, you may command him to rise among your holy elect. Through Christ.

# MASS ON THE ANNIVERSARY

Grant, we beseech you, Lord, that the soul of your servant N., whose annual day of burial we commemorate, may receive both forgiveness and everlasting rest. Through Christ.

Secret. Be merciful, Lord, to our supplications for the soul of your servant N., whose annual day is celebrated today, for whom we offer you a sacrifice of praise, that you may deign to join him to the company of your saints. Through Christ.

Preface. (+) Through Christ our Lord, through whom is the salvation of the world, through whom is human life, through whom is the resurrection of the dead: through him we humbly beseech you, Lord, to deign to grant perpetual forgiveness to the soul of your servant N., whose anniversary we celebrate, and, stripped of the contagions of mortality, to restore him to a share in eternal salvation with the angels. And therefore.

Communion. Receive, Lord, our prayers for the soul of your servant N., whose anniversary we celebrate today, so that if any stains from earthly contagions clung to him, they may be wiped away by the mercy of your forgiveness. Through Christ.

# MASS FOR A BISHOP

God, who caused your servant N. to flourish among the apostolic priests in pontifical dignity, grant, we beseech you, that he may also be joined forever to their company. Through Christ.

Secret. Receive, Lord, we beseech you, for the soul of your servant the bishop, the offerings that we present, so that to him whom you granted priestly merit in this world you may also grant the reward. Through Christ.

Communion. Be merciful, Lord, to our supplications, and command that the soul of your servant, the bishop N., be joined to everlasting joys in the land of the living. Through Christ.

# MASS FOR AN ABBOT

God, who sanctified your servant as a priest and abbot by a merciful calling and received him through a blessed completion, graciously receive our prayers and grant that he may be with you through his merits and remain with us through his examples. Through Christ.

Secret. Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that the soul of your servant, the abbot and priest, to whom you granted the merit of governance and priesthood, may receive these holy mysteries, which he faithfully ministered to you, and so forth. Through Christ.

Communion. May it profit the soul of your servant, the abbot and priest, Lord, we beseech you, through the clemency of your mercy, which we implore, so that, by your mercy, he may receive an eternal share in him in whom he prevailed and believed. Through Christ.

# MASS FOR A PRIEST

God, whose mercy is without number, receive our prayers for the soul of your servant N., the priest, and grant him the light of joy and a place among your saints. Through Christ.

Secret. We offer you, Lord, sacrifices of praise for the soul of your servant, the priest, so that eternal light may possess it among your faithful. Through Christ.

Communion. By these sacrifices, we ask, O Lord God, that the soul of your servant, the priest, having been purified, may be deemed worthy to attain forgiveness and everlasting refreshment. Through [Christ our Lord].

## MASS FOR ALL THE DEPARTED

[Col. 0872B]

Incline your ear, O Lord, to our prayers, by which we humbly implore your mercy, that you may establish the soul [souls] of your servant [servants], N., whom [whom] you have commanded to depart from this age, in the realm of peace and light, and command that he [they] be joined to your saints. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** Grant us, O Lord, that this offering may benefit the soul [souls] of your servant [servants], N.; by offering it, you have granted that the sins of the whole world may be forgiven. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** May the divine celebration of the sacrament benefit, we ask, O Lord, the soul [souls] of your servant [servants], N., so that, by your mercy, he [they] may attain a share in the eternity in which he [they] hoped and believed. Through [Christ our Lord].

## ANOTHER MASS FOR THE DEPARTED

[Col. 0872C]

Almighty and eternal God, to whom supplication is never made without hope of mercy, have mercy upon the souls of your servants, that those who departed this life confessing your name may be joined to the number of the saints. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** Have mercy, we ask, O Lord, upon the souls of your servants, for whom we offer you sacrifices of appeasement; and because they remained in this life in the Catholic faith, may a reward be granted to them in the life to come. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** Grant, we ask, almighty God, that you may cause the souls of your servants, received by the angels of light, to be led into the prepared dwellings of the blessed. [Col. 0872D] Through [Christ our Lord].

## MASS FOR DEPARTED BROTHERS

God, giver of forgiveness and lover of human salvation, we ask your clemency: grant that the brothers of our congregation who have passed from this age may, through the intercession of blessed Mary ever-virgin and all the saints, attain a share in everlasting blessedness. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** God, whose mercy is without number, graciously receive the prayers of our humility, and grant through these sacraments of salvation the remission of all sins to the souls to whom you have given confession of your name. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** God, life of the living, hope of the dying, salvation of all who hope in you, graciously grant [Col. 0873A] that the souls of this congregation, freed from the darkness of our mortality, may, through the intercession of blessed Mary ever-virgin, rejoice in perpetual light with all your saints. Through [Christ our Lord].

## MASS FOR A DECEASED WOMAN

We ask, almighty Lord God, that in your goodness you may have mercy upon the souls of your handmaids, and, freed from the contagions of mortality, restore them to a share in eternal salvation. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** By these sacrifices, O Lord, we ask that the souls of your handmaids, N., may be freed from all sins, without which no one has ever existed free from guilt, so that through these devout services of appeasement they may obtain everlasting mercy. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Postcommunion.** May the souls of your handmaids, N., find, we ask, O Lord, [Col. 0873B] a share in eternal light, the sacrament of whose perpetual grace they have received. Through [Christ our Lord].

## MASS FOR MANY OF THE DEPARTED

God, creator and redeemer of all the faithful, grant the souls of your male and female servants remission of all sins, so that they may obtain, through devout supplications, the forgiveness they have always desired. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** Graciously regard, we ask, O Lord, the sacrifices that we offer to you for the souls of your male and female servants, N., so that, to those to whom you have granted the merit of Christian faith, you may also grant the reward. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Postcommunion.** May the prayer of those who supplicate benefit, we ask, O Lord, [Col. 0873C] the souls of your male and female servants, N., so that you may both free them from sins and make them participants in your redemption. Through [Christ our Lord].

## MASS IN HONOR OF ALL THE SAINTS FOR THE LIVING AND THE DEPARTED

Through the intercessions of your saints, we ask, O Lord, let your grace protect us; and extend your mercy everywhere to your male or female servants whose commemoration we make, whose alms we have received, and also to those joined to us by friendship and kinship, so that, defended from every assault, they may be saved by your help. And grant remission of all sins to the souls of all your male and female servants—that is, of all the faithful Catholic and orthodox—[Col. 0874A] whose commemoration we make and whose bodies rest in this monastery and in all the cemeteries of the faithful. Through [Christ our Lord].

[Note: [Col. 0873D]

The final Appendix of this sacramentary begins with the Mass for the translation of Saint Mark. The translation of the body of Saint Mark the Evangelist is commemorated on 31 January and is recorded in the Roman Martyrology and in other ecclesiastical calendars. Augustine Calmet (*Universal History*, vol. IV, chap. 54) reports the opinion of those who maintain that the body of Saint Mark was transferred to Venice under Leo the Armenian, around the year 815. It should be regarded as certain that by the year 870 this translation had already taken place and that his sacred body was being preserved by the Venetians. Thus Bernard the monk, cited by Mabillon (*Acts of the Saints*, vol. IV, chap. 54). Baronius mentions this festive translation under the year 820 (no. 22) and argues that it took place around that time. The Bollandists adhere to this opinion in the section entitled “On the Cult of Saint Mark”; they likewise report the history of this translation from a manuscript of the Vatican Library, also cited by Baronius in his notes to the Martyrology. According to that manuscript, the translation belongs to the year [Col. 0874D] 820. Sabellicus assigns it to the year 831, during the rule of Duke Justinian in Venice. Platina mentions this translation during the pontificate of Gregory III, who began to sit in the year 823 and lived for sixteen years in the pontificate. But since Justinian was duke of Venice for only two years, this translation must necessarily be placed either in the fourth or fifth year of Gregory, and consequently in the year 831 or 832. Antonius Pagi in his critical notes (on the year 820, no. 9), Antonius Sandinus in his *Apostolic History* (on Saint Mark), and most recently the highly learned Venetian senator Flaminio Cornaro in his exceptionally detailed work *On the Venetian Churches* (Decade XIII, part 1), discuss this translation.

The propagation of this feast among the Benedictine monks must be assigned to the time of Saint Peter Damian, when the Appendix was added to this missal, and who also preached sermons (vol. II, p. 31, etc.) on his feast day (vol. II, p. 31, etc.), where he speaks of the same translation.]

## ON THE TRANSLATION OF SAINT MARK

God, who willed that the truth of the Gospel be revealed to us through the ministry of your blessed evangelist and martyr Mark, grant, we ask, that, aided by your grace, we may be able to put into practice what we have learned from his mouth. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** May this offering, O God, through the intercession of your blessed evangelist Mark, cleanse and renew us, govern and protect us, and lead us to the kingdoms of our heavenly homeland. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** Having received the gifts of the heavenly mystery, we humbly beseech you, O Lord, that, through the intercession of [Col. 0874B] your blessed evangelist and martyr Mark, you may grant us to rejoice in the peace of temporal life and to find the assistance of eternal life. Through [Christ our Lord].

## APPENDIX

Brother, guard this holy garment, so that you may bring it without stain before the tribunal of our Lord Jesus Christ, through the power and mercy of that same Lord, who with the coeternal Father and the Holy Spirit lives and reigns.

We beseech you, O Lord, that through the intercession of your blessed confessor Benedict, you may grant this servant of yours, upon whom we place the habit of holy religion, forgiveness of all his sins; bring his work to completion for good; grant him your mercy and grace; fill him with faith, hope, and charity; lift his mind toward heavenly desires; defend him from every adversity; and lead him to good perseverance. Through [Christ our Lord].

## ON THE CIRCUMCISION OF OUR LORD JESUS CHRIST

(+) Through Christ our Lord. As we celebrate today the day of his circumcision and the eighth day of his birth, we venerate your wonders, O Lord: for she who gave birth is both Virgin and Mother; he who was born is also God. Rightly, therefore, the heavens spoke, the angels rejoiced, the shepherds were glad, the magi were changed, kings were troubled, and little children were crowned with glorious suffering. And therefore, with the angels [we say]:

## ON THE PASSING OF SAINT BENEDICT

(+) Eternal God. And with abundant prayers we beseech your glory, that, as we venerate the feast of your blessed confessor Benedict, [Col. 0875A] we may, with your help, be able to imitate the examples of his holiness; and although we can in no way equal his merits, may we deserve to be aided by his prayers, through Christ.

## ON THE ANNUNCIATION OF THE LORD

(+) Eternal God. Through the childbirth of the blessed Virgin Mary you granted your Church a wondrous mystery and an ineffable sacrament, in which chastity remains untouched, modesty undefiled, and steadfastness firm; she rejoices that a Virgin conceived, that she carried the Lord of heaven in chaste womb, and that a Virgin brought forth a child. O wondrous working of the divine dispensation: she did not know a man and is a mother, and after the Son she remains a Virgin! For she rejoiced in two gifts: she marvels that a Virgin gave birth, and she rejoices [Col. 0875B] that she brought forth Jesus Christ our Lord, the Redeemer of the world. The angels and archangels praise him, and the cherubim and seraphim also, who do not cease daily to cry out with one voice, saying: Holy, holy.

## ON THE NATIVITY OF THE HOLY VIRGIN MARY

(+) It is right and salutary for us to give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, for the advancement of all your saints, and especially to praise, bless, and proclaim your almighty power for the merits of the blessed Mary, Mother of God, full of grace. The angels praise him, as above.

## ON THE SOLEMNITY OF ALL THE SAINTS

(+) Eternal God. Humbly imploring your mercy, [Col. 0875C] grant that you may join our joys with those of the rejoicing saints in the chambers of the heavenly kingdom. And those whom we cannot follow by imitating their virtue, may we touch through the affection of due veneration, through Christ our Lord. Through him.

## ON THE FEAST OF SAINT MARTIN, BISHOP

(+) Eternal God. By whose gift blessed Martin, confessor and priest alike, grew in the increase of good works, abounded in various gifts of virtue, and shone forth through miracles. What he taught in words he completed by the exhibition of deeds, and by both instruction and example he offered his subjects guidance toward the heavenly kingdoms. Therefore we ask your mercy: may we be conformed to the examples of him who pleased you in doing good; may we be fortified by his merits and aided by his intercessions, [Col. 0875D] so that, through his intervention and with your help, we may deserve to reach the heavenly kingdom. Through Christ our Lord.

God, who gladden us by the annual expectation of our redemption, grant that we may confidently behold as Judge when he comes him whom we joyfully received as Redeemer, your Only-Begotten, our Lord.

[Col. 0876A] Grant us, we ask, almighty God, that just as we anticipate the adorable Nativity of your Son, so we may receive his eternal gifts with rejoicing. He who lives with you.

(+) Eternal God, through Christ our Lord. Today we anticipate his face in confession and humbly beseech you with suppliant voice: may he make us so watchful during the services of the coming night that, with sincere minds, we may deserve to receive his coming Nativity. In it, the invisible one appeared visibly in our flesh from your substance; begotten with you not in time, and not inferior in nature, he came to us in time, Jesus Christ our Lord. Through him [is your majesty praised].
