[Note: [Col. 0875D] According to the prescription of the Rule of Saint Benedict (chapter 38), the weekly reader at table was to ask everyone after Mass and Communion on Sunday, using the verses written above, to pray for him, and, after repeating three times, “O Lord, open my lips,” to receive the blessing. This custom is still observed among monks, as the often-mentioned Cardinal Bona writes (*Book I*, chapter 3, no. 3), and the practice itself makes this clear.]

O Lord, open my lips. Save your servant. O Lord, send him help from the sanctuary. May the Lord guard you from every evil. May the Lord guard your going in and your going out. And may he take away from you the spirit of arrogance. Amen.

“Now I, Nicolaus Giomi of San Severino, public notary by the grace of God and by apostolic and imperial authority, recorded in the archive of the Roman Curia, caused this copy to be faithfully extracted and transcribed by another trustworthy person from the aforementioned very ancient missal, formerly serving the use of blessed Cardinal Peter Damian and given by him as a gift to his devoted disciple, blessed Dominic Loricatus; it was delivered to me for this purpose and afterward returned. This Missal is kept in the parish priory church of Saint Anne of Castel Frontalis of the diocese of San [Col. 0876C] Severino, and is exposed and preserved for public veneration in a reliquary of circular form, blue and decorated within with paintings of various colors, likewise ornamented externally on the rear portion; on the front it is closed by glass panels joined together and bound with lead, and surrounded by several gilded branches and flowers carved from wood, as is all clearly established by the authentic certificates of the Right Reverend Lord Alexander Calvi, formerly Bishop of Organis and Bishop of San Severino, and subsequently by those of the Right Reverend Lord Dionysius Pieragostini, likewise Bishop of San Severino, under whose seals it was kept. Having compared this copy with that Missal, I found it to agree in every respect and throughout, even [Col. 0876D] as regards the form of certain Greek letters. Saving always, etc. Therefore, at the request made to me, I have written, signed, and published this document here as evidence, and secured it with my customary sign, which I use.

“Written at Apyri on this fifteenth day of May in the year 1746.

“In place of the notarial sign +.”

[Col. 0877]

# EXCERPTS FROM OLD LITURGICAL MANUSCRIPTS OF FONTAVELLANA, FROM TWO SACRAMENTARIES AND A BREVIARY OF FIVE HUNDRED YEARS AND MORE

(*Camaldolese Annals*, at the place cited above, p. 375.)

## NOTICE

[Col. 0877A] These excerpts, collected a few years ago from three codices of the abbey of Avellana and courteously sent to us by monks of that place, will shed light on the old Suavincinian Sacramentary that we have just presented. The first codex, which is an ancient missal or sacramentary, was written for the use of the ascetics of the hermitage of Fontavellana in or before the fourteenth century, since it mentions the prior of the place; the title of prior continued until the time of John XXII, Roman pontiff. For around the year 1325 he gave the Avellanese their first abbot, Ubaldus, and honored the hermitage with the dignity of an abbey.

This sacramentary begins with the order to be observed on Wednesday at the beginning of the Fast and during the greater week of Lent. The order of Mass to be celebrated by a bishop or priest follows. Then there are proper prayers for the birthdays of the saints, and finally certain Masses whose recitation was formerly customary.

We are of the opinion that it was written chiefly for the Avellanese. We find no insignificant evidence for this in the octave of Saint Andrew the Apostle, which is prescribed; for we know that their church was dedicated both in honor of the Holy Cross and of Saint Andrew the Apostle. Yet since the Avellanese possessed monasteries and churches in many places and cities, whose monks followed the rite and discipline of the principal hermitage, the Sacramentary also contains prayers that were used in other dioceses and not in the Eugubine diocese, in whose territory Avellana arose.

All the prayers or collects found in the missal without an assignment of a day are the following, distributed in this same order: for the Nativity of Saint Ambrose, bishop; of Saint Lucy, virgin and martyr; of Saint Thomas the Apostle; of Saint Anastasius, martyr; of Saint Projectus, martyr; and of Saint Bridget, virgin. Prayers for the day of the Purification of the blessed Virgin Mary, and the blessing of candles. For the Nativity of Saint Blaise, martyr; of Saint Benedict, abbot; and for the feast of the Annunciation of the blessed Virgin Mary. For the birthday of Saint Euphemia, martyr; and for that of Saints Laurence and Pergentinus, brothers. The prayers of these martyrs, unless they were composed for the Avellanese, were for the monasteries subject to Avellana that were established in the territory of Arezzo and that of Città di Castello, where the cult of those martyrs flourished. A sermon of Peter Damian in honor of these holy martyrs survives.

The prayers for the Nativity of Saint Boniface, martyr—namely, the Boniface of Mainz—with his companions Eoban and Adelar, follow; then those of Saints Albinus, Paulinus, and Nicetius, bishops, with 989 companions; those for the vigil and feast day of Saint John the Baptist; those for the vigil as well as the feast days of the holy apostles Peter and Paul; of Saint Mustiola; of the seven holy brothers; and of Saint Paternianus. This holy bishop was the patron of the city of Fano, in which city and territory there were monasteries and churches of the Avellanese ascetics.

For the Nativity of Saint Margaret, virgin; of Saints Quirinus and Jolitta, martyrs; of the holy martyrs Hermagoras and Fortunatus; of Saint Praxedes, virgin; of Saint Mary Magdalene; of Saint Apollinaris, martyr and pontiff; of Saint Christina, martyr; of Saint James the Apostle; of Saint Christopher, martyr; of Saints Nazarius and Celsus, martyrs; and of the holy virgins Flora and Lucilla. Their cult was especially prominent at Arezzo, and on their birthdays Damian preached sermons and wrote their acts and translation.

There are prayers for the Finding of Saint Stephen; for the feast of Saint Donatus, bishop and martyr; for the vigil and Assumption of the blessed Virgin Mary; and for the Nativity of Saint Magnus, martyr. He was venerated at Trani in Apulia and elsewhere, where Avellanese cenobitic monks lived.

There are collects for the dedication of the basilica of Saint Floridus. Saint Floridus was the patron of the city of Tifernum, or Città di Castello, and it is known from the privileges of Innocent II and Honorius III, Roman pontiffs, that the Avellanese possessed monasteries and churches in the city and territory of Città di Castello. Innocent says: “In the county of Castello, the fortress of Monte Maggiore, and the monastery of the Holy Cross in that fortress, together with the churches and villages.” Honorius says: “The church of Saint Cassian and of Saint Fortunatus, with their chapels and appurtenances; the church of the Holy Cross of Monte Maggiore; and of Saint Giles of Castello; of the Holy Cross of Citerna; of Saint Peter of Agilone, with their chapels and appurtenances; and whatever you possess throughout the entire county of Castello.”

There are likewise prayers for the Nativity of Saint Symphorianus, martyr; of Saint Bartholomew the Apostle; of Saint Rufus, martyr; for the day of the beheading of Saint John the Baptist; for Saint Felicity, martyr; for the holy confessors Floridus and Amantius—the feast occurred on 26 September—and for All Saints. Other Masses and other [Col. 0878C] collects follow, as well as Masses for the departed. In the prayer for a deceased priest, the intercession of Saint Floridus the confessor is implored. Other Masses and prayers to God for various needs follow, and finally the liturgy for the departed.

The second Sacramentary, which appears older than the first, mentions an abbot. Perhaps it was used by the monks and parish priests of the church of Saint Blaise at Fabriano, which in the thirteenth century was subject to the monastery of Saint Victor at Clusis; it is now an independent abbey, to which two others were united, Saint Romuald of Valle Castri and Saint Urban at the Aesis. For in the confession before Mass, after the holy apostles Peter and Paul, Saint Blaise is named. Likewise, in the canon before the consecration, he is named after Saints Cosmas and Damian. In the prayer *Nobis quoque peccatoribus*, after Saint Anastasia the name of Saint Scholastica is added; in the prayer *Libera nos*, the names of Saint Apollinaris, Saint Lawrence, and Saint Benedict are added to the names of the archangels and apostles.

This Sacramentary contains the order for making a catechumen, the order of baptism for emergency administration, the order for giving penance, the order for visiting the sick, and finally the order for burying the dead. It also contains the order for performing the sacred liturgy, along with certain Masses and prayers for various needs—some from the commons and others for various classes of the departed.

The third is finally a breviary, whose title is: “Here begins the office of the breviary according to the order of the hermitage of the Holy Cross of Fonte Avellana.” It begins with Advent. Ancient hymns are read on the day of the Nativity of the Lord, on the Nativity of Saint Andrew the Apostle, of Saint Benedict the Abbot, on the feast of the Finding of the Holy Cross, and on the other feasts of the apostles Peter and Paul, Saint Mary Magdalene, the Assumption of the blessed Virgin Mary, and Saint Martin.

Proper prayers are included for Saints Ambrose, Zeno, Syrus, Blaise, Gregory, and Emigdus. The latter is especially celebrated in the city of Ascoli. The church of Saint Hilary and another of the Holy Cross in that city belonged to the monks of Avellana. A complete proper office for Saint Apollinaris, whom the Avellanese have always honored with the greatest devotion, is read. Finally, at the end of the breviary is found the office of the blessed Virgin Mary.

Let us now bring forward the excerpts themselves, omitting everything that is found in the published missals and breviaries.

# EXCERPTS FROM THE FIRST AVELLANESE CODEX

[Col. 0879]

## WEDNESDAY. BEGINNING OF THE FAST. COLLECT AT SAINT ANASTASIA

[Col. 0879B]

First of all, the blessing of ashes.

Almighty and eternal God, etc. This first prayer is the same as that found in the published editions.

**Another prayer.** Grant us, O Lord, to begin the defenses of Christian warfare with holy fasts, so that, as we prepare to fight against spiritual wickedness, we may be fortified by the aids of self-restraint. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Another.** God of forgiveness, God of goodness and mercy, who came to the aid of the Ninevites clothed in ash and sackcloth and crying out for your mercy, graciously hear us as we cry out to you, and deign to bless this creature of ash, which sinners use while imploring the indulgence of your holy mercy, and to pour into it the grace of your sanctification, so that whoever is sprinkled with the burning of this dust may first receive from you, O God, forgiveness and remission of all sins. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Another prayer.** God, who by humiliation, etc. This prayer likewise is the same as that found in the published editions; but the other prayer that follows there is absent from our manuscript missal.

The antiphon follows: “Let us change our clothing.” Meanwhile ashes are to be placed upon the heads of the people. “Remember, human being, that you are dust, and to dust you will return.” When these things have been completed, the cantor says: “You have mercy upon all.”

## AT MASS. STATION AT SAINT SABINA

**Prayer.** Grant, O Lord, etc., as also in the published editions, including the Secret and Communion, except that in the manuscript only one prayer is given.

## PALM SUNDAY

At the middle of the second hour of the day they assemble in the church. Thus, while the brothers sing Terce, the ministers vest in the sacristy: one for the cross, two for the candlesticks, another for the holy water; the subdeacon for the thurible in a tunic, the deacon in a dalmatic, and the priest in a cope.

When Terce is finished, after the cantor has intoned the antiphon “They gathered together,” the ministers pass through the choir followed by the congregation, singing the antiphon [Col. 0880B] until they reach the place of the palms. When the antiphon and the verse “But one of them” have been completed, and “Lest perhaps” has been repeated, the subdeacon, facing east over the title, begins the reading: “Say to the daughter of Zion.” When it is finished, the response “Christ became obedient” is sung.

Then the deacon, facing north, begins the Gospel: “When he had drawn near.” When it is finished, the priest, facing east, blesses the palms and olive branches:

“The Lord be with you.” — “Let us pray. Increase faith,” etc. Here all the prayers are given as in the published editions, except the longer one that begins: “O God, who by a wondrous order of dispensation,” etc.

Then the blessed branches are sprinkled with holy water with the antiphon: “Sprinkle me, O Lord.” Afterward water is duly cast over the congregation as it approaches and over the people.

**Prayer.** God, who your Son, etc.

After this the cantor begins the antiphon: “The children of the Hebrews,” and others. Meanwhile the ministers receive branches from the priest’s hand, and afterward the congregation kisses his hand. Then the branches are given to the people, repeating the antiphon until everyone has received one.

When this is completed, the cantor begins the antiphon: “When he drew near.” Accompanying the Lord himself with every expression of reverence, they proceed to the church. There, after they have been arranged before the entrance and the antiphon has ended, two brothers enter the church and sing: “Glory, praise, and honor to you.” After the end of the two verses, they repeat from outside: “Glory, praise.” When the verses have been sung through, they enter the church singing the response “As he entered,” while all the bells are rung.

Finally, the ministers prepare themselves for Mass, and two officials put on copes in the choir. During the Tract, two others put on copes, and four sing, two by two.

## HOLY THURSDAY

At the ninth hour, fire is struck from crystal or flint, so that a candle may be lit from it. The priest blesses the fire among us, wearing only a stole and cope, and then holy water is used: “Sprinkle.” Among some, the deacon gives the blessing.

**Prayer.** God, who through your Son, namely the cornerstone, have bestowed upon your faithful the fire of charity, sanctify this new fire produced from flint for our useful purposes, and grant us to be so inflamed by heavenly desires through these Paschal feasts that with pure minds we may be able to reach the feasts of everlasting brightness. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Another prayer.** Lord God, almighty Father, unfailing light and holy creator of all lights, bless this light (Latin *bene+dic*: the marked prefix is *bene-*), which has been sanctified and blessed by you, who illumined the whole world, so that we may be kindled and illumined by that light with the fire of your brightness; and just as you illumined Moses with fire, so illumine our hearts and minds, that we may deserve to attain eternal life. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Another prayer.** Let the abundant outpouring of your blessing, we ask, almighty God, come upon this incense, and kindle this nocturnal brightness, invisible ruler, so that not only may the sacrifice offered this night shine forth through the admixture of your light’s mystery, but wherever it is carried by the mystery of this sanctification, the power of your majesty may be present, the wickedness of diabolical deceit having been driven away. Through [Christ our Lord].

One lamp is to be kept burning from this new fire until Holy Saturday, to light the candle that is to be blessed on that same day according to the order contained in the Sacramentary.

When this has been completed, and the church has been adorned with every light, they enter for Mass, which is to be sung with the greatest devotion because of the recent institution of the present sacrifice. For on this day the sacrifice of the sacred body and of the sacred blood of the divine gift took its beginning from the Lord himself. On this day the sacred chrism is made throughout the whole world. On this day also penitents are assisted through indulgence.

While None is being sung, the priest and ministers prepare festively for Mass: the deacon in a dalmatic, the subdeacon in a tunic, the candle-bearers, and the one who carries the thurible. The cantor in the choir, wearing a cope, solemnly begins the Mass, which is to be sung with the greatest devotion because of the recent institution of the present sacrifice. In it the response is repeated; and “I believe in one God” and “Glory to God in the highest” are sung.

Where the chrism is made, it is sung.

## MASS AT SAINT JOHN LATERAN

**Prayer**, etc. As in our published editions up to and including the consecration of the body and blood. After the “Lamb of God,” the priest divides the offerings, and all who are able communicate. So many hosts are to be consecrated on this day that from them there may be enough for Communion both on that day and on the following day.

It should be noted, however, that whole offerings of the Lord’s body are to be kept until the morning of Good Friday, and Communion is taken from them. The Lord’s blood, however, is to be entirely consumed on that same day.

Meanwhile, as they communicate, “Lamb of God” is said, and the Communion is “The Lord Jesus,” without the kiss.

Afterward the antiphon for Vespers, “The cup of salvation,” is begun, with the psalms, which are to be sung gently. Response: “Christ became obedient.” Antiphon: “While they were eating, he took.” After the *Magnificat*, when the antiphon has ended, the concluding prayer follows:

[Col. 0882A] Refreshed with the nourishment of life, we ask, O Lord our God, that what we carry out in the time of our mortality we may obtain through the gift of immortality. Through [Christ our Lord].

After the deacon says, “Let us bless the Lord,” in many churches “Go, the Mass is ended” is said, because they also say “Glory to God in the highest,” which we do not say.

## GOOD FRIDAY

While None is being sung, the priest and ministers put on black chasubles, if they have them, and make confession there in the sacristy. No candles are then lit around the altar, and a small but very clean linen cloth is placed upon the altar.

After the priest and ministers have come before the altar, the deacon immediately approaches to read, announcing the prophet’s name in the reading in this way: “A reading from the prophet Hosea.” When it has ended, they sing the Tract in the choir, etc., as in the published editions up to and including the final prayer: “Almighty and eternal God.”

When the prayers have ended, the prior gives a sermon to the people concerning peace and takes the greatest care to recall all the dissenting children of his Church to harmony, so that they may be worthy of the sacrament of human reconciliation.

When this has been done, they approach to uncover the cross, as prescribed in the order. After it has been uncovered and adored, the priest comes with the ministers before the altar. The deacon is vested in his chasuble, as is customary for him when ministering; the subdeacon is likewise vested in his own. After confession has been made before the altar, the deacon carries the corporal to the altar and spreads it out.

In the sacristy, in a suitable place, the deacon prepares the chalice with unconsecrated wine. The Lord’s body—that is, the whole offerings preserved from the Lord’s body on the preceding day—is carefully and reverently placed upon the paten; over it he places the folded corporal, because it is fitting that the Lord’s body, in which all our salvation and redemption lie, be handled with the greatest reverence.

Two candle-bearers in white approach him, together with a third carrying a smoking thurible, and the subdeacon carrying a cruet of water. The deacon carries the chalice with the Lord’s body, saying privately:

“This body, which will be handed over for you; this chalice is the New Testament in my blood, says the Lord. Do this, as often as you receive it, in remembrance of me.”

[Col. 0882D] While the deacon holds the chalice, the priest mixes in the water. When these offerings have been made, the priest bows before the altar, saying: “In a spirit of humility and with a contrite heart, may we be received by you, O Lord,” etc.

After this, rising, he begins in a moderate voice: “Let us pray. Instructed by saving commands”; “Our Father.” He completes the whole prayer, while the choir responds: “But deliver us from evil.”

Then he says silently: “Deliver us, we ask, O Lord,” as is customary. When he has said, “World without end,” and “Amen,” “The peace of the Lord” is not said, nor is it given by kisses; rather, he takes from the holy offering and places it in the chalice, saying nothing.

The unconsecrated wine is sanctified by the Lord’s body being placed in it, and all the brothers communicate in silence.

When all have communicated, they say Vespers plainly, with the psalms of the feria. Then: “My soul magnifies the Lord,” followed by “Our Father,” “Have mercy on me, O God,” and “Christ became obedient.”

On Holy Saturday, while None is being sung, the ministers put on more splendid vestments: the deacon a dalmatic, the subdeacon a tunic for the thurible, and two for the candlesticks, in white. When None has ended, the deacon blesses the candle.

“Let the angelic host of heaven exult,” etc., as in the published editions up to the words “and our bishop.” Except that among us there is no lighting of lamps. After the aforementioned words “and our bishop,” the following immediately appear:

“And our most serene emperor N., together with his most noble offspring or his entire army, and all who are present, may you deign to preserve in the peace of the times during these Paschal joys. Therefore, O Lord, may you deign to accept this candle, which your servant N. offers to you, so that for many years he may happily and joyfully pay his vows to you, the Lord, and reach the old age he desires.

“Therefore I bless you (Latin *bene+dico*: the marked prefix is *bene-*), creature of wax, by the living God, by the holy God, by God, who commanded you to be gathered from all the flowers of the field and ordered a fire to be kindled in the presence of his glory, so that wherever you are placed, that place may be fortified, protected, and defended from every divine anger and every assault of the enemy, through the power and name of our Lord Jesus Christ, who lives and reigns with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit forever and ever.” [Col. 0883C] Amen.

After the candle has been blessed, the reader ascends to the ambo and announces: “A reading from the book of Genesis. In the beginning he created.” The first reading. He reads plainly and clearly, for understanding.

There are individual prayers for each reading. The first is said by the lord prior, wearing a cope and stole; the following ones are said by other priests. For none of these prayers is “The Lord be with you” said, but only “Let us pray.”

**Prayer.** God, who wondrously, etc., as in the published editions through the entire twelfth reading, after which the following Tract is added: “As the deer.”

## Prayer

Almighty and everlasting God, look favorably upon the devotion of the people being reborn, who, like a deer longing for springs of water, thirst; and mercifully grant that, through the mystery of baptism, the thirst of their faith may sanctify soul and body. Through [Christ our Lord].

At the last reading, the priest leaves the choir with the ministers and is vested in the finest vestments, unless he is going to celebrate the baptism; in that case he uses humbler vestments until Mass. When these things have been completed, two cantors vested in copes are to perform the threefold litany, extending it according to the season. When it is finished, the assembly waiting in the choir is to sit. The ministers, having returned to the sacristy, remain there until the bells have been blessed; when they cease, a procession is made through the cloister, and the antiphon *When the Lord had descended into hell* is sung, until they return to the choir.

There, when the antiphon has ended, the priest, standing before the base of the altar, begins in a moderate voice: *Now Christ the Lord has risen*, and the choir responds: *Thanks be to God*. This is done three times. After these words, the cantor begins in a loud voice: *Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia*. Then: *Lord, have mercy*. When this is finished, the priest begins most devoutly: *Glory to God in the highest*. After the prayer comes the Epistle, and after the Epistle, *Alleluia*. Then the tract: *Praise the Lord*. When it is finished, the deacon begins the Gospel; before it, no light is carried, but only incense. [lacuna]

Afterward the priest says: *I believe in one God*. Then: *The Lord be with you*, and *Let us pray*. The Offertory is not sung, nor the *Agnus Dei*, nor the Communion; nevertheless, the kiss is given according to the custom of our Church. After the peace has been given and the priest and ministers have communicated, *Alleluia* is begun in the choir with the psalm *Praise the Lord, all nations*, for the newly baptized. When it is finished, *Alleluia* is repeated with the *Gloria*, and it ends without a neume. Afterward the prior, if he has not celebrated Mass, begins the antiphon *Now on the Sabbath evening*, with the psalm *My soul magnifies*. When the antiphon has ended and the brothers have communicated, Vespers is finally concluded with the prayer from the Mass. For this reason, among some people it is not inappropriately said by the deacon: *Let us bless the Lord*; but among us, whenever *Glory to God in the highest* is sung, the deacon also says: *Go, the Mass is ended*.

## On Holy Saturday Night, at Mass

Prayer. God, who made this most sacred night, etc., as in the printed editions, through this prayer, the Secret, the Preface, the *Communicantes*, the *Hanc igitur*, and the Communion; all these are found only in the stated manuscript missal.

## The Order of How a Bishop or Priest Is to Prepare for Mass

In the first place, let three psalms be sung, either by him personally or by the clerics standing nearby: the psalm *How lovely*; *You have blessed*; *Incline*; and the prayers [lacuna]. The following chapters are recited: *Arise*; *Let it be done*; *O God, turn us*; *Show us*; *From hidden faults*; *Do not enter*; *Your priests*.

Then, when he has removed the tunic, he says:

“Strip me, Lord, of the old man with his deeds, and clothe me with the new man, who has been created according to God in righteousness and the holiness of truth.”

For the amice:

“Tear, Lord, my sackcloth and give joy to my heart. Amen.”

For the alb:

“Clothe me, Lord, with the breastplate of righteousness and the helmet of salvation. Amen.”

For the girdle:

“Gird, Lord, the loins of my mind, and circumcise the vices of my heart. Amen.”

For the stole:

“Surround my neck, Lord, with the stole of righteousness, and purify my mind from every corruption of sin.”

For the chasuble:

“Clothe me, Lord, with priestly righteousness, so that I may deserve to be brought into the everlasting tabernacles.”

As he enters toward the altar, let him say:

“I will go in to the altar of God, to God”; the psalm *Judge me, O God*.

When he has reached the altar, with his face humbly inclined, let him say the whole confession in order:

“Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy. Our Father, who are. Our help. He who made heaven and earth. Confess to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy is forever.

“And I, miserable and wretched, confess to almighty God, to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, and to all his angels and saints, and to you, brother, that I have sinned exceedingly through my fault, through my fault, through my fault, in thought, speech, pleasure, consent, and deed. Therefore I beseech all the saints of God and you, brother, to pray and intercede for me with our Lord Jesus Christ.”

“May almighty God have mercy on you and forgive you all your sins; may he free you from every evil, save and strengthen you in every good work, and may Christ, the Son of God, lead you into eternal life. Amen.”

“May almighty God grant us the indulgence and forgiveness of all our sins, and a period of true and fruitful penance.”

**V.** God, turning us, will you give us life?  
**R.** And your people will rejoice in you.  
**V.** Show us, Lord, your mercy.  
**R.** And grant us your salvation.  
**V.** Do not enter into judgment.  
**R.** For no one will be justified.  
**V.** Be favorable.  
**R.** Lest they ever say.  
**V.** Lord, hear my prayer.  
**R.** And let my cry come to you.  
**V.** The Lord be with you.  
**R.** And with your spirit.

### Prayer

Take away from us, Lord, we beseech you, through the intercession of these and all your saints, all our iniquities, so that we may deserve to enter the Holy of Holies with pure minds. Through the Lord.

When he kisses the altar, he says:

“We beseech you, almighty Lord our God, that through the merits of the saints whose relics are here, you may deign to forgive us all our sins.”

Then, when he kisses the Gospel:

“May the peace of Christ, which he handed down to us through his Gospel, strengthen and preserve our hearts and bodies unto eternal life. Amen.”

Before the Gospel, when he has placed incense in the thurible, or before the deacon bows, he says:

“May the Lord kindle within us the fragrance of his heavenly inspiration, and fill our hearts to hear and fulfill the commandments of his Gospel. He who lives.”

Another prayer:

“In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. May this incense, etc. Let it be directed, Lord, etc.”

When the deacon has asked for a blessing:

“May the Lord be in your heart and on your lips, so that you may suitably proclaim the Gospel of peace.”

After the Gospel has been read, let him say:

“Peace be with you.”

When he kisses the Gospel, he says:

“Through these words of the holy Gospel of his Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, may the Lord forgive all our offenses.”

Before he receives the oblation, let him say most humbly:

“Before your eyes, O God, I, guilty and a witness to my conscience, stand; I do not dare to ask for what I do not deserve to obtain. For you know, Lord, what is being done within us. We are ashamed to confess what we do not fear to admit. We obey you only in words, but lie in our hearts, and what we say we wish, we prove by our actions that we do not wish. But spare those who confess, Lord; forgive those who sin; have mercy on those who beseech you. And because every understanding is weak in your sacraments, and words before you are not without guilt, grant, Lord, that you may not receive words from us, the unworthy and sinful, but may grant pardon through yourself, who live and reign.”

While he washes his hands after the Gospel has been read:

“Grant, almighty Father, to our senses that, just as the stains of the hands are washed here, so the pollutions of our minds may be cleansed inwardly by you, and that the increase of holy virtues may grow within us.”

Before approaching the sacraments, let him bow before the altar, saying:

“I, a sinner, about to commemorate the saving Victim of the whole world, when I contemplate its dignity and my own foulness, am tormented by the consciousness of sins. Yet because you are greatly merciful, I implore you to deign to give me a contrite spirit—the sacrifice you have revealed to be pleasing to you—so that, purified by it, I may approach with devout hands the life-giving Victim, which may blot out all my sins, instill in me the care to avoid them forever, and grant the benefits of salvation to all for whom it is offered. Through [Christ our Lord]. Amen.”

When someone offers the oblation to the priest, let him say:

“In the spirit of humility and with a contrite heart, I offer a victim to you, Lord, my Creator, for the forgiveness of all my sins and of all the living and departed faithful.”

The priest, receiving the oblation, says:

“Receive, holy Trinity, this oblation, which your servant offers to you, and grant that it may ascend pleasing to you in your sight.”

Another prayer:

“Receive, holy Trinity, what I offer to you for the souls of your male and female servants, so that you may grant them eternal rest among your saints and elect, and that in their fellowship we may enjoy eternal life. Through [Christ our Lord].”

When the priest or deacon offers the chalice, let him say:

“Lord Jesus Christ, who willed that blood and water should flow from your side on the cross of your Passion, by which you would consecrate the Church, receive this sacrifice placed upon your altar, and mercifully grant that it may ascend before the sight of your divine majesty with the fragrance of sweetness, for our redemption and that of the whole world.”

When the oblation has been placed [read: “he offers”], let him say:

“May this sacrifice placed upon your altar be acceptable to you, almighty God.”

Then the chalice is placed upon the altar:

“We offer you, Lord, the chalice of salvation; we beseech your mercy, that our sacrifice may ascend before the sight of your divine majesty with the fragrance of sweetness.”

Then, blessing the oblation and the chalice with devout hand, let him say:

“Come, almighty and everlasting Sanctifier, bless+ and sanctify this sacrifice prepared for you.”

Another prayer:

“In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, may this sacrifice be immaculate, united to you, the living and true God, consecrated and blessed.”

Over the oblations:

“Sanctify, we beseech you, Lord, this obla+tion, that it may become for us the body of your Only-Begotten Son.”

Over the chalice, let him say:

“Sanctify, we beseech you, Lord, this cali+cem (‘chalice’), that it may become for us the blood of your Son.”

When he has placed incense in the thurible, let him say:

“Through the intercession of the holy archangel Gabriel, etc.”; as in our printed editions. In the manuscripts, however, the conclusion is lacking.

Here let him incense the sacrifice, or incense around it, saying:

“This incense.” See above.

When incense is offered to each person, let him say:

“May the Lord kindle in us the fire of love and the flame of eternal charity.”

Afterward let him turn toward those standing nearby and say:

“Pray, brothers, for me, that my office and yours may be fulfilled.”

Those responding are to say:

“May all the saints and elect of God pray for you. May the Lord hear you praying for our salvation and that of all. May the Lord remember all your sacrifice, and may your holocaust be made rich.”

Afterward let him say these psalms:

“To you, Lord, I have lifted up”; the psalm *Have mercy on me, O God*; the psalm *Lord, you have become our refuge*; the psalm *He who dwells in the help*; *Save your servant*; *Let your mercy, Lord, be upon us*; *Arise, Lord*.

### Prayer

May your servants rejoice, Lord, in the benefits they have obtained, and mercifully grant the desired fulfillment of mercy to those to whom you have given confidence in hoped-for salvation. Through [Christ our Lord].

“World without end,” etc., as in our printed editions, both with respect to all the Prefaces, common and proper, and with respect to the Canon up to the names of John and Paul, Cosmas and Damian. After these names the following words occur:

“and also those whose triumph is celebrated today, on the occasion of the solemnity, in the presence of your glory.”

What follows in the manuscript missal agrees with the printed editions through the entire prayer *Deliver us, we beseech you*, etc.

### Prayer

“May the mingling and consecration of the Body and Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ bring eternal life to those who receive it. Amen.”

“Lamb of God, who take away the sins of the world, have mercy on us.” Three times.

For the peace, while kissing the altar: “Lord Jesus Christ,” etc., as in the printed editions through the entire third prayer.

When he takes the Lord’s body in his hands, let him say:

“I will receive the heavenly bread and call upon the name of the Lord. Lord, I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof; but only say the word, and my servant will be healed.”

When he communicates:

“May the Body of our Lord Jesus Christ preserve my soul unto eternal life.”

At the sound of the paten, let the brothers say this prayer:

“May the reception of this sacrament, Lord, be for us the forgiveness of all our sins, through Christ.”

The rest is the same as in the printed editions through the entire prayer *May it please you, holy Trinity*, with which the Mass of the stated manuscript missal ends. There is no mention there either of *Go, the Mass is ended*, or of the blessing, or of the Gospel, as among us. Likewise, nowhere in the Canon is there mention of genuflections.

## Masses for the Birthdays of the Saints

### On the Feast of Saint Ambrose

#### Prayer

May the prayer of Saint Ambrose continually accompany us, Lord, so that what our petition does not obtain may be granted through his intercession for us. Through [Christ our Lord].

#### Secret

May these sacrifices in us, through the intercession of your most blessed confessor Ambrose, remain in action and be strengthened in operation. Through [Christ our Lord].

#### Communion

May this Communion cleanse us from guilt, Lord, and, through the intercession of your blessed confessor and pontiff Ambrose, make us participants in heavenly remedies. Through [Christ our Lord].

### On the Octave of Saint Andrew

#### Prayer

May the frequently repeated solemnity of your blessed apostle Andrew protect us, Lord, so that we may experience perpetual defense from him whose patronage we continually recall. Through [Christ our Lord].

#### Secret

May these gifts, which are offered to you for the venerable intercessions of Saint Andrew, obtain for us, we beseech you, Lord, a more abundant pardon. Through [Christ our Lord].

#### Communion

May the venerable apostle Andrew aid your family, Lord, by his supplication, and may he become a devout intercessor, since he was a preacher and ruler of your name. Through [Christ our Lord].

### On the Birthday of Saint Lucy the Virgin

The Prayer and Secret are the same as in the printed editions.

#### Communion

Having joyfully received the heavenly sacraments, Lord, may they advance us toward eternal life through the intercession of blessed Lucy the martyr. Through [Christ our Lord].

### On the Birthday of Saint Thomas the Apostle

The Prayer and Secret are as in the printed editions.

#### Communion

We beseech you, Lord, help us through the intercession of your blessed apostle Thomas, for whose solemnity we have joyfully received your holy things. Through [Christ our Lord].

### On the Birthday of Saint Anastasius the Martyr

#### Prayer

May the birthday of your blessed martyr Anastasius always receive us as worshipers, Lord; may it pour into us the joy of his glorification and make us acceptable to you. Through [Christ our Lord].

#### Secret

Look upon these present gifts, we beseech you, Lord, with such serene compassion that they may be filled with the blessing of the Holy Spirit, and that they may breathe into our hearts that strong love by which the holy martyr conquered all bodily torments. Through [Christ our Lord].

#### Communion

We have received the heavenly sacraments at the solemnity of your martyr Saint Anastasius, Lord. Through his intercessions, we beseech you, grant that what we undertake temporally we may attain in eternal joys. Through [Christ our Lord].

### On the Birthday of Saint Projectus

#### Prayer

May the glorious intercession of your blessed martyr Projectus commend us, Lord, so that through his prayers we may obtain what we do not deserve by our own deeds. Through [Christ our Lord].

#### Secret

Mercifully receive our prayer, Lord, together with the sacrificial offerings placed upon the altar, and graciously make them acceptable to your mercy through the supplication of the martyr Projectus; mercifully inspire in us that strong love which burned in him. Through [Christ our Lord].

#### Communion

We have received votive gifts, Lord, for the Passion of your blessed martyr Projectus. We beseech you to grant us, through his prayers, assistance alike for the present life and for eternal life. Through [Christ our Lord].

### On the Birthday of Saint Brigid the Virgin

#### Prayer

Almighty and everlasting God, who pour the light of your radiance into the lamps of the prudent, adorned with the oil of a good conscience, mercifully grant that, through the intercession of your blessed virgin Brigid, whose birthday we celebrate, we may be freed from association with the foolish. Through [Christ our Lord].

#### Secret

Sanctify, we beseech you, Lord, through the merits of your holy virgin Brigid, the peaceful offerings that we solemnly offer to your majesty, so that they may both release us from the bonds of our sins and multiply for us, your servants, the gifts of your mercy. Through [Christ our Lord].

#### Communion

Redeemed, we beseech you, Lord, by the divine mysteries, may we be raised up through the intercessions of your blessed virgin Brigid and freed from the adversities of the present life, and may we attain the rewards of eternal blessedness. Through [Christ our Lord].

## The Purification of Saint Mary

Collect at Saint Adrian. First let Tierce be sung; afterward let the candles be blessed, and then the priest says:

Let us pray. Hear, we beseech you, Lord, your people, whom you grant outwardly to venerate you annually with devotion; inwardly grant that they may attain the light of your grace.

World without end. Amen. The Lord be with you. And with your spirit. Lift up your hearts. We have them with the Lord. Let us give thanks to the Lord our God. It is worthy and just.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, everlasting God, Creator of heaven and earth, King of kings and Lord of lords. Mercifully deign to hear us, your suppliants, crying out and entreating you. You who created all things from nothing, and by your command caused this liquid to come to the perfection of a candle through the work of bees, and who on this day fulfilled the petition of the just Simeon: we humbly beseech you to bless+ and sancti+fy these candles for human use and for the health of bodies and souls, whether they are lit on land or on water, through the invocation of your most holy name and through the intercession of holy Mary, mother of your Son, whose feast is devoutly celebrated today, and through the prayers of all your saints. Thus may you hear from your holy heaven and from the seat of your majesty the voices of this people of yours, who carry them honorably in their hands and praise you in song; and may you be merciful to all who cry out to you, whom you redeemed by the precious blood of your Son, who lives and reigns with you, God, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, forever and ever. Amen.

Let us pray. Instructed by saving commands and formed by divine teaching, we dare to say: “Our Father, who are in heaven,” through “And lead us not into temptation. But deliver us from evil.”

Here he changes his voice, as though reading:

Let us pray. Bless, Lord Jesus Christ, this creature of wax at our supplications, and pour into it, through the power of the holy cross, a heavenly bene+diction, so that it may receive such strength and bene+diction through the sign of your cross—since you have granted it to the human race for driving away darkness—that wherever it is lit or placed, the devil may depart and tremble, and flee pale with all his ministers from those dwellings, and may no longer presume to disturb or mock those who serve God.

Therefore, suppliantly we beseech you, Lord, send your holy angel Raphael, who tore out and drove away from Sarah and Tobias the deadly demon troubling them. May he crush and destroy that demon from all the dwellings of those who worship God: from basilicas, houses, corners, beds, refectories, and every place in which those serving God dwell and rest, sleep, keep watch, walk, and stand. May that wicked one no longer be able to disturb them or send terrors upon those whom you have made secure through the anointing of your holy chrism.

“I bless+ you, wax, in the name of God the almighty Father, and of his only-begotten Son, and of the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, so that, the devil being put to flight, you may everywhere be the destruction of all his companions, with the assistance of that same holy and undivided Trinity, which lives and reigns in the unity of its essence forever and ever. Amen.”

When the blessing is finished, the priest takes blessed water and sprinkles it over the candles, then takes some of the wax and lights it. When they begin to be lit, the cantor begins this antiphon: *A light for the revelation of the nations*. Psalm: *Now*. The antiphon is repeated after every verse of the same psalm. *Glory to the Father. As it was*. This continues until all the candles have been lit. When they have been lit, they say this prayer:

### Prayer

Almighty and everlasting God, who on this day presented your Only-Begotten Son to be received in your holy temple in the arms of the holy Simeon, we humbly beseech you to bless+ and sancti+fy these candles of yours, which we, your faithful, desire to carry with every magnificence, brightly lit; and to kindle them with the light of heavenly blessing, so that, offering them to you, Lord our God, we may deserve to be presented in the temple of your glory, worthy and kindled by the holy fire of your sweetest charity. Through the same [Christ our Lord].

When the prayer is finished, let them proceed to Saint Mary while singing the antiphon: *Hail, Mary, full of grace, virgin Mother of God. Adorn your bridal chamber, O Zion, and receive*.

### Prayer

Complete your grace in us, Lord, we beseech you. You fulfilled the expectation of the just Simeon; grant that, just as he did not see death before he deserved to see Christ the Lord, so we too may obtain eternal life. Through the same [Christ our Lord].

## On the Feast of Saint Blaise

### Prayer

God, who have made this day honorable for us through the solemnity of your blessed martyr Blaise, grant your peoples the gift of spiritual joys, and direct the minds of all the faithful into the way of eternal salvation. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Secret

May the prayer of your martyr Saint Blaise accompany these offerings, Lord, which we offer to be consecrated to your name; through it, we beseech you, grant that we may be purified and defended. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Communion

We beseech you, Lord, help us through the intercession of your blessed martyr Blaise, for whose solemnity we have joyfully received your holy gifts. Through [Christ our Lord].

## On the Feast of Saint Benedict

### Prayer

God, who adorned your blessed confessor Benedict on earth with a praiseworthy life and exalted him in heaven with eternal glory, we beseech you that, through the assistance of his merits, our life may be commended to you. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Secret

May your blessing, Lord, descend upon these offerings through the intercession of your blessed confessor Benedict; may it mercifully work blessing for us and obtain the gifts of blessed immortality. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Communion

Confident in the prayers of your blessed confessor Benedict, Lord, we beseech your mercy, so that through what we have received we may obtain eternal remedies. Through [Christ our Lord].

## The Annunciation of Saint Mary

God, who on this day willed your Word to be united to the womb of the blessed Virgin, make us so to fulfill our duty that we may be able to please you. Through the same [Christ our Lord].

The Secret is as in the printed editions.

### Communion

Be present, Lord, to your people, so that through the intercession of blessed Mary ever-virgin they may faithfully preserve in mind and body what they have received. Through [Christ our Lord].

## On the Feast of Saint Euphemia

### Prayer

Grant us, almighty God, both to rejoice in the merits of your holy martyr Euphemia and to return thanks for her intercessions. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Secret

Magnifying you, Lord, by our gifts, we beseech you to obtain for us heavenly joys in the solemnities of Saint Euphemia and to grant us everlasting patronage. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Communion

May the pleasing prayer of your holy martyr Euphemia accompany us, Lord, and never cease to ask your forgiveness for us. Through [Christ our Lord].

## On the Feast of Saints Laurentinus and Pergentinus

### Prayer

Protect us, Lord, through the prayers of your saints, so that, continually venerating the feasts of your martyrs Laurentinus and Pergentinus, we may be fortified by the help of faith and advance through their magnificent example. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Secret

Venerating the feasts of your martyrs Laurentinus and Pergentinus, Lord, we offer gifts dedicated to your name. Grant, we beseech you, that by showing them reverence we may obtain pardon for ourselves. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Communion

Protect your people, Lord, and grant through the prayers of the saints that we may continually render to you the due observance of the feast of your martyrs Laurentinus and Pergentinus, which you have handed down to us. Through [Christ our Lord].

## On the Feast of Saint Boniface with His Companions

God, who strengthened the blessed bishop Boniface with steadfastness in his Passion, and who deigned to join to him Eoban and Adhelarius for proclaiming your glory to the nations, etc.

## On the Feast of Saints Albinus, Paulinus, and Niceta, with Eight Hundred Eighty-Nine Others

### Prayer

Be favorable, Lord, to our supplications, and, through the assisting merits of your holy martyrs Albinus, Paulinus, and Niceta the bishop, together with eight hundred eighty-nine who suffered for your name, graciously hear our prayers, so that our sins may be forgiven and we may deserve to live with you forever. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Secret

Mercifully receive, Lord, our prayers together with the sacrificial offerings, and graciously complete, with compassionate favor, the petition of your martyrs whose notable glory we celebrate; and mercifully grant that the strong love which burned in them may breathe within us. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Communion

Through the intercession of your saints whose feasts we celebrate, grant us the help of your mercy, Lord, so that although we do not deserve the crown of your martyrdom, at least we may not be rejected from pardon. Through [Christ our Lord].

## On the Vigil of Saint John the Baptist

The Prayer is as in the printed editions.

### Secret

Mercifully regard the gifts of your people, Lord, we beseech you, and grant that we may rejoice in the intercessions of blessed John the Baptist, whose solemnity you grant us to anticipate. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Mass at First Light

#### Prayer

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we who celebrate the solemnity of blessed John the Baptist may be fortified before you by his intercessions. Through [Christ our Lord].

#### Secret

The gifts, we beseech you, Lord, etc., as in the printed editions.

#### Communion

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we who have received heavenly nourishment may, through the intercession of blessed John the Baptist, be fortified by these things against every adversity. Through [Christ our Lord].

#### Another Prayer at Vespers

God, who grant us to attend annually the solemnity of blessed John the Baptist, grant, we beseech you, that we may celebrate it with devout minds and, through the merit of his patronage, fully receive an increase of security. Through [Christ our Lord].

## On the Vigil of the Apostles Peter and Paul

### Prayer

God, who grant us to anticipate the glorious birthdays of your blessed apostles Peter and Paul, grant, we beseech you, that we may always be preceded by their benefits and assisted by their prayers. Through [Christ our Lord].

The Secret is as in the printed editions.

### Communion

God, who consecrated your Church through the faith and name of your apostle Peter, and who deigned to join blessed Paul to him for proclaiming your glory to the nations, grant that all who have gathered for the solemnity of your apostles may be enriched with spiritual reward. Through [Christ our Lord].

## On the Feast of the Apostles Peter and Paul

### Prayer

Almighty and everlasting God, who rescue your Church, founded upon apostolic solidity, from the terror of the inner gates, grant that, persisting in your truth, it may receive no fellowship with the faithless. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Secret

Mercifully regard your family, Lord, and defend it with apostolic protections, so that it may be governed by the prayers of those whom, by your appointment, you have established as its princes. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Communion

Hear us, God our Savior, and protect us with the safeguards of your apostles, whose teachings you have granted us to be faithful to. Through [Christ our Lord].

### At Vespers

#### Prayer

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we who are continually fortified by apostolic protection may neither succumb to vices nor be overwhelmed by adversities. Through [Christ our Lord].

## On the Octave of Saint John the Baptist

### Prayer

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that your Church, which on the octave venerates again the birth of the precursor of your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, John the Baptist, may deserve, through his going before it before your mercy, to be freed by your compassion from all sins. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Secret

Your Church most devoutly celebrates the honorable birth of Saint John the Baptist with doubled gifts on the eighth day. O most merciful Lord, grant by your customary clemency that, through his intervening for it, it may deserve before you to receive that gift as a saving one. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Communion

May your gifts, which were received in honor of your name at the repeated solemnity of John the Baptist, the precursor of your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, provide assistance to your Church, almighty God, we beseech you, so that, cleansed from every attack of the ambusher, it may bless you, serve you, and, under your protection, always be free from every evil. Through [Christ our Lord].

## On the Feast of Saint Mustiola

### Prayer

May the effect of holy joy continually increase in us, Lord, so that the venerable solemnity of your blessed martyr Mustiola may be enlarged. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Secret

Celebrating the feast of your holy martyr Mustiola, Lord, we offer prayers and sacrifice a victim. Grant, we beseech you, that together with temporal protection they may provide us with life and everlasting increase. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Communion

God of the heavenly powers, we beseech you: may the sacrifices offered for the Passion of your holy martyr Mustiola teach us to despise temporal desires and to love the gifts of heavenly joys. Through [Christ our Lord].

## On the Octave of the Apostles Peter and Paul

The Prayer and Secret are as in the printed editions.

### Communion

As we recall the desired solemnities of your blessed apostles Peter and Paul, Lord, grant, we beseech you, that we may be cleansed through their supplications, since we are governed by their leadership. Through [Christ our Lord].

## On the Feast of the Seven Brothers

### Prayer

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we who have known the glorious martyrs Januarius, Felix, Philip, Silvanus, Alexander, Vitalis, and Martial to be strong in their confession, etc., as in the printed editions, including the Secret and Post-Communion.

## On the Feast of Saint Paternianus

### Prayer

God, who through your angel Raphael showed the way to blessed Paternianus and revealed his death, hear the prayers that we offer to you at his solemnity, etc., as in the printed editions, in the second Mass of a confessor and bishop.

## On the Feast of Saint Margaret

### Prayer

God, who on this day caused blessed Margaret the virgin to come to heaven through the palm of martyrdom, mercifully grant that, following her example, we may deserve to come to you. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Secret

May this victim, Lord, offered for the martyrdom of the blessed virgin Margaret, obtain for us both purity of mind and holiness of body. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Communion

Through reception of this sacrament and the intercession of the blessed virgin Margaret, deign both to remain in us and grant that we in turn may remain in you. Through [Christ our Lord].

## On the Feast of Saints Quiricus and Julitta

### Prayer

God, who kindle the flame of your love in the hearts of your saints Quiricus and Julitta, grant our hearts that same power of faith and charity, so that, rejoicing in their triumphs, we may be stirred by their examples. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Secret

May that truth which kindled the flame of your love in the hearts of your saints always illuminate us, Lord. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Communion

God, who grant your holy martyrs Quiricus and Julitta the solace of conquering and immense eternal glory to those who conquer, and who receive their lacerated flesh as a good and sweet-smelling fragrance, grant, we beseech you, that just as you bestowed on them the crown of martyrdom, so you may grant us the forgiveness of our sins. Through [Christ our Lord].

## On the Feast of Saints Hermagoras and Fortunatus

### Prayer

Through the intervention of your holy martyrs Hermagoras and Fortunatus, Lord, mercifully accept the voices of your Church, so that, when all adversities have been destroyed, it may serve you in secure freedom. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Secret

Offering the gifts of our humility, Lord, for the glorious Passion and solemnity of your holy martyrs Hermagoras and Fortunatus, we beseech you to deign to regard them favorably, and through their intercession grant us, in your accustomed compassion, the saving things both for advancement in life and for the soul. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Communion

As we receive the heavenly gifts of the mystery, we beseech you, Lord, to let us be assisted by the merits of your holy martyrs Hermagoras and Fortunatus, whose solemnity we celebrate with due veneration. Through [Christ our Lord].

## On the Feast of Saint Praxedis, Virgin and Martyr

### Prayer

God, who, among the other miracles of your power, also bestowed the victory of chastity and martyrdom upon the weaker sex, grant, we beseech you, that we may be assisted by the merits of your blessed and holy martyr Praxedis, whose blessedness shines upon us through her example. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Secret

Receive, Lord, the gifts that we bring on the solemnity of your blessed martyr Praxedis, since what such a mortal woman has become, taken up by you, returns to your praise and proclamation. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Communion

May your grace always exercise itself in us, Lord, we beseech you, so that it may both restore our hearts through the divine mysteries and gladden us through the commemoration of your holy martyr Praxedis. Through [Christ our Lord].

## On the Feast of Saint Mary Magdalene

The Prayer and Secret are as in the printed editions.

### Communion

Give life, Lord, to our soul and spirit wounded by the injury of sin. Through the intercession of blessed Mary Magdalene, by whose prayers you raised the four-days-dead Lazarus from the tomb through your unconquered power. You who live.

## On the Feast of Saint Apollinaris

The Prayer is as in the printed editions.

### Secret

Look, Lord, upon these offerings of ours, which we offer to be consecrated to your name, and may the prayer of blessed Apollinaris, your martyr and pontiff, accompany them; through it make us purified and defended. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Communion

Grant us, we beseech you, Lord, that your holy things which we have received may be supports of mind and body [lacuna], and, through the intervention of the merits of blessed Apollinaris, absolve us from all sins. Through [Christ our Lord].

## On the Feast of Saint Christina

### Prayer

May the effect of holy joy continually increase in us, Lord, so that the venerable solemnity of your blessed martyr Christina may be enlarged. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Feast of Saint Christina

**Secret.** We offer prayers for your holy martyr Christina, O Lord, and immolate the victim; grant, we ask, that together with temporal protection they may provide us with life and perpetual increase. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** O God of the heavenly powers, we ask that the sacrifices offered for the passion of your holy martyr Christina may teach us to hold temporal desires in contempt and make us possess the gifts of heavenly joys. Through [Christ our Lord].

## On the Vigil of Saint James the Apostle

**Prayer.** Grant us, almighty God, to anticipate with fitting honor the coming solemnity of your blessed apostle James, and to celebrate it when it arrives with worthy devotion. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** May the offering of our devotion be acceptable to you, O Lord, and may it make us come purer to the approaching feast of your holy apostle James. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** Grant us, eternal Savior, that we may everywhere be protected by the devout prayer of your blessed apostle James, whose birthday we anticipate through these holy things that we have received, with a service offered in fulfillment of our vows. [Col. 0896A] Through [Christ our Lord].

## Feast of Saint Christopher

**Prayer**, as in the printed editions.

**Secret.** By the prayers of this saint, O Lord, we ask that this offering, which is to be immolated for his feast, may be made pleasing to you. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** We have been filled, O Lord, with the gift of the desired solemnity; grant that through it we may live both by the celebration and by the prayers of your blessed martyr Christopher. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Feast of Saints Nazarius and Celsus

**Prayer**, as in the printed editions.

**Secret.** Appeased by the intercession of your holy martyrs Nazarius and Celsus, grant, we ask, that what we celebrate through a temporal rite we may receive in perpetual salvation. [Col. 0896B] Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** Hear our prayers, O Lord, and may your people, established under the great patronage of your holy martyrs Nazarius and Celsus, be freed from their offenses and defended from every adversity. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Birthday of the Holy Virgins Flora and Lucilla

**Prayer.** Grant us, O Lord our God, to rejoice in the unceasing veneration of your holy martyrs Flora and Lucilla, so that what we cannot celebrate with a worthy mind, we may at least continually honor with humble services. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** We offer prayers and gifts to your majesty, O Lord, rejoicing in honor of your holy virgins Flora and Lucilla. Grant, we ask, that we may both perform these things fittingly [Col. 0896C] and be able to acquire everlasting healing. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** May we be fortified by the sacraments we have received, O Lord, and, through the intercession of your holy virgins Flora and Lucilla, may we be protected by heavenly weapons against every assault of wickedness. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Finding of Saint Stephen, Protomartyr

**Prayer.** O God, who are the wondrous splendor of your saints, and who on this day revealed through a glorious finding the bodies of your saints Stephen, Nicodemus, Gamaliel, and Abibon, grant us to rejoice in their company in eternal gladness. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret**, as in the printed editions for the time of Easter concerning several martyrs.

[Col. 0896D] **Communion.** We have received the heavenly sacraments while celebrating the solemnities of your saints Stephen, Nicodemus, Gamaliel, and Abibon. Grant, we ask, that what we perform in time we may attain in eternal joys. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Blessing of Grapes

**Bene+dic**—bless, O Lord, these new fruits of the vine, which you, O Lord, have deigned to bring to maturity through the dew of heaven, the abundance of rains, and the serenity and calm of the seasons; and you have granted that we may receive them for our uses with thanksgiving, in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, through whom you, O Lord, always create all these good things. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Feast of Saint Donatus, Bishop and Martyr

**Prayer.** O God, who deigned to restore fragments of a cup in the hands of your blessed martyr [Col. 0897A] and pontiff Donatus, mercifully hear the prayers of those who plead with you, so that what does not possess confidence through merit may be granted to us through his intercession. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** O God, who deigned to restore fragments of a cup in the hands of your blessed bishop and martyr Donatus, look favorably upon the gifts of your people, so that the supplication of him whose solemnity we celebrate today may become saving for us. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** Almighty and merciful God, etc.; as in the printed editions.

## On the Vigil of the Assumption of Saint Mary

**Prayer**, as in the printed editions.

**Secret.** May the prayer of the Mother of God [Col. 0897B] intervene greatly for us with your clemency, O Lord; for this reason you transferred her from the present age, so that she might confidently intercede for our sins. Through the same [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** Grant, we ask, almighty God, that we may reach the eternal joys of blessed Mary ever-virgin, whose venerable assumption you grant us to celebrate with an annual solemnity. Through the same [Christ our Lord].

## Assumption of Saint Mary

**Prayer.** May the venerable solemnity of this day bring us saving assistance, O Lord, on which the holy Mother of God underwent temporal death, yet could not be overcome by the bonds of death—she who gave birth from herself to your Son, our Lord, made incarnate. Who lives and reigns with you.

**Secret.** May it assist us, O Lord, we ask, etc., [Col. 0897C] as in the printed editions, including the post-communion.

## Octave of Saint Lawrence

**Prayer.** May the venerable passion of blessed Lawrence make us rejoice, O Lord, and make us worthy to remember him adequately. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** Protect us, O Lord, by the prayers of blessed Lawrence the martyr, whose honorable passion we may commemorate with doubled gifts; although it is to be remembered in its own beginnings, it nevertheless remains continually glorious. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** May the intercession of blessed Lawrence the martyr, O Lord, grant us solemn assistance, we ask, so that participation in the heavenly table, which we have received, may bestow renewed joy upon your Church. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Feast of Saint Magnus

[Col. 0897D]

**Prayer.** Be present to our supplications, O Lord, and, through the intercession of your blessed martyr Magnus, mercifully defend us from the assault of our enemies. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** Grant us, we ask, almighty God, that the offering of our humility may be pleasing to you both in honor of your saints and may purify us alike in body and mind. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** As we receive your holy things, we ask, O Lord, that the blessed protection of Magnus may favor us. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Dedication of the Basilica of Saint Floridus

**Prayer and secret**, as in the printed editions for the dedication of a church.

[Col. 0898A] **Communion.** O God, who deigned to call your Church a bride, so that she who possessed grace through devotion to God might also possess piety through her name, grant that all this people serving your name may be deemed worthy to share in this designation; and that your Church, gathered for you in the temple whose anniversary day is celebrated, may fear you, love you, and follow you, so that, while continually walking in your footsteps, she may deserve, with you as guide, to reach the heavenly promises. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Feast of Saint Symphorian

**Prayer.** Guard us, O Lord, by the protection of your blessed martyr Symphorian, so that, as we recall his solemnity with annual devotion, we may be rescued from every adversity through his intercessions. Through [Christ our Lord].

[Col. 0898B] **Secret.** Receive favorably, O Lord, we ask, our prayer together with the offerings of the sacrifices placed upon the altar; and, through the supplication of your martyr Symphorian, graciously make it acceptable to your mercy. Kindly inspire in us that fervor which burned in him, so that, remaining in your love, we may be found steadfast in your faith, harmonious in conduct, and effective in our work. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** Satisfied with the sacred gift, we ask, almighty God, that through the intervention of your blessed martyr Symphorian you may command us all to be admitted to the company of your saints. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Feast of Saint Bartholomew the Apostle

**Prayer and secret**, as in the printed editions.

**Communion.** Protect your people, O Lord, and preserve forever in your defense those who trust in the patronage of your apostle Bartholomew. [Col. 0898C] Through [Christ our Lord].

## Feast of Saint Rufus the Martyr

**Prayer.** Be present to our supplications, so that, trusting in the intercessions of blessed Rufus, we may neither be frightened by the threats of our adversaries nor disturbed by any assault. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** Be appeased, we ask, O Lord, by the gifts offered, and, with your blessed martyr Rufus interceding, defend us from every danger. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** Refreshed by heavenly sacraments and joys, we humbly ask you, O Lord, that by the assistance of those whose triumphs we glory in, we may be protected. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Feast of Saint John the Baptist

**Prayer**, as in the printed editions.

[Col. 0898D] **Secret.** We bring you gifts, O Lord, for the passion of your holy martyr John the Baptist, because, when his earthly life ended, he was made perpetual in the heavenly dwelling; and we ask that through his favor this may advance us toward salvation. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** May the twofold solemnity of Saint John the Baptist bring us this gift, O Lord: that we may both reverently honor the magnificent sacraments we have received, now sanctified, and rejoice that they have been brought forth in us. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Feast of Saint Felicity

**Prayer.** Grant, we ask, almighty God, that as we recall the solemnity of your blessed martyr Felicity, we may be protected by her merits and prayers. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** Mercifully regard the vows of your people, O Lord, [Col. 0899A] and grant that we may rejoice in the intercession of those whose solemnity you grant us to celebrate. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** We humbly ask you, almighty God, that through the intervention of your saints you may both multiply your gifts within us and order our times. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Birthday of Saint Bartholomew

**Prayer.** Hear your people, O Lord, as they plead with the patronage of your apostle Saint Bartholomew, so that they may always serve you with secure devotion through your help. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** May the holy prayer of your apostle Bartholomew, O Lord, commend our sacrifice to you, we ask, so that it may become acceptable through the merits of him in whose honor it is solemnly offered. Through [Christ our Lord].

[Col. 0899B] **Communion.** We have received the divine mysteries, O Lord, rejoicing in the commemoration of the apostle Bartholomew. Perfect them so that, just as they bring glory to your saints, they may likewise, we ask, bring us forgiveness. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Feast of the Holy Confessors Floridus and Amantius

**Prayer.** Be favorable to us, your servants, we ask, O Lord, through the glorious merits of these your holy confessors Floridus and Amantius, who are venerated in this present Church, so that through their devout intercession we may always be protected from every adversity. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** May your clemency receive, O Lord, we ask, the gift offered from our hands, and through the prayers of these your holy confessors Floridus and Amantius [Col. 0899C] cleanse us from every sin. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** As we taste the divine mysteries that we have offered to your majesty for the veneration of these your holy confessors Floridus and Amantius, grant, we ask, O Lord, that through them we may deserve forgiveness of sins and be refreshed by the gifts of heavenly grace. Through [Christ our Lord].

## In Honor of All the Saints

**Prayer.** Grant, we ask, almighty God, that the intercession of holy Mary, ever-virgin Mother of God, and of all the heavenly powers, and of all the holy apostles, martyrs, confessors, and virgins, and of all the elect [Col. 0899D] may everywhere gladden us, so that, while we recall their merits, we may experience their patronage. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** Be appeased, O Lord, by the gifts offered, and, with blessed Mary and all your saints interceding, defend us from every danger. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** We have received the heavenly sacraments, O Lord, while recalling the commemoration of blessed Mary ever-virgin and all your saints. Grant, we ask, that what we perform in time we may attain in eternal joys. Through [Christ our Lord].

## In Honor of All the Saints Whose Relics Are in the Church

**Prayer.** Grant, we ask, almighty God, that holy Mary the Mother of God, and your holy apostles, martyrs, confessors, virgins, and all the saints, [Col. 0900A] whose patronage is contained in this church, may everywhere assist us, so that here, through their present aid, we may rejoice in peaceful worship of your praise. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** Merciful God, graciously receive, we ask, the gifts offered to your majesty, so that through the prayers of those whose most sacred relics are preserved in this basilica they may become saving for us. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** As we taste the divine mysteries, we ask, O Lord, that the intercession of blessed Mary ever-virgin and of those whose sacred presence we rejoice in here may protect us everywhere.

## Feast of All the Saints

**Prayer.** O God, who continually gladden us by the commemoration of blessed Mary ever-virgin and of the blessed apostles, martyrs, confessors, [Col. 0900B] virgins, and all the saints together, grant, we ask, that those whom we venerate in our daily service we may also follow by the example of a devout manner of life. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret**, as in the printed editions.

**Communion.** Grant us, O Lord, we ask, through the merits of blessed Mary ever-virgin and of all your saints interceding, that what we touch with our mouth we may receive with a pure mind. Through [Christ our Lord].

## For the Salvation of the Living and the Dead

**Prayer.** In your loving-kindness, we ask, O Lord, release all the bonds of our offenses; and, with blessed Mary ever-virgin and all the saints interceding, preserve in complete holiness our bishop and the entire congregation entrusted to him, [Col. 0900C] and us your servants, male and female, and this place; cleanse from vices and enlighten with virtues all who are joined to us by kinship or friendship, and all Christians; grant us peace and salvation; remove visible and invisible enemies; bestow charity upon our enemies; and grant to all the faithful, living and dead, life in the land of the living and eternal rest. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** O God, who through the sacrifice of your singular Body took away the sins of the whole world, appeased by this offering, wipe away the stains of our sins, forgive the sins of all Christian believers, living and dead, and grant them eternal rewards. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** May the sacraments [Col. 0900D] we have received, we ask, O Lord, cleanse all the faults of your servant, our bishop, and of us; may they drive far from us every depravity and weakness, as well as the fury of enemies and sudden death, through the merits of blessed Mary the Virgin and all the saints; and may they benefit all the faithful, living and dead, for forgiveness, for whose salvation they have been offered to you. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Mass to Ask for the Grace of the Holy Spirit

**O God, to whom every heart is open**, etc., as in the printed editions through the three prayers.

**Reading from the Book of Wisdom.** “The spirit of discipline will flee deceit,” etc., up to “he has a voice.”

## Mass for a Living Bishop

**Prayer**, the same as in the printed editions for the pope.

**Secret.** In your servant, our bishop, we ask, O Lord, graciously establish good conduct; mercifully pour into him whatever is pleasing to you, so that he may be worthy and able to merit your benefits. [Col. 0901A] Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** “May these things,” we ask, O Lord, etc., as in the printed editions.

## Another Mass for the Priest Himself

**Prayer.** I humbly beseech you, most loving God, almighty Father, creator of all things: while I confess that I, your servant, have grievously sinned before the omnipotence of your majesty, may you, through the intercession of blessed Mary ever-virgin and all your saints, mercifully extend to me the hand of your mercy, so that, while I offer this oblation of your compassion, you may most mercifully deign to absolve me from what I have wickedly committed. [Col. 0901B] Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** God of mercy, God of compassion, God of forgiveness, forgive, I ask, and have mercy on me, your servant; graciously deign to receive the sacrifice that I humbly offer through the grace of your compassion; and, through blessed Mary ever-virgin and all your saints, lovingly, favorably, and mercifully forgive the sins that I have contracted through my failing vices. Grant me a place for repentance and rivers of tears, so that I may deserve to receive forgiveness of offenses. Through [Christ our Lord].
