**Communion.** O God, who are the Savior of all the living, who do not desire the death of sinners nor rejoice in the destruction of those who die, I humbly beseech you to grant me forgiveness of my sins, so that I may mourn what I have committed and afterward not commit what must be mourned; [Col. 0901C] and when my final day and the end of my life arrive, may an angel of holiness receive me cleansed from every sin. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Mass for a Living Friend

**Prayer.** O God, who justify the ungodly and do not desire the death of sinners, we humbly beseech your majesty that, in your mercy, you may graciously protect your servant N., who trusts in your mercy, with heavenly assistance, and preserve him through continual protection, so that he may always serve you and not be separated from you by any temptations. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** Through the power of this mystery, O Lord, we ask, cleanse us from our own offenses and absolve your servant N. from every sin. Through [Christ our Lord].

[Col. 0901D] **Communion.** May the sacraments we have received purify us, O Lord, we ask; grant that your servant N. may be free from every guilt, and may he who is bound by the guilt of conscience glory in the fullness of heavenly healing. Through [Christ our Lord].

## For Living Friends

**Prayer.** Almighty and everlasting God, have mercy on your servants and direct them according to your clemency in the way of eternal salvation, so that by your gift they may desire what pleases you and accomplish it with all their strength. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** May this offering, which we humbly present to your majesty, we ask, O Lord, advance the salvation of your servants, so that through your providence their life may everywhere be directed amid adversity and prosperity. Through [Christ our Lord].

[Col. 0902A] **Communion.** As we receive the sacraments of perpetual salvation, we implore your clemency, O Lord, that through them you may protect your servant N. from every adversity. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Another Prayer for Friends

**Prayer.** O God, who through the grace of the Holy Spirit have poured the gifts of charity into the hearts of your people, grant your servants N., for whom we implore your clemency, health of mind and body, so that they may love you with all their strength and accomplish with complete devotion whatever pleases you. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** Have mercy, we ask, O Lord, on your servants for whom we offer this sacrifice of praise to your majesty, so that through these sacraments they may obtain the grace of heavenly blessing and acquire the glory of eternal [Col. 0902B] blessedness. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** As we taste the divine mysteries, we ask, O Lord, that these saving sacraments may bring prosperity and peace to those for whose love we have offered them to your majesty. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Another.** O God, who deign to receive the vows of those who plead with you through works of charity, grant your servants to advance in your love, so that they may serve you with a secure mind and always deserve to stand in your peace. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Mass for Sins

**Prayer.** Divine exultation, paternal compassion, immeasurable majesty: I humbly and tremblingly beseech you for your servant N., that you grant her a pure mind, perfect charity, sincerity in her deeds, purity in her heart, [Col. 0902C] virtue in her work, and discipline in her conduct, so that she may recognize that what we, although unworthy, faithfully and devoutly offer before the sight of your majesty on her behalf has been obtained through the grace of your compassion. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** Forgive me, your servant, as I plead, O Lord; grant me the favor of asking, so that I may safely offer to you, the Lord our God, a victim for your servant N., that she may obtain forgiveness for her offenses and, having likewise received holy gifts through you, may reach, with your assistance, the salvation of eternal grace. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** Confirm this, O God, which you have wrought in us, and preserve the grace that you have deigned to confer [Col. 0902D] upon us through the intercession of your saints; deign to confer the gift of your mercy upon your female servant. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Another Mass for Sins

**Prayer.** God of mercy, God of forgiveness, forgive, I ask, and have mercy on your servant N., so that no inner stain may remain in him from the offenses that he has confessed to you with his mouth, but that through the sorrow of repentance he may deserve to reach your promises. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Reading from the Prophet Ezekiel.** “Turn back to me,” etc., up to “says the Lord.”

**Continuation of the Holy Gospel according to Matthew.** “At that time, while Jesus was reclining at table,” etc., up to “sinners to repentance.”

**Secret.** Regard, we ask, O Lord, the prayers of your servant, who confesses to you in mind and heart that he has gravely sinned; and grant that through the offering of your Body and Blood, which we offer to you for him, we may be able to obtain forgiveness. [Col. 0903A] Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** Refreshed by your gifts, we humbly entreat you, O Lord, that, as our brother has turned back to the way of righteousness, you may stir up in him a fountain of tears, and guard him with paternal compassion so that he may not commit again what must be mourned. Through [Christ our Lord].

## For Those Confessing Their Sins

**Prayer.** Hear, we ask, O Lord, the prayers of those who plead with you, etc., as in the printed litanies.

**Secret.** We offer you sacrifices of reconciliation, O Lord, so that in your mercy you may absolve our offenses and grant us peace. Through [Christ our Lord].

[Col. 0903B] **Communion.** Grant us, eternal Savior, that, receiving forgiveness of sins through this gift, we may always glory in your benefits.

## Mass for Sins

**Prayer.** O God, who do not desire the souls of sinners to perish, but their faults [to perish], restrain the punishment we deserve and pour upon us the mercy we implore, so that from sorrow we may deserve to attain the joy of your mercy. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** May the offering of the present sacrifice assist us, O Lord, we ask, so that it may powerfully absolve us from every error and rescue us from the assault of complete destruction. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** Hear the groaning of your people, O Lord, so that the offense of those who sin may not have greater power with you than your mercy, granted to those who plead with tears. [Col. 0903C]

## For the Remission of Sins

**Prayer and secret**, as in the printed editions.

**Communion.** Protect with divine assistance those whom you refresh with a heavenly gift, O Lord, so that, enjoying your mysteries, we may be subjected to no adversity; and strip us, almighty God, of all our iniquities, and grant that we may rejoice in your peace. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Mass for Evil Thoughts

**Prayer and secret**, as in the printed editions.

**Communion.** Through this sacrifice, we ask, O Lord, which we have offered to your majesty, cleanse the heart of your servant from every temptation. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Mass for Asking for Tears

[Col. 0903D]

**Prayer and post-communion**, as in the printed editions.

**Secret.** May these sacrifices, we ask, O Lord, which we have offered to your compassion, advance us toward forgiveness of our sins and always grant us the consolation of your mercy. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Mass for Tribulation

**Prayer.** Mercifully show us your ineffable mercy, O Lord, we ask, so that you may at once strip us of sins and rescue us from the punishments that we deserve for them. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** May the offering of the present gift purify us, O Lord, we ask, and make us worthy to share in holy things. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** Grant, O Lord, we ask, that, cleansed from earthly desires, we may strive toward the fullness of the heavenly sacrament whose holy gifts we have tasted. [Col. 0904A] Through [Christ our Lord].

## Another Mass

**Prayer.** O God, who do not despise the groaning of the contrite or reject the feelings of those who mourn, be present to our prayers, which we offer to your compassion for our tribulation, imploring you to receive us mercifully and, solely out of regard for your goodness, to grant that whatever the adversities of the devil and of human beings plot against us you may reduce to nothing and crush by the counsel of your mercy, so that, wounded by no adversities but freed from every tribulation and distress, we may give thanks to you in your Church. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** O God, who heal those troubled in heart, graciously regard this sacrifice and, through it, by which you willed the sins of the whole world to be released, mercifully accept it for our tribulation; release all our dangers, regard our tribulation, drive away our miseries, remove distress and oppression, so that, stripped of all the evils we suffer, we may always delight to exult in your benefits. [Col. 0904B] Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** Forgive our sins, we ask, O Lord, and grant us your mercy; entreated by the address of our mouth, regard our humility, release our bonds, erase our offenses, look upon our tribulation, repel adversity, and continually and mercifully hear the fulfillment of our petition. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Mass in Time of War

**Prayer.** Almighty and merciful God, we ask you to make us peaceful amid the whirlwinds of wars, because you will grant us good things if you give peace to mind and body. [Col. 0904C] Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** “The sacrifice,” etc., as in the printed editions.

**Communion.** Strengthened by receiving the most holy Body and Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, we humbly ask you, almighty God, that through this singular remedy you may cleanse us from every sinful thought and fortify us against the assault of every danger. Through the same [Christ our Lord].

## Mass for Those Who Persecute

**Prayer.** Crush, we ask, O Lord God, the pride of our enemies, and through the intercession of blessed Mary the Virgin and all the saints, overthrow them by the power of your right hand. [Col. 0904D] Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** Through the power of this mystery, O Lord, we ask, and through the intercession of blessed Mary the Virgin and all the saints, may we be cleansed from our hidden faults and freed from the snares of our enemies. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** May the sanctification of your holy mystery, we ask, O Lord, bring us life; and through the merits of blessed Mary the Virgin and all the saints, may it grant us both purification and protection. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Mass in Time of Pestilence

**Prayer and secret**, as in the printed editions.

**Communion.** As we receive your holy sacraments, we ask, O Lord, mercifully defend us from every iniquity and danger. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Mass for Travelers

**Prayer and secret**, as in the printed editions.

[Col. 0905A] **Communion.** O God of infinite mercy and immeasurable majesty, whom neither distances of place nor intervals of time separate from those whom you protect, be present to your servants who everywhere trust in you, and deign to be their guide and companion throughout every road they are to travel. May no adversity harm them, no difficulty obstruct them; may everything be healthful and everything prosperous for them, so that under the support of your right hand they may quickly attain whatever they rightly desire. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Mass on the Day of Burial of a Deceased Person: the Third, Seventh, or Thirtieth Day

**Prayer**, as in the printed editions for the third day.

[Col. 0905B] **Secret.** Be present to our supplications, O Lord, and graciously and kindly receive this offering, which we offer to you for the soul of your servant N. on the third day of his burial (or the seventh or thirtieth). Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** Almighty and everlasting God, deign to place the souls of your male and female servants whose day of burial we celebrate in the bosoms of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, so that, when the day of knowledge of you arrives, you may command them to be raised among your saints and elect. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Mass for One Deceased Priest

**Prayer.** Protect us, we ask, O Lord, through the intercession of your confessor, blessed Floridus, and join the soul of your servant, the priest, to the company of your saints. [Col. 0905C] Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** Receive, we ask, O Lord, the sacrifices of reconciliation and praise that we bring to you to be consecrated in honor of your confessor, blessed Floridus, and that we humbly immolate to you for the rest of your servant, the priest N. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** May our prayers ascend to you, O Lord; may eternal joys receive the soul of your servant, the priest N.; and may you command him whom you made a participant in adoption to be a sharer in your inheritance. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Mass for Deceased Deacons

**Prayer.** Be present to our supplications, O Lord, and may the souls of your servants, the deacons and all the clerics, obtain the abundance and forgiveness of your reconciliation, and may you grant them a dwelling in perpetual light. [Col. 0905D] Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** Hear us, holy Father, almighty and eternal God, so that, appeased by these sacred gifts, everlasting redemption may possess the souls of all your servants, the deacons. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** Almighty and eternal God, mercifully receive our prayers for the souls of your servants, the deacons, so that you may cause them to be gathered among your saints in the region of light. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Mass for Subdeacons

**Prayer.** O God, whose proper work is always to show mercy and forgive, etc., as in the printed editions.

**Secret.** We offer you sacrifices of reconciliation and praise, O Lord, so that through the abundance of perpetual mercy you may perfect the souls of your servants, the subdeacons, in the region of eternal light, that they may rejoice. [Col. 0906A] Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** Through these sacrifices, we ask, almighty God, may the souls and spirits of your servants, the subdeacons, be cleansed, so that they may deserve to reach forgiveness and eternal refreshment. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Mass for One Deceased Person

**Prayer.** Almighty and everlasting God, to whom no one pleads without hope of mercy, be favorable to the soul of your servant, so that you may cause him who departed this life in confession of your name to be gathered among your saints. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** Be favorable, we ask, O Lord, to the soul of your servant N., for whom we offer you sacrifices of reconciliation; and because he remained in the Catholic faith in this light, may he be granted in the future life the heavenly recompense of joy. [Col. 0906B] Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** Grant, we ask, almighty God, that you may lead the soul of your servant N., received by the angels of light, into the prepared dwellings of the blessed. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Mass for Several Deceased Persons

**Prayer.** O God, whose mercy is without number, mercifully receive our prayers for the souls of your servants, and grant them the joy of light and fellowship in the region of your saints. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** For the rest of the souls of your servants N., O Lord, receive the gracious sacrifice which you offered to God the Father for us, so that, since you came down from heaven for the sake of humankind, they may deserve, when you return, to be numbered in the company of the saints—you who live and reign with God the Father and [Col. 0906C] the Holy Spirit forever and ever.

**Communion.** May this communion, O Lord, cleanse us from guilt and grant the souls of your servants a share in heavenly joy, so that, separated among the right hand before the throne of your glory, they may have nothing in common with those on the left. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Mass for Many Deceased Persons

**Prayer.** O God, whose proper work is always to show mercy and hear the prayers of those who plead with you, be favorable to the souls of your servants N., so that, freed by your mercy from the bonds of sins, they may deserve to reach the rest of eternal blessedness. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.** Most merciful Father, receive for the commemoration of your servants N. a sacrifice of reconciliation [Col. 0906D] and praise, so that, by your mercy, the offering of the present sacrifice may reach the refreshment of their souls. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** Absolve, we ask, O Lord, the souls of your servants N. from every bond of offenses, so that, raised among your saints in the glory of the resurrection, they may breathe freely. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Mass for One Deceased Woman

**Prayer.** Almighty and everlasting God, creator and redeemer of souls, who have bestowed the reward of eternal blessedness upon the souls of your saints, grant, we ask, that the soul of your servant N., whom you commanded to depart from this world and whose commemoration we celebrate, may deserve to enjoy the company of the saints. Through [Christ our Lord].

[Col. 0907A] **Secret.** For the soul of your servant N., O Lord, mercifully receive the sacrifice offered, we ask, so that through this singular rite, released from the bonds of dreadful death, she may deserve eternal life. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Communion.** Incline your ear, we ask, to our supplications, and grant the soul of your female servant an abode of perpetual light. Through [Christ our Lord].

## Mass for Deceased Women

**Prayer and secret**, as in the printed editions for one deceased woman.

**Communion.** May the souls of your female servants, we ask, O Lord, find a share in eternal light, whose sacrament of perpetual grace they have obtained through Jesus Christ our Lord, risen from the dead, who lives and reigns with you, God, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, forever and ever.

## Mass in Honor of the Holy Trinity

[Col. 0907B]

Blessed be the Holy Trinity and undivided Unity; we shall confess it, because it has shown us its mercy.

**Psalm.** “Let us bless the Father and the Son.”  
**Response.** “Blessed are you, O God, who behold the depths and sit above the cherubim.”  
**Verse.** “Bless God, heavens of heavens, because he has shown us his mercy.” Alleluia.  
**Verse.** “Blessed are you, Lord God of our fathers, and worthy of praise forever.”

**Offertory and communion**, as in the printed editions.

## In Honor of the Holy Cross

But we ought to glory in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, in which is our salvation, life, and resurrection; through him we have been saved and liberated.

[Col. 0907C]

**Psalm.** “May God have mercy.”  
**Response.** “Christ became obedient for us unto death, even death on a cross.”  
**Verse.** “Therefore God also exalted him and gave him the name that is above every name.” Alleluia.  
**Verse.** “But we ought to glory in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ.”

**Offertory and communion**, as in the printed editions.

## In Honor of Saint Mary

“They shall entreat your countenance,” etc.  
**Psalm.** “My heart has uttered.”  
**Response.** “Grace has been poured forth,” etc.  
**Verse.** “Because of truth,” etc. Alleluia.  
**Verse.** “In your appearance and beauty,” etc.

**Offertory.** Virgins shall be brought to the King after her; her companions shall be brought to you.

[Col. 0907D] **Communion.** Most worthy Queen of the world, perpetual Virgin Mary, intercede for our peace and salvation, you who gave birth to Christ the Lord without human seed.

## In Honor of Saint Michael

Bless the Lord, all his angels, mighty in strength, who do his word, obeying the voice of his commands.

**Psalm.** “Bless the Lord, O my soul.”  
**Response.** “Bless the Lord, all his angels, mighty in strength, who do his word.”

**Verse.** “Bless the Lord, O my soul, and all that is within me, his holy name.” Alleluia.

**Verse.** “The sea was shaken and the earth trembled where the archangel Michael descended from heaven.”

[Col. 0908A] **Offertory.** An angel stood at the altar of the temple, holding a golden censer in his hand; and much incense was given to him, and the smoke of the perfumes rose before God. Alleluia.

Communion. Bless the Lord, all angels of the Lord; sing a hymn and exalt him above all forever.

## IN HONOR OF THE HOLY SPIRIT

The love of God has been poured into our hearts. Alleluia, through his Spirit dwelling within us. Alleluia, alleluia.

Psalm: “O Lord God.”  
Response: Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord, the people whom the Lord chose as his inheritance.

Verse: By the word of the Lord the heavens were established, and by the Spirit of his mouth all their host. Alleluia.

Verse: Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful and kindle in them the fire of your love.

Offertory. Send forth your Spirit, and they will be created, and you will renew the face of the earth; may the glory of the Lord endure forever. Alleluia.

Communion. The Holy Spirit will teach you, alleluia, whatever I have said to you. Alleluia.

### Sequence

May the grace of the Holy Spirit be with us, making our hearts his dwelling places, after all spiritual vices have been driven out from them.

Gracious Spirit, enlightener of all, cleanse the dreadful darkness of our mind.

Holy lover of ever-perceptive thoughts, mercifully pour your anointing into our senses.

Spirit, purifier of every defilement, purify the eyes of our inner person, so that the supreme Father may be seen by us with the pure heart whose eyes alone can behold him.

You inspired the prophets, so that they might proclaim beforehand the illustrious praises of Christ.

You strengthened the apostles, so that they might carry Christ’s trophy throughout the whole world.

When God made the fabric of heavens, earth, and seas through his Word, you, Spirit, spread your name over the waters when he was about to make them.

You make the waters fruitful for the giving of life to souls.

By breathing upon them, you grant that human beings may be spiritual.

You united the world, divided by languages and customs, calling idolaters back to the worship of God, most excellent teacher.

Therefore, hear us who implore you, gracious Holy Spirit, without whom all prayers are believed to be empty and unworthy of God’s ears.

You, Holy Spirit of all ages, who taught [them] by inspiration to embrace the Name, yourself today—by granting Christ’s apostles an extraordinary gift unheard-of throughout all ages—made this day glorious.

## MASS FOR SINS

[Col. 0909A]

“You have mercy on all,” etc., as in the printed editions, through the Alleluia.

Gradual. Alleluia.  
Verse: O Lord, hear my prayer, and let my cry come to you.

Offertory. Have mercy on me, O God, according to your great mercy. Blot out my iniquity, O God.

Communion. Incline your ear; hasten to rescue us.

## ON THE FEAST OF MANY MARTYRS

Let the peoples recount the wisdom of the saints, and let the Church proclaim their praises; but their names shall live forever and ever.

Psalm: “Great.”  
Response: The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and the torment of evil shall not touch them. In the eyes of the foolish they seemed to die, but they are in peace, alleluia. Your saints, O Lord, shall flourish like the lily; they shall be like the fragrance of balsam before you.

Offertory. The saints shall rejoice in glory; they shall exult in their dwellings; the praises of God shall be in their throats.

Communion. I chose you from the world so that you might go and bear fruit.

## ON THE FEAST OF CONFESSORS

Your priests, O Lord, shall be clothed, etc., as in the printed editions.

Psalm: “Remember.”  
Response: Let his priests put on salvation, and let his holy ones rejoice with gladness. There I shall bring forth a horn for David; I have prepared a lamp for my Christ. [Col. 0909C] Alleluia. Your saints, O Lord.

Offertory. The saints shall rejoice in glory.

Communion. The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and the torment of evil shall not touch them. In the eyes of the foolish they seemed to die, but they are in peace.

## OFFICE OF VIRGINS

Your countenance.  
Psalm: “My heart has uttered.”  
Response: Because of truth and meekness, etc. Hear, O daughter, and see, etc. In your beauty, etc.

Offertory. Grace has been poured upon your lips; therefore God has blessed you forever and unto ages of ages.

Communion. You have loved righteousness and hated iniquity; therefore God, your God, has anointed you.

[Col. 0910A] The continuation of the holy Gospel according to Mark. At that time Jesus said to his disciples: “Watch, keep vigil, and pray,” etc., through the words “I say to all: Watch,” inclusively.

## OFFICE OF HOLY MARY

Hail, holy mother, who, having given birth, brought forth the King who rules heaven and earth unto ages of ages.

Psalm: Virgin Mother of God, whom the whole world cannot contain, he, having become man, enclosed himself within your womb.  
Response: Blessed and venerable are you, Virgin Mary, who, without violation of your purity, were found to be the Mother of the Savior. Virgin, Mother of God, whom the whole world cannot contain, he, having become man, enclosed himself within your womb. Alleluia.  
Verse: After giving birth, you remained an inviolate Virgin; Mother of God, intercede for us.

### Sequence

On this bright day the festive company offers praises, celebrating Mary with honey-sweet harmony: Lady of the world, the one most chaste of virgins, Queen.

Cause of salvation, gate of life, filled with the grace of heaven.

For in former times the angelic messenger spoke such words to her: “Hail, Mary, full of the grace of God forever.”

Among the devout companies of women, you are ever blessed: Virgin and untouched pregnant Mother, with glorious offspring. In reply Mary speaks these words: “How will your announcements come to pass in me? Certainly I know no union with a man, and since I was born I have remained incorrupt.”

The divine messenger, sent for this purpose, replies: “Mary, you shall become full through the breath of the Holy Spirit.”

Offering new joys, he fills the holy woman with the beginnings of her child.

Within the enclosure of your womb reigns he who governs the heavens and all things, he who grants peaceful times.

The continuation of the holy Gospel according to Luke. At that time Elizabeth was filled, etc., through the words “in my Savior,” inclusively.

Offertory. Hail, Mary.

Communion. Blessed is the womb of Mary, which bore the Son of the eternal Father.

## EXCERPTS FROM THE SECOND CODEX OF AVELLANA

[Col. 0909]

## MASS IN TIME OF TRIBULATION

[Col. 0909D]

“I am the salvation of the people,” says the Lord. “From whatever tribulation they cry out to me, I will hear them, and I will be their Lord forever.”  
Psalm: “Attend, O people.”  
Glory.

Prayer. Almighty and eternal God, consolation of the sorrowful and strength of those who labor, may the prayers of those who cry out to you from whatever tribulation reach you, so that all may rejoice that your mercy has been present to them in their necessities. Through [Christ our Lord].

[Col. 0910D] Reading from the Book of Wisdom. Have mercy on us, O God, etc., through the words “that they may recount your wonders, O Lord our God.”

Gradual. Be gracious, O Lord, to our sins, lest the nations ever say: “Where is their God?”

Verse: Help us, O God our Savior, and for the honor of your name, O Lord, deliver us. Alleluia.  
Psalm: O Lord, hear my prayer, and let my cry come to you.

The continuation of the holy Gospel according to Luke. At that time Jesus said to his disciples: “It is necessary always to pray,” etc., through the words “their vindication,” inclusively.

Offertory. If I walk in the midst of tribulation, you will revive me, O Lord; against the anger of my enemies you will stretch out your hand, and your right hand has saved me.

Secret. We offer you these sacrifices, O Lord, for our salvation and for all the afflictions pressing upon us, that you may deign to free and enlighten our bodies and souls by the grace of the Holy Spirit. Through [Christ our Lord].

Communion. Amen, I say to you: Whatever you ask for when you pray, believe that you will receive it, and it shall be done for you.

At Communion. Grant us, we beseech you, O Lord, joy after tribulation, so that we who have long been afflicted for our sins may, through the intercession of all your saints, breathe again in your mercy. Through [Christ our Lord].

## ANOTHER MASS IN TIME OF TRIBULATION

I am the salvation of the people, says the Lord.

Prayer. God, Father of orphans and judge of widows, mercifully regard the tears of your Church, and may your majesty mercifully rescue her, whom no earthly power defends. Through [Christ our Lord].

Reading from the prophet Jeremiah. If they contended against our iniquities, etc., through the words “us, O Lord our God.”

Gradual. Be gracious, O Lord; help us, O God. Alleluia. O Lord, hear us.

[Col. 0911C] Gospel. “It is necessary.”

Offertory. “If I walk.”

Secret. May this sacrifice, O Lord, which we offer for the wars of the unbelievers, be acceptable to you, so that with your help we may obtain through it what we devoutly ask. Through [Christ our Lord].

Communion. Amen, I say to you.

At Communion. We beseech you, O Lord God, bring low the rights of the tyrants who oppose you, so that they may learn that you are the protector of your Church, redeemed by your precious blood. Through [Christ our Lord].

## HERE BEGINS THE ORDER FOR MAKING A CATECHUMEN

First ask his name—that is, by what name he wishes to be called—and, once the saint’s name has been stated:

Why have you come to the Church?  
Response: To become a Christian.

What do you ask for?  
Response: Faith.

What does faith prepare for you?  
Response: Eternal life.

Do you renounce Satan?  
Response: I renounce him and all his pomp; I renounce him and all his works.

Do you believe in God the Father almighty, Creator of heaven and earth?  
Response: I believe.

Do you also believe in Jesus Christ, his only Son, our Lord, born and having suffered?  
Response: I believe.

Do you also believe in the Holy Spirit, the holy catholic Church, the communion of saints, the forgiveness of sins, the resurrection of the flesh, and eternal life?  
Response: I believe.

Then the priest shall blow three times upon his face, saying: Come out from him, unclean spirit; give honor to Jesus Christ, his Son, and to the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete.

Then he signs him on the forehead, saying: I place upon your forehead the sign of the holy + cross of our Lord Jesus Christ.

Then he shall sign him also on the breast, saying: I place upon your breast the sign of the salvation of our Lord + Jesus Christ. Receive the sign + of Christ’s cross both in your heart and on your forehead. Accept the faith of the heavenly commandments. Let your conduct be such that you may be able to be a temple of God. Rejoice that, having entered the Church of God, you have escaped the snares of death; gladly recognize idols, reject images, and worship God the almighty Father and Jesus Christ his Son, who with him and the Holy Spirit lives and reigns as God forever and ever.

[Col. 0912B] Amen.

Another prayer. Almighty and eternal God, etc.

Another: Hear our prayers, etc. Another: God, who [created] the human race, etc.

Another prayer: Exorcism of salt, etc., as in the Roman Ritual.

Bless +, almighty God, this creature of salt with a heavenly blessing, in the name of the Lord + Jesus Christ and in the power of the Holy Spirit, for driving away the enemy. May you, O Lord, by sanctifying + sanctify it; by blessing, bless + it. May it become a perfect medicine for all who receive it, remaining in the inward parts of those who take it, in the name of the Lord + Jesus Christ, who is to come in the Holy Spirit to judge.

[Col. 0912C] Then let him take some of that salt, and let it be placed in the infant’s mouth: Receive the salt of wisdom; may it be propitious to you unto eternal life. Amen.

The Lord be with you.  
Response: And with [your spirit].

Prayer. God of our fathers, etc., as in the published Ritual.

Then let him take him by the right hand and lead him into the church, saying: Enter into the temple of the Lord, so that you may have a share with Christ.

## HERE BEGINS THE ORDER FOR MAKING THE CREED

God of Abraham, etc., as in the published Ritual.

Adjuration against the demon: Therefore, accursed devil, etc., as above in the Rituals, with this one difference: in the manuscript the conclusion is not included.

Adjuration over a woman. God of heaven, etc., as in the printed editions, but without the conclusion.

Adjuration over a man. God, immortal protection, etc., as in the printed editions.

Another common adjuration. Therefore, hear, accursed one, etc., as in the printed editions.

Exorcism. I exorcize you, unclean spirit, in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, so that you may come out and withdraw from this servant of God. May he himself command you, accursed and condemned one, who walked upon the sea and extended his right hand to Peter as he was sinking. Therefore I exorcize you, unclean spirit, by the + Father, and the S+on, and the Spirit + holy, so that you may come out and withdraw from this servant of God. For he himself commands you, accursed and condemned one, who opened the eyes of the man born blind and raised Lazarus, dead four days, from the tomb. Therefore let it be, etc.

The Lord be with you. And with your spirit.

Prayer. Eternal [God], etc., as in the printed editions.

Reading. Thus says the Lord: “All you who thirst,” etc., through the words “in the fatness of your soul.”

Gradual. Come, children, hear me; I will teach you the fear of the Lord.  
Verse: Draw near to him and be enlightened, and your faces shall not be put to shame.

The continuation of the holy Gospel according to Matthew. At that time children were brought to Jesus, etc., through the words “he departed from there.”

Then let this be said: Our Father, and “I believe in God.” And let another man lift him up—not the one who is holding him—saying likewise: Our Father, and “I believe in God.”

## HERE BEGINS THE ORDER OF BAPTISM FOR ONE IN NEED

[Col. 0913B]

I implore your healing, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, who have granted that your servant, weighed down by the weariness of illness, may be raised from human weakness; deign to refresh all his senses by your visitations, so that by the grace of your baptism he may receive health with joy. Therefore drive away from him every protection of contrary sickness, so that he may gladly hasten to your grace. Raise up the one whom you have deigned to redeem, so that in him baptism may be the palm of victory, not death, and so that he may always bear gloriously the sign of the holy + cross that he has received.

Conjuration. May it not be hidden from you, etc., as in the printed editions, except for the conclusion “in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ.”

The beginning of the holy Gospel according to Matthew. The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the Son of Abraham. Abraham begot Isaac; Isaac begot Jacob; Jacob begot Judah and his brothers. From that generation was born the Virgin Mary, Mother of our Lord Jesus Christ.

The beginning of the holy Gospel according to Luke. There was in the days of Herod, etc., through the words “without reproach.”

The continuation of the holy Gospel according to Mark. The beginning of the Gospel of Jesus Christ, etc., through the words “the salvation of God for all flesh.”

The beginning of the holy Gospel according to John. In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and God was the Word. He was in the beginning with God. All things were made through him, and without him nothing was made, etc. And thus let the whole passage be said.

## BLESSING OF WATER FOR BAPTIZING A SICK PERSON

First let the litanies be said. Then the following prayer follows.

Hear us, almighty God, and mingle power with the substance of this water, so that through being washed by it we may deserve to receive both health and eternal life. Through [Christ our Lord].

### Exorcism of the Water

I exorcize you, creature of water, in the name of + God the almighty Father, and in the name of Jesus Christ his Son +, and in the power of the Holy Spirit +, so that every power of the adversary, every assault of Satan, and every phantom may be uprooted, destroyed, and driven away from this creature of water; so that it may be a spring of water leaping up into eternal life, and so that whoever is baptized from it may become a temple of the living God, and the Holy Spirit may dwell in him for the forgiveness of all sins.

In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I exorcize you, creature of water, by the + living God, by the + holy God, by the God of all creation, who in the beginning separated you from the dry land and commanded you to flow forth in four rivers and irrigate the whole earth; who walked upon the sea and was baptized by John in the Jordan; who brought you forth together with his blood and commanded his disciples to baptize in you, saying: “Go, baptize all nations in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.”

Therefore I adjure you, water, by the + living God, that you may become holy water +, blessed water +, water that washes away filth and cleanses sins; so that, when the infant of Christ descends into you, you may become a spring of water leaping up into eternal life. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, unto eternal life. Amen.

[A rubric appears in the margin of the codex:] Then let the priest place a lighted candle into the font, saying: May the power of the Holy Spirit descend into this fullness of the font. After this let him sprinkle the font with chrism, saying: May the infusion of chrism, salvation, and water be in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ unto eternal life. Amen.

Then let him blow three times upon the water and place chrism in the form of a cross +. Then let him touch both the nostrils and the ears with spittle, saying into his left ear: Ephphetha, which means “Be opened”; but you, devil, be driven away, for the judgment of God is drawing near.

Afterward let him touch his breast and the space between his shoulders with exorcized oil, making a cross with his thumb; and, having called him by name, let him say:

Do you renounce Satan?  
Response: I renounce him.

And all his works?  
Response: I renounce them.

And all his pomps?  
Response: I renounce them.

[The margin adds: Flee, unclean spirit; give honor to the living and true God. Come out, unclean spirit; give place to the Holy Spirit.]

Let him ask: Do you believe in God the Father? etc., as above, through the final response, “I believe.”

And let him ask him three times in this way: Do you wish to be baptized?  
Response: I do. [Three times.]

And I baptize you in the name of the Father—and immerse him—and of the Son—and immerse him—and of the Holy Spirit—and immerse him.

After the infant has been baptized, let the presbyter make the sign of the cross with chrism with his thumb upon the crown of his head, invoking the holy Trinity, saying: In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. And let him say this prayer:

Almighty God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who regenerated you from water and the Holy Spirit and gave you forgiveness of all sins, may he himself anoint you with the chrism of salvation in Christ Jesus our Lord. Peace be with you unto eternal life. Amen.

## HERE BEGINS THE ORDER FOR GIVING PENANCE

First the priest says: Lord God almighty, be gracious to me, a sinner, so that I may worthily give you thanks, because you have deigned to call me, unworthy and sinful, to your ministry and have appointed me, insignificant and humble, to intercede with our Lord Jesus Christ for sinners. Therefore, Lord ruler, who wills all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth, who does not will the death of sinners but that they should be converted and live, receive my prayer, which I make before your presence for me, a sinner, and for others who come to me for penance, Savior.

He asks: Do you believe in God the almighty Father, and in the Son, and in the Holy Spirit?  
Response: I believe.

Do you believe that in this flesh in which you now are you must rise on the day of judgment and receive what you have done, whether good or evil?  
Response: I believe.

Do you wish to forgive those who have sinned against you, as the Lord says: “If you do not forgive people their sins, neither will your Father forgive you your sins”?  
Response: I do.

Let him say: Into your hands, O Lord, I commend my spirit.

Three times: “We have received the chapter, O God, your mercy, unto your right hand.”  
Psalm: “Great is the Lord.”  
Glory.  
Kyrie, Christ, Kyrie.  
Our Father.  
“And lead us not.”  
Chapter: “Convert us, O God,” briefly.  
“And implore.”  
Save your servants and handmaids, my God.  
“May the enemy accomplish nothing.”  
“And the son of iniquity.”  
Send him, O God, help from the holy place.  
“And from Zion.”  
O Lord, hear my prayer.  
“And let my cry.”  
The Lord be with you.  
“And with [your spirit].”

Prayer. Receive, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, this your servant, who desires to abandon the way of error and hastens toward the way of truth. Grant, I beseech you, O Lord, that just as you have deigned to regenerate him from water and the Holy Spirit through the gift of your grace, so you may mercifully grant that through true and holy confession he may deserve to be joined to your holy Church. Through [Christ our Lord].

Another. Hear our prayers, O Lord, and spare the one who confesses to you his sins, so that the mercy of your forgiveness may absolve him whom the guilt of his conscience accuses. Through [Christ our Lord].

Another. May your mercy, we beseech you, O Lord, go before this your servant, so that all his iniquities may be erased by swift forgiveness. Through [Christ our Lord].

Then the seven psalms with a reading.

Chapter. Convert us, O God our salvation.  
“And turn away.”  
Let your mercy be upon us, O God.  
“As we have hoped.”  
O Lord, hear my prayer.  
“And let my cry.”  
The Lord be with you.

Prayer. I beseech your clemency, O Lord, and the mercy of your majesty, that you may release forgiveness for this your servant confessing his sins and offenses, and deign to forgive the guilt of his former crimes. You brought back upon your shoulders the lost sheep to the folds; you were appeased by the prayers and confession of the publican. Be appeased also by this your servant, O Lord; graciously receive his prayers, forgive him all crimes and sins, and grant him forgiveness in place of punishment, joy in place of sorrow, and life in place of death. May he who has fallen into such great hope of the heavenly summit, trusting in your mercy, reach eternal joys under your protection. Through [Christ our Lord].

Another prayer. Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, who do not will the death of sinners but always seek their life, we humbly beseech you: regard your weeping servant, prostrate before you, and turn his lament into the joy of your mercy. Tear apart the sack of his offenses and clothe him in saving gladness, so that after the long hunger of his pilgrimage he may be satisfied from the holy altars, and, having entered the chamber of the King, may bless the name of your glory in his own court. Through our Lord.

Blessing. May the almighty Lord bless you and keep you. May the Lord show his face to you and have mercy on you. May the Lord turn his countenance toward you and give you peace.

Another blessing. May the Lord God almighty bless you and keep you; through the abundance of the Holy Spirit may he strengthen your heart, sanctify your mind, enlarge your life, adorn your chastity, and form your senses in good works. May he grant prosperity, give peace, bestow health, nourish quiet, foster love, and always defend you by his protection from every diabolical and human snare, so that whatever you ask of him he may mercifully grant; may he remove all the evils you have committed and grant you the grace for which you have always prayed. He who lives.

Then let him admonish him and say: Our Father, and “I believe in God.” Then let the priest make him confess and accuse himself of his sins.

I confess to almighty God, and to blessed Mary, perpetual Virgin, and to blessed Michael the archangel, and to the holy apostles Peter and Paul, and to your blessed martyr Blaise, and to all the saints, and to you, Fathers: through my fault, through my fault, through my fault; because I have sinned in thought, speech, pleasure, consent, words, and deeds; in adultery, perjury, murder, false witness, sacrilege, theft, robbery, lust, and greed; through my fault, through my fault, through my most grievous fault.

I have sinned through the five senses of my body: sight, hearing, taste, smell, and touch; through my fault.

I have sinned in the eight principal vices and in the seven criminal sins, and in all my evil vices by which wretched human beings can sin in any way.

Therefore I beseech blessed Mary the Virgin, and blessed Michael the archangel, and the holy apostles Peter and Paul, and your blessed martyr Blaise, and all the holy men and women of God, and you, Fathers, to pray for me, a sinner, to our Lord Jesus Christ. And for this I wish to receive penance for life and death.

### Absolution

On behalf of almighty God and blessed Mary, perpetual Virgin, and blessed Michael the archangel, and the blessed apostles Peter and Paul, and blessed Blaise the martyr, and all the holy men and women, by virtue of our office we give and confirm to you true judgment and true penance for all your sins, as the holy Fathers command and as justice rightly requires.

From this hour onward remain under the yoke of penance and under the fruit of penance. And if you are overtaken by death and cannot approach a priest or undertake another penance, may the Lord, through this penance, bring your souls to eternal life. Amen.

### When the Priest Imposes Penance

We impose upon you penance for all your sins, which you committed willingly or unwillingly, of which you have confessed, or which have been unknowingly concealed in you, so that you may redeem them through prayer, sacrifice, fasting, and almsgiving, and remain in this penance until the end of your life. And if you are overtaken by death, may the Lord, through this penance, bring your souls to eternal life. Amen.

### Absolution

Through the intercession of blessed Mary ever-Virgin with all the saints, may almighty God have mercy on you and forgive you all your sins, past and present. May he free you from every evil work, save and strengthen you in every good work, and lead you with the angels and archangels to eternal life. Amen.

May almighty, kind, and merciful Lord grant you indulgence, forgiveness, and absolution of all your sins, and the grace of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

Chapter. Save your servants and handmaids, my God, who hope in you.  
Send them, O Lord, help from the holy place.  
“And from Zion.”  
Arise, O Lord, help us.  
“And deliver us.”  
O Lord, hear my prayer.  
“And let my cry.”  
The Lord be with you.  
“And with your spirit.”

Prayer. Almighty and eternal God, who have given your male and female servants, in the confession of the true faith, to acknowledge the glory of the eternal Trinity, etc.

### Absolution

Almighty and eternal God, who has power to forgive the sins of human beings, and holy Peter the apostle, to whom Christ gave the power of binding and loosing, and to his other disciples, saying: “Whose sins you forgive, they are forgiven them forever”—may God himself also absolve you from all your sins, and may you not render an account for these sins in the judgment.

And if you pass from this world, may almighty God, Jesus Christ our Lord, absolve you. He who lives with the Father and the Holy Spirit.

May God look upon you and give you an angel who guards you everywhere, governs your minds, strengthens your works, fulfills your vow, directs your life, forgives the past, corrects the present, and considers future things in you.

May he himself bless you from heaven, who redeemed you on earth with his own blood; he who lives with the Father and the Holy Spirit, etc.

### Blessing

May God the Father bless you, who in the beginning created all things through the Word. Amen.

May the Son of God bless you, who for our salvation descended from the Father’s seat to earth. Amen.

May the Holy Spirit bless you, who in the form of a dove rested upon Christ in the waters of the Jordan. Amen.

May he himself sanctify you in Trinity and unity, whom all people await as the Judge who is to come. Through [Christ our Lord].

May the bless + ing of almighty God, of the Father + and of the Son + and of the Holy Spirit +, guard your body, your soul, and your spirit, here and throughout perpetual ages of ages. Amen.

## HERE BEGINS THE ORDER FOR VISITING THE SICK

First let this be said: Peace to this house. Amen. The Lord be with you.  
Response: And with your spirit.

Look mercifully, O Lord, upon this your servant, and deign to bring aid upon his bed of pain. Place your hand upon his hands and command his illness, lest infirmity despise the hand of me, a sinner, but, at the invocation of your name, let it fear and flee; and, restored to health after his illness has been lifted, may this your servant rise and be presented to your Church, so that he may give thanks to your holy name.

Heal me, O Lord, for all my bones are troubled, and my soul is greatly troubled. And you, O Lord, how long? Turn and rescue my soul. O Lord, not in your anger.

Antiphon. There was a certain royal official whose son was ill at Capernaum. When he heard that Jesus was coming into Galilee, he asked him to heal his son.  
Psalm: Blessed are those whose.  
Antiphon. Lord, my boy is lying paralyzed at home and is suffering terribly. Amen, I say to you, I will come and heal him.  
Psalm: O Lord, not in your anger.

[Col. 0918C] Another antiphon. God does not despise a contrite and humbled heart, but, because of your great mercy, have mercy on me, O God.  
Psalm: Have mercy on me.

Another antiphon. Lord, come down, so that you may heal my son before he dies. Jesus said to him: Go, your son lives.  
Psalm: O Lord, hear my prayer.

Another antiphon. Lord, I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof, but only say the word, and my boy will be healed.  
Psalm: Out of the depths.

Another antiphon. When the sun had set, all who had sick people afflicted with various illnesses brought them to Jesus, and they were healed.  
Psalm: O Lord, hear my prayer.  
Kyrie eleison, Christ eleison, Kyrie eleison.  
Our Father.  
“And lead us not.”

[Col. 0918D] Chapter. Show us, O Lord, your mercy.  
Response: And your salvation.  
Save your servant.  
Response: My God, who hopes in you.  
Be for him, O Lord, a tower of strength.  
Response: From the face of the enemy.  
Send him, O Lord, help from the holy place.  
Response: And from Zion.  
May the enemy accomplish nothing against him.  
Response: And the son of iniquity.  
O Lord, hear my prayer.  
Response: And let my cry.  
The Lord be with you.  
Response: And with your spirit.

Prayer. O God, who granted your servant Hezekiah fifteen additional years of life, so also raise this your servant from his bed of illness to health by your power. Through [Christ our Lord].

Prayer. Look upon your servant, O Lord, laboring under the illness of his body, and refresh his soul, which you created, so that, corrected by chastisements, he may immediately feel himself saved by healing.

Another prayer. O God, who always rule your creation with devoted affection, incline your ear to our supplications, and, being appeased, look upon your servant laboring under adverse bodily health; visit him with your salvation and grant him the medicine of heavenly grace.

Prayer. O God, who have bestowed upon the human race both the remedy of salvation and the gifts of eternal life, preserve in your servant the gifts of your virtues, and grant that he may feel your healing not only in his body but also in his soul. Through [Christ our Lord].

Another prayer. God of the heavenly powers, who by the power of your command drive away every sickness and every infirmity from human bodies, mercifully be present to this servant, so that, his infirmities driven away and his strength restored, he may immediately bless your name with renewed health. Through [Christ our Lord].

Another prayer. Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, who strengthen the weakness of our condition through the gracious infusion of your power, so that our bodies and limbs may be invigorated by the salutary remedies of your mercy, mercifully look upon this your servant, so that, every bodily need of infirmity having been removed, the grace of his former health may be perfectly restored in him.

Prayer. Hear our prayers, O Lord, and spare those who confess to you their sins, so that the indulgence of your forgiveness may absolve him whom the guilt of his conscience accuses. [Col. 0919C] Through [Christ our Lord].

Another prayer. O God, most kindly creator of the human race, who redeemed the human being cast down from eternity by the devil’s envy through the blood of your only Son, revive this your servant, whom you by no means wish to die for you do not abandon the straying but receive him when corrected.

Let the tearful sighs of this your servant, we beseech you, O Lord, move your mercy. Heal his wounds; extend your saving hand to him as he lies there, lest your Church be ravaged in any portion of her body, lest your flock suffer loss, lest the enemy rejoice at the damage to your household, lest a second death possess one reborn through the saving bath.

Therefore we pour out suppliant prayers to you. Spare the one who confesses, so that in this mortal life he may lament his sins in such a way that on the day of the fearful judgment he may escape the sentence of eternal condemnation, and may not know what terrifies in darkness or what crackles in flames. Having returned from the path of error to the way of righteousness, may he never again be wounded by injuries, but may there remain whole and perpetual for him both what your grace has bestowed and what your mercy has restored. Through the same [Christ our Lord].

Here the priest shall ask the sick person whether he wishes to receive anointing. When he answers, “I do,” then let him make his confession.

Let the priest anoint him—his sight and his other senses—saying: God, in your name; God, come to my assistance.  
Psalm: Blessed are the undefiled.

Through this anointing, and through his most loving mercy, may the Lord forgive you whatever you have sinned through sight.

Through this anointing, etc., whatever you have sinned through hearing.

Through this anointing, etc., whatever you have sinned through taste.

Through this anointing, etc., whatever you have sinned through smell.

Through this anointing, etc., whatever you have sinned through touch.

Through this anointing, etc., whatever you have sinned through the ardor of lust.

Through this anointing, etc., whatever you have sinned through the movement of your feet.

Then let the priest wash his hands and say:

Save your servant, my God. Be for him, O Lord, a tower.  
“From the face of the enemy.”  
Send him, O Lord, help from the holy place.  
“And from Zion.”  
May the enemy accomplish nothing.  
“And the son of iniquity.”  
O Lord, hear my prayer.  
“And let my cry.”  
The Lord be with you.  
“And with your spirit.”

Prayer. Almighty and eternal God, who through your blessed apostle James taught us: “Is anyone among you sick? Let him bring in the presbyters of the Church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord; and the prayer of faith will save the sick person, and the Lord will raise him up; and if he is in sins, they will be forgiven him”—we earnestly beseech you that this servant of yours, through the mystery of our anointing, may deserve to obtain forgiveness of his sins through the gift of your holy mercy and to come to eternal life. Through [Christ our Lord].

Another prayer. Merciful God, gracious God, who according to the multitude of your mercies blot out the sins of the penitent and cancel the guilt of past crimes by the pardon of remission, look upon this servant of yours and graciously hear him as he asks, with wholehearted confession, for the remission of all his sins. [Col. 0920C] Renew in him, most loving Father, whatever has been corrupted by earthly frailty or violated by diabolical deceit, and restore him, having received remission, to the unity of the body of your Church. Have mercy, Lord, on his groaning and tears, and admit him to the sacrament of reconciliation, for he has no confidence except in your mercy. Through.

When these prayers have been completed, the priest gives Communion to the sick person, saying: “May the Body of our Lord Jesus Christ cleanse you from every sin and preserve your soul unto eternal life.” Amen.

After giving the Body, he says the short reading: “Save your servant, my God.” “Send him, Lord.” “And from Zion.” “Lord, hear my prayer.” “And let my cry come to you.” “The Lord be with you.” [Col. 0920D] “And with your spirit.”

Prayer. Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, we faithfully beseech you for your servant, our brother, as he receives the most holy Eucharist, the Body and Blood of your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ: may it be salvation both for body and soul. Through the same Lord.

Therefore, as soon as he sees that the sick man is approaching his end, let him give him Communion, even if he has eaten, because Communion will be a help to him.

## Litanies

Christ, hear us. (three times.) Holy Abel, pray for him. Holy Isaac, pray. Holy Enoch, pray. [Col. 0921A] Holy Abraham, pray. Holy Jacob, pray. Holy Elijah, pray. Holy Isaiah, pray. Holy Jeremiah, pray. Holy Ezekiel, pray. Holy Daniel, pray. Holy Hosea, pray. Holy Joel, pray. Holy Obadiah, pray. Holy Habakkuk, pray. Holy Jonah, pray. Holy Nahum, pray. Holy David, pray. Holy Zephaniah, pray. [Col. 0921B] Holy John the Baptist, pray. All holy patriarchs and prophets, pray for him. Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy. Our Father. And lead us not.

Short reading. “I said: Lord, have mercy on me. Heal my soul, because I have sinned against you.”

“Grant him eternal rest, O Lord. And let perpetual light shine upon him.”

“Do not enter into judgment with your servant. For no one will be justified.”

“Lord, deliver his soul. Merciful and compassionate.”

“Do not remember, Lord, the sins of youth and ignorances.”

“Do not destroy him with the ungodly, O God, nor with men of bloodshed.”

[Col. 0921C] “May it please you, O God, to deliver him. Lord, look upon him for help.”

“Lord, hear my prayer. And let my cry come to you.”

“The Lord be with you.”

“And with your spirit.”

Prayer. God, to whom alone it belongs to prepare healing after death, grant, we ask, that the soul of your servant, stripped of earthly contaminations, may be counted among those who share in your redemption. Through.

When the prayer is finished, let him begin: “The Passion of the Lord according to Matthew. At that time Jesus said to his disciples: You know that after two days the Passover will take place,” etc.

## Other litanies

[Col. 0921D] Christ, hear us. (three times.) Holy Mary, pray for him. Holy Stephen, pray. Holy Lawrence, pray. Holy Clement, pray. Holy Sixtus, pray. Holy Cornelius, pray. Holy Cyprian, pray. Holy Sylvester, pray. Holy George, pray. Holy Benedict, pray. Holy Chrysogonus, pray. Holy Cosmas, pray. Holy Damian, pray. Holy Vitalis, pray. [Col. 0922A] Holy Gervasius, pray. Holy Nazarius, pray. Holy Celsus, pray. Holy Vitus, pray. Holy Modestus, pray. Holy Cassian, pray. Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.

## Other litanies

Christ, hear us. (three times.) Holy Hippolytus, pray. Holy Sebastian, pray. Holy Pancras, pray. Holy Domninus, pray. Holy Anthimus, pray. Holy Alexander, pray. [Col. 0922B] Holy Faustinus, pray. Holy Jovita, pray. Holy Donatus, pray. Holy Victor, pray. Holy Nabor, pray. Holy Felix, pray. Holy Fortunatus, pray. Holy Urban, pray. Holy Eleutherius, pray. Holy Anastasius, pray. Holy Gregory, pray. Holy Maurus, pray. Holy Isidore, pray. Holy Saturninus, pray. Holy Florian, pray. [Col. 0922C] All holy martyrs, pray for him. Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy. Our Father. And lead us not. The short reading as above.

Prayer. God, who grant life to the just after death, and for whom the bodies of the faithful do not perish in dying but are changed for the better, we humbly beseech you to command that the soul of your servant be received into eternal rest and into the assembly of the just. Through.

## Other litanies

Christ, hear us. (three times.) Holy Mary, pray for him. Holy Ambrose, pray. Holy Hilary, pray. Holy Severus, pray. Holy Barbatian, pray. [Col. 0922D] Holy Leo, pray. Holy Valerian, pray. Holy Marcellinus, pray. Holy Antoninus, pray. Holy John Chrysostom, pray. Holy Eusebius, pray. Holy Benedict, pray. Holy Syrus, pray. Holy Martin, pray. Holy Augustine, pray. Holy Columban, pray. Holy Geminianus, pray. Holy Marinus, pray. Holy Justin, pray. [Col. 0923A] Holy Tiburtius, pray. Holy Gaudentius, pray. Holy Paul, pray. Holy Macarius, pray. Holy Sabinus, pray. All holy confessors, pray for him. Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy. Our Father. And lead us not.

Prayer. God, creator and redeemer of the faithful, grant your servant remission of all sins, so that he may obtain the pardon he has always desired, and rest. Through.

## Other litanies begin

Christ, hear us. (three times.) God the Father of heaven, have mercy on him. [Col. 0923B] God the Son, redeemer of the world, have mercy. God the Holy Spirit, have mercy. Holy Trinity, one God, have mercy. Holy Mary, pray for him. Holy Michael, pray. Holy Gabriel, pray. Holy Raphael, pray. All holy angels and archangels, pray for him. Holy Peter, pray. Holy Paul, pray. Holy Andrew, pray. Holy John, pray. Holy James, pray. Holy Philip, pray. Holy Bartholomew, pray. [Col. 0923C] Holy Matthew, pray. Holy Thomas, pray. Holy Simon, pray. Holy Thaddeus, pray. Holy Matthias, pray. Holy Barnabas, pray. Holy Cleopas, pray. Holy Timothy, pray. Holy Mark, pray. All holy apostles and evangelists, pray for him. Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy. Our Father. And lead us not.

Prayer. We pray, almighty God, that you may mercifully receive the soul of your servant, who, at your holy command, has left the dwelling of his body; and, while at your command his body returns to the earth, command that the soul which you deigned to regenerate by baptism be joined to the company of the just. Through.

## Other litanies

Christ, hear us. (three times.) Holy Susanna, pray for him. Holy Felicity, pray. Holy Euphemia, pray. Holy Cecilia, pray. Holy Perpetua, pray. Holy Scholastica, pray. Holy Columba, pray. Holy Anne, pray. Holy Elizabeth, pray. [Col. 0924A] Holy Agatha, pray. Holy Agnes, pray. Holy Lucy, pray. Holy Christina, pray. Holy Anastasia, pray. Holy Eugenia, pray. Holy Innocentia, pray. All holy virgins, pray for him. All holy men and women of God, pray for him. Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy. Our Father. And lead us not.

Prayer. God, whose proper work is always to have mercy and to spare, receive our supplication for your servant; and let your merciful goodness release him whom the chain of sins binds. Through.

[Col. 0924B] ## Other litanies

Christ, hear us. (three times.) Holy Mary, intercede for him. Holy Mother of God, intercede. Holy Mother of the Lord, intercede. Holy choir of cherubim, intercede. Holy choir of seraphim, intercede. Holy choir of angels, intercede. Holy choir of patriarchs, intercede. Holy choir of apostles, intercede. Holy choir of martyrs, intercede. Holy choir of doctors, intercede. Holy choir of priests, intercede. Holy choir of levites, intercede. Holy choir of monks, intercede. [Col. 0924C] Holy choir of the innocent, intercede. Holy choir of virgins, intercede. Whole choir of all the saints, intercede. Son of God, have mercy on him. (twice.) Redeemer of the world, have mercy. That you may grant him pardon, we ask you. That you may grant him life, we ask you. That you may grant him the holy paradise, we ask you. That you may grant him a place of refreshment, we ask you. That you may spare him, we ask you. That you may forgive him, we ask you. That you may grant him a place of mercy and pardon, we ask you. That you may not remember his sins, we ask you.

[Col. 0924D] ## Other litanies

Christ, hear us. (three times.) Be favorable, spare him, O Lord. Be favorable, deliver him, O Lord. From your anger, deliver him. From the punishment of hell, deliver him. From eternal condemnation, deliver him. From the power of the devil, deliver him. From the places of punishment, deliver him. From the second death, deliver him. From the fiery Gehenna, deliver him. From dark places, deliver him. From every distress, deliver him. From vengeance for sins, deliver him. From the penalty of torments, deliver him. [Col. 0925A] From every evil, deliver him. Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy. Our Father. And lead us not.

Prayer. Almighty, everlasting God, preserver of souls, who rebuke those whom you love and mercifully discipline those whom you receive for correction, we call upon you, Lord, that you may deign to bestow your healing upon the soul of your servant, who in the body endures weakness of his limbs, the force of labor, and the goads of infirmity. Grant him, we ask, that your grace may be merciful toward him, so that at the hour of his departure from the body his soul may deserve to be presented to you, its own creator, without the stain of sin, by the hands of the saints. Through.

The commendation of the soul begins before it leaves the body.

[Col. 0925B] Come to his aid, you saints of God. May Christ receive you.

Depart, Christian soul, from this world, in the name of God the Father + almighty, who created you; in the name of Jesus Christ +, Son of the living God, who suffered for you; in the name of the Holy Spirit +, who was poured out upon you. May the holy Trinity assist you through the intercession of the holy angels and archangels, thrones and dominions, principalities and powers, and all the virtues, cherubim and seraphim, and of the whole human race—whatever has been received from God—of patriarchs and prophets, apostles and martyrs, confessors and virgins, priests and levites, and all the orders of the Catholic Church, monks and anchorites. Today may your place be made in peace, and your dwelling in the heavenly Jerusalem. [Col. 0925C] Through the Lord.

May the holy archangel Michael receive you, who deserved the leadership of the heavenly army. May the holy angels of God meet you and lead you into the holy city Jerusalem. May blessed Peter the apostle receive you, to whom the keys of the kingdom of heaven were given by God. May Saint Paul assist you, who was worthy to be the chosen vessel of God. May Saint John, God’s chosen apostle, intercede for you, to whom the heavenly secrets were revealed. May all the holy and chosen apostles of God pray for you, to whom the Lord gave the power of binding and loosing. Go forth in the name + of the Father, and + of the Son, and + of the Holy Spirit, who may enlighten you unto eternal life and raise you in the first resurrection on the last day. [Col. 0925D] Holy Lord, almighty Father, receive the soul of your servant in peace and forgive all his sins, Savior of the world. You who live and reign, God, in the unity of the Holy Spirit. Through.

Receive, O Lord, the soul of your servant for good.

Deliver, O Lord, the soul of your servant from all the dangers of hell, from the snares of punishments, and from all evil tribulations.

Deliver, O Lord, the soul of your servant, as you delivered Noah in the flood.

Deliver, O Lord, the soul of your servant, as you delivered Elijah and Enoch from the common death of the world.

Deliver, O Lord, the soul of your servant, as you delivered Abraham through faith and belief.

Deliver, O Lord, the soul of your servant, as you delivered Lot from Sodom and the flame of fire.

[Col. 0926A] Deliver, O Lord, the soul of your servant, as you delivered David from the hand of Saul the king and from Goliath, and from all his bonds.

Deliver, O Lord, the soul of your servant, as you delivered the three boys from the furnace of burning fire and from the hands of the wicked king.

Deliver, O Lord, the soul of your servant, as you delivered Susanna from a false accusation.

Deliver, O Lord, the soul of your servant, as you delivered the human race through the Passion of our Lord Jesus Christ.

Deliver, O Lord, the soul of your servant, as you delivered Peter and Paul from prisons.

Deliver, O Lord, the soul of your servant, as you delivered Thecla from the midst of the spectacle.

[Col. 0926B] Thus may you deign to deliver, O Lord, the soul of this man, and grant him to dwell with you in heavenly blessings. Through.

Prayer. With pious and loving remembrance, dearest brothers, we make remembrance of our dear one, whom the Lord has taken from the snare of the temptation of this age; we beseech the mercy of our God that he himself may deign to grant him a pleasing and peaceful dwelling, and forgive all offenses of slippery recklessness, so that, pardon and full indulgence having been granted, whatever he committed in this age through his own fault he may wholly erase and wipe away by his ineffable piety and goodness. May he himself deign to grant this, who lives and reigns with the Father and the Holy Spirit.

Prayer. God, to whom all live, and for whom our bodies do not perish [Col. 0926C] but are changed for the better, we humbly beseech you to command that your servant be received and led by the hands of your holy angels into the bosom of your friend, the patriarch Abraham, and be raised on the last day of the great judgment; and whatever vices he contracted through the devil’s deception, do you, gracious and merciful, wash away by forgiving them.

Prayer. Receive, O Lord, the soul of your servant, which you have deigned to call from the prison of this age, and deliver it from the rulers of darkness and from the places of punishment, so that, freed from every bond of sins, it may enjoy the blessedness of rest and eternal light, and may deserve to be raised among your saints in the glory of the resurrection. Through.

[Col. 0926D] Prayer. We commend to you, Lord, the soul of your servant, our brother, and we pray that, for whose sake you deigned in your mercy to descend to earth, you may not refuse, in compassion, to admit him into the bosoms of your patriarchs. You who live and reign.

Prayer. Deign, Lord, to raise him who departs in your name from this unstable and so uncertain life into that eternal life and joy, and into the heavenly blessings. Through.

## For washing the body

Prayer. Receive, O Lord, the soul of your servant returning to you; clothe it in a heavenly garment, and wash it in the holy fountain of eternal life, so that it may rejoice among those who rejoice, be wise among the wise, sit among the martyrs, advance among the patriarchs, and strive to follow Christ among the prophets [Col. 0927A] and apostles; so that among the angels and archangels it may see the glory of God, among the radiant stones of paradise possess joy, and recognize the knowledge of God’s ministries; so that among the cherubim and seraphim it may find the glory of God, among the twenty-four elders hear the singers chanting the Song of Songs, and among those washing their robes in the fountain of light wash its garment; so that among those knocking it may knock, find the gates of Jerusalem open, see the Lord among those who see him face to face, sing the new song among those who sing, and hear the heavenly sound among those who hear. Through all things.

Another prayer. Receive, O Lord, the soul of your servant returning to you and departing from the regions of Egypt, [Col. 0927B] and send your holy angels to meet it, and [show it] the way of righteousness; drive away from it all the rulers of darkness. Recognize, Lord, your creature, created not from foreign gods but by you alone, the living and true God, because there is no other God besides you, Lord, and there is none according to your works. Gladden, Lord, the soul of your servant, and do not remember the iniquities which the fury of evil desire stirred up in him. Although he sinned, nevertheless he did not deny the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, but believed, had zeal for God, and worshiped the God who made all things. He who lives and reigns.

Prayer. God, before whose presence everything that is done is brought, who, although you are the establisher, are also the governor of punishments, we ask for your servant that you grant him a portion with your saints and an inheritance [Col. 0927C] with your chosen ones. Throughout all ages.

Prayer. Receive, O Lord, the soul of your servant into a good dwelling. We are performing the service of washing his little body; grant him rest in the eternal kingdom, that is, in the heavenly Jerusalem, and deign to place him in the bosoms of your patriarchs, namely Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, so that he may have a share in the blessed and first resurrection. Receive his body, and may he come with the blessed who come to the right hand of God the Father, and among those possessing eternal life may he possess it. Through.

## The short readings, or prayers, after the body has been washed begin

Our Father. And lead us not.

[Col. 0927D] Short reading. “The just man shall be in everlasting remembrance. From the hearing.”

“Do not enter into judgment with your servant, O Lord, for no one will be justified.”

“Do not hand over to beasts the souls confessing you, nor the souls of the poor.”

“Grant him eternal rest, O Lord, and let perpetual light—”

“Lord, hear. And let my cry come to you.”

“The Lord be with you. And with—”

Prayer. God, giver of life and restorer of human bodies, who willed to be entreated by sinners, hear the prayers that we pour out to you with special devotion and tears for the soul of your servant, and deign to deliver him from the torments of hell and place him [Col. 0928A] among the ranks of your saints. Command him also to be clothed in a heavenly garment and the robe of immortality, and to be refreshed by the delights of paradise. Through.

Another prayer. God, eternal lover of human souls, return the soul of your servant, which held the true faith while he lived in the body, free from every torment of hell, so that, separated from the confines of hell, it may deserve to be joined to the company of the saints. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

Another prayer. God, with whom the spirits of the dead live, and in whom the souls of the elect, having laid aside the burden of the flesh, rejoice in complete happiness, grant, as we petition you, that the soul of your servant, who lacked the temporal sight of this age, may enjoy the comfort of that eternal light; may the torment of death not touch it, may the pain of a dreadful vision not afflict it, may penal fear not torture it, and may the worst chain of the guilty not bind it; but, with pardon for all sins granted, may it obtain the promised joys of the desired rest.

When all the prayers have been completed, let the body be placed in the bier, sprinkled with holy water, and incensed, and let them sing: “Come to his aid, you saints of God. May Christ receive you. God, in your name. Blessed are the undefiled.” And thus let them go to the church. When they have come to the entrance of the church, “Come to his aid, you saints of God” is said. Holy incense and water are then given, all the bells are rung, the bier is placed on the floor, and they sing the invitatory, “The King,” etc., as in the printed editions, up to but excluding the responsory of the second lesson of the first nocturn, whose words are these: “You who raised the girl within the house and the young man outside the [Col. 0928C] gate, you, Lord, to him.” The lesson “Your hand,” etc., up to but excluding the responsory of the next lesson. “Answer,” which is rendered as follows: “Come to his aid, you saints of God,” etc., as in the printed editions, when the corpse is led from the house. “A man born of a woman,” etc., as in the printed editions, up to the responsory of the next lesson. “Who will grant me,” where it reads: “Do not enter into judgment with your servant, O Lord.” In the third nocturn: “May it please you,” etc., up to the entire lesson. “To my skin,” whose responsory is: “Deliver me, Lord, from the power of hell; you who broke the gates of bronze, visited hell, and gave them light, so that those who were in the punishments of darkness might see you, crying out and saying: You have come, our Redeemer. Those who were.” Lesson: “The very brave Judas.” R\. “My Redeemer [Col. 0928D] lives, and on the last day I shall rise, and my bones shall be renewed again, and in my flesh I shall see my God. Praise the Lord, my soul; I shall praise the Lord in my life. And in my flesh.” “Eternal rest.” “And in my flesh.”

At Lauds: “They shall exult,” etc., as in the printed editions, up to but excluding the fourth antiphon. Antiphon: “I shall recall all my years in the bitterness of my soul.” Psalm as in the printed editions and up to the antiphon “Benedictus,” after which is read: “Everything that the Father gives,” etc. “Benedictus.” At Vespers, antiphon: “I shall please the Lord,” etc., through the psalm “I will confess,” inclusively, as in the printed editions.

Then follows: “Eternal rest. And light.” Antiphon: “I heard a voice from heaven saying to me: [Col. 0929A] Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord.” “Magnificat.” Psalm: “Out of the depths.” Psalm: “Praise.” Psalm: “With my voice.” Psalm: “To the Lord.” Our Father. And lead us not.

Prayer. God, whose proper work it is—. Another prayer. Incline, Lord.

Then the priest stands beside the bier. Meanwhile all the bells are rung until everyone gathers and receives candles, and the cantor stands beside the bier and speaks. Then the priest says the prayer, “Do not enter,” etc., as in the printed editions. R\. “You who raised Lazarus.” Meanwhile, while it is sung, he incenses the altar and then the body; the cantor says, “Lord, Christ, Lord”; and the priest says the prayer, “Grant, we ask,” as in the printed editions. “Come to his aid.” The priest incenses the altar and the body, and the cantor says, while the priest says the prayer, “Incline, Lord,” etc. [Col. 0929B] R\. “Deliver me, Lord,” etc. “That day, the day of wrath,” etc. Then: “All the tribes of the earth shall mourn over themselves.” “I have become trembling,” etc. “The just man will scarcely be saved, and where shall I, wretched man, appear?
