What shall I, most miserable man, say or do, when I bring nothing good before such a Judge? Now, Christ, I beseech you, have mercy; I ask it. You who came to redeem, come perpetually to save.” “Eternal rest,” etc. “And light,” etc. “Deliver me, Lord.” “Remember me, O God, because my life is like the wind, and let no human eye look upon me. Nor shall my eye return to see good things. Therefore I will not spare my mouth; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul. And let it not look,” etc. Then the altar and body are incensed.

After this, let the body of the deceased be lifted from the church, and let the younger members go first with the cross, incense, and [Col. 0929C] holy water, followed by the brothers singing: “May they lead you into paradise,” etc.; “When Israel went out,” etc. Let all the bells be rung until the tomb is closed. “Open for me the gates of righteousness; entering them I will confess to the Lord.” Psalm: “Give thanks.” Antiphon: “I shall enter into the place of the wondrous tabernacle, even to the house of God.” Psalm: “As the deer.” Antiphon: “This is my rest for ever and ever; here I shall dwell, because I have chosen it.” Psalm: “Remember.” Antiphon: “From earth you fashioned me; with flesh you clothed me. O Lord, my Redeemer, raise me on the last day.” Psalm: “Lord, hear my prayer.” Antiphon: “Do not enter into judgment with your servant, O Lord.” Psalm: “Lord, hear my prayer.” (twice.) Antiphon: “Let every spirit praise the Lord.” Psalm: “Praise the Lord.” Antiphon: “Grant him eternal rest, O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon him.”

At the Benedictus: “Everything that the Father gives me,” etc.

Prayer. Release his soul, O Lord, from every bond of sins, so that, raised in the glory of the resurrection, he may breathe again among your saints and chosen ones.

And let the priest incense the tomb, sprinkle it with holy water, and say these prayers while the others sing the psalm.

Prayer. Let us pray, dearest brothers, for the spirit of our dear one, whom the Lord has deigned to free from the temptations of this age, whose little body is today committed to burial, that the Lord’s compassion may deign to place him in the bosom of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and, when the day of judgment comes, may cause him to be raised and placed at the right hand among his saints and chosen ones. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, who with the Father and the Holy Spirit, etc.

[Col. 0930A] Another prayer. We implore your mercy, almighty God, who deigned to create man in your image, that you may receive gently and mercifully the spirit and soul of your servant, whom on this day you have commanded to be summoned to you, stripped of human affairs. May the shadows of death not dominate him, and may chaos and the darkness of gloom not seize him; but, stripped of every stain of crimes and placed in the bosom of Abraham, may he rejoice that he has attained a place of light and refreshment, so that, when the day of judgment comes, you may command him to be raised with your saints and chosen ones. Through.

Prayer. God, to whom all live and for whom our bodies do not perish [Col. 0930B] but are changed for the better, we humbly beseech you that, whatever the soul of your servant contracted through vices contrary to your will, through the devil’s deception, his own will, and frailty, you, gracious and merciful, may wash away by forgiving it, and command that it be received by the hands of your saints and led into the bosom of your patriarchs: namely, your friend Abraham, your chosen Isaac, and your beloved Jacob, where pain, sadness, and sighing are absent, and where the souls of the faithful rejoice in happy gladness; and on the last day of the great judgment may you cause it to receive among your saints and chosen ones a share in eternal glory, which eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has entered into the human heart, which you have prepared for those who love you.

[Col. 0930C] Prayer. It is presumptuous that a human being should dare to commend a human being, a mortal a mortal, ashes ashes, to you, Lord our God. But because earth receives earth and dust is converted into dust, until all flesh is reduced to its origin, therefore, most loving Father, we tearfully beseech your goodness, O God, that you receive into the bosom of your friend Abraham the soul of this servant of yours, whom you are leading from the muddy abyss of this world to his homeland, and drench him with the dew of refreshment. May he be separated from the fierce burning of blazing Gehenna and, by your gift, joined to blessed rest. And if he has any faults worthy of torments, Lord, forgive them in the grace of your gentlest kindness; let him not receive requital for his sins, but let him experience the gracious goodness [Col. 0930D] of your pardon. And when, at the end of the world, the heavenly kingdom has shone upon all, may the new man, joined to the assembly of all the saints, rise with your chosen ones, to be placed at the right hand. Through.

Another prayer. Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, we humbly beseech you for the spirit of your servant, whom you have commanded to be summoned from the darkness of this age to yourself. Deign, Lord, to give him a place of light, a place of refreshment and rest. May he be permitted to pass through the gates of hell and the punishments of darkness; may he remain in the dwellings of the saints and in the holy light which you once promised to Abraham and his descendants. May his spirit suffer no injury; but when that great day of resurrection and recompense [Col. 0931A] comes, deign, Lord, to raise him with your saints and chosen ones, forgive him his offenses and sins even to the last farthing, and may he attain with you the life and kingdom of immortality. Through.

Prayer. As men struck by the novelty of a wound and in some way wounded, we sorrowfully implore your mercy, Redeemer of the world, that you may receive gently and tenderly the soul of our dear one returning to you, its proper giver. If it contracted any stains from its dwelling in the flesh, forgive them in your goodness and consign them to perpetual oblivion; and command that, after returning to the body in due time, it may be joined to the company of your saints, to render this same praise to you with the others.

[Col. 0931B] Prayer. God, who are always present to just supplications and deign to regard devout vows, grant your servant, whose rites of deposition we perform, a share in the blessed gift with your saints and chosen ones. Through.

Prayer. As we fulfill, according to the custom of the faithful, the due duty of burying the human body, we faithfully beseech God, to whom all live, that he may raise this body of our dear one, buried by us in weakness, in the order of the saints, and command that his spirit be joined to the saints and faithful, with whom he may deserve to enjoy ineffable glory and everlasting happiness. Through.

Here is the end. After the body has been buried, let the priest say: “Say the Our Father.” And lead us not. Short reading: “From the gate of hell, deliver his soul, O Lord.” “The Lord be with you.” [Col. 0931C] “And with—”

Prayer. “To you, Lord,” etc., as in the printed editions. Then let him say: “Blot out, Lord.” “Have mercy.” Our Father. And lead us not. “From the gate.” “Deliver his soul, O Lord.” “The Lord be with you, and with—”

Prayer. God, in whose mercy the souls of the faithful rest, graciously grant to all your male and female servants resting in Christ here and everywhere the forgiveness of sins, so that they may rejoice without end, freed from every guilt. Through.

Blessing. May the blessing of God the Father + almighty, and of the Son +, and of the Holy Spirit + descend upon this body. Amen.

Then let him begin these seven penitential psalms: “Lord, rebuke me not in your fury,” and the others. Our Father. [Col. 0931D] And lead us not. Short reading: “From the gate of hell.” “Deliver, O Lord.” “The Lord be with you.” “And with the Spirit.”

Prayer. Release, O Lord, the souls of your servants, men and women, our brothers and all the faithful departed, from every bond of sins, so that, raised in the glory of the resurrection, they may breathe again among your saints. Through.

## The order of how the priest prepares himself for Mass begins

For washing the hands. Psalm: “How lovely.” Psalm: “I have blessed.” Psalm: “Incline, Lord.” Psalm: “Its foundations.” Psalm: “Judge me, Lord.” Psalm: “I believed.” Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy. Our Father. Short reading: “Arise, Lord.” “And deliver.” “God, when you turn, you will give us life.” “And your people.” “Show us, [Col. 0932A] Lord, your mercy.” “And your salvation.” “Be favorable, Lord.” “For the sake of.” “Do not enter into judgment.” “For no one.” “Lord, hear my prayer.” “And let my cry.” “The Lord be with you.” “And with—”

Prayer. Most gentle God, incline the ears of your goodness to my prayers, and illumine my heart with the grace of the Holy Spirit, so that I may deserve to minister worthily in your mysteries and love you with everlasting charity. Through.

Another prayer. Grant, we ask, almighty God the Father, to our senses that, just as the impurities of the hands are washed externally, so the pollutions of our minds may be cleansed by you, and the increase of holy virtues may grow in us. Through.

For the amice. Place, Lord, the helmet of salvation upon my head, to attack and overcome all diabolical [Col. 0932B] powers. Through.

For the alb. Clothe me, Lord, with the garment of salvation and the clothing of righteousness and joy, and surround me with the tunic of righteousness.

For the girdle. Gird, Lord, the loins of my mind, most merciful Father, and circumcise the vices of my heart.

For the maniple. Give me, Lord, right understanding and a pure voice, so that I may fulfill your praise.

For the stole. Surround my neck, Lord, with the stole of righteousness, and purify my mind from every corruption.

For the chasuble. Clothe me, Lord, with the breastplate of faith and the helmet of salvation, in Christ Jesus our Lord.

[Col. 0932C] When he enters at the altar, he says: “Our help is in the name of the Lord.” “Who—” I, wretched and unhappy, confess to almighty God, and to blessed Mary, perpetual Virgin, and to blessed Michael the archangel, and to the holy apostles Peter and Paul, and to all the saints, and to you, Father: through my fault, through my fault, through my fault, because I have sinned in thought, suggestion, delight, consent, word, and deed, and in all my evil vices. Therefore I beseech blessed Mary the Virgin, and blessed Michael the archangel, and the holy apostles Peter and Paul, and blessed N., and all the saints, and you, Father, to pray for me, a sinner, to our Lord Jesus Christ.

May almighty God have mercy on you and forgive you all your past and present sins, and guard you from future ones; may he free you from every evil work, save you and strengthen you in every good work, and lead you with his angels to eternal life. Amen.

May almighty and merciful Lord grant you pardon, remission, and absolution of all sins, a period of true repentance, and the grace of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

Short reading. “God, when you turn.” “And your people.” “Show us.” “And your salvation.” “Be favorable, Lord, to sins.” “For the sake of the name.” “From my hidden sins.” “And from those of others.” “Lord, hear.” “And let my cry.” “The Lord be with you.” “And with—”

Prayer. Take away from us, we ask, Lord, all [Col. 0933A] our iniquities, so that we may deserve to enter the holy of holies with pure minds. Through.

When the priest is at the altar, let him say: We pray you, Lord, that through the merits of your saints, whose relics are here, and through their intercessions, almighty God, you may deign to forgive me all my sins. Through.

While the epistle, gradual, and alleluia are sung, let the priest say this prayer: Receive my confession, O Lord my God, the one hope of my salvation. I am ruined by gluttony, drunkenness, fornication, lust, sadness, greed, anger, sloth, drowsiness, negligence, desire, envy, malice, hatred, detraction, perjury, falsehood, lying, vainglory, frivolity, and pride; and I am altogether deadened in thought, speech, [Col. 0933B] action, and in all my senses. O Lord, who justify the ungodly and give life to the dead, justify me and raise me again, Lord my God. Through Jesus Christ your Son, our Lord, who lives and reigns with you, etc.

Mary most blessed, glorious Mother of God and of man, blessed among all women, Lady of heaven and earth, exalted above all angels and archangels: deign to pour out prayers for me, a sinner, whose prayer cannot be despised by him who was born from you, nor can anything whatsoever be held in contempt by your Son and Creator. O singular and unprecedented mother, I adore the conception within your virginal womb. I adore the child born from the flower of the undefiled Virgin. I adore what ineffably proceeds from you, the seal of your virginity. [Col. 0933C] I adore him lying in the manger and crying like a child. I adore him suckling at his mother’s breasts. Pray for me, wretched one, blessed Mother of God, that he who deigned to assume true humanity from you may not disdain to dwell invisibly in my mind.

To you also, most merciful Lady, I am not ashamed to confess the shamefulness of my body and soul, because, conceived in sins and nourished in sins, and after baptism, up to this hour, having lived among all sinners, I have polluted my soul placed in the flesh, and defiled the temple of my body with every kind of fornication, pollution, and uncleanness. I, wretched and unhappy, have sinned through negligence and transgression of the holy law and of all the commandments of the Son of God, and of the priestly office [Col. 0933D] and the obedience entrusted to me, and of all their acts. There is no iniquity beyond my iniquity: I have fallen more often and more grievously than all sinners; more than all human beings, I have sinned without ceasing in carnal as well as spiritual vices from my childhood. Therefore, polluted in mind and body, I am not worthy to handle or receive the body of your Son. Now therefore, Mother of mercy, pray for me, a sinner, to that same Son of yours, our Lord, who suffered for us, whom you, glorious and blessed, bore as God and man for the redemption of all sinners.

At the blessing of the Gospel, the deacon should ask for the blessing, saying: “Bless, command.”

Response: “May the Lord be in your heart, so that you may worthily and suitably proclaim the Gospel of peace.” [Col. 0934A]

Then let him kiss the Gospel and say: “May the peace of Christ, which he has given us through his Gospel, strengthen and preserve our hearts and bodies unto eternal life. Amen.”

When incense is put into the thurible, he says: “May you be blessed by him for whose love you are burned.” Then the Gospel is incensed; after it has been read, let him kiss the Gospel, saying: “Through these holy words of the Gospel, may our Lord Jesus Christ forgive me all my sins. Amen.”

### Blessing of the corporal

“In your sight, O Lord, may these gifts of ours be pleasing to you, so that we may be able to please you.”

When he places the offerings upon the altar, let him say: “To you, O Lord, my Creator, I offer this sacrifice for the remission of all [Col. 0934B] my sins and of all your faithful, living and dead.”

When water is put into the chalice, the priest should say: “It is reported that blood and water came forth from Christ’s side; therefore they are mingled together, so that the merciful God may deign to sanctify them for the healing of our souls.”

When the chalice is placed upon the altar, let him say: “We offer you, O Lord, the chalice of salvation, humbly imploring your clemency, so that it may rise before the sight of your divine majesty with the fragrance of sweetness.”

Then, with the cross over both, he says: “Sanctify, O Lord, the gift offered to you, so that it may become for us the body and blood of your only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ.”

[Col. 0934C] Then: “Come, Sanctifier, almighty and eternal God; bless this sacrifice prepared for you.”

Then: “In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, may this sacrifice be immaculate and, by you, the living and true God, united and blessed forever and ever. Amen.”

When incense is put into the thurible, let him say: “Through the intercession, etc., as in the printed editions.”

When he incenses the offerings and the chalice, let him say this with three crosses over both, and, circling them three times, say: “Our Lord God, who accepted the gifts of Abel, Noah, Aaron, Samuel, and all your saints, may you likewise deign to accept this incense from the hand of our sins in your sight, [Col. 0934D] as a fragrance of sweetness, for the remission of our sins. Through Christ.”

When he incenses the offerings and the chalice, let him say: “May this incense, etc., as in the printed editions.”

The priest should humbly bow before the altar and say: “Receive, holy Trinity, this offering, which your servant offers to you, and grant that it may rise before your sight, pleasing to you.”

Then: “Receive, holy Trinity, this offering, which I offer to you for myself, a sinner, and for your male and female servants who have commended themselves to our prayers, and for the whole Christian people, living and dead, so that it may benefit me and them for healing and eternal life.”

Then the priest should rise and turn toward the brethren, saying: “Pray, dearest brothers, for me, so that my sacrifice and yours may be acceptable in the sight of the Lord.” [Col. 0935A]

And they should answer: “May the Lord receive the sacrifice from your hands, to the praise and glory of his name, and also for our benefit and that of his entire holy Church.”

### Preface for the Nativity of the Lord

“It is worthy and just, right and salutary, etc., unto eternal God.”

So also in the prefaces of Lent, the Resurrection, and Pentecost.

### Preface for the dead

“Through whom is the salvation of the world, through whom the life of lights, through whom the resurrection of the dead: through him, O Lord, we earnestly beseech you to deign to grant perpetual forgiveness to the soul of your servant and to the souls of your male and female servants, [Col. 0935B] and, freed from the contagions of mortality, to restore them to a share in eternal salvation. Through whom.”

### Another preface

“It is worthy and just, right and salutary. You who have granted us, in Christ your only-begotten Son, our Lord, the hope of blessed resurrection: grant, we beseech you, that the souls for whom we offer this sacrifice of our redemption to your majesty may, by your mercy, merit to reach with your saints the repose of blessed resurrection. Through the same Christ our Lord. Through whom.”

### Another preface

“It is worthy and just, right and salutary. You who are the source of life, the origin of light, and the author of all goodness, whose omnipotence must be entreated, whose mercy must be adored, and whose loving-kindness must be embraced: grant forgiveness of all sins to your majesty’s humble servant and to the souls of all [Col. 0935C] the faithful Christians, through the intercession of blessed and glorious Mary, Mother of God, together with all your saints, and lead them happily to everlasting life. Through Christ our Lord. Through whom.”

Before saying “Therefore,” let him say: “Open, O Lord, my mouth to bless your holy name, and cleanse my heart from every varied and wicked thought, so that I may merit to be heard as I pray for your people, whom you have chosen for yourself, through the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ. Who with the Father.”

“Therefore,” and the rest of this prayer, as in the printed editions. Here the priest should remember the names of the living: “Remember, O Lord,” etc., through “Deliver us, we beseech you, [Col. 0935D] O Lord.” In “In communion,” after the name of Damian, the name of Blaise is added; and in “Also to us sinners,” after Anastasia, Scholastica is added.

“Deliver us, we beseech you, O Lord, from all past, present, and future evils; and, through the intercession of blessed and glorious Mary, ever-Virgin, and of your chosen archangels Michael, Gabriel, and Raphael, and of blessed John the Baptist, and of your blessed apostles Peter and Paul, and Andrew and John, and of Saint Apollinaris, and Lawrence, and Benedict, together with all your saints:”

Here he makes the sign of the cross with the paten:

“Grant peace graciously in our days, so that, aided by the help of your mercy, we may always be free from sin and secure from every disturbance. Through our Lord Jesus, etc. Forever and ever.”

Response: “Amen.” [Col. 0936A]

“May the peace of the Lord be always with you.”

“Lamb of God” (three times).

When he places the body into the blood, the priest should say this prayer: “May this consecration and commingling of the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ be salvation unto eternal life for all who receive it, including us. Amen.”

Then let him kiss the altar and say this prayer: “Lord Jesus Christ, who said to your apostles, ‘My peace I give you,’ do not look upon my sins, but upon the devotion and faith of your Church; and deign to purify and unite it according to your will. Who live…”

Then let him give the peace, saying: “Hold fast the bond of charity and peace, so that you may be fit for the most holy mysteries, [Col. 0936B] and may the peace of Christ and of the Church always abound in your hearts.”

Before receiving the body and blood, the priest should bow before the altar and say this prayer tearfully: “Holy Father, almighty God, grant me to receive this body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ in such a way that through it I may merit to receive remission of sins and be filled with your Holy Spirit, for you are God, and there is no other besides you; your glorious name remains forever and ever. Amen.”

### Another prayer

“Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, good shepherd, most glorious creator of the world, who by the will of the Father, with the cooperation of the Holy Spirit, gave life to the world through your death: through this most holy body and blood of yours free me from all my iniquities and from all my evils; make me obey your holy commands; and never permit me to be separated from you forever. May the reception of your body and blood, which I, unworthy, presume to take, not come upon me for judgment and condemnation, but, by your goodness, benefit me for the protection of mind and body through you, Jesus Christ, who with the Father and the Holy Spirit live and reign forever and ever. Amen.”

Then the priest should say three times: “Lord, I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof.”

Afterward let him say three times: “May the body of our Lord Jesus Christ preserve my soul unto eternal life.” [Col. 0936D] “Amen.”

After receiving the body and blood, for the ablution let him say this prayer: “May the communion and strengthening of your body and blood, Lord Jesus Christ, benefit me for the remission of all my sins, and preserve me and lead me to eternal life. Amen.”

### When folding the corporal and putting it away

“May your body, O Lord, which I have received, and the chalice from which I have drunk, always cling to my inward parts, so that no stain may remain in me, into whom these pure and holy sacraments have entered.”

When the Mass is finished, the priest says this prayer: “May the service of my ministry, which I, unworthy, have offered before the eyes of your majesty, be pleasing to you, holy Trinity; may it be pleasing to you, and, by your mercy, propitious to me and to all for whom I offered it.” [Col. 0937A]

When the Mass is finished, the priest says: “By the merits and intercessions of these, may almighty God have mercy on us.”

When the priest removes his vestments, let him say these psalms:

“Bless the Lord, priests of the Lord. Praise the Lord in his holy places.”

“Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.”

“Our Father.”

“And lead us not…”

“Chapter: Let all your works confess to you, O Lord, and let your saints bless you. The saints shall exult in glory, and they shall rejoice in their dwelling places. Let the righteous exult in the sight of God, and let them rejoice in gladness. Let your priests, O Lord, be clothed with righteousness, and let your saints exult.”

“O Lord, hear my prayer.”

“And let my cry come to you.”

“The Lord be with you.”

“And with your spirit.”

[Col. 0937B]

### Prayer

“God, who moderated the flames of fire for the three children, graciously grant, through the intervention and merits of all your saints, that the flame of vices may not consume us, your servants. Through.”

## MASS IN HONOR OF THE HOLY TRINITY ON SUNDAY

“Blessed be,” etc., as in the printed editions.

Psalm: “Let us bless the Father and the Son with the Holy Spirit.”

Prayer: “Almighty and everlasting God, etc.”

Gradual: “Blessed are you, O Lord, who behold the depths and sit above the Cherubim. Bless the God of heaven and of the heavens, because he has shown his mercy toward us.”

Alleluia: “Blessed are you, O Lord, God of our fathers, and worthy of praise forever.”

[Col. 0937C]

Continuation of the holy Gospel according to John. At that time Jesus said: “When the Paraclete comes,” through “I have told you.”

The Offertory, Communion, and Postcommunion are as in the printed editions.

### Another prayer

“Lord God, almighty Father, always bless and protect us, your servants subject to your majesty, through your only Son and in the power of the Holy Spirit, so that, secure from every enemy, we may continually rejoice in your praise. Through the same.”

## MASS FOR MONDAY IN HONOR OF THE HOLY ANGELS

“Bless the Lord,” etc.

Prayer: “Grant us perpetual assistance from your mercy, O Lord, to whom you have granted that angelic aid should not be lacking. Through.”

Reading from the Book of the Apocalypse of the Apostle John. In those days the angel said to me: “Write, blessed,” etc., through “Worship God.” [Col. 0937D]

Gradual: “Bless the Lord, all his angels, mighty in strength, who do his word. Bless the Lord, O my soul, and all that is within me, his holy name.”

Alleluia: “Praise the Lord, all his angels; praise him, all his powers.”

Continuation of the holy Gospel according to John. At that time the Lord went up to Jerusalem, through “was being held by an infirmity.”

The Offertory and Secret are as in the printed editions.

Communion: “Bless the Lord, all angels of the Lord; sing a hymn and exalt him above all forever.”

The Postcommunion is as in the printed editions.

## MASS OF WISDOM

“Let the heart of those who seek the Lord rejoice; seek the Lord [Col. 0938A] and be strengthened; seek his face always.”

Psalm: “Give thanks to the Lord and call upon him.”

Prayer: “God, who through Wisdom coeternal with you created man when he did not exist, and mercifully reformed him when he was lost: grant, we beseech you, that, with that same Wisdom inspiring our hearts, we may love you with our whole mind and hasten to you with our whole heart. Through.”

Reading from the Epistle of blessed James the Apostle. “Dearly beloved, if any of you lacks,” etc., through “in his lowliness.”

Gradual: “O Lord, our Lord, how wonderful is your name throughout all the earth! For your magnificence has been exalted above the heavens.”

Alleluia: “Praise the Lord, O my soul. I will praise the Lord in my life; I will sing psalms to my God as long as I am.”

Continuation of the holy Gospel according to John. At that time, “Jesus, having lifted up,” [Col. 0938B] etc., through “Jesus Christ.”

Offertory: “I will meditate on your commandments, which I have greatly loved, and I will lift up my hands to your commandments, which I have loved.”

Secret: “May the gift of this offering be sanctified, we beseech you, Lord God, with your Wisdom cooperating, so that it may be pleasing to you for praise and benefit us for salvation. Through.”

Communion: “I will remember your righteousness alone, O Lord; God, you have taught me from my youth, and even unto old age and gray hairs, O God, do not forsake me.”

Postcommunion: “Pour into our hearts, we beseech you, Lord God, through these sacraments that we have received, the light of your Wisdom, so that we may truly acknowledge you and faithfully love you. Through.”

## MASS OF CHARITY ON WEDNESDAY

[Col. 0938C]

“The charity of God has been poured into our hearts, alleluia, through his Spirit dwelling in us, alleluia, alleluia.”

“O Lord, God of my salvation.”

Prayer: “God, who have prepared invisible good things for those who love you, pour the affection of your love into our hearts, so that, loving you in all things and above all things, we may attain your promises, which surpass every desire.”

Reading from the Epistle of blessed Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians. “Brothers, charity is patient,” etc., through “never fails.”

Gradual: “I rejoiced in the things that were said to me: We shall go into the house of the Lord. Let peace be in your strength, and abundance in your towers.”

Alleluia: “Attend, my people, to my law; incline your ear to the words of my mouth.”

Continuation [Col. 0938D] of the holy Gospel according to John. At that time Jesus said to his disciples: “Little children, yet a little while,” etc., through “to one another.”

Offertory: “Blessed are you, O Lord; teach me your statutes. With my lips I have proclaimed them.”

Secret: “God, who recall us to your image through sacraments and commandments, perfect our steps in your paths, so that through these sacrifices which we offer you may truly cause us to grasp the gift of charity, which you have made us practice. Through.”

Communion: “I will remember your righteousness alone, O Lord; God, you have taught me from my youth, and even unto old age and gray hairs, O God, do not forsake me.”

At the Postcommunion: “Pour into us, O Lord, the Spirit of your charity, so that those whom you have satisfied with one heavenly bread you may, by your goodness, make harmonious. Through.”

## MASS TO ASK FOR THE GRACE OF THE HOLY SPIRIT

[Col. 0939A]

Prayer: “God of our fathers, give us the Spirit who may pour flame into our hearts.”

Psalm: “Bless all works.”

Reading: “In those days Solomon said: ‘God of our fathers,’” etc., through “your handmaid.”

Gradual: “Look upon your covenant, O Lord, and do not forget the souls of your poor forever. Arise, O Lord, and judge your cause; remember the reproach suffered by your servants.”

Alleluia: “Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful and kindle in them the fire of your love.”

Continuation of the holy Gospel according to Matthew. At that time, the Lord Jesus answered and said: “I confess,” etc., through “the Son reveal.”

Offertory: “The judgments of the Lord are right, rejoicing the hearts and sweeter than honey and [Col. 0939B] the honeycomb; for your servant also keeps them.”

Secret: “May this offering, Lord God, cleanse the stains of our hearts, so that it may become a worthy dwelling place of the Holy Spirit. Through.”

Communion: “Taste and see that the Lord is sweet; blessed is the man who hopes in him.”

At Communion: “Grant us, we beseech you, almighty God, to merit the Holy Spirit through constant prayers, so that by his grace we may be freed from all temptations and may merit to receive forgiveness of our sins. Through.”

## FRIDAY IN HONOR OF THE HOLY CROSS

“But we,” etc., as in the printed editions, through “alleluia.”

Alleluia: “But we ought to glory in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ.”

Continuation of the holy Gospel according to Matthew. At that time Jesus “took,” etc.

Communion: “Redeemer of the world, by the sign of the cross preserve us from every adversity; you who saved Peter at sea, have mercy on us.” [Col. 0939C]

Postcommunion: “Refreshed by heavenly food and drink, we beseech you, almighty God, to defend from fear of enemies those whom you have redeemed by the precious blood of your Son. Through the same.”

## SATURDAY: MASS IN HONOR OF HOLY MARY

“Hail, holy mother,” etc.

“Virgin Mother of God, whom the whole world cannot contain, he, having become man, enclosed himself within your womb.”

Prayer: “Grant us,” etc.

Alleluia: “After childbirth you remained an inviolate virgin, alleluia.”

Continuation of the holy Gospel according to Luke. At that time: “Exalting,” etc.

### In another Mass of holy Mary: prayer

“God, who apply healing [Col. 0939D] to violated nature through the beauty of virginity, grant that through the prayers of blessed Mary the Virgin we may cast away the leaven of conceived depravity and pass from the old condition into the unleavened bread of newness.”

## MASS FOR THE COMMUNITY

Prayer: “Almighty and everlasting God, who alone work wonders, extend over your servants and over all the communities entrusted to them the spirit of saving grace; and, so that they may please you in truth, pour continually upon them the dew of your blessing. Through.”

The Secret and Communion are as in the printed editions.

## MASS FOR THE PETITION OF TEARS

Prayer: “Almighty,” etc., as in the printed editions.

Postcommunion: “Satisfied with your body and blood, O Lord, we beseech you always [Col. 0940A] to grant us, for our sins, contrition of heart, mourning, and streams of tears, so that in the future we may merit heavenly consolation. Through.”

## MASS FOR TRIBULATION

“Almighty and everlasting God, consolation of the sorrowful and strength of those who labor: may the prayers of those crying out to you from whatever tribulation reach you, so that all may rejoice that your mercy has been present to them in their necessities. Through.”

Secret: “We offer these sacrifices to you, O Lord, for our salvation and for all the distresses threatening us, so that you may deign to free and enlighten our bodies and souls by the grace of the Holy Spirit.”

At Communion: “Give us joy from tribulation, we beseech you, so that we who are afflicted for a long time because of our sins may, through the intercession of all [Col. 0940B] your saints, recover our breath in your mercy. Through.”

## MASS FOR TRAVELERS

The Prayer, Secret, and Postcommunion are the same as in the printed editions. The following is added:

“May God grant us a prosperous journey; may a good angel of the Lord accompany us, and may our God order our routes well.”

“May he arise.”

“Glory.”

“Prosperous.”

Prayer: “God, who always show your mercy to those who love you, and are not far away in any region from those who serve you, direct the way of your servants according to your will, so that, with you as protector and guide, they may walk without stumbling along the paths of righteousness. Through.”

Reading from Genesis: “In those days Israel departed,” through “returning.”

“May a good angel of the Lord accompany you, and [Col. 0940C] may he order your journeys well. May our saving God grant you a prosperous journey. Alleluia. May our saving God grant us a prosperous journey. Alleluia.”

At that time Jesus said to his disciples, through “that city.”

Offertory: “May a good angel of the Lord accompany you and order your journey well, alleluia.”

Communion: “Just as the archangel Raphael went before Tobiah to prepare the way, so may he accompany you and order your journeys well.”

Postcommunion: “Direct, we beseech you, O Lord, the way of your servants according to your will, and graciously hear us as we entreat you, so that they may have a prosperous journey and a heart directed toward you. Through.”

## MASS FOR TEMPTATION OF THE FLESH

[Col. 0940D]

“Burn,” etc., as in the printed editions, through “the whole secret prayer.”

At Communion: “Lord, helper and protector, help us; may our flesh blossom again with the vigor of chastity and the newness of holiness, and may you command that, snatched from the hand of Tartarus, it be restored in the joy of the resurrection. Through.”

## MASS FOR UNCLEAN THOUGHTS

“Almighty,” etc., as in the printed editions.

Secret: “Through this sacrifice, we beseech you, O Lord, which we have offered to your majesty, cleanse our hearts from every temptation. Through.”

## MASS FOR SINS

“If you observe iniquities, O Lord, Lord, who will endure? For with you is propitiation, our God.”

Psalm: “From the depths I have cried to you, O Lord.”

Prayer: “Spare, O Lord, spare our sins; and although [Col. 0941A] continual punishment is owed to those who offend without ceasing, grant, we beseech you, that what deserves perpetual destruction may pass over into the aid of correction. Through.”

Reading from the Epistle of blessed Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians. “Brothers, I rejoice with,” etc., through “Christ our Lord.”

Gradual: “Cleanse me from my hidden faults, O Lord, and spare your servant from those belonging to others. If they do not rule over me, then I shall be blameless and cleansed from the greatest offense.”

Alleluia: “From the depths I have cried to you, O Lord; Lord, hear my prayer. Let your ears be attentive to the prayer of your servant.”

Continuation of the holy Gospel according to Mark. At that time Jesus said to his disciples: “Have faith in God,” through “your sins.”

Offertory: “Have mercy on me, and according to your great mercy blot out my iniquity.” [Col. 0941B]

Secret: “May this sacrifice, O Lord, we beseech you, always release your Church from hidden offenses and suitably cleanse it from manifest ones. Through.”

Communion: “Cleanse me from my hidden faults, O Lord, and spare your servant from those belonging to others.”

At Communion: “Grant us, eternal Savior, that, receiving forgiveness of sins through this gift, we may henceforth avoid sins. Through.”

## MASS FOR THE TRIBULATION OF THE CHURCH

“God, Father of orphans and judge of widows, mercifully regard the tears of your Church, and may your majesty mercifully rescue her, whom no earthly power defends. Through.”

Secret: “May this sacrifice, O Lord, which we offer for protection from the weapons of unbelievers, be acceptable to you, so that, with your help, we may attain through it what we devoutly ask. Through.” [Col. 0941C]

Postcommunion: “Bend down, we beseech you, almighty God, the rights of tyrants who oppose you, so that they may learn that you are the protector of your Church, redeemed by your precious blood. Through.”

## MASS FOR SERENITY

Prayer: “To you, O Lord, etc.”

At Communion: “May your people, O Lord, receive an increase of holy blessing and be raised up by abundant assistance from your benefits; they are aided by the prayers of so many intercessors. Through.”

## MASS FOR PENITENTS

[Col. 0941D]

“You are righteous, O Lord, and your judgment is right; deal with your servant according to your mercy.”

Psalm: “Blessed are the undefiled in the way.”

Prayer: “God, who justify the wicked and do not desire the death of sinners, we humbly beseech your majesty to protect your servant, who trusts in your mercy, with heavenly aid in your kindness, and to preserve him through continual protection, so that he may always serve you and never be separated from you by any temptations. Through the Lord.”

Reading from the Epistle of blessed Paul the Apostle to the Romans. “Brothers, just as through one man,” etc., through “our Lord.”

Gradual: “Save your servant, O merciful Lord God, who hopes in you. Give ear, O Lord, to my prayer, and let my cry come to you.”

Continuation of the holy Gospel according to Luke. At that time: “Those who were approaching,” etc., through “doing penance.”

Offertory: “From the depths I have cried to you, O Lord; Lord, hear my prayer.”

Secret: “Receive, we beseech you, O Lord, the gifts which we bring to you from your generosity for your servant, so that these most holy mysteries, through the power of your grace at work, may sanctify him in the conduct of the present life and lead him to eternal joys. Through.” [Col. 0942A]

Communion: “I tell you, there is joy before the angels of God over one sinner doing penance.”

At Communion: “May your holy things, which we have received, purify us, O Lord; and grant that your servant may be free from every fault, so that he who is bound by the guilt of his conscience may glory in the fullness of heavenly healing. Through.”

## MASS FOR THE PRIEST HIMSELF

“I earnestly beseech you, most merciful God, almighty Father, creator of all things: while I confess that I, your servant, have gravely offended before the omnipotence of your majesty, may you, through the intercession of blessed Mary ever-Virgin and all your saints, extend to me the hand of your mercy, so that, while I offer this oblation to your goodness, you may most mercifully deign to absolve me from what I have wickedly committed. Through the Lord.” [Col. 0942B]

Secret: “God of mercy, God of compassion, God of forgiveness, forgive, I beseech you, and have mercy on me, your servant; and graciously deign to receive the sacrifice which, by the grace of your goodness, I humbly offer. Through the intervention of blessed Mary ever-Virgin and all your saints, kindly, graciously, and mercifully forgive the sins which I have incurred by falling into vices, and grant me a place of repentance and streams of tears, so that I may merit to receive forgiveness of my offenses. Through the Lord.”

[Col. 0942C]

Postcommunion: “Merciful and compassionate Lord, who sustain by sparing and sanctify by forgiving, grant me through these holy things which I have received cleansing of mind and body; and through the intercession of blessed Mary ever-Virgin and all your saints, may I merit absolution from my faults. Through.”

## ANOTHER MASS FOR THE PRIEST HIMSELF

Introit: “Save me, O God, by your name, and judge me by your strength. O God, hear my prayer.”

Psalm: “Give ear.”

Prayer: “Almighty and everlasting God, etc.; the same as that which is read in the printed editions in the Postcommunion.”

Reading from the Epistle of blessed Paul the Apostle to Timothy. “Dearest, faithful is the word,” through “forever and ever. Amen.”

Gradual: “I said: O Lord, have mercy on me; heal my soul, because I have sinned against you. Blessed is he who understands concerning the needy and the poor; on the evil day the Lord will deliver him.”

Alleluia: “O Lord, God of my salvation, by day I have cried out and by night before you.”

Continuation of the holy Gospel according to Mark. At that time: “A leper came to Jesus,” etc., through “as a testimony to them.”

Offertory: “O Lord, hear my prayer, and look upon my help. Let my enemies who seek my soul to take it away be confounded and put to shame.”

Secret: “Be appeased, we beseech you, O Lord, by the prayers of my humility; and where no assistance of merits is available, come to my aid with your protection. Through.”

Communion: “Cleanse me from my hidden faults, O Lord, and spare your servant from those belonging to others.”

Postcommunion: [Col. 0943A] “We have received, O Lord, God of our salvation, the heavenly sacraments; grant, we beseech you, that their participation may benefit me, your servant, unto perpetual salvation. Through.”

## ON THE VIGIL OF ONE APOSTLE

“But I,” etc.

Prayer: “God, who grant that we may anticipate the glorious feast of your blessed apostle N., grant us, we beseech you, always to be preceded by his benefits and aided by his prayers. Through.”

Reading from the Book of Wisdom. “Blessed is the man,” etc., through “the assembly of the saints.”

The Gradual and Verse are as in the printed editions.

Continuation of the holy Gospel according to John. At that time Jesus said to his disciples: “I am the true vine,” etc., through “may be fulfilled.”

The Offertory is as in the printed editions.

Secret: “With our gifts, we beseech you, O Lord, we anticipate the feast of your blessed apostle N.; by his merits may they be rendered pleasing to you for us. Through.” [Col. 0943B]

At the Postcommunion: “Having received the heavenly sacraments, O Lord, we humbly beseech your majesty that, with your blessed apostle N. interceding, what we carry out temporally we may receive unto eternal life. Through.”

## MASS ON THE FEAST OF SEVERAL APOSTLES

Introit.

Prayer: “Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that just as we anticipate the glorious feasts of the apostles N. and N., so may they themselves go before your majesty on our behalf to obtain your benefits. Through.”

Reading from the Epistle of blessed Paul the Apostle to the Ephesians. “Brothers, to each of you,” etc., through “the fullness of Christ.”

Gradual: “Avenge, O Lord, the blood of your saints that has been poured out. They have given the corpses of your servants as food to the birds of heaven, the flesh of your saints to the beasts of the earth.” [Col. 0943C]

Continuation of the holy Gospel according to Matthew. At that time: “Jesus went around,” etc., through “give freely.”

Offertory: “The saints shall exult in glory; they shall rejoice in their dwelling places. The exaltations of God are in their throats.”

Secret: “With our gifts we anticipate, O Lord, the feast of your apostles, humbly imploring that what is hindered by obstacles in our conscience may, through their merits, be rendered pleasing to you. Through.”

Communion: “The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and the torment of malice shall not touch them. In the eyes of the foolish they seemed,” etc.

At the Postcommunion: “Having received the heavenly sacraments, O Lord, we humbly beseech your majesty that, with your blessed apostles N. and N. interceding, what we carry out temporally we may receive unto eternal life. Through.” [Col. 0943D]

## MASS ON THE VIGIL OF ANY ONE YOU WISH

“But I have flourished like an olive tree in the house of the Lord; I have hoped in the mercy of my God, and I will await your name, for it is good in the sight of your saints.”

Psalm: “Why do you glory?”

Prayer: “Grant us, we beseech you, almighty God, to anticipate the coming solemnity of blessed N. with appropriate honor and to celebrate it when it comes with worthy veneration. Through.”

Reading from the Book of Wisdom. “The blessing of the Lord,” etc., through “a crown of glory.”

Gradual: “The righteous shall flourish like a palm tree; he shall multiply like a cedar of Lebanon. To proclaim your mercy in the morning [Col. 0944A] and your truth throughout the night.”

Gospel: “I am the vine.”

The Offertory is to be sought above.

Secret: “May the offering of our devotion be acceptable to you, O Lord, so that it may make us come to the feast of Saint N. purer. Through.”

Communion: “Great is his glory in your salvation.”

At the Postcommunion: “Grant us, eternal God and giver, to be protected everywhere by pious devotion to him, whose feast we anticipate through these holy things that we have received as a votive service. Through.”

## MASS ON THE FEAST OF ONE MARTYR

“Let him rejoice,” etc., as in the printed editions.

Prayer: “May the feast of the birth of blessed N., your martyr, always receive us as votaries, and may it both pour into us the joy of his glorification and render us acceptable to you. Through.”

Reading from the Book of Wisdom. “The Lord led the righteous,” [Col. 0944B] etc., through “our God.”

Gradual: “You placed upon his head, O Lord, a crown of precious stone. You granted him the desire of his soul and did not deprive him of the will of his lips.”

Alleluia: “The righteous shall rejoice in the Lord and hope in him, and all the upright of heart shall be praised.”

Continuation of the holy Gospel according to Luke. At that time Jesus said to his disciples: “If anyone,” etc., through “to be a disciple.”

The Offertory, Secret, Communion, and Postcommunion are as in the printed editions.

## MASS OF ONE NON-BISHOP MARTYR
The righteous man will not be troubled, because the Lord strengthens his hands; all day long he shows mercy and lends, and his offspring will be in blessing; he will be preserved forever. Psalm: Do not be envious. Prayer: O God, who gladden us through the feast and intercession of N. the martyr, graciously grant that we who seek his benefits may obtain them by the gift of your grace. Through [Christ our Lord].

Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Blessed is the man,” etc., up to “our God.” Gradual: “You have placed, O Lord.” “The desire.” Alleluia: “You have placed.” Sequence of the holy Gospel according to Luke: At that time Jesus the Lord said to his disciples: “If anyone wishes,” up to “the kingdom of God.” Offertory: “In your strength, O Lord, the righteous man will rejoice,” etc., up to “O Lord.”

Prayer over the offerings: Sanctify, O Lord, the gifts offered, and, through the intercession of blessed N. your martyr, cleanse us by these gifts from the stains of our sins. Through [Christ our Lord].

Communion: “Great is his glory in your salvation.”

Prayer after Communion: We have received the heavenly sacraments on the solemnity of your holy martyr N.; grant, we ask, through his intercession, that what we carry out in time we may attain in eternal joys. Through [Christ our Lord].

## MASS ON THE FEAST OF SEVERAL MARTYRS

“Wisdom of the saints,” etc. Psalm: “Rejoice, you righteous.”

Prayer: We ask, O Lord, that your devoted Church may reverently receive the feast-days of the birth [into glory] of your blessed martyrs N. and N., and may become more devoted through love of their great glorification. Through [Christ our Lord].

Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “The tongue of the wise,” etc., up to “from the Lord.”

Gradual: “The saints will exult in glory; they will rejoice in their dwelling places. Sing to the Lord a new song; his praise is in the assembly of the saints.”

Alleluia: “Your saints, O Lord, will flourish like the lily, and like the fragrance of balsam they will be before you.”

Sequence of the holy Gospel according to Matthew: At that time, when Jesus saw [this], etc., up to “in heaven.”

Offertory: “Wonderful is God,” etc.

Prayer over the offerings: “The gifts offered to you, O Lord,” etc.

Prayer after Communion: Protect your people, O Lord, and grant through the prayers of the righteous that those whom you continually make devoted on the feast of your martyrs may always be pleasing to you. Through [Christ our Lord].

## ANOTHER MASS ON THE FEAST OF SEVERAL MARTYRS

“Let [the prayer] enter,” etc.

Prayer: “O God, who [grant us],” etc.

Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “God will repay the reward of labors,” up to “O Lord our God.”

Another reading from the Letter of the blessed apostle Paul to the Hebrews: Brothers, “the saints through faith,” up to “our Lord.”

“Take vengeance, O Lord, for the blood of your saints that has been shed. They gave the dead bodies of your servants as food to the birds of heaven, the flesh of your saints to the beasts of the earth.”

Alleluia: “This is the true brotherhood, which conquers the crimes of the world; it followed Christ, holding the renowned kingdoms of heaven.”

Sequence of the holy Gospel according to Luke, as in the printed editions in the first Mass.

Offertory: “Rejoice.”

Prayer over the offerings: “The gifts.”

Communion: “The souls of the righteous.”

Prayer after Communion: “Grant us,” etc.

## MASS ON THE FEAST OF A CONFESSOR

“Priests,” etc.

Prayer: “Grant, we ask,” etc.

Reading from the Letter, the same as in the common of doctors.

Gradual: “Behold the priest.”

Alleluia: “I have found David.”

Gospel: that of the second Mass.

Offertory: that of the first Mass in the printed editions.

Prayer over the offerings: We ask, O Lord, that your holy bishop and confessor N. may beseech you to make the victims placed upon the sacred altars bring salvation to us.

Communion: that of the second Mass.

Prayer after Communion: Appeased by the supplications of your blessed confessor N., defend us, O Lord, by the power of your sacrament, which we have received. Through [Christ our Lord].

## MASS FOR YOUNGER CONFESSORS WHO ARE NOT BISHOPS

The Introit and prayer are from the common of abbots.

Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “The blessing of the Lord,” up to “glory.”

Gradual: “The mouth of the righteous,” up to “his steps.”

Alleluia: “He loved.”

Gospel: “Watch.”

Offertory: “The desire.”

Prayer over the offerings: We offer you, O Lord, sacrifices in commemoration of your holy confessor N., whom no temptation separated from union with your Body. Through [Christ our Lord].

The Communion and prayer after Communion are from the printed editions in the common of doctors.

## MASS ON THE FEAST OF A CONFESSOR

“He established.”

Psalm: “Your mercies forever,” etc.

Prayer: “Be present.”

Epistle: as in the printed editions in the first Mass of a confessor who is a bishop.

Gradual: “I have found David.”

Alleluia: “Lord, five talents.”

Gospel: “A man going abroad.”

Offertory: “Truth.”

Prayer over the offerings: Grant, we ask, O Lord, that we may serve freely in mind with heavenly gifts, and that the gifts we bring may, through the intervention of your blessed confessor N., become for us healing and glory. Through [Christ our Lord].

Communion: “Lord, five talents.”

Prayer after Communion: Filled with heavenly nourishment, we ask, O Lord, that, through the intercession of your blessed confessor N., we may deserve to obtain the grace of your mercy. Through [Christ our Lord].

## MASS ON THE FEAST OF A VIRGIN

“I was speaking.”

Prayer: Grant, we ask, almighty God, that as we celebrate the solemnity of your blessed martyr N., we may be protected by her merits and prayers. Through [Christ our Lord].

Epistle: Brothers, “whoever boasts,” etc.

Gradual: “You have loved.”

Alleluia: “Poured out.”

Gospel: “It is like.”

Offertory: “They will be offered to the king.”

Prayer over the offerings: Be favorable, O Lord, to the vows of your people, we ask, and grant that we may rejoice in the intercession of her whose solemnity you enable us to celebrate. Through [Christ our Lord].

Communion: “The five wise [virgins].”

Prayer after Communion: We humbly ask you, almighty God, that, through the intervention of your blessed martyr N., you may multiply your gifts in us and order our times. Through [Christ our Lord].

## ANOTHER MASS OF VIRGINS

The Introit, Psalm, and prayer are as in the printed editions for the first Mass of one virgin.

Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Wisdom conquers wickedness,” up to “the discipline of God.”

Gradual: “In your beauty.”

Alleluia: “O how beautiful is a chaste generation,” with radiance.

The Gospel is as in the printed editions for one martyr who is not a virgin.

Offertory: “The daughters of kings.”

The prayer over the offerings, Communion, and prayer after Communion are as in the printed editions for the second Mass of one virgin.

## MASS ON THE DAY OF BURIAL

We ask you, O Lord our God, to receive the soul of this deceased person, for whom you shed your blood. Remember, O Lord, that we are dust, and that a human being is like grass and the flower of the field.

Psalm: And just as all die in Adam, so also all will be made alive in Christ.

Prayer: O God, whose proper nature it is to show mercy, etc.

Reading from the Letter of the blessed apostle Paul to the Thessalonians: Brothers, “concerning the times and moments,” etc., up to “died for us.”

Gradual: You who raised foul-smelling Lazarus from the tomb, grant him, O Lord, rest and a place of forgiveness. Grant him eternal rest, O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon him.

Tract: “Absolve, O Lord,” etc.

Sequence of the holy Gospel according to John: At that time Jesus said to his disciples: “No one can come,” up to “for the life of the world.”

Offertory: “Come to the aid of the saints of God.”

Prayer over the offerings: “Be favorable, O Lord.”

Preface: Eternal God, who, in your gratuitous kindness, granting forgiveness to sinners, prepared life for the dead, so that severity might not hold longer in punishment those whom mercy had freed from guilt. Therefore we pour out humble prayers to you, and to you we commend the body and soul of your servant, so that, received among the ranks of the blessed, he may not know the places of the underworld. May nothing harm him, O Lord, whatever he committed through the attraction of fragile flesh, or whatever, weighed down by the habit of human desire, he sinned in deed, word, or thought; but, following the footsteps of the Savior, may he enjoy infinite sweetness, and, instructed by the presence of truth, may he also confidently await the redemption of his body, and receive as a gift whatever he formerly possessed in faith. Through Christ our Lord.

Communion: as in the printed editions.

Prayer after Communion: as on the day of death.

## ANOTHER MASS FOR THE DEAD

“Grant rest,” etc.

Prayer: Be present, O Lord, we ask, to the souls of your servants and handmaids, for whom we perform the service of commemoration on the day of their burial, so that, if any worldly stain clung to them or any vice of the world infected them, you may forgive and wipe it away by the gift of your goodness. Through [Christ our Lord].

Prayer over the offerings: Look favorably, we ask, O Lord, upon these gifts that we offer to you for the souls of your servants and handmaids, whose day of death we commemorate, so that, cleansed by heavenly remedies, they may rest in your goodness.

At Communion: Be favorable, O Lord, to our supplications, and deign to place the souls of your servants and handmaids in the bosom of our patriarch Abraham, so that they may await the day of resurrection in the refreshment of your blessedness. Through [Christ our Lord].

## ANOTHER MASS FOR THE DEAD

Prayer: We ask, O Lord, that it be as in the printed editions.

Prayer over the offerings: Be present, we ask, O Lord, to our supplications, and, favorable and kind, receive this offering which we offer to you on the day of burial for the souls of your servants and handmaids. Through [Christ our Lord].

At Communion. Prayer: Almighty, everlasting God, deign to place the souls of your servants and handmaids whose day of death we commemorate in the bosom of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, so that, when the day of knowledge of you has come, you may command them to be raised among your saints and elect. Through [Christ our Lord].

Another prayer: O God, to whom alone it belongs to provide healing after death, grant, we ask, that the souls of your servants and handmaids, stripped of earthly contagions, may glory in the gift of your redemption. Through [Christ our Lord].

## MASS ON AN ANNIVERSARY

Prayer: “O God of indulgences,” etc., up to the Communion.

Prayer after Communion: Receive, O Lord, our prayers for the souls of your servants and handmaids whose anniversary we celebrate today, so that, if any stains from earthly contagions have clung to them, they may be erased by the mercy of your forgiveness. Through [Christ our Lord].

## ANOTHER MASS ON AN ANNIVERSARY

Prayer: “Grant, we ask.”

Prayer over the offerings: Sanctify, O Lord, the gifts offered, cleanse the souls of your servants and handmaids from the stains of their sins, and make them sharers in eternal life. Through [Christ our Lord].

Prayer after Communion: Incline the ears of your goodness, O Lord, to our prayers, and grant forgiveness of all sins to the souls of your servants and handmaids whose anniversary we commemorate today, so that they may rest in the pleasantness of light until the day of resurrection. Through [Christ our Lord].

## MASS FOR BISHOPS AND CLERICS

Prayer: Grant, we ask, almighty God, that the souls of your servants, bishops, priests, deacons, and all clerics, to whom you granted attainment of the mystery of your sacred altar, may share in eternal blessedness.

Prayer over the offerings: Be favorable, O Lord, to our supplications, and to the souls of your servants, bishops, priests, deacons, and all clerics, for whom we offer you the sacrifice of praise, so that you may deign to join them to the company of your saints. Through [Christ our Lord].

Communion: Filled with the draught of your sacred Body and precious Blood, we ask, almighty God, that through these holy gifts the souls of your servants, bishops, priests, deacons, and all clerics may attain the glory of eternal blessedness. Through [Christ our Lord].

## MASS FOR BISHOPS

Prayer: Grant, we ask, O Lord, that the souls of your servants, the bishops whom you adorned with sacred gifts while they dwelt in this world, may always rejoice gloriously in the heavenly seat. Through [Christ our Lord].

Prayer over the offerings: We ask, O Lord, that this offering may absolve the souls of your servants, the bishops, from all vices of the human condition. Through [Christ our Lord].

Prayer after Communion: Grant, we ask, almighty God, that you may command the souls of your servants, the bishops, to share in eternal blessedness in the assembly of the righteous. Through [Christ our Lord].

## MASS FOR A PRIEST

[Col. 0948B]

Prayer: O God, who [are] among the apostolic [ministers], etc.

Prayer over the offerings: Receive, we ask, O Lord, the sacrifices which we offer for the souls of your servants, the priests, so that those to whom you granted the priestly mystery in this world you may also grant the reward.

Prayer after Communion: Be favorable, O Lord, to our supplications, and deign to join the souls of your servants, the priests, to eternal joys in the land of the living. Through [Christ our Lord].

## MASS FOR DEACONS

Prayer: Be present, O Lord, to our supplications, and grant that the souls of your servants, the deacons and all clerics, may obtain the abundance of your favor and forgiveness, and grant them a dwelling in perpetual light. Through [Christ our Lord].

Prayer over the offerings: We offer you, O Lord, sacrifices of praise for the souls of your servants, the deacons and all clerics, so that eternal light may possess them among the number of your faithful. Through [Christ our Lord].

Prayer after Communion: Almighty, everlasting God, graciously receive our prayers for the souls of your servants, the deacons and all clerics, and grant them a place of light in the region of your saints. Through [Christ our Lord].

## COMMON MASS FOR THE DEAD

Prayer: Almighty, everlasting God, to whom supplication is never offered without hope of mercy, be favorable to the souls of your servants and handmaids, so that you may make those who departed this life confessing your name members of the number of your saints. Through [Christ our Lord].

Prayer over the offerings: Be favorable, O Lord, we ask, to the souls of your servants and handmaids, for whom we offer you sacrifices of reconciliation, so that, because they remained in this life with Catholic faith, an eternal recompense may be granted to them in the future. Through [Christ our Lord].

Prayer after Communion: Grant, we ask, almighty God, that you may cause the souls of your servants and handmaids, received by the angels of light, to be led into the prepared dwellings of the blessed. Through [Christ our Lord].

## MASS FOR THE COMMUNITY

Prayer: O God, giver of forgiveness, etc.

At Communion: O God, life of the living, hope of the dying, salvation of all who hope in you, graciously grant that the souls of our community, freed from the darkness of this mortality, may, through the intercession of blessed Mary ever-virgin, rejoice in perpetual light with all your saints. Through [Christ our Lord].

## MASS FOR ONE WHO, PREVENTED BY DEATH, WISHED TO RECEIVE PENANCE BUT COULD NOT

Prayer: Almighty, everlasting God, in whose power the human condition rests, absolve, we ask, the souls of your servants and handmaids from all sins, and do not let them lose the fruit of penance, which their will desired but death prevented them from receiving. Through [Christ our Lord].

Prayer over the offerings: May the offering of the present sacrifice satisfy you, O Lord, for the souls of your servants and handmaids, so that they may find the forgiveness of sins which they sought, and may receive, by compensation through the penance they desired, what they could not fulfill by the service of the tongue. Through [Christ our Lord].

At Communion: O God, from whom every good thing beneficial to humankind is hoped for, grant through these holy gifts which we have received that, just as you granted the souls of your servants and handmaids the will to desire the fruit of penance, so, in your mercy, you may grant the forgiveness they desired. Through [Christ our Lord].

## GENERAL MASS

Prayer: Through the intercessions of your saints, we ask, O Lord, protect us by your grace, and extend your mercy everywhere to your servants and handmaids whose commemoration we make and whose alms we have received, and also to those joined to us by friendship or blood relationship, so that, defended from assaults, they may be saved by your help; and deign to join to the company of your elect the souls of your servants and handmaids, namely, all the faithful Catholic orthodox, whose commemoration we make, whose bodies rest in this cemetery and in all the cemeteries of the faithful, and whose names appear to be written upon your holy altar. Through [Christ our Lord].

Prayer over the offerings: Be favorable, O Lord, to our supplications, and kindly receive these offerings which we bring to be consecrated to your name for the safety of your servants and handmaids, and for the souls of all the faithful orthodox dead, whose names appear to be written upon your holy altar, so that, by your mercy, the offering of the present sacrifice may bring refreshment to their souls. Through [Christ our Lord].

At Communion: May the reception of the divine sacrament and the glorious prayer of your saints purify us, we ask, O Lord, and grant forgiveness of all sins to the souls of your servants and handmaids whose commemoration we make. Through [Christ our Lord].

## COMMON MASS FOR THE LIVING AND THE DEAD

Prayer: By your goodness, we ask, O Lord, release us from the bonds of all our offenses; and, through the intercession of blessed and glorious Mary ever-Virgin, Mother of God, together with all your saints, preserve in all holiness the apostolic lord, our bishops, priors, and abbots, all the communities entrusted to them, our kings and princes, all the Christian people, and us your servants and our places; cleanse from vices and enlighten with virtues all who are joined to us by blood, marriage, or friendship; grant us peace and health; remove visible and invisible enemies; repel carnal desires; grant wholesome air; rescue us from evil and sudden death; bestow charity upon our enemies; and grant eternal life in the land of the living to all the faithful, living and dead. Through [Christ our Lord].

Prayer over the offerings: O God, who by the sacrifice of the singular Body released the sins of the whole world, appeased by this offering, wipe away the stains of our crimes and forgive the sins of all Christian faithful, living and dead, and grant them eternal rewards, Savior of the world.

At Communion: May the heavenly sacraments we have received, we ask, O Lord, wipe away all our crimes and repel far from us every perversity and weakness, as well as the rage of enemies and sudden death, through the merits of blessed Mary ever-Virgin and all your saints; and may they benefit all the faithful, living and dead, for whose salvation they have been offered to you. Through [Christ our Lord].

## MASS FOR BENEFACTORS

Prayer: O God, who through the grace of the Holy Spirit poured the gifts of charity into the hearts of your faithful, grant your servants and handmaids, for whom we implore your clemency, health of mind and body, so that they may love you with all their strength and accomplish with complete love what is pleasing to you. Through [Christ our Lord].

Prayer over the offerings: Have mercy, we ask, O Lord, on your servants and handmaids, for whom we offer this sacrifice of praise to your majesty, so that through these holy gifts they may obtain the grace of heavenly blessing and acquire the glory of eternal blessedness. Through [Christ our Lord].

At Communion: As we partake of the divine mysteries, we ask, O Lord, that these saving sacraments may benefit those for whose love we have offered them to your majesty, bringing prosperity and peace. Through [Christ our Lord].

# HERE BEGINS THE OFFICE OF THE BREVIARY ACCORDING TO THE ORDER OF THE HERMITAGE OF THE HOLY CROSS OF FONTE AVELLANA

[Col. 0949]

[Col. 0949D] First Sunday of Advent. At Vespers on Saturday, reading: “Behold, the days are coming,” etc., up to “on the earth.” R\. “Gabriel was sent.” V\. “He will give him.” Hymn, etc., up to the entire prayer, as in the printed editions. Here the antiphon of the Cross is omitted until the octave of Epiphany, and this antiphon of blessed Mary is said: “The angel Gabriel was sent to Mary, a virgin betrothed to Joseph.” V\. “Grace has been poured forth.” R\. “Therefore.” Prayer: “O God, who [from] blessed [Mary],” etc.

Invitatory: “Behold, the King will come; let us go to meet our Savior.”

All the lessons of this breviary are remarkably brief. The first four lessons of the first nocturn of this Sunday comprise our first and second lessons up to the responsory. This indicates that this codex was written at a time when monastic discipline had withdrawn from our once most holy monastery.

R\. The first, second, and third responsories of the first nocturn are the same as in our printed editions. The fourth: “Hail, Mary, full of grace,” up to “he said to her.”

R\. The first of the second nocturn is the second of the printed editions. The second, however: “Hear the word of the Lord, all nations,” etc., up to “shout.” The third: “Behold the Virgin,” etc., up to “forever.” The fourth: “Strangers will not pass through,” up to “and condensed.”

The remaining responsories are also different from ours and are not reproduced, lest the volume become too cumbersome. After the antiphon at the Benedictus there is an antiphon of the Virgin: “Hail, Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with you; blessed are you among women, alleluia.” V\. “Poured out.” Prayer: “O God, who [from] blessed Mary,” etc.

At Prime, antiphon: “Alleluia.” This reading is said on all Sundays and feast days up to the Nativity, and from Septuagesima to Easter: “O Lord, have mercy on us,” etc.

At Sext: “Our consciences,” etc.

At None, prayer: Be favorable, O Lord, to all who truthfully await you, so that at the coming of your Son, our Lord, we may be presented to you with actions pleasing to you. Through [Christ our Lord].

The remaining rites during the week differ from ours; it would be lengthy to copy them.

Second Sunday: Invitatory: “Rise, let us keep watch; come, let us adore, because we do not know the hour when the Lord will come.”

Invitatory of the third Sunday: “Behold, the King will come,” etc.

[Col. 0951C] Of the fourth Sunday, however, the invitatory is: “Behold, the fullness of time has come, in which God sent his Son, born of a Virgin, made under the law.”

## ON THE VIGIL OF THE NATIVITY OF THE LORD

The antiphons are as in the printed editions, but the Psalms are: “Praise, servants”; “Those who trust”; “When the Lord restored”; “Remember.”

Reading: “Therefore my people shall know my name on that day, because I myself who was speaking—behold, I am here.”

R\. “The Word became flesh and dwelt among us. And we saw his glory, glory as of the Only-Begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth.”

V\. “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God. And the Word was God.” And we saw [his glory]. Glory.

Hymn:

> God, Redeemer of the nations,  
> show forth the Virgin’s child;  
> let every age marvel;  
> such a birth befits the Lord.  
>   
> Not from human seed,  
> but from a mystical breath,  
> the Word of God became flesh,  
> and the fruit of the womb blossomed.  
>   
> The Virgin’s womb swells,  
> yet the enclosure of modesty remains;  
> the banners of virtues shine,  
> and God moves within the temple.  
>   
> Proceeding from his bridal chamber,  
> the royal hall of modesty,  
> a giant of twofold substance,  
> joyful to run his course.  
>   
> His going forth is from the Father,  
> his return is to the Father;  
> his journey extends even to the underworld,  
> his return to the seat of God.  
>   
> Equal to the eternal Father,  
> he attains the triumph of the flesh,  
> strengthening the weakness of our body  
> with enduring power.  
>   
> Now your manger shines,  
> and a new light breathes upon us;  
> may nothing obscure it from us,  
> and may it shine with unceasing faith.  
>   
> Praise and honor, etc.

V\. “With you is principality on the day of your power.”

The antiphon at the Magnificat and the prayer are as in the printed editions.

For the honor of holy Mary, antiphon: “Behold, Mary has given birth,” etc., up to “of the world,” with alleluia.

After Lauds have ended, the following rubric appears: This antiphon is to be said at Lauds in honor of holy Mary until the octave of Epiphany.

Antiphon: “The Virgin conceived by the Word, remained a virgin, and gave birth to the King of all kings.”

After Vespers on the day of the Nativity of the Lord the following is given. This antiphon is said until the octave of Epiphany: “The Virgin Mother, knowing no man, gave birth without pain. She alone, the Virgin, suckled the Savior of the ages, himself the King of angels, at her breast full from heaven.”

## ON THE VIGIL OF EPIPHANY

Among the principal items appointed in the office of this day are the following.

Antiphon at the Magnificat: “To Christ was given dominion and the honor of kingship; every people, tribe, and tongue will serve him forever. Alleluia.”

Prayer: May the splendor of the coming feast illumine our hearts, we ask, O Lord, so that we may be able to escape the darkness of this world and reach the homeland of eternal brightness. Through the same [Lord].

On the day itself of Epiphany, this prayer is appointed at Sext:

O God, illuminator of all nations, grant your peoples joy in perpetual peace, and pour into our hearts that splendid light which you breathed into the minds of the three Magi. Through our Lord.

At None, prayer: O God, who first consecrated this day of the calling of the nations, and showed yourself manifest to us through the star of your light, grant, we ask, that the new and wondrous brightness of heaven may always arise in us.

In place of the prayer of the second nocturn during the octave, the following prayer is given:

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that, with the star of the Savior of the world as guide, the revealed birth may always be disclosed and increase in our minds. Through the same [Lord].

## FIRST SUNDAY AFTER THE OCTAVE OF EPIPHANY

After the lesson, etc., up to and including the Apostles’ Creed, the following occurs as in the printed editions:

“Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good.”  
R\. “For his mercy endures forever.”

Confession: I confess to God and to all the saints and to you, Fathers, through my fault, because I have sinned greatly through pride in thought, suggestion, consent, words, and deed. I beseech you: pray for me, a wretched sinner.

Absolution: May almighty God have mercy on you and forgive you all your past, present, and future sins; may he free you from every evil, preserve, strengthen, and fortify you in every good work, and lead you to eternal life. Amen.

Chapter: Turn us, O God our Savior. And turn away your anger from us. Deign, O Lord, on this day to preserve us without sin. Let your mercy, O Lord, be upon us. As we have hoped in you. Let your priests be clothed with righteousness. And let your saints exult. Send them, O Lord, help from the holy place. And from Zion protect them. O Lord, hear my prayer. And let my cry come to you.

Creed: “Whoever wishes to be saved.”

Chapter: May God bless us, our God; may God bless us, and may all the ends of the earth fear him.

The Lord be with you. And with your spirit.

The prayer is the same as that in the printed editions for the feast of the Trinity.

After the lesson: “Holy Mary.” The following rubric is read: On ordinary days, say three times here: “O God, come to my aid,” with the Gloria.

At Compline everything is as in the printed editions up to “who made heaven and earth.”

Chapter: Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good. For his mercy endures forever.

The confession and absolution are as above.

“Turn us, O God,” etc., up to the Creed.

Chapter: Blessed are you, O Lord, God of our fathers. And worthy of praise and glorious forever. Let us bless the Father and the Son with the Holy Spirit. Let us praise and exalt him above all forever. Blessed are you in the firmament of heaven. And worthy of praise and glorious forever.

May almighty God bless us. Amen.

Deign, O Lord, this night to preserve us without sin. Let your mercy, O Lord, be upon us. As we have hoped in you. Let your priests be clothed with righteousness. And let your saints exult. Send them, O Lord, help from the holy place. And from Zion protect them. O Lord, hear my prayer. And let my cry come to you.

O Lord God of hosts, turn us. And show your face, and we shall be saved.

Prayer: “Visit,” etc., after which two other prayers follow:

Enlighten our darkness, we ask, O Lord, and graciously repel from us by your help all the snares of the night.

May your truth, we ask, O Lord, always remain in our hearts, and through the power of the holy cross may every falsehood of the enemy be destroyed. Through [Christ our Lord].

After Lauds on the Monday following the Sunday mentioned above, the following are read. These chapters are to be said at all times on weekdays at Lauds, at Terce, and at Vespers, with “Have mercy on me, O God.” At Vigils, however, at Sext and None, they are said without “Have mercy on me, O God.”

Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy. Our Father. And lead us not [into temptation].

Chapter: I said: O Lord, have mercy on me. Heal my soul, because I have sinned against you. Turn again, O Lord, for a little while. And be entreated on behalf of your servants. Let your mercy, O Lord, be upon us. As we have hoped in you. Let your priests be clothed with righteousness. And let your saints exult. Send them, O Lord, help from the holy place. And from Zion protect them. O Lord, hear my prayer. And let my cry come to you.

Psalm: “Have mercy.”

Chapter: O Lord God of hosts, turn us. Show your face, and we shall be saved.

The Lord be with you. And with [your spirit].

Prayer: Look graciously, O Lord, upon the morning vows of those who entreat you, and illumine the hidden places of our heart with the remedy of your mercy, so that dark desires may not hold those whom the heavenly light of grace has restored, Jesus Christ the Son, etc.

## SUFFRAGES OF THE SAINTS

These are said at all times except on the feasts of the Nativity of the Lord, the Resurrection, the Ascension, and Pentecost, and their octaves.

Antiphon of the Cross: “But it is fitting for us to glory in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ. The whole earth,” etc.

Prayer: Be present to us, we ask, O Lord, and defend perpetually by the assistance of the holy cross those whom you make rejoice in its honor. Through [Christ our Lord].

Antiphon of blessed Mary: “Glorious Mother and unwedded Virgin, Queen of the world, intercede for us with the Lord our God.”

“Grace has been poured out,” etc.

Prayer: “Of your servants.”

Antiphon of Saint Michael: “Michael the archangel, come to the aid of the people of God.”

“In the sight of the angels.”

Prayer: O God, who [arranged all things] in wondrous order.

Antiphon of Saint Benedict: “There was a man venerable in life, Benedict by grace and by name.”

“The mouth of the righteous.”

Prayer: “Intercession.”

Antiphon of Saint John the Baptist: “Among those born of women no one has arisen greater than John the Baptist.”
