**The sign of Lord Conrad, the unconquered Roman emperor augustus. (L. M.)**

Odalric, chancellor, acting on behalf of Aribo, archchaplain, authenticated this.

Given on the thirteenth day before the kalends of February, in the fourteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1031, in the seventh year of the reign of Lord Conrad II, and in the fourth year of his empire.

Done at Altstete.

### XII. For the Paderborn Church. (Year 1031.)

[ERHARD, *Cod. diplom. Westph.*, p. 92.]

[Col. 1055C]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity. Conrad, by the clemency ordained by God, emperor augustus of the Romans.

We wish it to be known to the whole community of God’s faithful and of our own people how, out of regard for divine reward, and through the intervention of our most beloved consort Gisla, empress augusta, as well as of our beloved son King Henry, and because of the constant service so often faithfully rendered to us by Meinwerk, bishop of the Paderborn Church, we have granted in ownership to that same church, built in honor of Saint Mary, Mother of God, Saint Kilian the martyr, and Saint Liborius, bishop and confessor, the estates of Bennanhusun, Ualabroch, and Dadanbroch, situated in the districts of Wetiga and Tilithi and in the county of Widukind, together with everything legally belonging to that estate, with male and female slaves, courtyards, buildings, fields, open fields, cultivated and uncultivated lands, meadows, pastures, woods, hunting rights, waters and watercourses, fisheries, millstones, mills, roads and trackless ways, exits and entrances, things acquired and things to be acquired, and every benefit that can in any way be written down or named.

We transfer them completely from our right and dominion into the right and dominion of that church, on the condition that the aforesaid bishop and his successors thereafter have free power over the same estate to hold, exchange, or do whatever they deem beneficial to the church, without anyone’s opposition.

And so that the authority of our grant may remain stable and unshaken throughout the ancient courses of the ages, we have confirmed with our own hand the page written concerning it and ordered it to be sealed with the impression of our seal.

**The sign of Lord Conrad, the unconquered Roman emperor augustus. (L. M.)**

Odalric, chancellor, acting on behalf of Aribo, archchaplain, authenticated this.

Given on the eleventh day before the kalends of March, in the fourteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s [Col. 1056B] Incarnation 1031, in the seventh year of the reign of Lord Conrad II, and in the fourth year of his empire.

Done at Goslar.

### XIII. For the Paderborn Church. (Year 1031.)

[ERHARD, *Cod. diplom. Westph.*, p. 93.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Conrad, by the favor of divine clemency, emperor augustus of the Romans.

If we generously bestow upon one of our bishops, mindful of his faithful service, something from what is assigned to our right, we undoubtedly believe that he will afterward be readier and much more zealous in prayer and service to us. Therefore, we wish it to be clear to all lovers of Christ and of ourselves, present and future, how Wicilo approached our serenity, humbly asking us to receive into our imperial hand the estate called Sannanabiki, situated in the following villages: Hornan, Frodinctorp, Vinesbiki, Rafseti, Knechtahusen, Buckinhusen, Bennanhusen, Scuni, Berchem, Homan, and Holthusen, at the petition and with the approval of himself, his wife Oda, his daughter Cecilia, and Gerburch and her son Odo; and, in exchange, to place under their control the estate of Zurici, which had belonged to our ownership.

Thus, satisfying their desire through the counsel of our leading men, we amicably relinquished to them what was their right and what had been our right. After all these matters had thus been settled, we gave as an estate the aforesaid Sannanabiki, which at that time was judged to be our property, situated in the county of Widukind and the district of Wetiga, with all the benefits belonging to it: courtyards, buildings, fields, open fields, cultivated and uncultivated lands, meadows, pastures, woods, hunting rights, waters and watercourses, fisheries, millstones, mills, roads and trackless ways, exits and entrances, things acquired and things to be acquired.

Because of the loving intervention of our wife Gisla, empress augusta, and because the petition of our most beloved son King Henry was not to be refused, and also at the intervention of Margrave Hermann, we granted it in ownership to Meinwerk, venerable bishop, and to his church, built in honor of Saint Mary, Mother of God, the most precious martyr Kilian, and the most glorious confessor Liborius, on the condition that he and his successors thereafter have free power over it to hold, transfer, sell, exchange, or do whatever they wish, provided that it serves the benefit of the aforesaid saints’ church.

For we have remembered that not only in this matter, but also in other estates which, God willing, we shall yet grant to him, his constant service has been more devoted and more frequent than that of our other bishops, and has proved reliable not merely once but almost at every time.

And so that the authority of our grant may remain stable and unshaken throughout the passage of time, we have confirmed this decree, written concerning it, below with our own hand [Col. 1057B], strengthened it, and ordered it to be carefully marked with the impression of our seal.

**The sign of Lord Conrad, the unconquered Roman emperor augustus. (L. M.)**

Odalric, chancellor, authenticated this.

Given on the third day before the nones of August, in the fourteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1031, in the seventh year of the reign of Lord Conrad II, and in the fifth year of his empire.

Done at Immeteshusun.

### XIV. Emperor Conrad I confirms various rights and the county of the city itself to Hubald, bishop of Cremona. (Year 1031.)

[MURATORI, *Antiq. Ital.* II, 73.]

[Col. 1057C]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Conrad, by the favor of divine clemency, emperor augustus of the Romans.

If we strive to exalt and defend holy and venerable places, we do not doubt that this certainly belongs to the condition of our kingdom. Therefore, let the whole community of our faithful, present and future, know that Hubald, venerable bishop of the holy Church of Cremona, through the intervention of our most beloved wife Gisla, empress, humbly approached our clemency, asking that, for God’s sake and for the remedy of our soul, we confirm and strengthen the decrees granted to his church by our predecessors.

Agreeing to his worthy petitions, insofar as we can do so justly and lawfully, we confirm and strengthen them. Thus, whatever rights of *curatura*, toll, transport duty, or river toll, and the county within the aforesaid city or outside it for a distance of five miles, are contained in the decrees of that church, let both he and his successors hold, possess, and firmly retain them.

Moreover, let them likewise perpetually exact the other customary dues and the *angariae* (compulsory services) which his predecessors formerly possessed as belonging to that authority, as well as the *fotrum* (provision levy) from that city, which was customarily collected for our service, the pigs of the *Arimanni*, and the lodging obligations. We therefore command and order that no duke, count, etc.

[Col. 1058A]

**The sign of Lord Conrad, most serene emperor augustus.**

Bruno, chancellor, acting in the place of Aribo, archbishop of Mainz and archchancellor, authenticated this.

Given on the third day before the kalends of March, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1031, in the fourteenth indiction, in the sixth year of Lord Conrad’s reign and the fourth year of his imperial rule.

Done successfully at Goslar. Amen.

### XV. Conrad II, king and first emperor, confirms all privileges and possessions to Hubald, bishop of Cremona, and to his church. (Year 1031.)

[MURATORI, *Antiq. Ital.* I, 417.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Conrad, [Col. 1058B] by the favor of divine clemency, emperor augustus of the Romans.

If holy and venerable places, etc. Therefore, let the whole community of the faithful of the holy Church of God and of our people, present and future, know that Hubald, venerable bishop of the holy Church of Cremona, through the gracious intervention of Gisla, beloved consort of our empire and empress, earnestly and humbly asked our majesty to confirm and strengthen, for the love of God and the safety of our empire, by our imperial authority, the decrees granted to his church by our predecessor kings and emperors, especially Berengar, Rudolf, and the Ottos and Henry, illustrious emperors augustus of blessed memory.

Agreeing to his worthy petitions, insofar as we can do so justly and lawfully, etc., we confirm and strengthen for the same holy Church of Cremona whatever rights of *curatura*, toll, transport duty, or river toll, by whatever means, belonged to the public revenue from the aforesaid city of Cremona—both from the portion of the county belonging to that city and from the portion of the estate of Sexpilas—as well as the riverbanks and fisheries from Vulpariolo to the head of the Adda, with the mills and their milling dues, namely, five Cremonese *modii* of grain for each mill, and the customary tax of each ship, namely four *orales* of salt for each ship, as contained in the records made before Cesso the deacon and Lord Otto’s imperial envoy, and Heribert the chancellor, who were sitting in judgment at Cremona, and legally confirmed by the authority and command of the aforementioned Emperor Otto [Col. 1058D].

Also the palisade duty of four denarii, together with payment from all ships, and the *curatura* of all the commercial transactions carried out on the aforesaid bank, both by residents of the city and by others who come from elsewhere for trade, together with all the rights and customs of the church. As for the jurisdiction of the city, inside and outside it for a distance of five miles, etc. If anyone, therefore, etc.

**The sign of Lord Conrad, most serene emperor augustus.**

Bruno, chancellor, acting in the place of Aribo, archbishop of Mainz and archchancellor, authenticated this.

[Col. 1059A] Given on the third day before the kalends of March, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1031, in the fourteenth indiction, in the sixth year of the reign of Lord Conrad II, and in the fourth year of his empire.

Done successfully at Goslar. Amen.

### XVI. Letter of Emperor Conrad I to the citizens of Cremona, instructing them to satisfy the bishop of Cremona concerning certain grievances. (Around the year 1031.)

[MURATORI, *Antiq. Ital.* VI, 53.]

Conrad, by the grace of God emperor augustus of the Romans, sends greetings to all the citizens of Cremona.

We wish and firmly command that you pay the money which you promised your lord bishop for the damage, burning, and plunder that you carried out against his castles, [Col. 1059B] if you care to retain our favor. As for the church’s land, just as Bishop Landulf held it in the time of Lord Emperor Henry, we wish this present lord of yours likewise to hold it peacefully.

Regarding the church’s woods that lie around the city, concerning which you daily act in opposition to him and use them against his will, we command that you no longer interfere in them, unless you have given him a payment such as Milan, Pavia, and Piacenza give him. Do not under any circumstances retain Osbert or his peers against the will of your lord, if you ever wish to enjoy our favor.

Lead the murderers and robbers who are within the city, concerning whom the bishop wishes to administer law and justice, in good faith into his presence, and assist him in judging them lawfully.

### XVII. For the Paderborn Church. (Year 1032.)

[ERHARD, *Cod. diplom. Westph.*, p. 92.]

[Col. 1059C]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Conrad, by the favor of divine clemency, emperor augustus of the Romans.

Let the diligence of all God’s faithful and our own people, present and future, know how, for our faithful Meinwerk, bishop of Paderborn, and the church over which, by God’s gift, he presides, because of the intervention and petition of our beloved wife Gisla, empress augusta, our most beloved son King Henry, and Egilbert, venerable bishop of the Church of Freising, and because of his frequent and devoted service, we have granted as an estate a certain property of ours called Gardenebiki, situated in the district of Lacni and in the county of Count Hermann, together with everything we possessed in the villages of Hwinadal, Molduggane, and Liudulveshusun, situated in the same district and in the county of the aforementioned Count H.

We grant it with all that belongs to it: courtyards, buildings, male and female slaves dwelling there, fields, open fields, cultivated and uncultivated lands, meadows, pastures, woods, hunting rights, waters and watercourses, fisheries, millstones, mills, roads and trackless ways, exits and entrances, things acquired and things to be acquired, and every benefit that can be written down or named.

We transfer it completely from our right and dominion into his right and dominion, on the further condition that our aforesaid faithful bishop M., whether he is near or far away, may recognize that we are not forgetful of his service to us, and that he and his successors thereafter have free power over the estates named above to hold, transfer, sell, exchange, or do whatever they wish, provided that it is for the use of the aforesaid church, built and consecrated in honor of Saint Liborius.

And so that the authority of this grant of ours may remain stable and unshaken at all times, we have ordered this decree, written concerning it and confirmed below with our own hand, to be marked with the impression of our seal.

**The sign of Lord Conrad, the unconquered Roman [Col. 1060B] emperor augustus. (L. M.)**

Odalric, chancellor, acting in the place of Archbishop Bardo, authenticated this.

Given on the fifteenth day before the kalends of February, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1032, in the eighth year of the reign of Lord Conrad II, and in the fifth year of his empire.

Done successfully at Hiltiwardeshusun. Amen.

### XVIII. For the Paderborn Church. (Year 1032.)

[ERHARD, *Codex diplomaticus Westphaliae*, p. 94.]

### C.

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, CONRAD, by the favor of divine clemency, Roman emperor Augustus.

Because, by the ordering of divine clemency, we surpass other mortals, it is fitting that we strive in every way to obey the will of him by whose gift we excel. Therefore we wish it to be known to all the faithful of Christ and of ourselves, present and future, how, at the intervention and request of our beloved wife Gisla, empress Augusta, and of our son Henry, king, and of Egilbert, bishop of the church of Freising, we have granted and bestowed by this imperial charter, as a hereditary possession, upon our faithful Meginwerch, venerable bishop of Paderborn, and upon the church built and consecrated in honor of holy Mary, Mother of God, and of Saint Chilian the martyr and Saint Liborius the confessor, over which he presides by God’s gift, all the comital authority which Count Hermann holds in those three districts—Auga, Netega, and Hessiga—with every right justly and legally belonging to that county; and all estates held in those districts in our hands, as well as those to be acquired later, together with everything properly belonging to them: courtyards, buildings, bondmen and bondwomen, fields, cultivated and uncultivated lands, meadows, pastures, open country, woods, hunting rights, waters and watercourses, fisheries, mills and millworks, roads and trackless places, outgoings and incomings, things acquired and things to be sought, and every utility that may in any way arise from them, all opposition by any person having been removed.

This grant is made with the further provision that our aforesaid faithful M., the bishop, whether he be far away or near at hand, may recognize that we are not forgetful of his service to us, and that he and his successors may henceforth have free power over these estates to hold, transfer, sell, exchange, or do whatever they please with them, provided that it is for the use of the aforesaid church. To give this grant full validity in God’s name, we have confirmed it below with our own hand and ordered it to be marked with the impression of our seal.

Sign of Lord Conrad, the unconquered Roman emperor Augustus. (L. M.)

Odalric, chancellor, recognized this in place of Archbishop Bardo.

Given on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of February, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1032; in the eighth year of the reign of Lord Conrad II and the fifth of his empire.

Enacted at Fritzlar, successfully. Amen.

### XIX. For the Church of Paderborn. (Year 1032.)

[ECHARD, *Codex diplomaticus Westphaliae*, p. 95.]

### C.

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, CONRAD, by the favor of divine clemency, Roman emperor Augustus.

Just as we rejoice in the ready and continual services of our faithful, so it also seems worthy and just to us that we should cause them to rejoice in rewards worthy of them. Therefore let the diligence of all the faithful of God and of ourselves, present and future, know how, at the intervention and request of our beloved wife Gisla, empress Augusta, and of our dearest son Henry, king, we have given and permanently bestowed as a hereditary possession, by this imperial charter, upon our faithful Meginwerch, venerable bishop, and upon the church over which he presides by God’s gift, built in honor of holy Mary, Mother of God, Saint Chilian the martyr, and Saint Liborius, distinguished confessor, six unfree persons, whose names are these: Thiethard, priest; Liuza; Heregrim; Ethilier; Athalward; and Wieburch, together with all their possessions. We have wholly transferred them from our right and lordship into his right and lordship and bestowed them, with the provision that our aforesaid faithful Meginwerch, the bishop, and his successors may henceforth have free power over these bondmen and bondwomen to sell, transfer, exchange, or do whatever they please with them, provided that it is for the use of his church called Paderborn. And so that the authority of this grant may possess full validity in God’s name, we have ordered this charter, written for that purpose and confirmed below with our own hand, to be marked with our seal.

Sign of Lord Conrad, the unconquered Roman emperor Augustus. (L. M.)

Odalric, chancellor, recognized this in place of Archbishop Bardo.

Given on the twelfth day before the Kalends of September, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1031; in the eighth year of the reign of Lord Conrad II and the sixth of his empire.

Enacted at Magdeburg.

### XX. Privilege of Emperor Conrad for the Monastery of Saint Martin. (Year 1033.)

[ERHARD, *Codex diplomaticus Westphaliae*, p. 96.]

### C.

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, CONRAD, by the favor of divine clemency, Roman emperor Augustus.

If we show zeal in building monasteries or give our assent to others who join in the same undertaking, we do not doubt that this will benefit us not only for temporal advantage but also for the good of the eternal kingdom. Therefore let it be known to all who profess the Christian religion, present and future, how, at the intervention and request of our beloved wife Gisla, empress Augusta, and of our most cherished son Henry, king, and also of Aribo, archbishop of the church of Mainz, and Pilgrim, archbishop of the church of Cologne, and likewise with the consent of all our faithful who were then present there, we granted Sigebert, bishop of the church of Minden, permission to build there a monastery in honor of Saint Martin.

Moreover, let everyone’s diligence know how the bishop of that see had exchanged with the monastery of Saint Martin the one curtilage on which the monastery, cloister, and cemetery were built, six curtilages on both sides of the monastery, and three manses of salic land with the estate held by its own right, namely twelve manses from the property of the monastery of Saint Peter. At the place called Hildiwardingahusun and in other villages legally belonging to the same place, he gave seven manses in exchange; at Chizzindorf, two manses; at Lohe, one mansus; and at Westirbracha, one mansus. In these four places there were twenty-five bondmen and bondwomen.

For the brothers serving God in the aforesaid monastery, he transferred for their use an estate called Chemmin, which, through the intervention of our beloved wife G. and our son H., king, he had received from our right into his own right and authority. He also granted for the use of the same brothers the wine tithe at Rotherisdorfa which he had acquired from us. In addition, he assigned another vineyard in the same place for the use of his successors, on the condition that they inflict no injustice or molestation upon the brothers with respect to the wine tithe; and whenever they drink wine from it, they should bear in mind that previously they had not possessed so much wine for their entire bishopric that it could fill a cup. Thus they should be more frequent intercessors with God for us, our beloved wife G., and our son H., king, at whose request we transferred these vineyards in ownership to S., bishop of the aforesaid see.

Furthermore, the same bishop transferred to the monastery of Saint Martin the following places belonging to his right: Egisberun, Wolgatingahusun, one mansus and the use of the woodland at Diotanhusun, and such an estate as he possessed at Nianburg. In addition, three manses at Ubhusen; one mansus at Loha; and in the district of Lainga, in the villages Triburin, Stocheim, Helingaburstalla, and Holinbeke, six manses. In the district of Marstem, in the village called Brunhildisfort, two manses; at Hupida, one mansus; at Oribe, two manses; and at Volkeressun, two manses. In the district of Cizide, in the village Herisivroda, two manses; at Munnere, one mansus, with the use of the saltworks. Likewise at Munnere, one curtilage, with the use of the saltworks; at Bodukun, one mansus; at Beddure, one mansus; at Hemezungahusum, one mansus; at Helan, five manses; at Uanebeke, one mansus; at Fridegerssun, one mansus; at Nisinun, two manses; at Lierbeke, one mansus; at Folchardesdorf, the use of the woodland with three curtilages; at Hervide, one mansus; at Hemmincburun, four manses; at Uvoluaradingahusun, one curtilage with the use of the woodland.

At Eildissun, one curtilage with the use of the woodland; at Haddenhusun, half a mansus; at Ekishusun, two manses; at Nitalstete, one mansus; at Rodun, one mansus; at Holzhusun, three manses; at Lippeke, one curtilage with the use of the woodland. At Retbere, half a mansus; at Sueverdun, four manses and two and a half manses of willow-land; at Honredere, six and a half manses; at Eddorunhusun, two manses; at Morsilen, one mansus; at Nitalstete, ten manses, with every use belonging thereunto; at Weluen, four manses.

To all these places noted above he transferred permanently to the aforesaid monastery of Saint M. every estate that he then held under his authority or later acquired, or that he received by a lawful exchange involving the aforesaid places or by another legal arrangement, except those which he had assigned to other monasteries, together with bondmen and bondwomen, villages, courtyards, buildings, fields, cultivated and uncultivated lands, roads and trackless places, outgoings and incomings, things acquired and things to be sought, meadows, pastures, woods, hunting rights, waters and watercourses, fisheries, mills and the use of the woodland, as well as all appurtenances that can be spoken of or named.

But so that the same monastery might be placed in greater security, and so that the goods given to it might be less readily dissipated by its successors or by others, he placed it under the protection of the monastery of Saint Peter and decreed that it should pay that monastery each year a census of five solidi. He also established that every year, on the feast of Saint M., the bishop of that see should come with the brothers of the monastery of Saint Peter to the aforesaid monastery, celebrate the solemn masses, and fulfill the duties of charity by other demonstrations. But if something else should prevent him from being present, the brothers should assemble there and do the same together, so that in this way concord and friendship might be strengthened between them, and through this mutual expression of charity they might be joined together in unanimity in the service of God.

Moreover, let it be known to all how we wish that this monastery of Saint M. and the brothers serving God there should be defended under our imperial protection and that of our son H. and our other successors. No successor of that bishop shall have power in any way to destroy the monastery’s property or take anything from those goods, because the aforesaid bishop S. began to build the monastery from its foundations and transferred no other estates to it except those which he acquired from our gift into his own right or which he himself held by right of ownership without any opposition.

Therefore, if anyone is a destroyer of that monastery or a dissipator of the aforesaid goods, let him truly know that the same monastery and the brothers serving God there have certain refuge in us and in our successors. And so that this charter of our grant may remain stable and unshaken for all time, we have ordered this document, written for that purpose and confirmed below with our own hand, to be marked with the impression of our seal.

Sign of Lord Conrad, the unconquered Roman emperor.

Burchard, chancellor, recognized this in place of Pardon, archchaplain.

Given on the sixth day before the Nones of July, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1033, in the first indiction; in the ninth year of the reign of Lord Conrad II and the sixth of his imperial rule.

Enacted at Merseburg, successfully. Amen.

### XXI. Charter of Conrad for the Church of Paderborn. (Year 1033.)

[ERHARD, *Codex diplomaticus Westphaliae*, p. 98.]

+ C. In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, CONRAD, by the favor of divine clemency, Roman emperor Augustus.

Let it be known to all the faithful of Christ and of ourselves, present and future, how our predecessor, the emperor Henry, of blessed memory, whose mind was always watchful for the improvement and enlargement of the churches of God, taking pity on the poverty of the church of Paderborn, bestowed upon it with a generous hand many goods, both estates and other resources, for the love of God and because of the constant and devoted service of its bishop Meginwerch, whom he loved.

Among these things he also lawfully gave, transferred, and assigned to that church, through imperial munificence, the county formerly held by Count Duodico. After that predecessor of ours had died, we, who had risen to the kingdom in his place, took that same county away from the aforesaid church, at the suggestion of the bishop of Mainz, and, while still inexperienced in the kingdom and persuaded by an unjust counsel, irrationally transferred and conveyed it into the right of the church of Mainz.

But when, by the grace of God, our imperial power had been increasingly confirmed and strengthened in the kingdom, Meginwerch, a most devoted servant and lover of the emperors, diligently striving in Martha’s assiduous service, did not cease or rest from petitioning and serving until, admonished by the prompting of almighty God, in whose hand are the hearts of kings, and through the intervention of our beloved wife Gisla and of our son Henry, the magnificent king, we lawfully returned, restored, and re-granted to his church, namely the church of Paderborn, the entire county formerly held by Count Bernhard, which lies in the districts of Hesse, Nitergo, Netgo, and Ohteresgo.

Taking precautions and thinking ahead lest any controversy or disagreement should later arise between these churches concerning this matter, we granted to the church of Mainz, for the confirmation of peace and by our imperial right, the county situated in Cluvinga. On our part, therefore, this was agreed and so defined: neither of those churches shall suffer any injury whatsoever concerning the aforesaid matters claimed by it.

But if anyone, led astray by diabolical persuasion, violates this grant of ours in any respect, let him know that he will incur the hatred of God and his saints and shall pay one thousand pounds of pure gold, half to our treasury and half to the rector of the aforesaid church of Paderborn. And so that this may be believed more firmly and diligently observed by all forever, we have confirmed this charter written for that purpose below with our own hand and ordered it to be marked with our seal.

Sign of Lord Conrad, the unconquered Roman emperor.

Burchard, chancellor, recognized this in place of Bardo, archchaplain.

Given on the fourth day before the Nones of August, in the first indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1033; in the ninth year of the reign of Lord Conrad II and the seventh of his imperial rule.

Enacted at Limburg, successfully. Amen.

### XXII. Privilege of Emperor Conrad I confirming all the rights of the monastery of Saint Peter at Pavia, called “In the Golden Heaven.” (Year 1033.)

[MURATORI, *Antiquitates Italicae*, I, 595.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, CONRAD, by the favor of divine clemency, emperor Augustus.

If we bestow the generosity of our benevolence upon places dedicated to God, we believe that this contributes both to the stability of our kingdoms and to the salvation of our soul. Therefore let the whole body of the faithful of the holy Church of God, present and future, know that our dearest wife Gisla approached our imperial clemency so that, for the love of God and the remedy of our soul, we might deign to assist the monastery of Saint Peter, called the Golden Heaven, and by the authority of our charter confirm and strengthen all the courts and properties which it is known previously to have possessed by whatever means; the lands and courts until now called vassals’ holdings; Munesengo; and the village and castle called Saint Peter’s; and that we might invest with all these the abbot named Alpisus, who now presides over it.

Gladly inclining our ears to her requests and caring for the welfare of our soul, for the love of God we grant, give, and in every way strengthen to the aforesaid venerable place and its abbot all the goods, properties, and possessions, and all those estates which anyone has hitherto held by benefice and which were called the vassals’ holdings, and whatever the same monastery is known to have possessed for a long time, granted by Liudprand, founder of that place.

Among other things, this includes the estate called Alpe Plana and all the goods belonging or pertaining to that estate, in whatever places they may be, with their territories and boundaries announced in each place by the charter of King Liudprand, or the tithes of those goods, however they may be cultivated there; and the church built in honor of Saint Augustine not far from the city of Genoa by Liudprand himself, founder of the aforesaid monastery; also the estates called Lardiriacus and Villarasca; the manses lying at Rovorri; and the estates of Cressiani, Turine, and Gerentiano; and at Cartiano one church of Saint Juliana with all its rights.

Also the possessions which it appears to hold in the counties of Lodi and Bergamo, namely Amfenengo with the estate called Flumbo and everything belonging to it; the estate of Saint Peter; the estate of Aribald; and the castle of Aichard in the county of Parma; and the estate called Sindesi, with all its goods and appurtenances.

Also the lands which it possesses at Luciano and Spariano and at Rosioni, with everything lying around them and pertaining to those places. Furthermore, we confirm to the aforesaid monastery and abbot the estate of Pavone, and also the estate called the Royal Estate at Roboreto, and the church of Saint Mary at Tergui, with all their appurtenances and adjacent properties, mills, fisheries, waters and watercourses, cultivated and uncultivated goods, wherever those belonging to the same estates may be found.

We confirm also all that belongs to the same place on Mount Farrato, in the counties of Vercelli and Ivrea, and in the county of Novara; whatever the same monastery appears to possess at Caselle, Ponte Corioni, and Solariolo; also the estate called Diana in the county of Albenga, and everything within and outside that city which appears to belong to the monastery.

Also the port called Rosariolum, held for a long time by the monastery itself, and all the land lying in the plain of the city of Pavia and lawfully belonging there, together with the tithes. We also give and strengthen for the same venerable place the lands which it appears to possess in the regions of Tuscany, in various counties and places.

Also the two small estates Maliace and Calavadum with Sussello and Leuco; and the chapel dedicated to Saint Mary, Mother of God, called Primasca, built in the valley of Belizona; and those lands which it appears to possess at Belingno and Liventina, with all their appurtenances. Furthermore, the estate called Vergonto and the fishery at Tauxa.

We establish, judge, order, and command in every way, and firmly decree by the authority of our predecessors, kings and emperors, that no archbishop, bishop, margrave, count, viscount, gastald, or any ministerial, no judicial authority, and no officer of the state shall presume, without any pretext, to hold a court or exercise jurisdiction in the aforesaid estates, lands, possessions, or any places belonging to the aforesaid venerable place, or to demand or take from the inhabitants or dependents of those places fodrum, any public service, or any payment.

Among other things, we have judged that this should be specially established: we shall particularly protect the aforesaid estate called Maliace, and whatever the monastery is said to possess in the valley of Luvana and the valley of Agno, because these places have suffered greater and more grievous misfortunes and troubles than the others. Therefore we order, and by every threat within our power command, that no official, minister, envoy, or servant shall ever presume henceforth to inflict any trouble upon the inhabitants or dependents of those places, impose any jurisdiction upon them, take fodrum from them, cut down their trees, seize any of their property or livestock, or dare, with any rash presumption, to take anything by force from their possessions.

If anyone has a complaint against one of them, he shall not presume to avenge it himself or seek legal redress through anyone except us or the abbot of that monastery, or through an envoy of ours or of the abbot.

Therefore, by this authority of our charter, we confirm and strengthen for the aforesaid monastery, its abbot, or whoever may preside there at the time, all the estates and places mentioned above, together with their goods and households, ports and market, jurisdictional rights, mills and fisheries, waters and watercourses, and all movable and immovable goods belonging in full to the estates and places written above, mindful of the divine commandments.

We also confirm all the carpenters whom that holy place possesses by the charter of King Liudprand from the time of our predecessor in the valley called Antelamo, and those who are at Besozolo, together with their sons and daughters and all their descendants, so that, when the proper time comes, they and their descendants may serve there permanently without any revocation.

We also confirm the fishing fords on the Ticino, at Rivo Poloni, Morasca, and the ford called Landemarii; at Costa and Teveredum; another called Sextemascum; the middle section called Sepem; and that called Aunella. We confirm also the fords in the Po whose upper boundary begins at the place called Popula Pagana and extends to the place called Caput Asi, on both sides of the Po, together with the islands situated near the aforesaid fishery; and whatever the holy place obtained from ancient times by the donation of ancient kings or emperors, or whatever the Po has taken away or may in future encroach upon, we transfer to that holy place.

We also wish and grant that, with respect to the mills which the monastery possesses at Caterona or on any of the aforesaid rivers, both the abbot and the monks shall have the power to raise and lower them, for as long and in whatever manner they determine. The aqueduct called Liudprand’s Bauga shall likewise be in their power for irrigating the gardens of the monastery.

Let all the goods of the monastery, and the abbot, monks, holders of leases, and servants, be strengthened and defended under our imperial protection. If necessity should arise concerning the monastery’s goods, let the truth of the matter be established through an inquiry among the good men living round about, just as in the case of our imperial goods. And, according to the determination of our predecessor King Liudprand, let the monastery be permitted to choose an abbot from its own community, so that no outsider may ever be imposed over them.

We also establish that no officer of the state or anyone exercising judicial authority in any of the estates or villages of the aforesaid monastery shall henceforth presume to disturb free persons or servants, drag them to court, hold a court within any of its boundaries, or seize or dispossess anyone. Whatever the public authority might otherwise claim, we confirm to the same holy monastery with solemn and perpetual stability, according to the grant and confirmation of King Liudprand and of other kings and emperors.

Whenever necessity arises, the ships of the monastery may travel through the port of the Ticino and the Po, and through any other waterway, without hindrance from anyone or payment of toll.

In accordance with these royal charters, we also enact and in every way forbid all who live under our authority to exercise henceforth any power over the aforesaid places assigned to the monks for our benefit, or to trouble the abbot in any matter. Rather, let the abbot and his successors be permitted to live under the rule of Saint Benedict, offer daily praises to God there for the remedy of our soul and the stability of our kingdom, and perpetually feed and nourish the entire community entrusted to them with constant provisions.

We also wish, and in every way forbid, any powerful or humble person to attempt to invade the aforesaid monastery by right of ownership, by benefice, or by authority of a charter.

Therefore we order and command, for present and future time, and to the party of the aforesaid monastery, that no one at any time presume to inflict trouble or opposition upon what has been granted and confirmed above by us. Rather, everything shall remain wholly intact, as it has been granted by us for the use of that monastery, without any diminution.

If, therefore, anyone at any time, deceived by diabolical fraud, attempts to act against this authority and our grant and confirmation, and tries to harass the aforesaid holy place concerning the goods mentioned above, let him know that he shall pay one thousand pounds of pure gold, half to our treasury and half to the aforesaid monastery or its abbot.

And so that this may be more firmly believed and more diligently observed by all, we have confirmed it with our own hand and ordered it to be marked below with the impression of our seal.

Sign of Lord Conrad, the unconquered Roman emperor Augustus.

### XXIII. Privilege of Emperor Conrad I for the Church of Bremen. (Year 1035, October 16.)

[LAPPENBERG, *Hamburgisches Urkundenbuch*, p. 69.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, CONRAD, by the favor of divine clemency, Roman emperor Augustus.

We wish it to be clear to all lovers of the divine name and of ours, present and future, how, because of the request of our most beloved wife Gisla, empress Augusta, which could not rightly be denied, and also because of the gracious intervention of our dearest son Henry, king, we have granted Becelin, venerable and beloved archbishop of the holy church of Bremen, a market in that place, together with the toll, coinage, and all the revenues belonging to the market.

The condition is that twice each year all those who come there for the purpose of trading shall hold an annual market there: once for seven days before Pentecost, and a second time likewise for seven days before the feast of Saint Willehad, who rests there bodily.

We impose our ban upon all who come there, so that they may have peace while going and returning; and, on account of his faithful service, we grant this same ban to the aforesaid archbishop, so that, if any rash act should occur during the appointed period among those coming there, no duke, count, or any other person shall have the authority to administer justice concerning it except the archbishop himself and his successors.

And so that this grant of ours may remain stable and unshaken for all time, we have ordered this document to be written and marked with the impression of our seal.

Sign of Lord Conrad, the unconquered Roman emperor. (S.)

Burchard, chancellor, recognized this in place of Bartho, archchaplain.

Given on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of November, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1035, in the third indiction; in the eleventh year of the reign of Lord Conrad II and the ninth of his empire.

Enacted at Magdeburg.

### XXIV. Confirmation by Emperor Conrad of all the rights and privileges of the Church of Mantua. (Year 1037.)

[MURATORI, *Antiquitates Italicae*, I, 611.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, CONRAD, by the favor of divine clemency, Roman emperor Augustus.

If, through pious favor, we restore and increase places consecrated to almighty God that have been desolated by various people, we believe that this will undoubtedly benefit both the stability of our empire and the reward of eternal recompense.

Therefore let all Christendom know that Bruno, venerable prelate, and Cadelous, our beloved bishop and faithful chancellor, informed our majesty that, because of the sins of the church of the see of Mantua, the church of the see of Mantua, together with its charters and the binding instruments by whose writings it had until then deserved to retain the goods and households granted to it, appeared to have been burned. They requested that, for its restoration, we deign to grant this charter of our mercy to Hitulf, bishop of the same church of Mantua.

Gladly consenting to his requests, and judging that it is right that the goods of the churches of God should not be plundered by anyone or taken unlawfully from their control, we decreed that this should be done. Accordingly, we grant and confirm to the bishopric of Mantua all the goods which it appears to have lost by unlawful seizure or force, as well as those which it has hitherto possessed from the gifts of our predecessors, kings or emperors; namely, the monastery built in honor of Saints Memor, Probus, and Rufinus, where Reginzo, venerable abbot, is known to preside, with all its appurtenances; the water called Mulenellos, with its watercourses from the place where the water rises, including the spring itself as far as the river Mincio, twelve feet on either side of the riverbed, as the monastery has always held it, with all the appurtenances of that monastery; and also estates situated in the counties of Verona, Vicenza, Mantua, Brescia, Piacenza, Modena, and Cremona, called Bagniolo and Colonia, and around the river called Caput Alponis, Puliana, Alonte, Lonigo, and Sablone, as well as in the judicial district of Gardino, with servants and female servants and everything belonging there.

And all the other goods of the same small monastery situated in the aforesaid counties, or within our Italian kingdom, or granted by other persons, etc. (as in the charter of Henry III for the same church, below under the year 1045).

We grant to the same Bishop Hitulf whatever advocates he may choose, whether from among his own free men or those of others, to carry out the bishop’s business concerning these goods, so that they shall be exempt from every public service. No public official shall presume to demand anything from them, so that they may more securely and diligently conduct the affairs of that church, whether by combat or by legal judgment.

We also establish that, concerning all the goods and estates of that church, as concerning our royal estates, an inquiry shall be made through the neighbors, etc., as in the charter mentioned above.

Sign of Lord Conrad, the unconquered Roman emperor Augustus.

Cadelous, chancellor, recognized this in place of Hermann, archchancellor.

Given on the day before the Kalends of April, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1037, in the fifth indiction; in the thirteenth year of the reign of Lord Conrad II and the tenth of his empire.

Enacted at Canedulo beside the river Po, successfully. Amen.

### XXV. Diploma of Emperor Conrad I by which he receives the monastery of Saint Theonestus the martyr at Treviso under his protection and confirms its rights. (Year 1037.)

[MURATORI, *Antiquitates Italicae*, II, 877.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, CONRAD, by the favor of divine clemency, Roman emperor Augustus.

Whatever temporal benefit we confer, for love of the divine name, upon places devoted to divine worship, we confidently believe will undoubtedly help us obtain the rewards of everlasting recompense. Therefore let the diligence of all the faithful of the holy Church of God and of ourselves, present and future, know that our most beloved wife Gisla appealed to our serenity, asking that, for the love of God and of the blessed Virgin Mary, and of Saint Zeno, confessor of Christ, and likewise for the sake of Michael the abbot and the monks serving God in the monastery of that same Saint Zeno, we might deign to receive and confirm under the authority of our charter the small monastery of Saint Theonestus, martyr of Christ, situated at Treviso and belonging to the aforesaid monastery of Saint Zeno, together with the monks living there, its churches, household, and all its goods.

Inclining the ears of our majesty to this pious request, we have received that monastery, together with its monks and household and the goods justly belonging to it, under our protection, and have decreed that it shall remain so in the future.

We also grant them the right to hold an annual public market at the church of Saint Lawrence, martyr of Christ, at Pendia, and to receive from it the toll for the use of the church and its people.

Therefore, ordering and commanding through this page of our charter, we forbid everyone that henceforth no public judge, nor anyone exercising judicial authority, dare enter, in our time or in the time of our successors, the churches of Saint Theonestus and Saint Lawrence or their remaining possessions in order to hear cases, demand fines, require lodging or provisions, seek unlawful pretexts, or exercise jurisdiction over the people dwelling upon the land of the aforesaid small monastery; nor shall anyone presume to demand any of the things mentioned above.

Rather, let the monks be permitted to live in peace and devote themselves to God, and with tranquility to implore God’s mercy for us, or for our wife or offspring, and for the stability of our entire empire.

But if anyone, etc.

Sign of Lord Conrad, most serene Roman emperor Augustus.—Place of the lost wax seal.

Kadelohus, chancellor, recognized this in place of Hermann, archchancellor.

Given on the second day before the Ides of July, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1037, indiction 5, and in the thirteenth year of Lord Conrad II’s reign and the eleventh of his empire.

Done at Verona, at Saint Zeno, successfully. Amen.

## XXVI. Charter of Conrad II, king and first emperor, by which he grants to the Cremonese Church, as compensation for the loss, all the estates of a certain Adam, who had unjustly killed Henry, cardinal deacon of the Cremonese Church. (Around the year 1037.)

*[Muratori, Antiquitates Italicae, II, 327.]*

[Col. 1071D]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Conrad, by the favor of divine clemency, Roman emperor Augustus.

If the holy Church of God, etc. For we have truly learned that a certain Cremonese man named Adam, inflated by the spirit of pride and incited by diabolical boldness, had killed an innocent deacon named Henry, cardinal of the holy Cremonese Church, [Col. 1072A] a most useful servant whom we had received, together with all his movable and immovable possessions, under the protection of our authority; and, scorning the reverence due to our majesty, by his death he inflicted upon the Church, whose servant he had been in every respect useful, losses so great that we are unable adequately to estimate them.

Therefore, to all, etc., we wish it to be known that, through the intervention of our beloved wife Gisla, the empress, so that the Church might in part recover the losses inflicted upon it by the death of its servant, and so that the contagion of so great a crime might in no way break out into customary practice, we grant by this page of our charter to the aforesaid holy Cremonese [Col. 1072B] Church, to have and retain under proprietary right, all the estates which the aforesaid Adam appears to possess within the city of Cremona and outside it throughout the entire extent of the bishopric, and every movable and immovable thing which he had possessed; and by our imperial authority we transfer them into the right and dominion of the aforementioned Church.

This is to be understood on the condition that both our beloved and faithful Hubald, the venerable bishop of that Church, and his successors may perpetually do with all the aforesaid property of the aforementioned murderer whatever they rightly judge useful for the benefit of the Church.

Moreover, by imperial decree we command that no duke, margrave, count, viscount, judge, sculdascio, or any great or small person of our kingdom presume by any device or pretext to dispossess or disturb the holy Cremonese Church, Hubald, the bishop of that see, or his successors, with respect to all the aforesaid property of the aforementioned murderer.

If anyone, however, etc.

Sign of Lord Conrad, most serene emperor Augustus.

The rest is lacking.

## XXVII. Charter of Conrad I Augustus by which the possessions granted to the monastery of Saint Justus at Susa by Bishop Alric and Margrave Mainfred are confirmed. (Year 1037.)

*[Muratori, Antiquitates Italicae, I, 347.]*

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Conrad, Roman emperor Augustus, by the favor of divine mercy.

If we do not doubt that those who, inwardly touched by the breath of divine inspiration, serve worthily the holy nourishing mother Church and provide assistance to the affairs of this world, contribute no little to the advancement of our Roman commonwealth and to the increase of both kinds of life; and if we mercifully incline our imperial ears to the pious petitions of our faithful, we firmly believe that we thereby make them more faithful and more ready for both public and private service.

Therefore, let the devotion of all the faithful of the chaste mother Church take notice of how our imperial majesty, moved by the intervention of Lord Poppo, archbishop, and also of Berta, countess, distinguished by the character of her virtues, grants what has been asked in worthy petitions and, confirming it through this page of our charter, establishes all the estates and all those possessions which formerly the venerable Bishop Alric, [Col. 1073A] the illustrious Margrave Mainfred, and also the illustrious Countess Berta offered to the holy church at Susa, dedicated in honor of the holy and undivided Trinity and under the name of the Mother and Virgin, and of Peter, prince of the apostles, and Paul, and all the saints, where the body of the most holy martyr Justus and of Saint Maurus has been laid to rest, for the salvation of their souls and of all Christians, for the use and support of the community of that monastery, which Lord Bertram, an abbot of extraordinary devotion, presently rules and governs.

We therefore decree, and by this page of our charter, confirming it, command that the aforesaid abbot and his successors, and the entire community living in that monastery according to the rule of blessed Benedict, possess, hold firmly, and own all the estates granted to God and his saints by the aforesaid bishop, margrave, and countess, and arrange and dispose of them according to what seems right and just to them, in precisely the manner in which the aforesaid Bishop Alric, Margrave Mainfred, and Countess Berta determined to dispose of them for the salvation of their souls and of all Christians, with all contradiction and disturbance from us and our successors completely removed.

Namely: one third of the same city of Susa, or of its territory, except for the castle situated within that city; and one third of the entire valley of Susa, both in the mountains and on the plains, as far as the mountains called Genevii and Cinisii extend, up to the territory and boundary of the village called [Col. 1073C] Vaga; in the places and estates of Sesana, Ulei, Bardonesca, Salebertani, Exilio, Caput Montis, Gallionis, Mediana, Matingo, Foresto, Bozoleto, Saint George, Canusso, Brusiolo, Burbono, Villare Fulcardi, and Saint Agatha, with their houses, chapels, and all their possessions, appurtenances, and dependencies.

Moreover, two complete curtis, Almesia and Rubiana, with their appendages and dependencies; likewise Vigodone, and the curtis of Volveria with all its dependencies; Petra Oriola with its chapel and all its appendages and dependencies, with fisheries, pastures, crags, ruins, from the bank of the Stura to the seashore; one manse at Carisione and another at Genecula, with their dependencies; two manses at Ferruciaso, with two chapels, one with its endowment, and one third of the tithe; and two mills of the curtis of Mauce with all their dependencies.

Moreover, the lake of Aviliania and the fishpond called Vuangery, with their appurtenances; and everything named above, with their building-sites, vineyards, threshing floors, arable lands, chapels, meadows, hayfields, pastures, large and small woods, with their plots, mills, fisheries, Alps, banks, ruins, and marshes, cultivated and uncultivated, divided and undivided, together with additions, boundaries, borders, and uses of the waters and the courses of the waters.

Therefore, ordering, we command, and altogether forbid, that no duke, archbishop, bishop, margrave, count, viscount, sculdascio, gastald, or any great or small person of our empire disturb, molest, or dispossess the aforesaid abbot, his successors, or the community itself of the church’s treasure, or of all its movable and immovable possessions, servants, and things that are there or will be granted to it; nor may anyone presume to exact lodging-tax, impose a legal summons, hold a court, unless the abbot of that place or his envoy should undertake it, or dare to inflict any violence in their houses.

Therefore, if any rash presumptuous person, struck by the devilish spur of avarice, attempts to resist this precept of our authority or in any way violate it, let him know that he shall pay one hundred pounds of purest gold, namely, one half to our treasury and one half to the aforesaid Church. [Col. 1074B] So that this may be believed more truly and observed more carefully by everyone, we have strengthened it with our own hand and ordered it to be marked below with the impression of our seal.

Sign of Lord Conrad, most invincible Roman emperor Augustus.

Archbishop Poppo of Trier intervened.

Kadelous, chancellor, acting in place of Hermann, archchaplain, examined and authenticated this.

Given on the fourth day before the Kalends of January, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1038, indiction 6, and in the fourteenth year of Lord Conrad’s reign and the eleventh of his empire.

Done at Parma, successfully. Amen.

## XXVIII. Charter of Conrad I, emperor, by which he confirms all the privileges and rights of the nunnery of Saint Sixtus situated in the city of Piacenza. (Year 1038.)

*[Muratori, Antiquitates Italicae, I, 561.]*

[Col. 1074C]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Conrad, by the favor of divine clemency, Roman emperor Augustus.

Let the diligence of all the faithful of the holy Church of God, both present and future, clearly know that, at the intervention and petition of Gisla, the empress—our beloved wife and partner of our empire—and of Henry, king, our most beloved offspring, and of our faithful bishop and chancellor, by this page of our charter we grant, confirm, and strengthen for the abbey of Saint Sixtus, presided over by the venerable abbess Adelaide, [Col. 1074D] all those things which are contained and written in the charter that our predecessors, the emperors Karloman and Louis, made and confirmed for the same Piacenzan monastery at the prayers and intervention of Angilberga, Karloman’s sister and Louis’s wife.

That is, they granted the farmers and rent-payers of the aforesaid monastery free and private authority, and granted them whatever they gave within the city of Piacenza or along the public roads for extending or at some time fortifying the boundaries of that monastery; and, just as they added all the aqueducts in the Piacenzan county for the benefit of the aforesaid monastery, so we grant, confirm, and [Col. 1075A] strengthen them, on this condition: that the aforesaid monastery may possess, hold, and exercise dominion; and that no one presume to disturb the farmers and rent-payers of that place.

Moreover, by the authority of our charter, it shall be lawful for it, whenever it wishes, as stated above, for the benefit of the monastery, to dig up the streets of the city of Piacenza inside and outside, to repair old aqueducts, establish new ones, or move whichever it wishes to another place, without any opposition from the public authority; but the streets must be provided with bridges or other structures in such a way that those going and returning may cross.

Therefore, if anyone wishes to oppose or obstruct this charter of ours, let him know that he shall pay one hundred pounds of tested gold, one half to our treasury and one half to the aforesaid monastery. [Col. 1075B] So that this may be believed more truly and observed more carefully by everyone, we have strengthened it with our own hand and ordered this page to be marked with the impression of our seal.

Sign of Lord Conrad, Roman emperor Augustus.

Kadelous, chancellor, acting in place of Hermann, archbishop and archchancellor, examined and authenticated this.

Place of the seal.

Given on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of April, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1038, indiction 6, and in the fourteenth year of Lord Conrad’s reign and the thirteenth of his empire.

Done near Perugia, in the monastery of Saint Peter, successfully. Amen.

## XXIX. Charter of Conrad I, emperor, by which he confirms all the rights and possessions of the monastery of Saint Vincent at Vulturnum. (Year 1038.)

*[Muratori, Rerum Italicarum Scriptores, I, II, 508.]*

[Col. 1075C]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Conrad, by the favor of divine clemency, Roman emperor Augustus.

Let the whole body of all the faithful of the holy Church of God, both present and future, know that Hilary, abbot of the monastery of Christ’s martyr Vincent, situated in the Beneventan territory above the river Vulturnus, approached our majesty and presented the charters of our predecessors, emperors [Col. 1075D] and kings, by which they granted possessions from their own property to the aforesaid monastery and confirmed the possessions and estates granted there by princes, dukes, and other faithful persons.

Therefore, the aforesaid abbot begged us to grant and confirm to the aforesaid place, by a charter of our confirmation, those same charters and legal documents, as well as the estates lying in various parts of the Italian kingdom that had been granted to the same monastery.

Favoring his petitions, through the intervention of Gisla, our beloved wife, the empress, and of King Henry, our most beloved son, by this charter of confirmation, insofar as we can justly and legally do so, we grant, confirm, and wholly strengthen in the aforesaid monastery all the charters of our predecessors, emperors and [Col. 1076A] kings—namely, those of Desiderius, Charles, Louis, and Lothair, and of the emperor Henry.

And also all the possessions and estates situated in various parts of the Italian kingdom by those same charters, or by any legal documents, granted there by princes, dukes, and other faithful persons, as well as the monasteries and cells named below.

First, declaring the estates themselves which surround the monastery within these boundaries: beginning, therefore, at the river called Sangro, etc.

Therefore, ordering, we command that no king, duke, prince, margrave, etc.

If anyone, therefore, etc.

Sign of Lord Conrad, Roman emperor Augustus.

Kadelous, chancellor, acting in place of Hermann, archchancellor, [Col. 1076B] examined and authenticated this.

Given on the third day before the Kalends of June, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1038, indiction 6, and in the fourteenth year of Lord Conrad’s reign and the thirteenth of his empire.

Done in Old Capua, successfully. Amen.

## XXX. Charter of Conrad I Augustus by which he grants to Ingo, bishop of Modena, the county of that city and its lands with their rights. (Year 1038.)

*[Muratori, Antiquitates Italicae, I, 445.]*

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Conrad, by the disposition of heavenly clemency, emperor . . .

If . . . [lacuna] . . . is enriched by recompense, whoever grants his possessions to places dedicated to God will prosper in merit, [Col. 1076C] and whoever confirms with his authority what has been granted sincerely by the worshipers of the Churches of God will prosper.

Therefore, let the diligence of all the faithful of the holy Church of God and of our people, present and future, know that Wido, bishop of the holy Turin Church and our faithful, approached our majesty, asking that, for the love of God and the salvation of our soul, we might deign by our imperial decree to confirm and strengthen all the possessions granted to the holy Modenese Church, dedicated in honor of Saint Geminianus, confessor of Christ, which the venerable Bishop Ingo serves by God’s authority, by our predecessors, kings as well as emperors, and by religious men.

Granting assent to his worthy petition, and considering the constant help to be sought from that most blessed Geminianus, bishop and confessor of Christ, we ordered this charter to be made, by which [we grant] both cultivated and uncultivated lands, or, in the places inserted above, the entire county of that city with all movable and immovable things belonging to it.

And we grant whatever appears to belong to our right: namely, lands, the entire district, public buildings, and the wall of that city, with the treasury and the whole toll, or with all civil jurisdiction inside and outside around it, up to all its boundaries.

The boundaries of this county are as follows. The first extends to the end [lacuna]. The second extends to Bologna. The third also extends to [lacuna]. The fourth, namely, to the beginning of the county of Lucca.

Also the curtis and territories of that county, castles, villages, manses, families of both sexes, male and female servants, free tenants, male and female, houses, possessions, fisheries, forests, pastures in the mountains and on the plains, watering places, courses and channels of waters, marshes, and everything held, possessed, and owned on behalf of that [lacuna] of salt by the aforesaid Bishop Ingo or by any of his predecessors; and everything hitherto donated, granted, and handed over by any persons or powers to the aforesaid holy Modenese Church under any written title or investiture—we donate, grant, confirm, and strengthen in every way.

This includes fields, vineyards, meadows, pastures, hayfields, woods, brushlands, forests, mountains, hills, valleys, plains, banks, crags, waters, [Col. 1077B] watercourses, mills, fisheries, and everything with all things that can be said or named, belonging in their entirety to the aforesaid episcopal see.

By this charter of our confirmation, we wholly transfer and assign from the right and dominion of ourselves and the kingdom into the right and dominion of the aforesaid holy Modenese Church the district of the aforesaid county and its toll or market, with every royal function, as well as houses, walls, lands, male and female servants, and everything called public, fiscal, comital, or vice-comital, which appears to be situated and constructed in the aforesaid Modenese county, both within and outside it, around it, as far as the aforesaid boundaries.

This is on the condition that Lord Ingo, the venerable bishop who appears to preside over that Church, and his successors shall have authority there, personally or through their envoys, to judge, distrain, hold court, [lacuna], or do whatever their benefit requires, for the increase and honor of the aforesaid Modenese Church; and that they may act, judge, and distrain in every way as though they were in our presence or that of margraves or counts, with all contradiction, diminution, or molestation by us, our successors, or any persons removed from this time onward.

Therefore, whoever resides within the aforesaid city, the aforesaid county, or its entire province, or in the aforesaid curtes and castles, or whoever establishes a castle there, and likewise the vassals of that county, shall not be permitted to conduct or settle their disputes in any other way, or in the presence of alien counts, margraves, or our envoys, except before Ingo, the most reverend bishop, his successors, or their delegates, as we have granted above. Whatever has been settled and judged in their presence shall remain with perpetual stability.

Therefore, ordering, we command that from now on no duke, margrave, count, viscount, sculdascio, gastald, any administrator of the public affairs, or any other great or small person of our realms dare dispossess, molest, or disturb the aforesaid holy see of God or its representatives, impose lodging-tax, exact toll, district, court, or any other levy, or inflict violence concerning the aforesaid possessions.

If anyone therefore violates this charter of our confirmation, or attempts by any rash undertaking to do so or diminish it, let him know that he shall pay two hundred pounds of the finest gold: one hundred to our treasury and one hundred to the aforesaid bishop and his successors.

So that this may be believed more truly and observed more carefully by everyone, we have ordered it, strengthened with our own hand, to be marked with the impression of our ring.

Sign of Lord Conrad, most invincible emperor.

Kadelous, chancellor, acting in place of Lord Hermann, archchancellor, examined and authenticated this.

Place of the wax seal.

Given on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of April, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation [Col. 1078B] 1038, indiction 7, and in the fourteenth year of Lord Conrad’s reign and the twelfth of his empire.

Done at Cologne, successfully.

## XXXI. Charter of Emperor Conrad for the Hamburg Church. (Year 1038, December 10.)

*[Lappenberg, Hamburgische Urkunden, p. 70.]*

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Conrad, by the favor of divine clemency, Roman emperor Augustus.

The concern of imperial power, which has watched over us after the passing of kings and emperors of blessed memory, not unaware of the disposition of God who governs all things, warns and urges us to devote the care of our prudence to the Churches of God established throughout our kingdom with vigilance proportionate to the fact that, in the promotion of our rank, we have received the benefits of heavenly grace with such liberality.

For from this we undoubtedly hope to earn the greatest reward of profit before God, creator of all, if venerable places, at a suitable time, are brought to a better condition, with God’s help and our power cooperating.

Therefore, let all our faithful and Christ’s faithful know how, for the salvation of our soul and through the intervention of our beloved wife Gisla, empress Augusta, and also of our dearest offspring Henry, king of the Burgundians, we have granted to Becelin, the venerable man and archbishop of Hamburg, and his successors [Col. 1078D] permission to establish a market at a place called Heslingoa, in the district of Eilangoa.

This is on the condition that the advocate of that Church shall have authority, on those days when the annual market is customarily celebrated there and a great gathering of people usually takes place—namely, on the feast of Saint Vitus the martyr—to compel under our ban all who have gathered there to render every form of justice.

Moreover, we grant by imperial largesse, for our perpetual remembrance, to the same Church and to the nuns living there, for the love of the aforesaid martyr, to whom that place is consecrated, the toll and whatever belongs to our imperial right, for their free use.

We have also added, at the request and petition of the same venerable man, since we have found him faithful in all our business, that he shall have authority, if the need or advantage of the matter should demand it, to establish a complete market at the place called Stade, on the Church’s estate. We grant to the aforesaid Hamburg see the ban and toll, as well as the mint, and whatever the royal treasury of the commonwealth may be able to obtain from it.

But the people who in any way make dwellings for themselves on the aforesaid estate shall remain under the ban and coercion of the bishop’s advocate, and of no one else.

And so that this grant of our benevolence may remain stable and unshaken for all time, we have ordered this charter to be written, strengthened with our own hand, and marked with the impression of our seal.

Sign of Lord Conrad, most invincible emperor [Col. 1079B] Augustus.

Theodoric, chancellor, acting in place of Bardo, archchaplain, examined and authenticated this.

Given on the fourth day before the Ides of December, indiction 7, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1038, and in the fifteenth year of Lord Conrad II’s reign and the thirteenth of his empire.

Done at Nierstein, successfully. Amen.

## XXXII. Charter of Conrad I, emperor, by which he confirms all the rights and privileges of the Modenese Church to Bishop Ingo and appoints him count of Modena. (Year 1038.)

*[Muratori, Antiquitates Italicae, VI, 41.]*

[Col. 1079C]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Conrad, by the disposition of heavenly clemency, emperor.

If [lacuna] is enriched by recompense, whoever grants his possessions to places dedicated to God will prosper in merit, and whoever confirms with his authority what has been granted sincerely by the worshipers of the Churches of God [will prosper].

Therefore, let the diligence of all the faithful of the holy Church of God and of our people, present and future, know that Wido, bishop of the holy Turin Church and our faithful, approached our majesty, asking that, for the love of God and the salvation of our soul, we might deign by our imperial decree to confirm and strengthen all the possessions granted to the holy Modenese Church, dedicated in honor of Saint Geminianus, confessor of Christ, which the venerable Bishop Ingo serves by God’s authority, by our predecessors, kings as well as [Col. 1079D] emperors, and by religious men.

Granting assent to his worthy petition, and considering the constant help to be sought from that most blessed Geminianus, bishop and confessor of Christ, we ordered this charter to be made, by which [we grant] both cultivated and uncultivated lands, or, in the places inserted above, the entire county of that city with all movable and immovable things belonging to it; and we grant whatever appears to belong to our right: namely, lands, the entire district, public buildings, and the wall of that city, with the treasury and the whole toll, or with all civil jurisdiction inside and outside around it, up to all its boundaries.

The boundaries of this county are as follows. The first extends to the end [lacuna]. The second extends to Bologna. The third also extends to [lacuna], Mantua. The fourth, namely, to the beginning of the county of Lucca.

Also the curtis and territories of that county, castles, villages, manses, families of both sexes, male and female servants, free tenants, male and female, houses, possessions, fisheries, forests, pastures in the mountains and on the plains, watering places, courses and channels of waters, marshes, and everything held, possessed, and owned on behalf of that [lacuna] of salt by the aforesaid Bishop Ingo or by any of his predecessors; and everything hitherto donated, granted, and handed over by any persons [Col. 1080B] or powers to the aforesaid holy Modenese Church under any written title or investiture—we donate, grant, confirm, and strengthen in every way.

This includes fields, vineyards, meadows, pastures, hayfields, woods, brushlands, forests, mountains, hills, valleys, plains, banks, crags, waters and watercourses, mills, fisheries, and everything with all things that can be said or named, belonging in their entirety to the aforesaid episcopal see.

By this charter of our confirmation, we wholly transfer from the right and dominion of ourselves and the kingdom into the right and dominion of the aforesaid holy Modenese Church, and assign to it, the district of the aforesaid county and its toll or market, with every royal function, as well as houses, walls, lands, male and female servants, and everything called public, fiscal, comital, or vice-comital, which appears to be situated in the aforesaid Modenese county, both within and outside it, around it, as far as the aforesaid boundaries.

This is on the condition that Lord Ingo, the venerable bishop who appears to preside over that Church, and his successors shall have authority there, personally or through their envoys, to judge, distrain, hold court, or do whatever their benefit requires, for the increase and honor of the aforesaid Modenese Church; and that they may act, judge, and distrain in every way as though they were in our presence or that of margraves or counts, with all contradiction, diminution, [Col. 1080D] and molestation by us, our successors, or any persons removed from this time onward.

Therefore, whoever resides within the aforesaid city, the aforesaid county, or its entire province, or in the aforesaid curtes and castles, or whoever establishes a castle there, and likewise the vassals of that county, shall not be permitted to conduct or settle their disputes in any other way, or in the presence of alien counts, margraves, or our envoys, except before Ingo, the most reverend bishop, his successors, or their delegates, as we have granted above. Whatever has been settled and judged in their presence shall remain with perpetual stability.

Therefore, ordering, we command that from now on no duke, margrave, count, or viscount, [Col. 1081A] sculdascio, gastald, any administrator of the public affairs, or any other great or small person of our realms dare dispossess, molest, or disturb the aforesaid holy see of God or its representatives, impose lodging-tax, exact toll, district, court, or any other levy, or inflict violence concerning the aforesaid possessions.

If anyone therefore violates this charter of our confirmation, or attempts by any rash undertaking to do so or diminish it, let him know that he shall pay two hundred pounds of the finest gold: one half to our treasury and one half to the aforesaid bishop and his successors. [Col. 1082A] So that this may be believed more truly and observed more carefully by everyone, we have ordered it, strengthened with our own hand, to be marked with the impression of our ring.

Sign of Lord Conrad, most invincible emperor.

Place of the lost wax seal.

Kadelous, chancellor, acting in place of Lord Hermann, archchancellor, examined and authenticated this.

Given on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of April, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1038, indiction 7, and in the fourteenth year of Lord Conrad’s reign and the twelfth of his empire.

Done at Cologne, successfully.

# Henry III, Emperor, third of that name among the kings, second among the Augusti, surnamed the Black. (Years 1039–1056.)

[Col. 1081]

[Col. 1081]

# Constitutions of Emperor Henry III

*(Pertz, Monumenta Germaniae historica, Laws, vol. II, p. 41.)*

## I. Constitution on the Oath of Calumny

*[Note: We publish this constitution with the aid of the eleventh-century manuscripts of London, Vienna, and Vienna II (Civil Law no. 39), as well as the Veronese manuscript from the eleventh or the beginning of the twelfth century, and the Este manuscript published by Muratori on p. 178. It also occurs in Bernard of Pavia’s Collection of Decretals, where it is cited by a certain Pope Honorius II—or rather, Victor II—and there it is said to have been issued at Rimini on the third day of the month of April (some manuscripts have the fourth), that is, on the third day before the Nones of April (some manuscripts have the fourth).]*

*(Year 1047, April 3.)*

[Col. 1081B]

Henry, by divine piety the second Roman emperor Augustus, to all.

*[Note: The London manuscript prefixes the following verse: “King Henry, father and husband of his country. This law of the second King Henry commands that clerics shall not swear.”]*

It is provided in the laws [Note: *aug.*: “Since in all laws,” V II.] that no cleric presume to swear (1. 25, § 1, *Code*, *On Bishops*). Elsewhere, however, it is found written (Julian, 122, 1) that all principal persons must undertake an oath against calumny at the very beginning of a lawsuit. It has therefore come into doubt among some legal experts whether clerics ought to take the oath against calumny, or whether they may delegate this duty to another person.

Since the constitutional edict by which clerics are forbidden to swear (1. 25, § 1, *Code*, *On Bishops*) appears to have been promulgated by the emperor Theodosius [Note: *Marco augusto*; “It was established by the emperor Marcus Augustus, because concerning the Constitution,” the editions read.] to Taurus, prefect of the praetorium, concerning the clerics of Constantinople, it is consequently not thought to apply to other clerics.

Therefore, so that this doubt may be completely removed from everyone, we decree that that divine constitution of Theodosius [Note: In the margin of V: “others have Marcus.” — “The constitution of Marcus,” V II and the editions.] shall be interpreted so that it is judged generally applicable to the clerics of all Churches.
