Diplomatic record concerning the letters of Pope Urban II. 281  

# Letters and Privileges of Blessed Pope Urban II

283. I.—Letter of Pope Urban II to the bishop of Salzburg and other bishops. He informs them of his election to the supreme pontificate and exhorts them to fight manfully for the Church. Same place.  
II.—Letter of Pope Urban II to Hugh, abbot of Cluny. He announces that the pontificate has been conferred upon him. He asks Hugh to come to him. 284  
III.—Letter of Pope Urban II to the bishops, clergy, and people of the province of Vienne. Concerning the election of an archbishop of Vienne, since this metropolitan church had long been without a shepherd. 285  
IV.—Letter of Pope Urban II to Lanfranc, archbishop of Canterbury. Concerning the Church’s difficulties and the pontificate he has undertaken. 286  
V.—The primacy of the Church of Toledo in Spain restored. 288  
VI.—Letter of Pope Urban II to Ildefonsus, king of Galicia. He congratulates him on the Church of Toledo’s recovery from the Saracens. He commends Bernard, archbishop of Toledo, whom he himself has given the pallium and established as primate throughout all the kingdoms of Spain. 289  
VII.—Urban II warns the archbishops of Spain concerning the restoration of the primacy of Toledo. 290  
VIII.—Letter of Pope Urban II to Hugh, abbot of Cluny, concerning the primacy conferred upon the Church of Toledo. 291  
IX.—Urban II confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of Cluny and grants Abbot Hugh the use of the mitre, dalmatic, gloves, and sandals. Same place.  
X.—Letter of Pope Urban II to Geoffrey, bishop of Maguelone. He receives the investiture of the county of Substantion and of the bishopric of Maguelone from Geoffrey’s hand. Therefore he places that Church and county under the special protection of the Roman Church and entrusts to it the task of receiving an annual census of one ounce of gold from the aforesaid county. 293  
XI.—Letter of Urban II to Pistoiese and Rusticus, abbots of Vallombrosa. Concerning Wezelo, archbishop of Mainz, deposed for simony. 294  
XII.—Privilege of Pope Urban II for the abbey of Saint John [Col. 1476] of the Vines.  
XIII.—Urban II grants a bull to the monastery of Saint Victor of Marseille. 296  
XIV.—Letter of Pope Urban II to Geoffrey, bishop of Constance. He orders that a fugitive from the monastery of Schaffhausen be recalled for the third time, and delivers the one who refuses obedience to anathema. Same place.  
XV.—Letter of Pope Urban II written from the Roman synod to Gebhard, bishop of Constance, a canonical letter by which he confers and confirms upon him the apostolic legation and the administration of the Churches in Saxony and Alemannia. 297  
XVI.—Letter of Pope Urban II to the bishops of Germany. He informs them whom they are to regard as excommunicated. 299  
XVII.—Bull of Pope Urban II for the regular canons of Saint Augustine in the monastery of Saint John of Ripoll, founded by Bishop Berengar. Same place.  
XVIII.—Privilege of Pope Urban II for the monastery of Jesus Nazarene. 301  
XIX.—Urban II grants Frotard, abbot of Saint Pontius of Tomerias, a privilege by which he exempts the place from the jurisdiction of every bishop and adorns it with several other prerogatives. 302  
XX.—Letter of Pope Urban II to the nobles of the province of Tarragona concerning the restoration of the Church of Tarragona. Same place.  
XXI.—Urban II grants a bull to the monastery of Saints Anianus and Lawrence. 304  
XXII.—Privilege of Urban II for the clergy and laity of Velletri. Same place.  
XXIII.—Letter of Pope Urban II to Anselm, abbot of Bec. He asks him to assist a bishop inexperienced in ecclesiastical affairs; not to delay visiting the apostolic see; and to send to it what Hubert, his legate and subdeacon, had collected from the census of Saint Peter. 305  
XXIV.—Letter of Pope Urban II to Pibo, bishop of Toul. 306  
XXV.—Urban II confirms the possessions of the monastery of Cava. 307  
XXVI.—Letter of Pope Urban II to Elias, bishop of Bari. Concerning the translation of the relics of Saint Nicholas and the dignity and rights of the Church of Bari. Same place.  
XXVII.—Letter of Pope Urban II to Rainald, archbishop of Reims. He grants him the pallium and asserts the primacy of the entire province of Second Belgica, together with the right to consecrate the kings of the Franks. 309  
XXVIII.—Urban II, at the request of Hugh, archbishop of Besançon, confirms the possessions of the monastery of Balmey among the Sequani. 311  
XXIX.—Letter of Pope Urban II to Raynerius, cardinal priest. He gives many instructions concerning affairs in Spain. 313  
XXX.—Letter of Pope Urban II to Raynerius, priest and legate of the Holy Roman Church. He appoints him judge between the bishop of Barcelona, Bertran, and Frotard, abbot of Saint Pontius of Tomerias. 314  
XXXI.—Letter of Pope Urban II to Frotard, abbot of Tomerias. He exhorts him to make satisfaction for the injuries inflicted upon the archbishop of Narbonne. 315  
XXXII.—Letter of Pope Urban II to Raymond, count, Aymeric, viscount, and the clergy and people of Narbonne. 316  
XXXIII.—Letter of Pope Urban II to the clergy and people of Vienne. He commends the archbishop of Vienne and orders that what Provost Ataldus had dissipated from the goods of the Church of Vienne be restored. Same place.  
XXXIV.—Letter of Pope Urban II to the suffragans of the Church of Arles. He informs them that the oaths extorted from Bishop Guibullus have been declared invalid by him; he declares infamous those who capture the bishop. 317  
XXXV.—Bull of Urban II for the canons of Pistoia. Same place.  
XXXVI.—Urban II undertakes the protection of the monastery of Raitenbuch, founded by Welf, duke of Bavaria, and his wife Jutta. 319  
XXXVII.—Privilege of Pope Urban II for the canons of Saint Antoninus in the diocese of Rodez. Same place.  
XXXVIII.—Privilege of Pope Urban II for the Church of Grenoble. 320  
XXXIX.—Urban II confirms the possessions of the monastery of Saint Theodfrid of Calmihac. 322  
XL.—Privilege of Urban II for the Vallombrosans. Same place.  
XLI.—Urban II undertakes the protection of the Greater Monastery and confirms its possessions. 324  
XLII.—Urban II grants a bull to Burchard, abbot of Saint Basolus. Same place. [Col. 1477]  
XLIII.—Urban II confirms the freedom and possessions of the Church of Ravello at the request of Bishop Ursus. 325  
XLIV.—Letter of Urban II to the clergy and people of Chartres. Concerning the deposition of Bishop Geoffrey and the substitution of Ivo, who was consecrated in his place. Same place.  
XLV.—Letter of Pope Urban II to Richer, archbishop of Sens. He commends Ivo, bishop of Chartres, to him. If Geoffrey attempts to invade the bishopric, he declares him anathematized. 326  
XLVI.—Letter of Pope Urban II to Altmann, bishop of Passau. 327  
XLVII.—Letter of Pope Urban II to the abbots Lanzo and Ralph and to Adalbero the primicerius. He confirms the election of the bishop of Metz made by them. Same place.  
XLVIII.—Urban II confirms the possessions of the Parthenon of the Holy Cross at Poitiers. 328  
XLIX.—Letter of Pope Urban II to Romuald, bishop of the Church of Monopoli. In accordance with the judgment of the Council of Benevento, he declares that the bishopric of Monopoli is subject not to the Church of Brindisi but to the Roman see. 328  
L.—Urban II undertakes the protection of the monastery of Saint Bartholomew on the island of Lipari and confirms its goods. 329  
LI.—Urban II entrusts the island of Corsica, restored under Gregory VII to the former jurisdiction of the Roman Church, to Daimbert, bishop of Pisa, and his successors. 330  
LII.—Letter of Pope Urban II to Berengar, bishop of Ausona. He appoints him archbishop of Tarragona. 331  
LIII.—Letters of Pope Urban II to the priors of Vallombrosa and Camaldoli, so that they may not be from…
from the communion of the Pisan bishop. 333

**LIV.** Urban II urges Guillelmus, archbishop of Rouen, to restore the monastery of Saint Austreberta at Pavilly; and to all who contribute anything to that monastery he remits a quarter of the penances imposed by a bishop or priest. 335

**LV.** Letter of Urban II to the clergy and people of Amiens. — He announces that he has sanctioned Bishop Gervinus. ibid.

**LVI.** Letter of Urban II to the prelates of laymen living the common life. 336

**LVII.** Letter of Urban II to Gebhard, bishop of Constance, the dukes Welf and Berthold, and Count B. — He exhorts them to protect the abbot of the monastery of Saint Saviour at Schaffhausen against Tutone, who is attempting to take away an estate donated to the monastery. ibid.

**LVIII.** Confirmation of the canonical foundation of Saint Mary at Rettenbach, which is received under the protection of the Apostolic See; and, after all its possessions have been confirmed, certain privileges are granted to it. 337

**LIX.** Bull of Pope Urban II for the monastery at Catania. 339

**LX.** Urban II undertakes to protect the Beneventan monastery of Saint Sophia and confirms its possessions and rights. 341

**LXI.** Privilege of Urban II for the monastery of Reinhardsborn. 342

**LXII.** Urban II confirms the possessions of the monks of Silvacane, although, he says, “your congregation and place are still unknown to us.” 344

**LXIII.** Urban II subjects the Corsican bishoprics to the Church of Pisa, on account of the citizens’ services to the Roman Church, at the request of Countess Matilda. ibid.

**LXIV.** Letter of Urban II to Berengar, archbishop of Tarragona. — He warns him not to act negligently in restoring the church of Tarragona, and to obey the primate, the archbishop of Toledo, now constituted his vicar throughout all Spain and the province of Narbonne. 346

**LXV.** Urban II grants Guarmo, abbot of the monastery of Saint Lawrence at Aversa, the use of the mitre and ring. ibid.

**LXVI.** Letter of Urban II to Peter, abbot of Cava. — Concerning the privileges granted to that monastery. 347

**LXVII.** Urban II asserts to Saint Bruno, founder of the Carthusians, and to Laninus that the site was granted by Count Roger and confirmed by Theodore, bishop of Squillace. 353

**LXVIII.** Letter of Urban II to Raynald, archbishop of Reims, and his suffragans. — He reproaches them for having allowed a king to divorce his wife and take another. 354

**LXIX.** Letter of Urban II to Goffridus, abbot of Saint Albans at Angers, and Berno, abbot of the Holy Trinity at Vendôme. — He exhorts them to observe his judgment concerning their dispute. 355

**LXX.** Letter of Urban II to Robert, count of Flanders. — That he should refrain from harassing the clergy. [Col. 1478] 356

**LXXI.** Letter of Urban II to the clergy and people of Arras. — That, having shaken off the yoke of the bishop of Cambrai, they should elect a bishop to be consecrated by the metropolitan. ibid.

**LXXII.** Letter of Urban II to Raynald, archbishop of Reims. — He orders him to consecrate as bishop the man whom the clergy and people of Arras have elected. 357

**LXXIII.** Letter of Urban II to Guimund, bishop of Aversa. — He approves what Guimund has done concerning Richard, son of Burrellus. ibid.

**LXXIV.** Letter of Urban II to Anselm, archbishop of Milan. — Concerning the reconciliation of those who have fallen. 358

**LXXV.** Guernerius of Merseburg is granted permission for a cleric who had killed a boy by throwing a stone to remain in his order after undertaking perpetual penance. ibid.

**LXXVI.** Letter of Urban II to Albert, bishop of Metz. — He instructs him to deal gently with a certain priest who had obtained his dignity by simony. 358

**LXXVII.** Letter of Pope Urban II to all the bishops of Britain. — He grants the pallium to the bishop of Dol, without prejudice to the rights of the Church of Tours. 359

**LXXVIII.** Letter of Pope Urban II to the princes and people of the Church of Dol. — That they restore the property taken from the Church of Dol. ibid.

**LXXIX.** Urban II confirms the intention of the canons of Saint Paul at Narbonne to profess the regular life. 360

**LXXX.** Letter of Urban II to Raynald, archbishop of Reims. — He again orders him to ensure that a bishop is appointed for the Church of Arras. 361

**LXXXI.** Letter of Urban II to the clergy and people of Arras. — He writes to them the same things that he wrote in the preceding letter to Archbishop Raynald. 362

**LXXXII.** Letter of Urban II to the clergy and people of Amiens. — He orders them to obey Bishop Gerewinus, after his purification from simony. ibid.

**LXXXIII.** Letter of Pope Urban II to all the faithful. — Concerning the church of Saint Mary of the monastery of Monte Cassino, which he consecrated and furnished with a privilege. 363

**LXXXIV.** Urban II decrees that those who visit the monastery of Saint Mary on appointed days shall enjoy absolution from their sins. 365

**LXXXV.** Letter of Urban II to Raynald, archbishop of Reims. — He censures him for not yet having consecrated the elected bishop of Arras. 366

**LXXXVI.** Letter of Urban II to Lambert, bishop of Arras. — He congratulates him and informs him about the preceding letter to Raynald. ibid.

**LXXXVII.** Letter of Pope Urban II to Gerald, abbot of the New Monastery at Poitiers. — He confirms to the New Monastery of that city the church of Saint Nicholas beside the city walls of Poitiers, which had been adjudicated to the canons at the Council of Saintes. 367

**LXXXVIII.** Letter of Pope Urban II to Raynald, abbot of Saint Cyprian at Poitiers. — Whatever right and canonical authority he had acquired over the church of Holy Cross at Engla, Urban grants to him and confirms by apostolic authority. 368

**LXXXIX.** Letter of Pope Urban II to the bishops and abbots of Aquitaine, Gascony, and Lower Burgundy. — That they arrange for financial aid to be collected for securing the freedom of the Apostolic See and sent to him through Raynald, abbot of Saint Cyprian at Poitiers. ibid.

**XC.** Letter of Pope Urban II to Raynald, abbot of Saint Cyprian at Poitiers. — He entrusts him with the task of collecting money in support of the Roman Church. 369

**XCI.** Urban II grants a bull to the regular canons of Saint Quentin at Beauvais. 370

**XCII.** Likewise to the monastery of Bourgueil. ibid.

**XCIII.** The Church of Syracuse, after Count Roger expelled the Agarenes, is confirmed; a penalty of excommunication is imposed upon anyone who disturbs it in any way. 370

**XCIV.** Urban II writes to the congregation of the monastery of Vendôme that it has been reported to him that the bishop of Chartres—Yves—exacted from their abbot, Gaufridus, a profession at his consecration. He rescinds this profession and orders that henceforth their monastery’s abbot is not to make a profession to the bishop. 372

**XCV.** Letter of Urban II to Raynald, archbishop of Reims. — He warns him not to listen to the people of Cambrai, who are claiming the Church of Arras for themselves. ibid.

**XCVI.** Pope Urban gives a canonical ruling concerning the king of Aragon, who had firmly promised under oath to give his niece in marriage to a certain knight. 373

**XCVII.** Letter of Urban II to the abbot of Saint John at Pinna. — He orders him not to take away certain tithes from the canons of the church of Saint Saturninus at Toulouse. ibid. [Col. 1479]

**XCVIII.** Letter of Pope Urban II to William, archbishop of Rouen, the canons of Saint Mellon at Pont-de-l’Arche, and the inhabitants of that castle. — He orders them not to prevent the monks of Bec from ringing their bells at the canonical hours according to their custom. 374

**XCIX.** Bull of Pope Urban II confirming the donation made by Countess Matilda to the monastery of Saint Blaise. ibid.

**C.** Letter of Urban II to the Catholic Saxons. — He announces that he has consecrated the elected bishop of Halberstadt, disregarding the metropolitan of Mainz on account of the schism. 375

**CI.** Urban II informs all the sons of the Catholic Church throughout Saxony that Herrand, bishop of Halberstadt, has been consecrated by him. He orders them to obey him and releases everyone from loyalty to the usurper. 376

**CII.** Letter of Urban II to the clergy and people of Halberstadt. — He praises them for having elected another bishop in place of the bishop who had fallen into schism, and approves their election. 376

**CIII.** Letter of Urban II to Fulk, bishop of Beauvais. — He enumerates many serious charges of which Fulk was accused. He orders him, for the purpose of clearing himself, to come either to Raynald, archbishop of Reims, or to Urban himself. 378

**CIV.** Letter of Pope Urban II to the clergy and people of Beauvais. — He announces that he has vindicated the castle-lordship for the knight Odo. 379

**CV.** Urban II confirms the rights and possessions of the monastery of Vendôme. 380

**CVI.** Letter of Urban II to Lambert, bishop of Arras, or privilege of the Church of Arras. ibid.

**CVII.** Letter of Urban II to Alard of Arras, Bernard, archdeacon of Ostrevent, and others. — He exhorts them henceforth to obey Lambert, bishop of Arras. 382

**CVIII.** Letter of Urban II to Alold of Saint-Vaast, Richard of Marchiennes, Albert of Hasnon, Hameric of Anchin, the abbots, and the abbesses of Saint Ragenfred and Strum. — He orders them to obey Lambert, bishop of Arras. ibid.

**CIX.** Letter of Urban II to Raynald, archbishop of Reims, and his suffragans. — He commends Lambert, bishop of Arras, to them. 383

**CX.** Letter of Urban II to William, count of Poitiers. — He exhorts him to return what he has taken from the monastery of Vendôme. 384

**CXI.** Urban II instructs Amatus, legate of the Apostolic See, and two other bishops to regard William, count of Poitiers, as excommunicated unless, within the time fixed by Urban, he causes the property taken from the monks of Vendôme to be restored to them. ibid.

**CXII.** Letter of Urban II to Robert, count of the Flemings. — He commends the Church of Arras and its bishop to him. 385

**CXIII.** Judgment of Pope Urban II concerning the subjection of the Church of Dol to that of Tours. ibid.

**CXIV.** Letter of Pope Urban II to all the bishops established throughout Britain. — He confirms the judgments of other supreme pontiffs and orders them to obey the archbishop of Tours as their metropolitan. 387

**CXV.** Letter of Urban II to Raynald, archbishop of Reims. — He complains that Raynald wanted Bishop Fulk of Beauvais, who had cleared himself before Urban of the charge, to undergo a further purification. 388

**CXVI.** Letter of Urban II to Hugh, archbishop of Lyons. 389

**CXVII.** Letter of Urban II to Hugh, bishop of Grenoble. — He informs him about the preceding letters to Hugh of Lyons. 390

**CXVIII.** Privilege of Urban II for the canons of Pistoia. ibid.

**CXIX.** Letter of Urban II to Durannus, bishop of Clermont. — He orders him to command the canons of Billom to restore the monastery of Blessed Lupus to the monks of Cluny. 392

**CXX.** Letter of Urban II to William, count of Toulouse. — He rebukes him concerning the abbots expelled from Moissac and Lézat. ibid.

**CXXI.** Letter of Urban II to William—or Gerald?—bishop of Cahors. — He orders him, after expelling Hunald, to return Ansquilinus to the monastery of Moissac. 393

**CXXII.** Letter of Urban II to Godefridus, bishop of Lucca. — Those who kill excommunicated persons out of zeal for the Church are not to be considered homicide perpetrators. 394

**CXXIII.** Letter of Urban II to Cyriacus, bishop of Genoa. — Concerning those who must establish kinship by oath. ibid.

**CXXIV.** Letter of Urban II to Duke Roger and his brother Bohemond. — He defends the monks against usurpers. ibid. [Col. 1480]

**CXXV.** Letter of Pope Urban II to Beringer, abbot of Saint Lawrence at Liège, persecutor of the Simonians and Wibertists, expelled by Emperor Henry and Bishop Obertus. 395

**CXXVI.** Bull of Pope Urban II for the monastery of Saint Peter at Pozzuoli in the diocese of Lucania. 398

**CXXVII.** Bulls of Urban II for the monastery of Saint Giles, confirmed at the Council of Piacenza. 399

**CXXVIII.** Urban II, pontiff, receives the monastery of Saint George in the Black Forest under his protection and grants it notable liberties. 400

**CXXIX.** The monastery of Hirsau in the diocese of Speyer is received under the protection of the Apostolic See, and all its possessions are confirmed to it. 402

**CXXX.** Letter of Urban II to the clergy and people of Noyon. — He sends back to them, with the fullness of his favor, Bishop Radbod, who had attended the Council of Piacenza, and confirms the privileges granted to the Church of Noyon by his predecessors. 404

**CXXXI.** Bull of Urban II for the abbey of Saint Peter in the Black Forest. ibid.

**CXXXII.** Letter of Urban II to Robert, count of the Flemings, and his nobles. — He exhorts them to assist Lambert, bishop of Arras, in recovering the possessions of the Church. 406

**CXXXIII.** Letter of Urban II to Gualcher, bishop of Cambrai. — He exhorts him not to injure the rights of the Church of Arras. ibid.

**CXXXIV.** Letter of Urban II to Guido, archbishop of Vienne. ibid.

**CXXXV.** Urban II confirms the transfer of the bishopric of Auch and the division of its parishes carried out at the Council of Fusellum. 407

**CXXXVI.** Bull of Urban II confirming the canonical life instituted in the Church of Maguelone. 408

**CXXXVII.** Privilege for the monastery of Cluny. 410

**CXXXVIII.** Privilege of Pope Urban II for the church of Saint Peter at Guastalla. 412

**CXXXIX.** Letter of Pope Urban II to Richard, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church. 414

**CXL.** Decree of Urban II establishing that, after the death of Bishop William, the Church of Orange is to be joined to the Church of Saint-Paul-Trois-Châteaux. 416

**CXLI.** Apostolic privilege of Pope Urban II for the monastery of Saint Abundius at Como. 417

**CXLII.** Apostolic letters of Urban II confirming the rule for regular clerics instituted by Peter, bishop of Carcassonne, in the church of Saint Nazarius and elsewhere. 418

**CXLIII.** Urban II undertakes the protection of the church of Saint Peter at Standalmont, which Countess Matilda had given to Saint Peter, and confirms its possessions, on the condition that its clerics pay each year to the Lateran palace one gold denarius, or every fourth year one bisant. 419

**CXLIV.** Letter of Pope Urban II to the people of Salm. 420

**CXLV.** Privilege of Urban II for the Church of Besançon. 421

**CXLVI.** Letter of Urban II to Lambert, bishop of Arras. 422

**CXLVII.** Privilege of Pope Urban II for the monastery of nuns of Saint Peter at Blaziliensis. ibid.

**CXLVIII.** The canons of the Church of Cahors are confirmed in the profession of the regular life, which they had recently professed. 423

**CXLIX.** Privilege for the monastery of La Chaise-Dieu. 424

**CL.** Urban exhorts all the faithful throughout Gothia and Provence to contribute toward the construction of the church of Saint Nicholas on the estate which Countess Stephania had transferred through him to the monastery of Saint Victor at Marseille near Tarascon. 425

**CLI.** Bull of Pope Urban II for the monastery of Saint Giles. ibid.

**CLII.** Pope Urban II confirms the regular discipline of the canons of the Church of Saint Rufus at Avignon; they, together with all the property belonging to that canonical institution, are received under the protection of the Apostolic See. 426

**CLIII.** Privilege granted by Urban II to the Church of Saint Rufus, with the canonical reverence of the bishop of Avignon preserved in all respects. 427

**CLIV.** Privilege of Pope Urban II for the Church of Mâcon. 428

**CLV.** Letter of Pope Urban II to Guarnerius of Châtillon. — Under penalty of excommunication, he orders him to release Lambert, bishop of Arras, who had been captured while traveling to the synod. 429

**CLVI.** Letter of Pope Urban II to the archbishop of Sens. — He orders him to warn Guarnerius to release the bishop of Arras. [Col. 1481] 430

**CLVII.** Privilege for the monastery of Silvacane. ibid.

**CLVIII.** Settlement reached at the Council of Clermont between Godefridus, bishop of Maguelone, and Peter, abbot of Aniane. 431

**CLIX.** Bull confirming the privileges of the monastery of Celsiniacum. 432

**CLX.** Letter of Pope Urban II to the canons of Angoulême, by which he confirms the grant of the provostship of Juilly made to them by Ademar. 433

**CLXI.** Pope Urban II confirms the possessions and rights of the monastery of Aubechies. 434

**CLXII.** Confirmation of Saint-Denis at Nogent, made by Lord Pope Urban II. 435

**CLXIII.** Letter of Pope Urban II to Count Guigo. 436

**CLXIV.** Synodal letter of Urban to the clergy and people of Cambrai. 437

**CLXV.** Decree of Urban II concerning the primacy of Lyons. 438

**CLXVI.** Privilege for the church of Saint James at Compostela. 440

**CLXVII.** Letter of Urban II to Hugh, abbot of Cluny. — He grants the monks of Cluny permission to retain altars and tithes that they have purchased, and to withdraw tithes from lay hands, if this can be done according to God’s will. 441

**CLXVIII.** Diploma of Pope Urban confirming all the privileges and possessions of the priory of Marcigny. 442

**CLXIX.** Letter of Pope Urban II to Ademar, bishop of Angoulême. — That he compel the monks of Saint Eparchius, by the penalty of excommunication, to obey the abbot of Saint Jean d’Angély. 443

**CLXX.** Bull of Pope Urban II for the monastery of Tulle. 444

**CLXXI.** Letter of Urban II to the suffragans of the Church of Reims. — He exhorts them to obey Manasses, who had been substituted in place of the deceased archbishop Raynald. 445

**CLXXII.** He exhorts the clergy, religious order, knights, and people of Reims to pledge their fidelity to Manasses, the elected archbishop. ibid.

**CLXXIII.** He congratulates Manasses, the elected archbishop of Reims. He warns him to take the utmost care and remain vigilant lest, through any instability, he become subject to royal arrogance. He promises assistance. 447

**CLXXIV.** Letter of Urban II to Philip, bishop of Châlons. — He commends to him and to his brother Hugh, count of Champagne, the monks of Saint Vanne at Verdun, who had been expelled by their parishioners from the church of Saint Nicholas in the Forest of Lugol. ibid.

**CLXXV.** Privilege granted by Urban II to the monastery of Saint Nicholas, with the canonical reverence of the bishop of Angers preserved. ibid.

**CLXXVI.** Letter of Urban II to the suffragans of the Church of Reims. 449

**CLXXVII.** Letter of Urban II to the clergy of Tours. — He confirms the privileges of the Church of Tours. ibid.

**CLXXVIII.** Letter of Urban II to the monks of Saint Peter at Bainson. — He protects by the authority of the Apostolic See the church of Bainson, which their parents had given to the monastery of Cluny, and determines the rights of the Church of Soissons. 450

**CLXXIX.** Pope Urban II receives all the property and rights of the monastery of Trenorcy under the protection of the Apostolic See. 451

**CLXXX.** Privilege for the monastery of Saint Vincent at Metz. 452

**CLXXXI.** Urban II confirms to the abbey of Saint Bertin of the Order of Saint Benedict at Saint-Omer all its altars and possessions. 453

**CLXXXII.** Privilege of Urban II for the church of Marbach. 455

**CLXXXIII.** Urban II confirms the privileges of the monastery of Corbie. 456

**CLXXXIV.** He grants Gerard, the new abbot of the monastery of Saint Maur at Glanfeuil, an extensive privilege. ibid.

**CLXXXV.** At the Council of Tours, Urban settled the dispute between the canons of Saint Martin and the monks of Cormery, with judgment rendered in favor of the canons. He decreed that the abbots of Cormery were to take the pastoral staff from the tomb of Saint Martin at the common command of the dean and chapter. ibid.

**CLXXXVI.** Letter of Urban II to the canons of Saint Martin of Tours. — Against the Simonians. 457

**CLXXXVI (second).** Privilege of Pope Urban II for the canons of Saint Martin of Tours. 459 [Col. 1482]

**CLXXXVII.** Letter of Urban II to Richer of Sens and the other bishops of France. — Concerning not absolving an excommunicated king. 460

**CLXXXVIII.** Bull of Pope Urban II for the New Monastery at Poitiers. — He receives the New Monastery, whose church he had dedicated, under the protection of the Apostolic See and subjects it to the monastery of Cluny. 461

**CLXXXIX.** Bull for the monastery of Saint Martial at Limoges. 462

**CXC.** Letter of Pope Urban II to Raymond, archbishop of Auch. — Against the clerics who had violated the cemetery of Saint Orientius. 464

**CXCI.** Urban II confirms the possessions of the monastery of Saint Aubin at Angers. 465

**CXCII.** He reports what was established at the assembly held at Saint-Hilaire on the occasion of the disputes that had arisen between the canons of Saint-Hilaire and the monks of the New Monastery at Poitiers who lived in the priory of Saint Nicholas. 465

**CXCIII.** Letter of Pope Urban II to Ansculf, abbot of Angers. — He confirms to him the church of Bury, acquired through the gift of the bishop of Beauvais and secured by the assent of the king of the Franks. ibid.

**CXCIV.** Urban II asserts the hill of Saint Michael at Monte Alto for the monastery of Cluny. ibid.

**CXCV.** Urban II confirms the privileges of the Church of Pamplona at the request of Bishop Peter of Roda. 466

**CXCVI.** Bull confirming the privileges of the monastery of Moissac. ibid.

**CXCVII.** Letter of Pope Urban II to Hugh, abbot of Cluny. 467

**CXCVIII.** Diploma of Pope Urban II concerning the donation of the abbey of Beaulieu. 468

**CXCIX.** At the council held at Nîmes, Urban, having abolished the order of Gregory VII, forbids the monasteries of Figeac and Conques to be united. He orders each monastery to be governed by its own abbot. 469

**CC.** Bull of Pope Urban II for Saint Martin of the Fields. 470

**CCI.** Urban subjects the Church of Burgos directly to the Roman Church, releasing it from obedience to other metropolitan churches. 471

**CCII.** Pope Urban II confirms the possessions of the monastery of Ripoll, to which he grants certain privileges of immunity and exemption. 472

**CCII (second).** Privilege of Pope Urban II for the monastery of Banyoles. 474

**CCIII.** Privilege of the monastery of Juvigny. 476

**CCIV.** Privilege for the monastery of Saint Giles. 477

**CCV.** Bull for the church of Saint Saturninus at Toulouse. 478

**CCVI.** Urban confirms the privileges and possessions of the monastery of Saint Andrew at Avignon. 480

**CCVII.** Letter of Pope Urban to Coloman, king of Hungary, against the antipope Guibert, or Clement III. ibid.

**CCVIII.** Letter of Urban II, Supreme Pontiff, to Gebhard, bishop of Constance, that he arrange for a certain monk to be returned by the people of Reitenbuch to the monks of Schaffhausen. 482

**CCIX.** Letter of the same pope to Odalric, or Udalric, provost of Reitenbuch. — Concerning the same matter. ibid.

**CCX.** Letter of Pope Urban II to the people of Bologna. — He praises their faith. He offers remission of sins to all who have taken part in the war for Jerusalem. 483

**CCXI.** Bull of Pope Urban II confirming all the rights of the nuns of Saint John the Evangelist at Cremona. 484

**CCXII.** Letter of Urban II to Alexius, emperor of Constantinople. — Concerning the expedition to the Holy Land and the taking up of the cross. 485

**CCXIII.** Letter of Urban to Gerard of Thérouanne. — Those who despise the canons are to be excommunicated. ibid.

**CCXIV.** Urban confirms and enlarges the liberties and privileges of the monastery of Cluny. ibid.

**CCXV.** Letter of Pope Urban II to the clergy and people of the Church of Trani. 488

**CCXVI.** Letter of Urban II to Hugh, archbishop of Lyons. ibid.

**CCXVII.** Urban commends the Church of Pamplona to Peter, king of the Aragonese and Pamplonese, and to all the faithful of those regions. 489

**CCXVIII.** Urban restores to Oderisius, cardinal of the Roman Church and abbot of the monastery of Monte Cassino, whom he himself had consecrated, the monastery of Glanfeuil, which had been adjudicated to the monks of Fosses. ibid. [Col. 1483]

**CCXIX.** Pope Urban II confirms the sacred monastery of Monte Cassino and all its possessions, free from every jurisdiction, under the protection of the Holy Roman Church, and declares that it is to be preferred to all the other monasteries of the West. 492

**CCXX.** Privilege of Pope Urban II to Saint Hugh for the immunity of the Cluniac cells, together with an interdict and the liberty to summon to Cluny any bishop he wished for the making of chrism and the blessing of oil. 493

**CCXXI.** Urban II confirms the privileges and possessions of the Church of Clermont and establishes that its bishop shall occupy the first place at the ordination of the metropolitan of Bourges. 494

**CCXXII.** Letter of Pope Urban II to Raymond, archbishop of Auch. — Against the clerics who had violated the cemetery of Saint Orientius. 494

**CCXXIII.** The district of Salm is asserted for the Church of Grenoble. ibid.

**CCXXIV.** Letter of Pope Urban II to Bertrand, archbishop of Narbonne. He strengthens the privileges of the Church of Narbonne. 495

**CCXXV.** Letter of Pope Urban II to Peter Goffridus, archbishop of Aix. — He orders him to show reverence to the archbishop of Narbonne as primate. 496

**CCXXVI.** Letter of Urban II to Hugh, archbishop of Lyons. — That he compel the archbishop of Aix to obey his primate, the archbishop of Narbonne. ibid.

**CCXXVII.** Privilege for the Church of Veroli. ibid.

**CCXXVIII.** Urban II undertakes the protection of the church of Saint Mary at Bouron; he confirms its possessions and establishes its privileges, imposing upon the brothers an annual census of one gold bezant. 498

**CCXXIX.** Letter of Urban II to Manasses, archbishop of Reims. 499

**CCXXX.** Letter of Pope Urban II to Bernard, bishop of Bologna. — He commends certain brothers who had been ordained unwillingly by heretics. 500

**CCXXXI.** Urban asserts to Jarento, abbot of Saint Benignus at Dijon, the monastery of Saint Vigor at Bayeux, which had been donated by Bishop Odo. ibid.

**CCXXXII.** Letter of Urban to Udalric, abbot of the monastery of Saint Michael at the Meuse. — He grants permission to establish a cemetery around the new church. ibid.

**CCXXXIII.** Bull of Pope Urban II for the monastery of Wiblingen. 501

**CCXXXIV.** Bull of Urban II for the Church of Urgell. 502

**CCXXXV.** Urban asserts to Landulf, provost of the church of Saint Ambrose at Milan, the offerings of the high altar and of the other altars that are or shall be established within the walls of the church of Blessed Ambrose. 504

**CCXXXVI.** Bull of Pope Urban II for the monastery of Jesus of Nazareth (Monte Aragón). ibid.

**CCXXXVII.** Letter of Urban to Peter, bishop of Huesca. — He constitutes the Church of Huesca the head of the Church of Jaca. ibid.

**CCXXXVIII.** Urban writes to William, king of the English, that he should set Anselm’s property free in his kingdom and reinvest him with all his possessions. 506

**CCXXXIX.** Letter of Urban II to Count Roger of Sicily. — Concerning the privilege of the Sicilian monarchy. ibid.

**CCXL.** At the request of Duke Roger, Urban asserts the primacy of the provinces of Acerenza and Cosenza for Alphano, archbishop of Salerno, and his successors. 507

**CCXLI.** Urban II confirms the possessions granted to Bruno and Lanuinus, hermits, by Count Roger and John, bishop of Squillace. 509

**CCXLII.** After consecrating Gerlandus bishop, Urban confirms the boundaries of the restored Church of Agrigento. 510

**CCXLIII.** Letter of Urban II to the brothers of Saint Hubert at Andage. 511

**CCXLIV.** Letter of Urban II to the people of Liège on behalf of Abbot Theoderic. ibid.

**CCXLV.** Rescript of Urban II for the monastery of Monte Cassino. 512

**CCXLVI.** Bull of Pope Urban II for the monastery of Saint Cucuphas. 513

**CCXLVII.** Bull of Urban II for the monastery of Monte Cassino. 515

**CCXLVIII.** Letter of Urban II to Manasses, archbishop of Reims. 517

**CCXLIX.** Bull for the abbot of the Greater Monastery at Tours. 518

**CCL.** Letter of Urban II to the bishop of Magdeburg. — He exhorts him not to waver but to stand firm in the just cause. [Col. 1484] 518

**CCLI.** Urban II appoints Hartmann, abbot of Göttweig, as an assistant to Gebhard, bishop of Constance, in the apostolic legation. 519

**CCLII.** Urban II confirms the privileges of the monastery of Göttweig at the request of Hartmann, its abbot. ibid.

**CCLIII.** Privilege of immunity granted to the monastery of Schaffhausen at Hirsau. ibid.

**CCLIV.** Letter of Urban II to Count Rudolf. — Concerning ecclesiastical immunity. 521

**CCLV.** Letter of Urban II to Hugh, archbishop of Lyons. ibid.

**CCLVI.** Letter of Urban II to the bishops of Embrun, Gap, and Die. — Before they are reconciled, no one is compelled to keep faith with excommunicated persons. ibid.

**CCLVII.** Letter of Urban II to Hugh, bishop of Grenoble. — Extraordinary pollution of the genitals does not impede marriage. 522

**CCLVIII.** Letter of Pope Urban II to Hugh, abbot of Cluny. — He grants him the monastery of Saint Bertin to be formed according to Cluniac customs. ibid.

**CCLIX.** Privilege of Pope Urban II granted to Rainer, abbot of the monastery of Saint Peter at Crispin, Rome. ibid.

**CCLX.** Urban II receives the monastery of Généré in Gascony into the right and ownership of the Apostolic See and fortifies it with a privilege, subject to an annual census of two ounces of gold. 523

**CCLXI.** Privilege of Pope Urban II for the monastery of Lagny. 523

**CCLXII.** Letter of Urban II to Roger, bishop of Soissons. — That regular canons be instituted in the parish churches. 524

**CCLXIII.** Letter of Pope Urban to Bernard, archbishop of Toledo. 525

**CCLXIV.** Bull of Pope Urban II to Peter, bishop of Jaca. ibid.

**CCLXV.** Privilege of Pope Urban II for the Church of Jaca. 526

**CCLXVI.** Urban absolves Petronius, bishop of León, born of an illegitimate mother, from the bond of this sin. 527

**CCLXVII.** Urban II entrusts Countess Matilda with the restoration of the church of Saint Florian, to be carried out by the bishop of Mantua in favor of the monastery of Saint Benedict at Polirone. ibid.

**CCLXVIII.** Letter of Urban II to the clergy and people of Salerno. — Concerning ecclesiastical immunity. 528

**CCLXIX.** Letter of Urban II to Godinus, bishop of Oria. — He orders him to return to the city of Brindisi the episcopal see that had formerly been transferred to the city of Oria. ibid.

**CCLXX.** Letter of Urban to Vitalis, a priest of Brescia. — Mercy may be shown to Simonians in preserving their dignity if their life commends them. ibid.

**CCLXXI.** To the same. — Sons or daughters born before or after spiritual kinship may legitimately be joined in marriage. 529

**CCLXXII.** To the same. — A wife, together with her husband, is not to receive someone’s son at baptism. ibid.

**CCLXXIII.** To Lucius, provost of Saint Juventius. — Concerning the validity of baptism and the other sacraments administered by criminal priests. ibid.

**CCLXXIV.** Urban establishes privileges for the church of the Holy Trinity at the place called Pons Guinizeli, on the condition that its clerics pay six coins of Milanese currency every four years to the Lateran palace. 533

**CCLXXV.** Pope Urban, in a letter to the people of Saint Vincent at San Vincenzo al Volturno near Capua. 534

**CCLXXVI.** Urban II permits the infant daughter of Prince Jordan, betrothed to Rainald, son of Rodel, against the wishes of her mother and relatives, to be married to another man. ibid.

**CCLXXVII.** Another decree of Urban II. 535

**CCLXXVIII.** Another decree of Urban II. ibid.

**CCLXXIX.** Urban II writes to certain regular canons concerning the restoration of canonical discipline. ibid.

**CCLXXX.** Letter of Urban to Bernard, archbishop of Toledo. — Since Richard, bishop of Marseille, has been deprived of his legation, Bernard himself is to supervise everything; the archbishop of Compostela, released from his bonds, is to be restored to his office. Urban asks whom Bernard thinks should be entrusted with the legation. 536

**CCLXXXI.** Letter of Pope Urban II to Galon, provost of Saint Quentin at Beauvais. — He confirms the donation of the land of Alnella made by William, bishop of Paris. 537

**CCLXXXII.** Urban sends letters on behalf of the monks of Saint Andrew at Vienne, whom Guido, archbishop of that city, had harassed so severely, together with their bailiffs, that he even detained some of them in prison. ibid. [Col. 1485]

**CCLXXXIII.** Urban writes to Yves, bishop of Chartres, and Ramnulf, bishop of Saintes, on behalf of the monks of Vendôme, whom he declares exempt from every subjection to bishops. ibid.

**CCLXXXIV.** The freedom of the monastery of Vendôme is confirmed. 537

**CCLXXXV.** Letter of Urban to the archbishops and bishops of France. — He rejoices that King Philip, who had dismissed his wife and given himself to an adulteress, has returned to his senses. 538

**CCLXXXVI.** Letter of Urban to Hugh, abbot of Cluny. — He informs him that he recently decreed at the Roman synod that the monastery of Saint Germain at Auxerre, which its abbot had surrendered to him at the Council of Nîmes, should be entrusted to Hugh. ibid.

**CCLXXXVII.** Bull of Urban II establishing the see of Barbastro. 539

**CCLXXXVIII.** Letter of Urban to Ingelrannus, bishop of Laon. — He exhorts him to restore the altar of Corbeny to the brothers of Blessed Remigius. 539

**CCLXXXIX.** Urban II confirms the monastery of Blaubeuren in the diocese of Constance, together with all the donations made to it by Adelaide and her uncles. 540

**CCXC.** Bull of Pope Urban II by which the monastery of Saint Blaise is received under the protection of the Apostolic See. 541

**CCXCI.** Bull of Urban II for the monastery of Saint Saturninus in the district of Urgell. 542

**CCXCII.** Letter of Urban to Hugh, archbishop of Lyons. — He announces that Hugh’s primacy has finally been recognized at Rome by Daimbert, archbishop of Sens. 543

**CCXCIII.** Urban orders that the institution of regular discipline established by Andrew, founder of the monastery of Casale Saint Peter, according to the custom of the Vallombrosan brothers, be perpetually preserved there. 544

**CCXCIV.** He confirms the possessions of the monastery of Saint Cross at the request of Amatus, archbishop of Bordeaux. 545

**CCXCV.** Letter of Urban to Hugh, archbishop of Lyons. — Concerning the recall of Robert, abbot of Cîteaux, from the wilderness. ibid.

**CCXCVI.** Letter of Urban II on behalf of John, archdeacon of Arras. ibid.

**CCXCVII.** Urban confirms the freedom of the monastery of Psalmodi, so that the people of Marseille may exercise no domination there. ibid.

**CCXCVIII.** Letter of Pope Urban II to the canons of Saint Andrew at Bordeaux. — He makes known that their dispute with the clerics of Saint Severinus was settled at the Roman council in such a way that the church of Saint Andrew should have its own cemetery in
perpetual. ibid.

CCXCIX.—Letter of Pope Urban II to Peter, provost, and the canons of the church of Rodez. 546

CCC.—Letter of Urban to Alfanus, archbishop of Salerno. 547

CCCI.—Bull of Pope Urban II declaring that the body of the most blessed lawgiver and patriarch of monks, Benedict, rests at Cassino, on the revelation of that same holy Father and the sign of restored health. 549

CCCII.—Urban grants to Peter, king of the Spains, and to his duly appointed successors that they may distribute among whatever monasteries they wish the churches of villages—both those they may capture in Saracen lands and those they themselves may build in the kingdom—excepting only episcopal sees. He grants the nobles of the kingdom the same permission, so that they may retain for themselves and their heirs, together with the firstfruits and tithes belonging specifically to their own inheritances, the churches which they have acquired by right of war in Saracen lands or founded on their own hereditary estates, or may place them under the jurisdiction of any chapels or monasteries. 550

CCCIII.—Urban commands the clergy and people of Limoges to obey Bishop Humbaldus, after he had been cleared of simony and fully restored by Urban himself. 551

CCCIV.—He again commends Bishop Humbaldus to the clergy and people of Limoges. 552

## Stephen I, First King of Hungary

1207. Life of Saint Stephen, by Carthuitius, Bishop.

1209. Chapter I.—The saint’s father; his birth, illumined by preceding visions; his baptism; the beginnings of his reign and his care for the propagation of religion; his victory over the rebels; and, consequently, the monastery of Saint Martin founded by vow.  
1213. Chapter II.—His care for advancing religion; the arrival of many people in Hungary; the monastery constructed; the bishoprics established; the legate sent to Rome, who obtains the royal crown and many privileges from the pontiff; his marriage to Gisela and the pious works of both.  
1218. Chapter III.—His devotion to the Blessed Virgin; the church at Alba Regalis constructed and adorned with gifts and privileges; pious foundations in Jerusalem, Rome, and Constantinople; the king’s mercy and generosity, and his miracles.  
1222. Chapter IV.—The war brought by Emperor Conrad, swiftly ended through God’s wondrous providence; the saint’s frequent prayer and rapture; a notable example of severity; the king’s illness and the death of his sons; and his various virtues.  
1222. Chapter V.—His illness; during it, a conspiracy of certain persons is discovered; his blessed death; burial; the decree for the elevation of his body; and the miracles performed when the tomb was opened.  
1230. Chapter VI.—The elevation of the body and the miracles; the wondrous discovery and incorruptibility of the right hand.

## Saint Mathilda, Queen
**Earlier Life.** 1311

**Mathildis’s Letter to Misego II, King of Poland.** Preface. 1327

**Critical-Historical-Exegetical Commentary on This Letter.** 1327

**Chapter I.** Method of treating the history. 1327

**Chapter II.** The manuscript liturgical book of Charlemagne and Alcuin is described. 1329

**Chapter III.** Mathildis the Swabian’s dedicatory letter to Misego. 1331

**Chapter IV.** On the form of the letters and the punctuation of the manuscript. 1331

**Chapter V.** An example of unusual syntax. 1333

**Chapter VI.** On Misego III, duke of the Poles. 1333

**Chapter VII.** Misego I from the Polish sources. 1334

**Chapter VIII.** On the same Misego I according to the German sources. 1335

**Chapter IX.** Whether Miseco could have been called the first king, and whether he is our Misego. 1337

**Chapter X.** On Bolizlav I, Misego II’s father. He obtains rule over all Poland and supplies assistance to the emperor. 1338

**Chapter XI.** Bolizlav I conquers the Pomeranians and perhaps the Prussians. 1339

**Chapter XII.** Adalbert’s life and death. 1340

**Chapter XIII.** Chrobatia subdued by Bolizlav I. 1342

**Chapter XIV.** Otto III comes to Gniezno. Archbishops and bishops are ordained. 1341

**Chapter XV.** Bolizlav I occupies Bohemia and the March of Meissen.

**Chapter XVI.** Bolizlav I is expelled from Bohemia. Lusatia is lost but recovered. Peace is made. 1345

**Chapter XVII.** War against Vladimir, the great prince of the Russians. 1347

**Chapter XVIII.** Bolizlav’s war against the emperor and the Russians, joined in alliance. Peace is made with the emperor. 1348

**Chapter XIX.** Kiev is captured by Bolizlav, and the cities of Cherven are occupied. 1349

**Chapter XX.** The coronation and death of Bolizlav I according to certain authorities. Bolizlav I can be called a certain source, etc. 1350

**Chapter XXI.** Misego II from the Polish sources. 1350

**Chapter XXII.** What Raepellius says about Misego on the basis of the Polish sources. 1352

**Chapter XXIII.** Misego II from the German sources. 1352

**Chapter XXIV.** On Rixa and Casimir, and what is related about Misego II’s other sons. 1355

**Chapter XXV.** That our book was in fact written to Misego II, apparently in the year 1027. 1359

**Chapter XXVI.** On Mathildis’s father Hermann. Whether Hermann was the first, third, or fourth [of that name]. 1360

**Chapter XXVII.** On Hermann II, duke of the Swabians, and his wife Gerberga. 1361

**Chapter XXVIII.** On Hermann II’s daughters. On the empress Gisela and on N., Adalbero’s wife. 1363

**Chapter XXIX.** On Mathilde, daughter of Gerberga (and Hermann II). 1364

**Chapter XXX.** Mathildis’s first husband, Conrad, duke of Carinthia; their sons. 1364

[Col. 1496] **Chapter XXXI.** Mathildis’s second husband, Frederick II, duke of Lorraine; his daughter Beatrix and his granddaughter Mathildis, the margravine. 1366

**Chapter XXXII.** Our book does not appear to have been written by Mathildis’s own hand, but to be the work of several Frankish-Gallic scribes.

**Chapter XXXIII.** Bolizlav I: did he subdue the Prussians before or after the martyrdom of Saint Adalbert? Only a very small part was subdued; the date remains uncertain. 1368

**Chapter XXXIV.** Bolizlav I could already have been called king before Otto III visited him. The use and abuse of royal authority among all peoples. 1370

**Chapter XXXV.** The names of rulers among the Slavonic peoples. 1375

**Chapter XXXVI.** Bolizlav, presented by Otto III with a royal crown, a lance or scepter, and a sword, is called “friend of the Roman people.” 1380

**Chapter XXXVII.** The crown in our picture is a model of Otto’s own crown. The Lombard crown appears in a new form on the seals of the Ottos. 1382

**Chapter XXXVIII.** A new anointing as king appears to have been performed by the archbishop of Gniezno, with the apostolic see’s approval; the sons together; and tribute was given to Saint Peter. 1385

**Chapter XXXIX.** Misego II held royal dignity among the Poles, despite the German writers, and was versed in letters, even Greek, as was the entire lineage of the empress Theophano, and so forth. 1387

**Chapter XL.** It is demonstrated that the Russians suffered defeat in the year 1026. 1388

**Chapter XLI.** Pagans and others hostile to the Latin Church and the king had already defected from Misego II. 1389

**Chapter XLII.** A certain Judith appears to have borne Misego II a son, apparently the firstborn, the younger Bolizlav, a supporter of the pagans or of the Slavonic-Greek Church. 1392

**Chapter XLIII.** Misego II was unfortunate, not because he was unwarlike, but because he had many enemies all around him at once. Expelled from the kingdom, he lived miserably as a monk at Prague. Sudden illness and death. 1393

**Chapter XLIV.** Rixa may have been exiled from Poland twice: the first time, indeed, with her son Casimir; the second time, she may have preceded her son. 1394

**Chapter XLV.** The younger Bolizlav, relying on the pagans or the Greek-Slavonic party, becomes king of the Poles after expelling his brother Casimir; but he is soon killed by Latin Christians. Poland is divided; the Latin Christians recall Casimir, while the Greeks or pagans use Maslao as king for a short time. 1395

**Chapter XLVI.** The cruelty of the Poles at that time was the same as that of the other peoples: Russians, Bohemians, Hungarians, Danes, Normans, and Germans. The origin of the word *Sklave*. 1396

**Chapter XLVII.** Why Mathildis sent this book to Misego. 1398
